Changing the field_map-driven scalar field extraction (datetime/info are post-parse enrichment, not field_map entries)
task.body:
Consumer trading_dashboard re-test (./BUGS.md 2026-06-21) and live tidewave verification confirm: after T152/T154 the unified ticker populates symbol + quote_volume, but datetime and info are still nil. Both are CONSUMER-side, universal CCXT conventions the read path does not yet apply:

- datetime: CCXT derives the ISO8601 datetime string from the integer timestamp in the unified layer (this.iso8601(timestamp)), not from a raw field. timestamp IS populated (e.g. 1782018260504 from closeTime); datetime stays nil because nothing derives it. A private iso8601 helper already exists at lib/ccxt/dispatch.ex:424 — extract it to a shared util and apply post-parse.
- info: by universal CCXT convention every unified struct carries info = the raw exchange response so consumers can reach exchange-specific fields the struct does not model. The read path drops it (info: nil). Stash the raw decoded body the parser consumed onto the struct.

Apply both as a single universal post-parse enrichment step in the unified read path (read_parse.ex) so it covers ticker, trade, order, market, orderbook, etc. — not a per-method patch. Anchor: trading_dashboard needs info to reach raw fields (named consumer impact, ./BUGS.md ticker + markets entries, defect 'info: nil'); datetime makes %CCXT.Ticker{} timestamps human/serializable. NOTE base_volume is explicitly OUT of scope — it is an upstream distill field_map source-key bug (reported), not a consumer gap.

task.title: T-A: Differential fixture gate (REST request + response) against in-repo CCXT static fixtures
acceptance_criteria: Response gate: each static/response/<ex>.json method case runs httpResponse through the normalizer and asserts equality with parsedResponse, for the 7 first-class venues

WS fixtures (T-G)
Removing distill tooling (T-E1)
task.body:
See docs/authored-specs.md (the anchor). This is the verification floor for the authored-specs pivot — nothing authored is trusted until this gate is green; it must land first.

Retarget Task 156's existing replay harness (test/support/test_generator/recorded_response_replay.ex, lib/ccxt/recorded_response_fixtures.ex) to consume the in-repo CCXT static RESPONSE fixtures at priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/response/<ex>.json: for each method case, feed httpResponse through the normalizer entrypoint (cleanest via the Unified.call/5 + Req.Test stub the harness already uses, reaching CCXT.Unified.ReadParse.parse) and assert the result equals parsedResponse.

task.title: T-B: Own the spec schema as a versioned compile-time contract (decouple from distill; split authored slice from frozen bulk)
acceptance_criteria: CCXT.Spec no longer requires _provenance or distill manifest fields; load!/strip/exchanges still pass
schema_version is an owned local constant (ours, e.g. @schema_version 1) — no distill major-3 assertion; a bump is a deliberate migration we own, not an upstream event
Never-read distill fields are dropped from the load path, each verified zero-reader by grep

First-class venue specs are split on the authorship seam: frozen mechanical bulk in <venue>.json, the AI-authored interpretive slice in a separate small reviewable file the loader merges at compile time; the long-tail catalog stays single-file frozen

The exchange macro enforces the contract at compile time: a spec marked authored/first-class missing a required authored slot raises with the offending venue + slot (keys off an authored marker so unauthored venues do not raise)

Authoring the actual venue slices (T-C/170, T-D/171) — this defines the layout + contract; authoring fills it
Building macro-generated pattern-match verification — a follow-on gated on 168; just keep the schema shape so it is reachable
Splitting the long-tail catalog (~103 venues stay single-file frozen)
task.body:
See docs/authored-specs.md (§ "The schema is ours — versioned compile-time contract"). Reshape the spec loader and exchange macro into the owned compile-time contract that every first-class venue authoring task consumes.

Three coupled moves, all "the schema is ours, not distill's":

1. Decouple from distill. Drop CCXT.Spec's non-empty _provenance requirement and the distill-provenance manifest fields (source_git_sha, source, ccxt_version, extracted_at); replace the "schema major 3" distill assertion with an owned local @schema_version constant. A version bump becomes a deliberate migration WE own, not an upstream churn event — this is what finally kills the five-times-re-dispatched treadmill. Keep load!/strip/exchanges working. Drop the ~20 never-read distill fields (method_inventory, interfaces, sign_method AST, descriptors, parse_methods_digest, symbols_index, etc.) — confirm zero readers by grep before removing each. Define "our schema" = the load-bearing key set actually read: raw.describe.*, auth.sign_recipe, normalization.{field_maps,response_envelopes}, markets.{patterns,currencies}, errors.handle_errors.error_code_fields, endpoints.*, rate_limits.*, testnet, websocket.{urls,heartbeat,auth}, fees, config, capabilities.

2. Split first-class specs on the authorship seam. The frozen mechanical bulk stays in <venue>.json; the AI-authored interpretive slice (sign_recipe, field_maps, response_envelopes, markets.patterns, error fields) moves to a separate small, git-diffable file the loader merges at compile time. Apply only to the 7 first-class venues — the split earns its keep only where slices get hand-authored and reviewed; the long-tail catalog stays single-file frozen. Under distill the file was one wholesale projection (splitting gained nothing); under authoring the two halves have different lifecycles (frozen-once vs hand-owned-reviewed-against-fixtures), which is the real seam. Do NOT split per-method — field_maps are co-authored in one reading session.

3. Make the schema an enforced compile-time contract. The exchange macro (use CCXT.Exchange) checks at compile time that a spec marked authored/first-class carries every required authored slot well-formed — raising with the offending venue + slot if not. Key the check off an authored marker so unauthored venues (pre-T-C/T-D) don't raise; T-C/T-D set the marker as each venue is authored, activating the check. A missing slice is a whole-surface defect the per-task reviewer is structurally blind to — encode it as a compile failure, not a consumer discovery.

See docs/authored-specs.md. Proof-of-loop: establish the AI-authoring workflow and measure its real cost before the fleet (T-D).

Use Deribit as the proof venue. Freeze its mechanical bulk from the current vendored spec. Author interpretive slices by reading CCXT-JS, the live API, and official Deribit documentation or SDK: CCXT execution establishes compatibility while the exchange sources establish correctness.

The loop is: read JS -> write slice -> run the T-A gate (mix test.json) -> diff -> iterate until green. Do not trust the authoring; the fixture diff is the offline acceptance signal — but it is tier-2 (compatibility with CCXT's interpretation), NOT proof of correctness against reality. So the loop does not end at green-offline: per the live-testnet-first behavioral default (CLAUDE.md / docs/authored-specs.md § "Compatibility ≠ correctness"), the FIRST and the FINAL verification move is a real signed testnet call — confirm the authored request-build + read-parse actually work against the live venue before freezing. A field can be tier-2-green and wrong/400ing live (the documented deribit fetch_ohlcv gap); proof-of-loop must prove the WHOLE loop including reality, or T-D inherits a tier-2-only gate. When both tiers pass, mark the spec hand-owned/frozen (a flag/marker so any future sync excludes it). task.body:
Apply the Deribit proof loop to Bybit as one bounded venue dispatch. Author from the live API, official Bybit documentation or SDK, and CCXT-JS as a compatibility reference; do not treat CCXT as the semantic arbiter.

REPRO EVIDENCE (live tidewave, 2026-06-23) — the tier1/tier2 gap is the fetchOHLCV request-build, and it is an AUTHORING gap, not a runtime-heuristic bug to patch. Measured across the whole catalog: 182 of 186 fetchOHLCV request_param_shape entries are `kind: "unresolved", value: nil` (85 venues) — authoring punted on nearly all of them, so the legacy `RequestShape.identifier_value` heuristic (slated for deletion, T-E2/173) guesses the source unified param from the native key STRING. That guess is wrong wherever a venue has both a renamed-symbol key and a renamed-timeframe key:
- okx fetchOHLCV: shape = {instId, bar, limit} (all unresolved). The greedy `:timeframe in required and native_key != "symbol"` branch assigns the timeframe value to BOTH `bar` AND `instId` -> builds `instId=1m&bar=1m`; instId should carry the denormalized symbol (BTC-USDT), bar the timeframe. Authoring each entry's source (instId<-symbol, bar<-timeframe, limit<-limit) + having RequestShape read the authored source fixes it without heuristics.
- kraken fetchOHLCV: shape = {pair} ONLY — no interval entry at all. Builds `pair=1` (pair wrongly gets the timeframe). Genuine authoring gap: the `interval` (timeframe) target is missing from the shape entirely; pair<-symbol must be authored too.
- binanceusdm fetchOHLCV: ENDPOINT-selection bug (distinct from param-shaping but same path) — resolves to `/fapi/v1/indexPriceKlines` (needs `pair`) instead of `/fapi/v1/klines`. Author the USD-M market-type endpoint mapping per binance.ts.
- binance + binanceus fetchOHLCV: now PASS live (500 real candles) after the RequestShape symbol-drop + timeframe-leak fixes (a2c87e4) — confirms the request-build path is correct once the shape disambiguates; the residual failures above are purely un-authored/wrong shapes.
The keyword-distribution swamp (interval/resolution/period/bar/granularity/tf/binSize... for timeframe; instId/pair/market/product_id... for symbol) is why a bigger heuristic keyword-set is the wrong fix — author the source per entry.

2026-07-15 — consumer re-verification sweep (BUGS.md, trading_dashboard) folded in: two bybit fetch_ohlcv residuals remain after 190/178 — (a) SPOT category resolution is not wired for fetch_ohlcv (linear works, spot errors "Category is invalid"), and (b) candles return as raw [ts,o,h,l,c] arrays because no bybit OHLCV parse slice is authored (the task-178 columnar transformer is deribit-proven and waiting). Both are per-venue authoring, owned here (see the two new ACs). Not a trading_dashboard v1 blocker.

ENDPOINT-SELECTION is the SAME authoring defect class (not a separate mechanical bug). A unified method can map to a LIST of candidate endpoints and dispatch defaults to spec-order index 0, which is arbitrary, not semantic. binanceusdm fetch_ohlcv resolves to a list [dapiPublic indexPriceKlines, dapiPublic klines, markPriceKlines, premiumIndexKlines, eapiPublic klines, fapiPublic indexPriceKlines, ...] and picks index 0 = `dapiPublic/indexPriceKlines` — wrong VARIANT (index-price, not plain klines) AND wrong MARKET TYPE (COIN-M dapi, not USD-M fapi). CCXT hand-writes this selection in its fetchOHLCV method (price param -> mark/index/premium variant; else plain klines; market type -> section). So authored request-build must also author WHICH endpoint, not just the params: default to the plain-klines variant in the correct market-type section, switch on the `price` param. Affects the whole binance family (variant + dapi/eapi/fapi sections) and any multi-endpoint method (bybit fetchOHLCV = 4 kline endpoints).

task.body:
Prerequisite surfaced by T-C (170): authoring deribit's public-read slices against the T-A static-fixture response gate (test/ccxt/recorded_response_replay_test.exs) revealed the unified read-parse path cannot currently express what CCXT's parse* methods do, so authored field_maps cannot go green no matter how correctly authored. Make the read-parse path capable of faithfully reproducing CCXT parse* for the public-read methods the 7 first-class venues expose. The T-A response gate is the only acceptance oracle — read CCXT JS (priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/<venue>.ts) for the exact semantics, verify against the static-fixture parsedResponse.

Four capability gaps found on deribit (all recur across venues/methods — verify against okx/bybit/binance too, do not overfit to deribit):

1. Nested / dotted key reads. CCXT reads e.g. ticker high/low/quoteVolume from a nested `stats` object (`stats = safeValue(ticker,'stats',ticker); high = safeString2(stats,'high','max_price')`). The current engine (CCXT.Safe.value_any via CCXT.ResponseParser) reads flat keys only. Add a declarative nested/dotted key path to the field_map vocab (e.g. key "stats.high" with fallback "max_price") so this is authorable as spec data, not per-method code.

2. Computed scalars. CCXT computes e.g. trade cost = amount * price (Precise.stringMul; inverse markets use stringDiv). The engine has no compute rule. Add a declarative computed-scalar rule (mul/div/etc. over sibling keys, market-aware where CCXT branches on inverse) to the field_map vocab.

3. Tier-1/2/3 return-type coverage. The read path only wires 9 core struct types (@parser_slots in lib/ccxt/unified/read_parse.ex, @struct_for in lib/ccxt/unified/field_maps.ex): ticker, trade, ohlcv, order, balance, position, market, transaction, deposit_address. Methods returning the other ~25 unified types (currency, open_interest, funding_rate, greeks, leverage, ...) have no parser slot -> the read path falls through to RAW PASSTHROUGH (the gate sees `%{"body"=>...,"status"=>200}` instead of a parsed struct -> guaranteed red). Wire the Tier-1/2/3 return types into the parser path so methods returning them parse to their unified struct. Note the field_map DATA often already exists in the spec (deribit already carries an `open_interest` field_map) — this is missing wiring + generated parse_* coverage, not net-new authoring, but verify per-type. Do it right: do not leave types raw-passthrough that a first-class venue's public-read method returns.

4. Columnar OHLCV. deribit (and others) return OHLCV as a columnar object (parallel ticks/open/high/low/close/volume arrays) -> the gate reports "Unexpected response shape for unified parse". Handle columnar OHLCV via a transformer (the order_book transformer pattern, :order_book_from_flat_list, is precedent) so it produces the [ts,o,h,l,c,v] rows CCXT emits.

Keep the declarative-field_map philosophy (authored not inferred): primitives 1 and 2 are CCXT-universal and belong IN the engine as spec-authorable vocab; reserve per-method transformers (3-array shapes) only for genuinely array-shaped outputs (order_book, columnar OHLCV). Raise this module's test coverage to tier before mutating (read-parse is correctness-critical; 95% if treated as money/parser-critical, else 80%). Add focused unit tests for each new primitive independent of any venue.
task.implemented: Wired currency + columnar OHLCV into the governed read path. New currency parse-type (list payload -> per-entry field-map struct -> re-keyed by safeCurrencyCode); Currency reshaped to canonical 14-key safeCurrencyStructure. Nested/dotted key reads + computed scalars added to field_map vocab; Tier-1/2/3 return types (incl currency, open_interest) wired into @parser_slots/@struct_for + generated parse_*; columnar OHLCV via authored transform. deribit fetchTicker/Trades/OHLCV/Currencies/OpenInterest green in T-A static-response gate; mechanisms cross-verified on derive (currency) + binance (OHLCV) - no deribit overfit. Live-verified via tidewave. ReadParse coverage tier, full offline suite + dialyzer green.

Observed 2026-06-22: running the gate with a loose `mix test.json --only exchange_<id> --include fixture_replay` co-runs the live network/raw probes (also tagged :exchange_<id>), which 500 and TRIP the shared circuit breaker; the gate tests then fail with `circuit_open: Circuit breaker is open` instead of a real parse diff — a false red that masks the true result. task.title: Tier-1 (reality-anchored) semantic oracle for CCXT-divergence-prone fields
acceptance_criteria: Each targeted field (initial set: fetchMarkets precision, inverse-perp cost/value branch, funding cadence/interval) has a frozen EXPECTED value sourced from a real captured response + a non-CCXT semantic source (exchange docs/SDK)
The expected side is provably NOT derived from CCXT (field_maps, CCXT JS, or CCXT static fixtures) — independence invariant documented per field
Capture reuses/extends Task 156's `mix ccxt.record_fixtures`; no second capture mechanism is built
An offline gate consumes the frozen expected values (extending 168's differential gate where shape allows) and goes green; mix test.json --quiet offline

A divergence report lists every targeted field where reality-anchored-expected != CCXT's parsedResponse, each with a human/Opus adjudication note (replicate / diverge / our-reading-wrong) — no auto-resolution toward CCXT
docs/authored-specs.md cross-references this task from the CCXT-tier-ceiling section

FIRST verification move is a live tidewave `mcp__tidewave__project_eval` call against the running app/testnet (e.g. a real `CCXT.fetch_*` against sandbox) — never a fixture/`Req.Test` replay as the opening move; the completion note records the actual tidewave call made
out_of_scope: Tier-1 coverage of the whole field surface (straight key-copy fields stay at tier-2 compatibility — 168/177)
The structural live drift-gate (157) — that asserts shape/non-nil, not exact reality-anchored values
Authoring the runtime spec slices themselves (T-C/T-D / 170/171) — this only produces a stronger verification oracle for select fields
Replacing 168/177 — tier-2 compatibility remains the floor for the bulk; this adds tier-1 only for divergence-prone fields
task.body:
See docs/authored-specs.md § "Compatibility ≠ correctness — the CCXT-tier ceiling" (the doctrine anchor for this task).

PROBLEM. Every SEMANTIC gate we have today sits at tier 2 (compatibility): the T-A differential gate (168) and the AI-graded oracle (177) both verify our parser output against CCXT's interpretation (a frozen `parsedResponse` is CCXT's parser output, not reality). A tier-2 green proves "we match CCXT," never "the value landed in the field whose real-world meaning matches." A CCXT parse bug (wrong unit, swapped key, an off inverse-vs-linear branch) is INVISIBLE to a CCXT-anchored oracle — the fixture freezes CCXT's error, we author to match, the gate goes green on a shared bug (the delta_calc trap surviving execution, because CCXT is the shared wrong source on both sides). The only thing that can falsify a CCXT-level error is reality + an INDEPENDENT, non-CCXT semantic source.

This is a real risk, not hypothetical: the fields below have already cost repeated re-dispatches precisely because their meaning is computed/branched rather than copied — fetchMarkets precision, the inverse-perp `cost` branch (amount*price vs amount/price), funding cadence/interval.

SCOPE. Do NOT build a tier-1 oracle for the whole surface — the bulk of straight key-copy fields are fine at tier-2 compatibility and CCXT-as-reference stands. Target ONLY the load-bearing, divergence-prone fields where CCXT-vs-reality mismatch is plausible AND consequential. Start from the re-dispatch evidence; the initial set is the precision fields on fetchMarkets, the inverse-market cost/value branch, and funding rate cadence/interval. Each gets its EXPECTED value anchored on:
  (a) a captured REAL response (reuse Task 156's `mix ccxt.record_fixtures`, extended if needed — do not build a second capture path), AND
  (b) an INDEPENDENT semantic source — the exchange's own API docs or official SDK — read to establish what the field actually means in reality, NOT CCXT JS.

INDEPENDENCE INVARIANT (load-bearing — this is the whole point). The expected side must NOT be derived from CCXT (neither our field_maps, nor CCXT JS, nor a CCXT static fixture). If the semantic source is CCXT, you are back at tier 2 and have built nothing. The source must be reality (the real response value) + a non-CCXT reading of meaning (exchange docs / SDK). CCXT is demoted to a CROSS-CHECK: where our reality-anchored expected AGREES with CCXT, note it; where it DIVERGES, that divergence is the high-value signal — it means either CCXT has a bug we should not replicate, or our reading is wrong — and it is adjudicated (human/Opus) before freezing, never auto-resolved toward CCXT.

OUTPUT. For each targeted field: a frozen expected value sourced per the invariant above, consumed by an offline gate (extend 168's differential gate where the shape allows, or a sibling assertion), plus a divergence report enumerating every targeted field where reality-anchored-expected != CCXT's parsedResponse, each with an adjudication note (replicate CCXT / diverge-from-CCXT-deliberately / our-reading-was-wrong). The deliverable is a SMALL, high-value set of reality-grounded fields, not exhaustive coverage.
task.implemented: Tier-1 reality-anchored semantic oracle: test/ccxt/tier1_semantic_oracle_test.exs (6/6, offline default suite — tier-1 GREEN asserts + adjudicated divergence pins) + docs/tier1-divergence-report.md adjudication artifact + 4 mainnet reality captures (deribit/bybit/hyperliquid fetch_markets, deribit fetch_funding_rate). Confirmed live defect: deribit inverse-perp cost fires linear mul branch (market.inverse nil). Live-first ACs satisfied via tidewave testnet probes before any replay.

task.title: Make the unified schema reality-answerable: confront CCXT-inherited carves against exchange semantics; register divergences
acceptance_criteria: A divergence-register section exists in docs/authored-specs.md; each entry records CCXT's carve, the exchange semantics from a non-CCXT source, our carve and rationale, and the compatibility cost
The authoring loop gains an explicit 'confront the carve, not just the value' step with CCXT as one reference rather than the arbiter

The bite carves (fetchMarkets precision, inverse-perp `cost`, funding cadence) are confronted for Deribit and at least one other first-class venue; confirmed and deliberate-divergence outcomes are recorded
No silent schema change: every divergence from CCXT struct shape or field semantics is registered and justified; AGENTS.md is regenerated
FIRST verification move is a live Tidewave call against the real testnet; the completion note records it
out_of_scope: Wholesale redesign of the full unified type system (36 types x 7 venues) — this confronts the divergence-prone carves + establishes the confrontation process + register, not a from-scratch rebuild
The VALUE-level reality oracle (task 180 — is the number right); this is CARVE-level (is the field/abstraction right)
Behavioral/semantic live tests (order-executed-as-priced, balance-matches-exchange-truth) — the one truly live-only test class, named here, scoped to its own task

Diverging from CCXT gratuitously / for purity — every divergence must weigh the consumer-compatibility cost (consumers expect CCXT semantics); divergence is for correctness about the exchange, not aesthetics
task.body:
See docs/authored-specs.md § "Compatibility ≠ correctness — the CCXT-tier ceiling". This task targets the DEEPEST uninspected CCXT dependency — one that demoting CCXT-fixtures and reality-sourcing inputs does NOT touch.

THE COLORING (what this fixes). Every verification we have — even reality-sourced frozen recordings, even live drift-checks — grades our parser against a TARGET schema: the unified struct shapes, field names (`last`, `bid`, `quoteVolume`, `cost`), and semantic carves (`cost = amount * price`; inverse markets divide; funding cadence) that we ported WHOLESALE from CCXT. So the raw input is reality, but the EXPECTED OUTPUT SHAPE is still CCXT's model of reality. The CCXT DNA lives in the schema, not in the fixtures — which is exactly why "delete all fixtures, test only live" does NOT decolor anything: a live assertion (`assert %Ticker{last: l} when is_number(l)`) inherits the same CCXT vocabulary, just asserts less of it. The fixture-vs-live axis is ORTHOGONAL to the CCXT-coloring axis. The coloring is on a third axis: is the unified MODEL itself correct about the exchange, or merely faithful to CCXT's carve of it?

THE GOAL. Demote CCXT from ORIGIN ("the model we ported, then correct") to ONE DISPOSABLE REFERENCE among several (exchange API docs, official SDK, observed behavior, training, web). The DEX venues already prove this orientation works — hyperliquid/derive author from the exchange's own docs + EIP-712 spec, CCXT-JS thin-to-absent; CCXT was never their center. The CEX venues feel CCXT-centered only by path-dependence ("CCXT-derived client"), not necessity. Generalize the DEX orientation to CEX where the exchange's own semantics are clear.

THE WORK — two durable mechanisms + a bounded proof, NOT a wholesale redesign:

1. CONFRONTATION STEP in the authoring loop (docs/authored-specs.md). When authoring a venue slice, each SCHEMA decision — does this field exist? what does it actually mean on THIS exchange? is CCXT's carve (single `cost`, inverse-divide, the funding period) the right abstraction or does it misrepresent the venue? — is checked against the exchange's OWN semantics, with CCXT as one reference, not the arbiter. This is distinct from authoring the field-MAP (which key -> which field); it questions whether the field/carve is right at all.

2. DIVERGENCE REGISTER section in docs/authored-specs.md. Every place the unified model deliberately diverges from CCXT's ontology gets an entry: CCXT's carve | the exchange's actual semantics (cited from exchange docs/SDK, NOT CCXT) | our carve + rationale | the consumer-compatibility cost weighed. Where CCXT is RIGHT, record it as a CONFIRMED carve (verified against reality), not an assumed one — so the register doubles as the audit trail that the schema was confronted, not inherited.

3. PROOF (bounded). Apply to the divergence-prone "bite" carves that have already cost rework — fetchMarkets precision, the inverse-perp `cost` carve, funding cadence — for deribit + >=1 other venue. Where CCXT's carve is wrong, diverge + register; where right, confirm + register.

RELATION TO SIBLINGS. Task 180 is the VALUE oracle (is the number in the field right against reality). THIS is the CARVE oracle (is the field/abstraction itself right). 180 assumes the schema is settled and checks values; this makes the schema answerable. They compose: confront the carve here, then 180 anchors its value. Feeds 170/171 per-venue authoring (gives them a confronted schema, not an inherited one).

A NOTE ON THE ONE TRULY LIVE-ONLY CLASS (scoped elsewhere, flagged here): behavioral/semantic reality — did the order execute at the price I meant? does balance match the exchange's own truth? — is the truest reality check and NO fixture (reality-sourced or not) captures it. Out of scope here; named so it is not lost.
task.implemented: Carve confrontation shipped: docs/authored-specs.md gains § 'The confrontation step — confront the carve, not just the value' (authoring-loop step, T-C/T-D wired) + § 'Carve register — schema-level confrontations' with 6 adjudicated entries (C1 precision discriminator surfaced per-market as precision_mode / C2 deribit amount step: min!=step live-proven on options, qty_tick_size docs-vs-live gap / C3 tick_size_steps shared-lossy kept / C4 inverse cost CONFIRM CCXT / C5 funding interval: CONFIRM bybit per-symbol 8h + HL 1h, DIVERGE deribit nil — continuous accrual, funding_rate = 8h-window integrated rate / C6 HL price rule: DIVERGE, no snapshot scalar). FIRST verification move was live tidewave against deribit/bybit/hyperliquid testnets 2026-07-15: fetch_markets future+option+linear+spot, fetch_funding_rate, get_funding_rate_value over 8h vs 1h windows (2.85e-6 vs 1.97e-9 — scalar proven window-integrated); non-CCXT sources fetched same day (docs.deribit.com get_instruments + private/buy, bybit v5, HL gitbook). Implementation encoded as ACs on 170/171/209; CLAUDE.md rule added; AGENTS.md regenerated. No code change — schema changes land with the venue authoring tasks, registered here first.

task.title: Rename project away from ccxt_client / CCXT.* namespace
acceptance_criteria: The Bourse name and rationale are recorded
OTP app name, top-level module namespace, mix.exs, configuration keys and public API references are renamed consistently
quantex and trading_dashboard path-dependency consumers are migrated in coordinated branches or pinned to the last CCXT-namespaced release with an explicit migration path
Genuine upstream-CCXT references remain unchanged and describe CCXT only as reference/compatibility material, never as the authority for venue semantics

Orientational CCXT references in lib/ and test/ comments, moduledocs and docs (CCXT-as-oracle phrasing: 'matches CCXT behavior', 'per CCXT's logic', 'CCXT does X so we do X') are rewritten to cite the provider-owned authority or deleted
Demarcating CCXT references survive verbatim: carve-register entries documenting deliberate divergence, the authority-ladder doctrine, and reference-corpus/compatibility-material markers
A guard test flags CCXT-as-authority phrasing in lib/ comments and moduledocs outside an explicit allowlist, so the orientational anchor cannot regrow
Compile, full suite and consumer compile/integration checks are green after the rename
CLAUDE.md and existing authored-spec documentation describe the final owned-schema, provider-authority model without current-tense sync or first-class heuristic doctrine
Retained module docs and inline comments describe present behavior; repository links and commands resolve
AGENTS.md is regenerated and its freshness check passes
out_of_scope: Renaming before T-E1/T-E2 land
Removing vendored CCXT specs or the ccxt-distill bootstrap path
Unrelated consumer refactors
task.body:
Decision-then-execute: rename the project and namespace to drop the CCXT origin label, which the authored-specs pivot has made misleading (see CLAUDE.md § North star + docs/authored-specs.md: CCXT was the bootstrap, not the destination; the client is "ours, by our rules", correct against the real exchange APIs, deliberately diverging from CCXT's ontology). The name ccxt_client / CCXT.* now overstates the dependency it describes.

GATED on T-E2 (173): do this only AFTER the legacy CCXT-coupled machinery is deleted (mix ccxt.sync removed in T-E1/172, heuristic-interpretation layers removed in T-E2/173). Renaming before then churns every open authored-spec branch/worktree with merge conflicts, and the CCXT dependency is still real in the code until those land — let the name follow the reality, not precede it.

NAME CHOSEN (2026-06-22): Bourse — module namespace `Bourse`, OTP app `:bourse`. Means "exchange" literally, multi-venue, crypto-neutral, no CCXT lineage; `bourse` confirmed available on hex.pm (2026-06-22) in case of a future publish. Execute the rename with this pair: `mix rename CCXT Bourse ccxt_client bourse`.

Then execute the mechanical rename: OTP app :ccxt_client, the CCXT.* module namespace, mix.exs, config keys (e.g. config :ccxt_client, :ccxt_distill_dir and Application.compile_env callsites), env-var prefixes where they encode the app name, and docs (CLAUDE.md, docs/, README). Keep the mix ccxt.* task names and the ccxt-distill / vendored-CCXT references that genuinely point at upstream CCXT — those are correct CCXT references, not the project's self-label.

quantex and trading_dashboard are real path-dependency consumers. Treat this as a coordinated breaking rename: migrate them alongside Bourse or pin them to the last CCXT-namespaced release with an explicit migration path. Do not report the rename complete from this repository's green suite alone.

MECHANICS: use the `rename` hex package (https://hex.pm/packages/rename) as the starting point — `mix rename CCXT NewName ccxt_client new_app_otp` (or Rename.run({"CCXT","NewName"}, {"ccxt_client","new_app_otp"}, ignore_files: [...])). CAVEAT — it does a projectwide find/replace of the two name pairs, so a blanket CCXT -> NewName ALSO rewrites the genuine upstream-CCXT references that must stay (mix ccxt.* task names, ccxt-distill, vendored-CCXT spec paths, and CCXT compatibility-reference prose). `ignore_files` only filters at file granularity, but several of those strings live in the same files (CLAUDE.md, mix.exs) as names that SHOULD change. So: run `mix rename` as the bulk pass, then manually diff-review and revert every legitimate CCXT reference token-by-token before committing. The rename tool is the bulk mechanism, not the final arbiter.

SCOPE EXPANDED (2026-07-26): the rename carries the CCXT-orientation comment/doc sweep — the two share the same repo-wide write-set and one solo wave, so they are one dispatch unit (one-session=one-task). Rationale: comments and moduledocs that phrase CCXT as the oracle steer every future LLM session back toward CCXT-as-truth; the namespace `CCXT.*` is the largest such anchor and the rename alone leaves the smaller ones in place. Classification rule for the sweep — ORIENTATIONAL (rewrite to cite the provider-owned authority, or delete): "matches CCXT behavior", "per CCXT's parse logic", "CCXT does X so we do X", any comment justifying a decision by CCXT rather than by the venue contract. DEMARCATING (keep verbatim): carve-register entries recording deliberate divergence FROM CCXT, the authority-ladder doctrine, tier-2/reference-corpus/compatibility markers — these explicitly name CCXT as NON-authority and deleting them would erase the doctrine itself. Encode the outcome as a guard test (allowlist-based scan of lib/ comments and moduledocs for CCXT-as-authority phrasing) so the anchor cannot regrow through future dispatched sessions — a defect class caught by hand twice is a missing test. Now additionally gated on task 523 (W3): sweeping before the tier-2 deletion would clean surfaces 523 deletes or rewrites anyway and collide with its write-set; after 523 the surviving CCXT reference set is exactly the one to triage.

task.title: Recalibrate integration-helper: request-malformation 4xx must FAIL, not pass inconclusive
acceptance_criteria: The inconclusive-vs-flunk decision keys on normalized error class, not the raw 400..499 status range
A 4xx that normalizes to a request-malformation class (bad_request / invalid argument / wrong-endpoint family) FLUNKS with the method + raw body
A 4xx that normalizes to a well-formed-but-declined class (bad_symbol on a probe symbol, insufficient_funds, order_not_found) stays inconclusive
The genuinely-infra @inconclusive_public set (rate_limit_exceeded, network_error, exchange_not_available, cloudflare_challenge) is unchanged
A regression test proves a synthesized request-malformation 4xx flunks and a synthesized bad-symbol 4xx logs inconclusive
mix precommit green; the public sweep (--include network) re-run shows the previously-masked binanceusdm/okx fetch_ohlcv 4xx now as failures, not inconclusive
out_of_scope: Fixing the underlying request-build bugs themselves (those are task 171 authoring work)
Changing the credential-gate flunk behavior (require_credentials!)
The fixture-replay tier-2 concern (separate doctrine, tasks 168/180)
task.body:
The integration helper's `allow_4xx: true` path (test/support/integration_helper.ex, used by the Task-83 raw-endpoint probes and the T39 unified probes) treats ANY normalized 4xx as inconclusive — "the pipeline worked end-to-end; the exchange rejected the request semantically." That conflates two cases that are NOT the same: (a) the exchange legitimately rejecting a well-formed request (a probe symbol it doesn't list, an out-of-range param) — genuinely inconclusive; vs (b) OUR request was malformed (wrong endpoint, missing/duplicated required param, wrong market-type section) — a real code/authoring bug the probe should catch. Today (b) is logged inconclusive and the suite reports green, hiding it.

This is the test-integrity gap behind "NEVER HIDE TEST FAILURES": a 4xx caused by our own request-build defect must FLUNK. Concrete repro this would have caught instead of masking: binanceusdm fetch_ohlcv selecting `/fapi/v1/indexPriceKlines` (wrong endpoint) → 400; okx fetchOHLCV building `instId=1m` (timeframe in the symbol slot) → 400. Both are our bugs; under blanket allow_4xx they pass inconclusive.

Recalibrate so the inconclusive-vs-flunk decision keys on the NORMALIZED ERROR CLASS, not the raw HTTP status: errors that mean "our request was malformed" (e.g. :bad_request, :invalid_params/:bad_request-family, and any class CCXT raises for argument/endpoint problems) FLUNK; errors that mean "well-formed request, exchange declined" (:bad_symbol on a probe-chosen symbol, :insufficient_funds, :order_not_found, plus the existing @inconclusive infra classes) stay inconclusive. The unified parser already distinguishes many of these via CCXT's exception map — lean on that classification rather than the 400..499 range check. Keep the genuinely-infra @inconclusive_public set (rate-limit/network/exchange-unavailable/cloudflare) as-is. The deliverable raises the signal quality of the full-catalog evidence doc (task 155) and the request-build authoring (task 171) by turning masked request-malformation 4xx into real failures.

task.title: Harden unified dispatch opts: extract :params, coerce map-opts — public functions must never raise
acceptance_criteria: `CCXT.fetch_volatility_history(ex, params: %{...})` no longer raises `encode_query values cannot be lists` — the `:params` map is merged into the venue query, not query-encoded as a literal `params=` pair

A unified read called with a map for `opts` (e.g. `CCXT.fetch_funding_rates(ex, %{...})`) no longer raises `FunctionClauseError` from `Keyword.split/2` — opts are coerced to a keyword list, or rejected with a clean `{:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :bad_request}}`
`split_opts/1` recognizes `:params` and routes its map into the exchange-native param map; the dispatch-opts allowlist is unchanged in meaning for the existing keys
Regression unit tests cover: `:params` keyword merge, map-opts coercion, and a public function returning an error tuple (never raising) on a bad opts shape
mix precommit green; touched module at its coverage tier
out_of_scope: Per-venue request-shape authoring (bybit category, hyperliquid body) — separate tasks
Changing the documented `:params` channel semantics beyond making it work
task.body:
Two live crashes reported by quantex (BUGS.md 2026-06-23), same fix site — `CCXT.Unified.split_opts/1` (lib/ccxt/unified.ex:727; `@dispatch_opts` at :24). A public dispatch function must NEVER raise — it breaks the `{:ok,_}|{:error,_}` contract both consumers rely on.

1. The documented `:params` keyword (CCXT JS's `params` object channel) is not split out of `opts`, so it lands in `extra` and is handed verbatim to query encoding -> `encode_query/2 values cannot be lists`. Pull `:params` out and merge its map into the venue query.

2. Passing `opts` as a map (the natural shape, since CCXT JS takes an object) hits `Keyword.split/2`'s `is_list` guard -> `FunctionClauseError` at the consumer (all venues). Coerce a map to a keyword list before splitting, or raise a clean `ArgumentError`/return `{:error, :bad_request}` — never `FunctionClauseError`.

Both have live repros in BUGS.md. Cheapest, highest-leverage fix in the consumer-blocker set: all-venue, both consumers.

task.title: Fix response classifier misreading HTTP/JSON-RPC success as :exchange_error (lighter code:200, deribit result-without-error)
acceptance_criteria: `CCXT.fetch_markets(ex)` on lighter returns `{:ok, _}` carrying the `order_book_details[]` payload (lighter signals success with `code: 200`) instead of `{:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :exchange_error}}`
`CCXT.fetch_markets(ex)` on deribit returns `{:ok, _}` carrying the JSON-RPC `result` (4636 markets) — a JSON-RPC envelope with `result` and no `error` member is success, not an error
A genuine exchange error (a real non-success code / a JSON-RPC `error` object) is still classified `:exchange_error` — no regression on binance/bybit error paths
Regression tests cover lighter `code:200`, deribit `result`-without-`error`, and at least one true-error case staying classified as error
out_of_scope: Authoring the lighter/deribit fetchMarkets carve (normalizing the now-unblocked payload into %CCXT.Market{}) — that is the parser/authoring tail (153 / 171), this task only fixes the success-vs-error classification
The hyperliquid 400 (a genuine request-shape bug, separate task)
task.body:
Reported by trading_dashboard (BUGS.md 2026-06-23). The error classifier flags HTTP/JSON-RPC SUCCESS envelopes as `:exchange_error`, dropping all data even though it is present in `.raw`. Fix site: `CCXT.HTTP.detect_error_from_code_fields` / `classify_by_success` (lib/ccxt/http.ex:340-403).

- lighter `fetch_markets` returns `%{"code" => 200, "order_book_details" => [...]}` — 200 is lighter's SUCCESS code, but the classifier treats the presence of `code` (or a non-0 code) as an error. Result: the whole call errors, nothing normalized. lighter has no fetchTradingFee/fetchLeverageTiers fallback, so fetch_markets is its ONLY fees/MMR/leverage source — this blocks lighter onboarding entirely.
- deribit `fetch_markets` returns a valid JSON-RPC success: `%{"jsonrpc" => "2.0", "result" => [...4636 markets...]}` with NO `error` member. JSON-RPC signals failure via an `error` object; `result`-present / `error`-absent must classify as success. `fetch_ticker` on deribit already works, so this is endpoint-specific envelope handling.

Fix only the classification (data is already in `.raw`). The carve/normalization of these markets is a separate authoring task. Treat venue success codes and JSON-RPC `result`-without-`error` as success.

task.body:
Reported by quantex (BUGS.md 2026-06-23). A PUBLIC funding rate fails demanding credentials:

  CCXT.fetch_funding_rate(ex, "BTC/USDT:USDT")  # bybit
  # => {:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :authentication_error, message: "Credentials required for fetch_markets"}}

The symbol-bearing path resolves the symbol to a market, which triggers a market load that is incorrectly gated behind credentials. In CCXT JS `fetchMarkets`/`loadMarkets` are public. Public symbol resolution must use the public market load; only genuinely private methods should require creds. Find where symbol resolution forces the credentialed `fetch_markets` and route it through the public path.

task.body: Reviewer follow-up from task 193: the production Deribit `fetch_funding_rate` request now works live and injects the CCXT JS 8h window, but the static request fixture replay is not a useful oracle for this dynamic request shape yet. CCXT's static Deribit `fetchFundingRate` fixtures freeze `this.milliseconds()` into `start_timestamp`/`end_timestamp`, while the replay path runs wall-clock time; the current URL comparison also reports query-string order differences as path mismatches before it reaches semantic query comparison. task.body:
Live finding 2026-06-23 (tidewave, recompiled, real APIs, post-190/191/193): four shortlist venues do not return symbol-populated [%CCXT.Market{}] from fetch_markets, in two distinct ways — but ONE capability gap: "the public markets read path yields symbol-populated Markets". The carve infrastructure exists (the read_parse fan-out + parse_market field-map + backfill_market_symbols path); these venues either never reach parse_market (enveloped) or reach it but lack a symbol field-map.

(A) ENVELOPE UNWRAP — markets list never reaches parse_market:
- bybit:   {:ok, %{"result" => %{"category" => "spot", "list" => [%{"baseCoin" => "BTC", "lotSizeFilter" => %{...}}, ...]}}}  -> unwrap result.list
- deribit: {:ok, %{"jsonrpc" => "2.0", "result" => [%{"base_currency" => "ADA", "contract_size" => ...}, ...]}}            -> unwrap result
- lighter: {:ok, %{"code" => 200, "order_book_details" => [%{"min_base_amount" => "10.0", ...}, ...]}}                     -> unwrap order_book_details

(B) SYMBOL BACKFILL — list reaches parse_market, 230 %Market{} structs build, but every :symbol is nil:
- hyperliquid: CCXT.fetch_markets returns 230 structs, first_is_struct true, but sample_symbol nil / any_symbol_nil true. market_symbol_from_raw handles "symbol"/"instId"/"baseAsset"+"quoteAsset" but NOT hyperliquid's coin field (`name`). Author the hyperliquid symbol field-map per CCXT JS hyperliquid fetchMarkets so symbol is backfilled.

This is THE keystone consumer blocker: trading_dashboard cannot onboard deribit/lighter/hyperliquid without a symbol-populated markets index, and lighter/hyperliquid have NO fetchLeverageTiers/fetchTradingFee fallback — fetch_markets is their only fees/leverage source. hyperliquid's nil-symbol index also breaks its fetchTicker live ("could not find a ticker for BTC/USDC:USDC" — downstream of this). It unblocks task 192 (bybit emulated fetch_funding_rate needs the linear contract in the symbol index) and the binance-markets oracle tasks 22/23/24.

LINEAGE — this EXTENDS done work, it does not re-wire it: task 152 (done) wired parse_market into the fetch_markets read path + symbol backfill, but was verified on BINANCE only; task 166 (done) added binance multi-ENDPOINT fan-out (spot/linear/inverse via Promise.all over multiple configured endpoints). The read-path mechanism therefore already exists — DO NOT rebuild it. This task closes the venue coverage 152/166 never reached: (1) the three enveloped venues whose markets list 152's parse_market never receives, (2) hyperliquid's missing symbol field-map (152's backfill_market_symbols runs but has no rule for hyperliquid's `name`), and (3) bybit's category merge, which is a request-PARAM fan-out (one endpoint, category=spot|linear|inverse) distinct from 166's multi-ENDPOINT fan-out — 166's select_endpoint generalization does not cover it.

Extracted from task 171 deliberately: 171 is the broad 'author + freeze + tier-1-verify all 7 venues (incl. private)' roll and depends_on 184 (human cred provisioning). The PUBLIC markets carve needs no creds and must not wait behind cred provisioning or the full authoring spine. Author each venue's envelope unwrap / symbol field-map by reading CCXT JS fetchMarkets (priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/<venue>.ts); the existing parse_market field-map + backfill_market_symbols path in read_parse.ex already handles the rest once the list reaches it with a mappable symbol. Where the envelope is spec-configured (normalization.response_envelopes), author the markets slot there per the pattern task 189 used.

task.body:
Live finding 2026-06-24 (tidewave, recompiled, post-195): CCXT.fetch_ticker(hyperliquid, "BTC/USDC:USDC") fails with :exchange_error "fetchTickers() could not find a ticker for BTC/USDC:USDC" — EVEN THOUGH that exact symbol is now present in the carved hyperliquid markets index (task 195: fetch_markets returns 230 %Market{}, sample_symbol "BTC/USDC:USDC", zero nil symbols). So hyperliquid fetch_ticker is emulated via fetchTickers and its symbol match/lookup does not consult (or does not match against) the carved index — it was masked before 195 by the markets index having nil symbols, and 195 surfaced it as the next layer.

This is the ticker-side analog of the 195 carve: the read path produces the data but the emulated single-ticker resolver can't find the symbol. Fix the emulated fetch_ticker symbol resolution to match against the carved markets index for hyperliquid. Generalize the capability — "emulated fetch_ticker resolves its symbol against the carved markets index" — rather than overfitting to one symbol string; lighter's fetchTicker is also currently ❌ (COVERAGE low-confidence "❌ ?") and may share this root cause (verify live, include only if same class).

Consumer impact: hyperliquid is a keystone DEX for trading_dashboard with NO fetchTradingFee/fetchLeverageTiers fallback, and live pricing via fetch_ticker is a v1 requirement. depends on task 195 (done) for the carved index this resolver reads.

task.body:
Verified during task 218 (CCXT static request fixtures + CCXT JS hyperliquid.ts): hyperliquid fetchTrades is NOT a public market-trade tape — CCXT implements it as a per-user fills read (type "userFills", or "userFillsByTime" when since is supplied) that resolves user via handlePublicAddress (falls back to the configured wallet/api_key). The base spec's user entry on fetchTrades is therefore real, not distill noise. Task 218 deliberately excluded it (AC4) because it needs distinct treatment beyond the pure account-read user injection: (a) user.source = api_key binding, (b) a conditional type of userFills vs userFillsByTime keyed on since, and (c) a semantic decision — surfacing the caller's OWN fills through the unified fetch_trades public-trades method is a divergence from the public-read contract other venues honor, so decide whether hyperliquid.fetchTrades should map to userFills at all in our client or should raise/redirect to fetch_my_trades. Author from CCXT JS (reading) and verify the request body against the CCXT static request fixture priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/request/hyperliquid.json (fetchTrades cases show type userFills + user). Reuse the generic source api_key mechanism from task 216 — no new venue hardcode in RequestShape.

DECISION 2026-07-15 (operator): registered divergence. CCXT JS offers no rationale — its fetchTrades docstring keeps the generic "most recent trades for a symbol" description while the implementation is a per-wallet fills read defaulting to the caller's own wallet (handlePublicAddress), duplicating its own fetchMyTrades (hyperliquid.ts:3468). Transport-public (unauthenticated, address-parameterized /info) != semantically public (market tape). Our carve: fetch_trades -> :not_supported pointing to fetch_my_trades; author userFills/userFillsByTime under fetch_my_trades instead. Scope now includes the fetch_my_trades authoring and the divergence registration.

task.body:
CCXT's vendored per-method structural validators (priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/Exchange/test.*.ts, vendored CCXT 4.5.54 per priv/specs/json/ccxt/package.json) carry a curated invariant catalog our existing test/support/struct_validators.ex only partially covers. Audit ours against theirs and extend — this is an AUDIT/EXTENSION of the existing module (already wired into the live integration flow via integration_helper.ex), NOT a wholesale port and NOT a new module.

Classify every CCXT check into three buckets before porting:
1. SOURCE-AGNOSTIC PHYSICS — port these (e.g. bid <= ask, non-crossed sorted books, high >= low, volume >= 0, trades timestamp ordering per test.fetchTrades.ts). Against fixture replays they are a regression net; against live testnet responses they are reality-anchored evidence.
2. CCXT ONTOLOGY — reject with a one-line rationale each (assertStructure canonical key-set/type expectations in test.sharedMethods.ts; the spot/contract/linear/inverse taxonomy checks in test.market.ts; the currency active/deposit/withdraw quota assumptions in test.fetchCurrencies.ts). These encode CCXT's carve, which our carve register (docs/authored-specs.md C1-C7) deliberately diverges from.
3. EMBEDDED POLICY — adopt, loosen, or reject case-by-case with rationale (timestamp window 2009-2038 and <=1min-ahead in test.sharedMethods.ts; the last-within-1%-of-midpoint check in test.ticker.ts, which false-reds thin/volatile testnet markets).

REPO-OWNED invariants beyond CCXT's catalog are explicitly allowed (operator decision 2026-07-15) — e.g. monotone OHLCV timestamp ordering, which CCXT itself leaves as a TODO in test.fetchOHLCV.ts. Label them repo-owned, don't claim they're ported.

Record provenance: the vendored CCXT version and per-file identity of every test.*.ts consulted, so upstream validator drift is detectable by diff, never auto-synced.

task.title: Machine-readable divergence contracts: fixture gates consume the carve register as expected-diff assertions, not skip-keys
acceptance_criteria: A documented machine-readable divergence-contract format exists and is consumed by the T-A response gate generator; format documented in docs/authored-specs.md next to the carve register

C6 is expressed as a contract: the gate asserts CCXT's expected side HAS the hyperliquid precision.price scalar while ours is nil — flipping either side (ours regaining the scalar, or the fixture losing it) turns the gate red with C6 named in the failure

Every divergence-motivated skip-key in the gates is either converted to a contract or explicitly documented as mechanical (struct_skip_keys OrderBook info may stay, with rationale) — the Position contract_size skip (C7, landed 33a62e4) is divergence-motivated and MUST convert

Fixture recapture mechanics (task 156) and the live drift-gate (task 157)
task.body:
The T-A/177 differential gates currently express known CCXT-vs-ours divergences as skip-keys (fixture skipKeys plus the hardcoded struct_skip_keys/1 in recorded_response_replay.ex). A skip silently stops testing the field on BOTH sides: it can't catch our value drifting back toward CCXT, drifting to a third wrong value, or CCXT's fixture changing under us. Replace divergence-motivated skips with path-level EXPECTED-DIVERGENCE contracts.

Contract shape (the architect decision, pre-encoded): machine-readable entries carried in the authored spec of the owning venue (or a dedicated register file consumed at test-generation time), each with: carve id (the docs/authored-specs.md C-entry it implements), a selector (venue + entity type + optional market-type predicate), the field path, a predicate for the CCXT/fixture side, and a predicate for our side. The gate then: (a) compares every UNREGISTERED path strictly, as today; (b) for every registered path asserts BOTH predicates — e.g. for C6: CCXT's parsed market HAS a precision.price scalar AND ours is nil. Either side drifting fails loudly with the carve id in the message.

Prose carve register entries in docs/authored-specs.md stay the human-readable rationale; the machine entries reference them by id so register and gate cannot drift apart. Only genuinely-mechanical skips (e.g. OrderBook info blob equivalence) remain skips — document why each surviving skip is mechanical, not divergence-hiding.

Scope the initial contract set to the registered DIVERGEs that a markets/response gate can observe. C6 hyperliquid precision.price is the anchor case. C7 deribit position contract_size (registered 2026-07-15, landed 33a62e4) is the second gate-observable DIVERGE: CCXT's side backfills contract_size from the loaded market (fixture carries 10 for BTC-PERPETUAL) while ours is nil at parse — currently hidden by a struct_skip_keys entry that this task must convert to a contract. Sweep C1-C5 for any other gate-observable divergence. CONFIRM-outcome carves need no contract.

For single-symbol reads the REQUESTED symbol/market context is authoritative for per-row symbol population (mirroring CCXT threading `market` into parse*); the native-id heuristic (dash-less => :swap) never overrides it on venues whose spot and derivative ids collide (bybit BTCUSDT)

A venue-wide audit enumerates (a) every single-record unified method whose envelope yields a list and (b) every list read whose rows lack an unambiguous native symbol, and verifies each returns populated results instead of []; the audit result is recorded in the completion note
Offline regression tests pin the multi-row-envelope single-record case and the ambiguous-native-id spot list case (never [])

task.body:
Live finding 2026-07-16 (orchestrator whole-surface pass after task 230 landed, bybit testnet): CCXT.fetch_open_interest(ex, "BTC/USDT:USDT") returns {:ok, []} — the venue returns its default ~50 rows under result.list, the rows parse to symbol-nil OpenInterest structs, and apply_request_filters drops them all. Only the limit: 1 call shape survives, which is exactly the one shape task 230's live integration test pinned, so the defect passed the per-task review. CCXT JS parses data[0] for fetchOpenInterest regardless of row count.

Root cause: normalize_payload in lib/ccxt/unified/read_parse.ex unwraps one-element list envelopes only for the hardcoded js_names fetchFundingRate/fetchGreeks. Any other single-record method whose envelope is a list (fetchOpenInterest today; audit for others) silently returns [] whenever the venue returns more than one row. Fix the class, not the instance: derive the first-row unwrap from the method's single-record nature, and audit all single-record methods with list envelopes venue-wide.

Raw layer is unaffected (public_get_v5_market_open_interest returns the rows correctly); this is purely the unified read-parse seam.

Second instance, same seam (2026-07-16, orchestrator pass after task 231 landed): CCXT.fetch_trades(ex, "BTC/USDT") (spot) returns {:ok, []} while the linear "BTC/USDT:USDT" call returns 500 trades. Root cause: bybit spot and linear share the native id BTCUSDT; backfill_native_symbol's native_market_type heuristic (dash-less and underscore-less => :swap) stamps spot rows with the LINEAR symbol, then filter_requested_symbols drops every row. Task 231's live evidence exercised only the raw endpoint + parse_trade, so the unified spot path was never hit. The shared invariant to implement: for single-symbol reads, the request's market context wins over any native-id guess (CCXT threads `market` into parse*); the terminal request filter silently emptying a result is the symptom to kill in both instances.

task.body:
Task 243 established the invariant that for single-symbol reads the REQUESTED symbol/market context wins over any native-id guess, but implemented it only for `CCXT.Trade` (`backfill_trade_symbol/2` in lib/ccxt/unified/read_parse.ex now overrides unconditionally when params["symbol"] is a binary).

Every other clause of `backfill_request_symbols/4` still reads `struct.symbol || params["symbol"]` — the native backfill wins whenever it produced ANY symbol, including a wrong one. On venues whose spot and derivative ids collide (bybit BTCUSDT), the same dash-less => :swap heuristic that emptied fetch_trades can stamp a wrong symbol on Ticker / Order / OpenInterest / Position / ADLRank / FundingRate / FundingRateHistory reads, where the terminal apply_request_filters then silently drops the row — the exact symptom class task 243 set out to kill.

Not observed live on bybit for these types (bybit OI/positions are category-scoped, so the guess happens to agree), which is why 243 scoped it to the demonstrated instance. Decide per parse_type whether request-authority is correct (CCXT threads `market` into every parse*), and either generalize the override or record why a given type must keep native precedence.

task.body:
Reviewer finding while gating task 247 (harness run run-1784190492006-153e8ba0, 2026-07-16).

`CCXT.Symbol.to_exchange_id/2` denormalizes a USDC-settled bybit option to
`BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC`. That id does not exist in Bybit's namespace. Live evidence
(2026-07-16, mainnet + testnet agree): `GET /v5/market/instruments-info?category=option&baseCoin=BTC&limit=1000`
returns 686 ids, 686/686 ending in `-USDT` and ZERO ending in `-USDC`. Bybit's USDC-settled
option generation is named bare (`BTC-27DEC24-55000-P`), settlement implied — exactly what the
CCXT static request fixture for fetchOption expects.

Task 247 closed the fetchOption red by stripping the suffix AT THE fetchOption CALL SITE
(`RequestShape.Bybit.option_symbol/1`). That closed the gate but not the root cause: the phantom
id still leaks from `Symbol.to_exchange_id/2` into every other option request path. Verified on
the real dispatch pipeline at that commit:

    fetchGreeks       -> %{"category" => "option", "symbol" => "BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC"}
    fetchTicker       -> %{"category" => "option", "symbol" => "BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC"}
    fetchOrderBook    -> %{"category" => "option", "symbol" => "BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC"}
    fetchTrades       -> %{"symbol" => "BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC"}
    fetchOpenInterest -> %{"category" => "option", ..., "symbol" => "BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC"}
    fetchOptionChain  -> %{"baseCoin" => "BTC-27DEC24-55000-P-USDC", ...}   # also a wrong baseCoin

Fix the carve at the symbol layer (settle suffix appended only for USDT-settled bybit options)
rather than adding a per-call-site strip, then drop the now-redundant strip in
`RequestShape.Bybit.option_symbol/1` if the layer fix subsumes it.

Severity is bounded today: Bybit currently lists NO USDC options (all 686 live ids are USDT), so
the phantom id only affects historical/expired USDC contracts and any future USDC relisting. That
is why 247 was approved with the call-site strip rather than blocked.

Confront the carve against Bybit's OWN namespace (instruments-info is the oracle), not the CCXT
fixture — the fixture only covers fetchOption. Record the outcome in the docs/authored-specs.md
carve register (C11 already notes this gap and points here).

task.body:
Orchestrator live finding (2026-07-16, whole-surface pass after task 247 landed, bybit testnet).

CCXT.fetch_markets(bybit) returns 1310 markets: %{"spot" => 785, "swap" => 497, "future" => 28} — ZERO option markets. The venue's own namespace disagrees: GET /v5/market/instruments-info?category=option returns option instruments (live 2026-07-16: BTC-25JUN27-45000-P-USDT, ...), and our own vendored spec records CCXT-JS's fan-out as raw/describe/options/fetchMarkets = {types: [spot, linear, inverse, option], options: [BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, MNT, DOGE]} (the options list is CCXT's per-baseCoin pagination loop for the option category).

Consequence: the entire unified options surface has no symbol index on bybit — fetch_option / fetch_option_chain cannot resolve a unified option symbol against markets (observed live: fetch_markets |> find(type == "option") => nil), even though fetch_all_greeks (which bypasses the market index) sees 598 live BTC options. Task 166 (fetch_markets multi-endpoint fan-out, done) built the union mechanism and task 233 (bybit market identity/type flags, done) authored the category semantics — both landed, but the option category never entered bybit's fan-out set. Convergence gap, append-only: this task closes it without reopening 166/233.

Confront the carve per the venue loop: Bybit v5 instruments-info is the oracle for what categories exist and whether option requires baseCoin (a bare category=option&limit=5 call succeeded live without baseCoin — CCXT's per-baseCoin loop may be pagination pragmatics rather than a hard requirement; decide from reality and record it).

acceptance_criteria: Live (tidewave, real API): with BYBIT_DEMO_API_KEY/SECRET from the env, CCXT.fetch_balance(ex, base_url: "https://api-demo.bybit.com") on a plain (non-sandbox) bybit exchange returns {:ok, %CCXT.Balance{}} with non-empty totals — the documented opt reaches the wire on the signed path
Live (tidewave, real API): a public raw call with base_url: "https://does-not-exist.invalid" now FAILS with a transport error (today it silently succeeds against the default host)

Offline: plug-based dispatch tests pin that opts[:base_url] wins over exchange.base_urls on both an authenticated and an unauthenticated endpoint, and that default resolution is unchanged when the opt is absent
FIRST verification move is a live tidewave project_eval against the real API — never a Req.Test/fixture replay as the opening move; the completion note records the actual call
out_of_scope: Reworking sandbox/hostname URL templating (OKX hostname task covers that)
A first-class bybit demo-trading mode (sandbox-style flag) — this task only makes the existing opt honest
task.body:
`:base_url` is a documented dispatch opt (`@dispatch_opts` in lib/ccxt/unified.ex:24, split via `split_opts/1`, also plumbed through the raw endpoint wrappers) — but `Dispatch.call/4` silently discards it on BOTH request paths. dispatch.ex:73 always resolves the URL from `exchange.base_urls`; the public path then overwrites the caller value via `Keyword.merge(http_opts, base_url: resolved, ...)` (line ~96), and the signed path passes the resolved URL positionally to `HTTP.signed_request/4` (line ~179), never consulting opts.

Live evidence (2026-07-16, orchestrator session): `CCXT.Bybit.public_get_v5_market_time(ex, %{}, base_url: "https://does-not-exist.invalid")` SUCCEEDED (retCode 0) — the request went to the default host. Practical cost: Bybit demo-trading keys (api-demo.bybit.com) could not be exercised via the documented opt — every "demo" probe silently hit mainnet/testnet and returned 10003, masking a valid key as invalid. ccxt-js against the same host+key succeeds; a struct-level `base_urls` rewrite through our own client also succeeds (balance, create/cancel order) — signing is correct, only the URL override is lost.

Fix: a caller-supplied `:base_url` must take precedence over `resolve_base_url/2` on both paths (one resolution site, before the authenticated/public branch). Bybit HMAC does not sign the host; confront any venue whose signature covers the host before assuming the same.

Demo creds for the live AC: env `BYBIT_DEMO_API_KEY` / `BYBIT_DEMO_API_SECRET` (in ~/.secrets), host https://api-demo.bybit.com, plain (non-sandbox) exchange.

acceptance_criteria: Live (tidewave, real API, bybit demo host): create a far-from-market spot limit order, then CCXT.fetch_open_orders(ex, symbol: "BTC/USDT") returns exactly that order with symbol "BTC/USDT" and status "open"; cancel it in the same eval (cleanup mandatory) — the completion note records ids and calls
Offline: plug test pinning the captured demo row shape (orderStatus New, category spot, symbol BTCUSDT) through fetch_open_orders(symbol: "BTC/USDT") yields 1 parsed order, not 0
Parsed bybit rows resolve native symbols using the market-type/category context: BTCUSDT resolves to BTC/USDT (spot) vs BTC/USDT:USDT (linear) correctly, pinned by tests for both categories
A sweep of bybit unified reads that pass through filter_requested_symbols shows none can silently drop rows for want of symbol resolution (list the audited methods in the completion note)

task.body:
Live evidence (2026-07-16, bybit demo host api-demo.bybit.com, orchestrator session): with an open far-from-market spot limit order verifiably resting on the venue (raw `privateGetV5OrderRealtime` category=spot returns 1 row, orderStatus "New"; a later cancel on the id succeeds), `CCXT.fetch_open_orders(ex, symbol: "BTC/USDT")` returns `{:ok, []}` — a silent, plausible-looking empty result, the worst failure shape for a trading consumer.

The chain, each link verified: (1) the wire request is CORRECT — plug capture shows `GET /v5/order/realtime?category=spot&symbol=BTCUSDT`; (2) `CCXT.Bybit.parse_order/1` on the live row parses status "New" -> "open" and all numerics, but leaves `symbol: nil` — the native `BTCUSDT` is never resolved back to the unified `BTC/USDT`; (3) `filter_requested_symbols/2` (lib/ccxt/unified/read_parse.ex:357) then drops every row whose symbol does not equal the requested `"BTC/USDT"` -> 0 rows. Offline repro: a plug returning the captured demo row through `CCXT.fetch_open_orders(ex, symbol: "BTC/USDT", plug: ...)` parses 0 orders.

This is a defect CLASS, not one method: any bybit unified read whose rows carry a native symbol and pass through the requested-symbol filter (fetchOpenOrders / fetchClosedOrders / fetchCanceledOrders / fetchMyTrades / fetchOrder...) silently returns [] for symbol-scoped calls. Sweep which js methods hit filter_requested_symbols and fix the class.

Resolution must use the venue category context — `BTCUSDT` is ambiguous between spot and linear, and the response carries `result.category` (the request category is also known); resolve native->unified via the exchange's symbol machinery WITH that market-type context, never by string guessing. Confront CCXT JS `parseOrder`/`safeSymbol` as one reference (it resolves via market lookup), the exchange's own semantics as the authority.

Demo creds for the live AC: env `BYBIT_DEMO_API_KEY`/`BYBIT_DEMO_API_SECRET` (~/.secrets), host api-demo.bybit.com. Until the :base_url dispatch-opt fix lands, reach the demo host by rewriting `exchange.base_urls` on the struct (recursive string-replace of api(-testnet).bybit.com -> api-demo.bybit.com) — verified working. Mutation safety: only far-from-market limit orders (e.g. BTC/USDT buy 0.001 @ 10000), always cancelled in the same eval; demo funds are fake but keep the cleanup discipline.

task.title: HTTP error/success-body robustness: scalar error keys crash the classifier, legit empty-200 rejected, batch and non-JSON error detail dropped
acceptance_criteria: A unit test feeding the recorded scalar-error gateway envelope through response classification yields a typed CCXT.Error with http_status 404 and the body retained in raw — no FunctionClauseError, no network_error mislabel
Live okx demo (OKX_TESTNET_* env, hostname my.okx.com): public_get_market_books_lite returns the exchange's own error class (matching ccxt-js), not network_error
An empty 2xx body is success ({:ok, ...}) consistent with ccxt-js semantics, pinned by a unit test; the live okx empty-200 endpoint no longer errors
okx batch-error envelopes retain data[] per-item sCode/sMsg in the error's raw; non-JSON error bodies retain their text as message — both pinned by tests with recorded bodies
rfq_cancel_all_after's 51000 body parses code/message correctly (root cause identified and named in the completion note)

Venue spec authoring
task.body:
okx live sweep 2026-07-16 (scripts/venue_compare, EEA demo my.okx.com vs ccxt-js 4.5.65) surfaced one client-wide robustness defect family in CCXT.HTTP.Errors, four facets:

(1) extract_error_code/2 (errors.ex:274) does get_in(body, ["error", "code"]) unconditionally; a gateway-style envelope with a SCALAR top-level error ({"timestamp":..,"status":404,"error":"Not Found","requestId":..}) raises FunctionClauseError in Access.get/3. The blanket rescue in http.ex:149-155 swallows the crash and mislabels it network_error. ccxt-js surfaces a normal ExchangeError for the same body. (Repro: okx public_get_market_books_lite / books_sbe, tidewave-verified.)

(2) handle_success_body/4 classifies ANY empty 2xx body (except 204/HEAD) as network_error "Empty response body from exchange" — okx legitimately answers HTTP 200 with an empty body (private_post_tradingbot_signal_sub_order); ccxt-js treats it as success.

(3) Error-detail fidelity: okx batch envelopes (top-level code "1" + per-item data[].sCode/sMsg) lose the nested per-item detail — our error carries raw: nil (trade_cancel_algos, cancel_advance_algos, cancel_batch_orders); a non-JSON error body's text is dropped entirely (405 "Method Not Allowed" -> blank message/raw).

(4) private_post_rfq_cancel_all_after: the exchange returns {"code":"51000","msg":"Parameter timeOut error"} yet our parse yields code: nil with the raw JSON string as message and generic exchange_error type, while sibling 51000 responses parse fine — root-cause during the fix (evidence: scratchpad vcx/w_post_7).

Errors classification is critical-tier (95% coverage gate) — raise coverage before mutating.

Live okx demo (hostname my.okx.com): fetch_transfers returns the account's 6 real transfer records as a parsed list (id/currency/amount/from/to populated), and fetch_funding_rates returns a populated map — neither raises the all-nil error
Unit test: a recorded body containing none of a struct's mapped fields returns {:error, _} naming the unexpected shape; {:ok, all-nil struct} is impossible

Existing venue suites stay green (bybit + deribit fixture gates, file-target)

task.body:
Cross-venue live evidence (bybit testnet + okx EEA demo, scripts/venue_compare sweeps 2026-07-16) shows three inverse failures of one read-parse invariant — task 152's landed AC said "a malformed/unexpected response shape (incl. an error body) yields {:error, _}, never an all-nil struct":

(1) LEGITIMATELY-EMPTY collections are rejected: bybit fetch_deposits / fetch_withdrawals with retCode 0 and rows: [] return {:error, "Response parsed to an all-nil struct"} (re-verified live on the post-task-235 base, 2026-07-16 evening: the error's raw carries an all-nil %CCXT.Transaction{}); ccxt-js returns []. An empty collection is a valid success: {:ok, []}.

(2) LISTS collapse into ONE all-nil struct: okx fetchFundingRates (~40 swap rows in info.data), fetchTransfers (6 real records), fetch_all_greeks, fetch_funding_rate, fetchOptionChain all fold a populated array into a single all-nil struct and then raise the all-nil error; fetch_ledger raises on populated data the same way (evidence: scratchpad vcx/w_uni_1..3). ccxt-js returns populated lists.

(3) FOREIGN bodies parse into all-nil SUCCESS structs: a body containing NONE of a struct's mapped fields must be a hard {:error, ...} naming the mismatch, never {:ok, all-nil-struct} (bybit sweep observed /v5/account/info parsed into an all-nil Order).

Fix the invariant in the generic layer, not per-venue: empty spec-envelope collection -> {:ok, []}; list payloads iterate rows (never fold); zero-mapped-fields parse -> {:error, ...}. Venue field-map gaps that make a slice all-nil are separate authoring tasks (239, okx slices) — this task makes their failure LOUD and empty-success honest.

Write-set note: read_parse.ex collides with pending tasks 244 and 253 — harness write-set serialization orders them; do not fold their scopes in.

task.body:

task.title: Confront unified positional-arg divergences from CCXT: add_margin/reduce_margin arg order, create_convert_trade missing quote id
acceptance_criteria: Each divergent signature (add_margin, reduce_margin, create_convert_trade) has a registered carve-register entry: CONFIRMED-as-ours or ALIGNED-to-ccxt, with the confrontation reasoning
create_convert_trade can express the convert-quote id (whatever the chosen arity/params shape) — a live okx demo error-compare proves the id reaches the wire

task.body:
Both venue sweeps (bybit + okx, 2026-07-16) hit the same unified-surface divergence: our method_defs order add_margin/reduce_margin as (exchange, amount, symbol) where CCXT is (symbol, amount, params); create_convert_trade's required_params [:from_code, :to_code, :amount] has no slot for CCXT's leading convert-quote id (the fetch_convert_quote id that okx/bybit convert flows require). Additionally, an unresolvable symbol in these paths is silently swallowed into an empty instId param instead of failing fast client-side (okx uni_4 evidence: reduce_margin with a junk symbol sent an empty-instId request).

This is a deliberate carve decision, not automatically a bug: our client is ours-by-our-rules, CCXT one reference. Confront each signature against the exchange flows (a convert trade NEEDS the quote id to be executable), decide keep-or-align per method, and register every outcome in the carve register. Whatever the decision: an unresolvable symbol must raise CCXT.Symbol.Error client-side, never ship an empty required param.

NOTE 2026-07-17 (live convergence re-run): unchanged live on both venues — add_margin/reduce_margin arg order, create_convert_trade quote id (now a loud identifier_reference raise via task 237 instead of a silent empty param). Additional positional-shape divergences hit by the sweep harness worth folding into the same confrontation: fetch_order_book has no positional depth/limit slot (okx + calls with a bare integer crash "opts must be a keyword list"), fetch_positions_adl_rank rejects a symbols list positionally, fetch_orders_classic crashes on a bare symbol string. Decide per method: our-rules signature (register carve) or align — but a bare positional that CCXT accepts must never crash with an opts TypeError.

task.title: Thread the effective host into signing config for host-signing venues (htx/huobi/bittrade)
acceptance_criteria: Overriding :base_url on a host-signing venue (htx/huobi/bittrade) produces a signature covering the overridden host, not the struct's construction-time hostname
Offline plug test pins that the hostname signature component tracks opts[:base_url] when supplied, and the struct hostname when absent
Non-host-signing venues (the 7 first-class) are unaffected — the Task 252 dispatch base_url tests stay green
The host-signing warning block in CCXT.Dispatch's moduledoc is updated or removed once the divergence is closed
out_of_scope: Re-authoring htx/huobi/bittrade interpretive slices beyond the hostname signing component
Provisioning htx/huobi testnet credentials
task.body:
Task 252 made the `:base_url` dispatch opt honest — it now wins over `resolve_base_url/2` on both the public and signed paths. That fix is correct for every venue whose signature covers only path/params (all 7 first-class venues; bybit demo verified live against api-demo.bybit.com).

But three long-tail venues sign the HOST: `htx`, `huobi`, `bittrade` carry a `"source" => "hostname"` signature component (see `component_value/2` in lib/ccxt/signing/hmac_recipe.ex:314). That component reads `config[:hostname]`, populated from the exchange struct at construction — NOT from the caller's `:base_url` override. So overriding `:base_url` on those venues signs the struct's hostname while the request travels to the overridden host, and the exchange rejects the signature.

The failure is LOUD (auth error, not a silently-wrong request), which is why task 252 shipped without gating on it. Make the signing hostname follow the effective base URL: derive the host from the URL actually being requested rather than from construction-time config, so an override and its signature agree.

Reality check first — htx/huobi signing is a long-tail slice with no provisioned creds. Confront the exchange's own docs (and CCXT JS `sign()` as one reference, never the arbiter) to confirm which host string the signature must cover: bare hostname vs scheme-qualified, and whether the per-section `urls.hostnames` override (htx `contract` -> api.hbdm.vn) interacts.
