task.title: bybit fetch_markets option index truncates at 500 rows per baseCoin — venue cursor says there is more
acceptance_criteria: Live (bybit testnet): fetch_markets option rows per baseCoin match the venue's own full set for that base — BTC and ETH no longer sit at exactly 500; the count equals a limit=1000 call's row count for the same base (modulo an explicitly registered status filter)

The completeness signal is the venue's nextPageCursor, not a hardcoded page size: a non-empty cursor after the final request either paginates or fails loudly — 'limit=1000 is enough' is not left as an unchecked constant

The Trading-vs-Delivering decision is confronted against the venue (not CCXT's loadAllOptions default) and registered as a carve entry in docs/authored-specs.md, whether the outcome is CONFIRM or DIVERGE
Offline regression pins the option request's completeness handling so a page-size regression cannot silently truncate the index again
mix check.dispatch stays green; bybit fixture gates stay at 0 failed
FIRST verification move is a live testnet call, never a fixture replay
out_of_scope: The option category fan-out set itself (delivered by task 251)
Pagination for spot/linear/inverse categories — file separately if proven truncated there
Option response field-map authoring beyond what fetch_markets rows need
task.body:
Reviewer live finding (2026-07-16, gating task 251 on bybit testnet). Refiled by the orchestrator
2026-07-16: the reviewer's original in-run filing only reached the main checkout's generated
data.json, not tasks.toml (known harness discovery-filing defect) — content recovered verbatim.

Task 251 landed the option category into bybit's fetch_markets fan-out (option bucket = 2082,
verified live). But each per-baseCoin option request sends no `limit`, so the venue returns its
default page of 500 rows AND a non-empty `nextPageCursor` ("0%2C500") that we ignore. The extra
rows are silently dropped:

  GET /v5/market/instruments-info?category=option&baseCoin=BTC            -> 500 rows, cursor "0%2C500"
  GET /v5/market/instruments-info?category=option&baseCoin=BTC&limit=1000 -> 640 rows, cursor ""
  (ETH: 500 vs 658)

Of the 140 missing BTC rows, 98 are live `status: "Trading"` and 42 are `Delivering`. Our index
therefore under-reports tradeable BTC/ETH options by ~100 each — fetch_option / fetch_option_chain
cannot resolve a symbol that fetch_markets never indexed. The `"BTC" => 500` / `"ETH" => 500`
round numbers in the live base histogram are the tell.

This is CCXT-JS-DEFAULT-COMPATIBLE, which is exactly why it needs its own task rather than a
silent fix: CCXT's `fetchOptionMarkets` only sets `limit: 1000` and walks the cursor when
`options.loadAllOptions` is true (default false), and it filters to active-only unless
`loadAllOptions`/`loadExpiredOptions`. So a green CCXT-fixture gate certifies the truncation
(tier 2 = we match CCXT; blind to CCXT being wrong). Per docs/authored-specs.md, decide from the
VENUE, not from CCXT.

The carve to confront and register: (a) single `limit=1000` per base vs walking `nextPageCursor`
(live says one limit=1000 call is sufficient today and empties the cursor — but the cursor is the
venue's own completeness signal, so relying on 1000 being "enough" is a constant that can rot);
(b) whether the market index carries `Delivering` instruments or only `Trading`, and whether that
is a `Market.active` flag rather than an exclusion. Diverging from CCXT here is allowed and
expected — register the outcome as a carve (C13 already records the truncation as known).

task.title: filter_requested_symbols raises KeyError on symbol-less structs (Transaction/LedgerEntry/TransferEntry/DepositAddress)
acceptance_criteria: Reachability established FIRST with a valid payload: an offline/plug test showing a currency-scoped read (e.g. fetch_deposits) reaching filter_requested_symbols with a symbol param either raises today (defect confirmed) or is documented as unreachable, naming the guard that prevents it (then close as not-a-defect)

If confirmed: passing symbol:/symbols: to a currency-scoped read no longer raises KeyError; the behavior is a deliberate documented choice (ignore the param, or return a typed {:error, _}) rather than a crash
If confirmed: offline tests pin the chosen behavior for Transaction, LedgerEntry, TransferEntry and DepositAddress rows
Symbol-bearing reads (order/trade/position/market) keep existing filtering behavior — existing read_parse tests stay green
out_of_scope: Bybit native-symbol category resolution (task 253)
Adding a :symbol field to currency-scoped structs (they legitimately have none)
task.body:
Found while reviewing task 253 (harness run run-1784197286385-d584f461).

`filter_requested_symbols/2` (lib/ccxt/unified/read_parse.ex) resolves each row's
symbol with an unguarded struct field access (`&1.symbol`) in both the `"symbols"`
and `"symbol"` param clauses. Four unified read structs have NO `:symbol` key in
their defstruct: `CCXT.Transaction`, `CCXT.LedgerEntry`, `CCXT.TransferEntry`,
`CCXT.DepositAddress` (verified: zero `:symbol` occurrences in
lib/ccxt/{transaction,ledger_entry,transfer_entry,deposit_address}.ex).

`apply_request_filters/3` runs for any list-shaped parse result, so a caller that
passes `symbol:`/`symbols:` to a currency-scoped read (fetch_deposits,
fetch_withdrawals, fetch_ledger, fetch_transfers, fetch_deposit_addresses_by_network)
would reach `&1.symbol` on a struct lacking that key — a KeyError raised out of the
unified API rather than an `{:error, _}` tuple or a graceful no-op.

CONFIDENCE — what is and is not established. The mechanism is certain by Elixir
struct semantics (`.symbol` on a struct without that key raises KeyError). But
end-to-end reachability was NOT reproduced during review: a probe against
fetch_deposits was rejected by the error-envelope guard before reaching the filter,
because the probe's body shape was wrong — not because a guard is known to protect
this path. So the FIRST step is to establish reachability with a valid payload
before changing code. If it proves unreachable, close this as not-a-defect and
record why — do not add a defensive guard for a path that cannot be hit.

These are currency-scoped methods that normally carry `"code"`, not `"symbol"`,
which is likely why this has not surfaced in the suite.

task.title: Confront Bybit fetchOpenOrders exclusion from the order pagination-cursor merge list
acceptance_criteria: A real Bybit v5 /v5/order/realtime response is captured showing whether result.nextPageCursor is populated when open orders span more than one page, and the observed value is recorded in the task or carve register

Either fetchOpenOrders merges the cursor onto the first raw row (matching the fetchClosedOrders branch) with an offline test pinning the merged value, or the deliberate exclusion is documented in read_parse.ex with the exchange-sourced reason
The existing test 'bybit fetchOpenOrders is outside the cursor method list and merges no cursor' is updated or removed to match the confronted behavior, never left asserting a contradiction
mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Changing cursor handling for non-order parse types (positions / open interest)
Fixing the separate task 253 finding that unified fetch_open_orders returns [] for resting orders
task.body:
`merge_bybit_pagination_cursor/5` in lib/ccxt/unified/read_parse.ex stamps `nextPageCursor` onto raw order rows only for the js_names listed in `@bybit_order_pagination_cursor_methods` — currently `fetchClosedOrder`, `fetchClosedOrders`, `fetchOpenOrder`. The plural `fetchOpenOrders` is absent, so a Bybit v5 `/v5/order/realtime` response whose `result.nextPageCursor` is populated loses the cursor and callers cannot paginate open orders.

The singular-included / plural-excluded asymmetry looks unintentional but was NOT confirmed against reality during task 244's review (that task's scope forbade changing authored field-map semantics), so it is filed rather than fixed. Surfaced by review of run-1784198739936-eaddbf27: a test named "open-order pagination cursor merges onto the first row" asserted the merge tautologically (`== "cursor-abc" or is_map(order.info)`) and passed while the cursor was in fact nil; the reviewer pinned the assertion to the real (nil) behavior and renamed the test.

Confront the carve against the exchange's own semantics before changing it: determine from a REAL Bybit response (demo host api-demo.bybit.com per CLAUDE.md; testnet is read-only) whether `/v5/order/realtime` returns a non-empty `nextPageCursor`, and read CCXT JS as one reference, never the arbiter. If the omission is a defect, add `fetchOpenOrders` to the list and record the outcome in the carve register; if deliberate, document why so the asymmetry is not re-litigated.

task.title: Balance reconciliation derives only `used` — safeBalance fills whichever of free/used/total is missing
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation derives free = total - used when free is nil and total/used are numeric, and total = free + used when total is nil — mirroring CCXT safeBalance's three-way fill
An already-parsed value is still never overwritten (task 241 invariant holds for all three keys)
Hyperliquid spot free is derived rather than authored: with total=999 and hold=1.5, free is 997.5 (CCXT parity) — the authored `free -> total` carve is removed
Static fixture gate shows no regression vs the pre-change baseline
task.body:
Surfaced while reviewing task 241 (reconcile_balance_used no longer clobbers parsed used).

CCXT's base safeBalance (ts/src/base/Exchange.ts, v4.5.65) fills in whichever ONE of free/used/total is undefined:
  total undefined -> free + used;  free undefined -> total - used;  used undefined -> total - free.

Our reconcile_balance_used/1 implements only the third. Venues whose CCXT parser omits `free` (rather than `used`) therefore have no derivation to fall back on, and have been authored around the gap instead: hyperliquid spot authors `free -> total` (the raw `total` field) even though CCXT sets only total+hold and derives free = total - hold. Result: hyperliquid spot free is overstated by `hold` (fixture: free 999.0 where CCXT gives 997.5), and free/used/total are mutually inconsistent.

Implement the missing derivations, then drop the compensating hyperliquid `free` carve. Do not reintroduce the pre-241 unconditional overwrite.

task.title: Balance field-map cannot express CCXT's per-currency used/free branch (okx availEq, bybit availableToWithdraw)
acceptance_criteria: okx: a details row WITHOUT availEq maps used = frozenBal and free = availBal, while a row WITH availEq derives used = eq - availEq — both shapes proven in one offline response
bybit: a coin entry WITHOUT availableToWithdraw/free maps used = locked + totalPositionIM + totalOrderIM, while an entry WITH availableToWithdraw derives used = walletBalance - availableToWithdraw
Divergences that remain unexpressible are recorded in the carve register per docs/authored-specs.md rather than left implicit
Static fixture gate shows no regression vs the pre-change baseline

Reconciliation derives free = total - used when free is nil and total/used are numeric, and total = free + used when total is nil — CCXT safeBalance's three-way fill; an already-parsed value is still never overwritten (task 241 invariant holds for all three keys)
Hyperliquid spot free is derived rather than authored: with total=999 and hold=1.5, free is 997.5 (CCXT parity) — the authored free -> total carve is removed
task.body:
Surfaced while reviewing task 241.

CCXT branches `used`/`free` PER CURRENCY ROW, not per response:
  okx parseTradingBalance - total = eq always; if availEq === undefined -> free = availBal, used = frozenBal; else free = availEq and used is left undefined (safeBalance derives total - free).
  bybit parseBalance (UNIFIED/CONTRACT/SPOT) - free = availableToWithdraw ?? free; when that is undefined -> used = locked + totalPositionIM + totalOrderIM; else used is left undefined and derived.

Our field-map DSL guards at the BRANCH level (a whole variant chosen by a body-level predicate such as hyperliquid's has_key "balances"), so a per-row condition cannot be authored. Task 241 review resolved this by setting okx/bybit `used` to null and letting reconciliation derive total - free, which matches CCXT exactly on the availEq/availableToWithdraw-PRESENT branch (the one both static fixtures exercise) and approximates the absent branch only because eq = availBal + frozenBal normally holds. It is an approximation, not parity, and it silently under-reports `used` for rows where free is genuinely absent.

Either extend the keyed_collection descriptor with a per-row conditional (e.g. a value_key that falls back when a named key is absent), or author these venues via a custom parse hook. Confront the carve against each exchange's own semantics before choosing - CCXT is one reference, not the arbiter.

2026-07-17 (orchestrator): folds task 264 (safeBalance three-way fill — reconciliation currently derives only used). Both tasks came out of the 241 review, live in the same balance reconciliation path, and one reviewer verifies both in one diff — merged per the coupling test.

task.title: Bybit legacy signing: decide auth-param precedence vs caller params (CCXT extend semantics)
acceptance_criteria: The chosen semantics are exercised by an offline regression test in test/ccxt/signing/hmac_recipe_test.exs that fails if the precedence flips
If adopting CCXT override semantics: a caller-supplied api_key/timestamp/recv_window is replaced by the credential/clock-derived value in both the signed canonical string and the sent request
If registering the divergence instead: docs/authored-specs.md C14 is updated from an open delta to a decided DIVERGE outcome with rationale
Live testnet evidence (BYBIT_TESTNET_* creds, sandbox: true): a legacy GET such as user/v3/private/query-api still returns retCode 0 after the change
mix check.dispatch stays green; bybit signing fixture gate green (file-target, bare --only exchange_bybit)
out_of_scope: The legacy POST body placement (landed in task 254)
Other venues' query_params injection
task.body:
Task 254 authored bybit's legacy (non-v5) query-param signing recipe. The executor injects the
declared `query_params` (api_key / recv_window / timestamp) with a put-if-missing rule, so a
caller-supplied param of the same name wins.

CCXT JS bybit.ts sign() does the opposite: `this.extend(params, {'api_key': ..., 'recv_window':
..., 'timestamp': ...})` places the auth object LAST, so credential-derived values always override
whatever the caller passed. Confront this against the venue (live testnet is the authority,
CCXT-JS the compatibility reference) and decide: adopt CCXT's override semantics, or register the
divergence deliberately.

Consequence today is mild — a caller passing api_key gets it signed and sent, and bybit rejects the
request — but it is an unregistered behavioural delta from the reference implementation in
auth-critical code. Decide it, don't leave it accidental. docs/authored-specs.md carve register
entry C14 already notes it as an open delta pointing at this task. (Refiled by the orchestrator
2026-07-16 as 266: the reviewer filed it as 264 in a dirty parallel checkout while task 241's
review landed a different 264 on origin — ID collision resolved by renumbering; C14's task
reference updated to match. Reassigned cursor -> codex/gpt-5.5, cursor budget-blocked.)

venues. This is an audit only: it must not implement venue mappings. Mark the task complete when

`:option_unknown`, so option symbol -> instId denormalization is lossy — `BTC/USD:BTC-260717-48000-C`
denormalizes to `BTC-260717-48000-C`, dropping the quote. The real okx instrument id is
`BTC-USD-260717-48000-C` (confirmed against `GET /api/v5/public/instruments?instType=OPTION&instFamily=BTC-USD`,
which returns instId=BTC-USD-260717-48000-C, instFamily=BTC-USD, uly=BTC-USD, settleCcy=BTC).

mangled id is `BTC-260717` rather than `BTC-USD`. Task 257 left the family derivation refusing to

but the underlying symbol defect is untouched.

This is the legacy heuristic `Symbol.classify_pattern/2` layer (CLAUDE.md: legacy, slated for
deletion in task 173 / T-E2) failing to classify okx options. Prefer authoring the okx option
pattern into the frozen spec over extending the heuristic. Note the blast radius: the pattern

task.title: Carve register ids collide and dangle — make carve_id a checked namespace, not a hand-typed number
acceptance_criteria: A check in the mix check.dispatch stack fails when a carve id is defined twice in docs/authored-specs.md, and passes on a clean register
The check fails when a divergence_contracts.json carve_id has no matching register entry
The duplicate C15 is resolved by an explicit decision recorded in the register; existing landed ids referenced elsewhere (B1/C6/C7/C9, task bodies) are not silently renumbered
Task 273's dangling 'carve C17' reference either resolves to a real entry or is corrected to point at where the OKX opt-summary gap is actually documented
Register documents the append-only rule so the next author does not fill the C17 hole with an unrelated carve

Changing the semantics of any existing carve decision
The Binance option carve itself (landed in 274 as C18)
task.body:
Surfaced by the task 274 review (run run-1784208243121-1510a20f). The carve register in
docs/authored-specs.md numbers entries by hand, and parallel write-set-disjoint worktrees each
pick "the next number" without seeing each other. The namespace has already drifted three ways:

- DUPLICATE: C15 is used twice — "GET array query encoding" and "OKX unified requests are keyed
  by instrument type". Two unrelated carves answer to one id.
- OUT OF ORDER: C14 (bybit legacy signing) sits after the first C15.
- DANGLING: task 273's body says the OKX opt-summary row-selection gap is "documented as a known
  gap under carve C17" — no C17 exists; that gap is actually recorded under C15's Known gaps.
  Task 274 originally renumbered deribit's landed C16 to C17, which would have silently resolved
  273's reference to an unrelated deribit carve. The review reverted that and parked the new
  Binance carve at C18, leaving C17 deliberately unused.

This is the cross-module global-invariant class from CLAUDE.md: no per-task reviewer can see the
collision because each worktree's diff is internally consistent. The ids are load-bearing —
priv/specs/json/output/authored/divergence_contracts.json binds gates by carve_id (B1/C6/C7/C9)
and the register says "these ids point back to this register".

Fix the namespace, don't just hand-repair today's drift: make uniqueness and reference integrity a
check that fails loudly (a manifest-consistency test in the mix check.dispatch stack) rather than
something an author is supposed to notice. Decide deliberately whether to renumber the duplicate
C15 (renumbering a landed id is itself the defect that caused this) or to disambiguate another
way — a suffix, or freezing ids and letting the check assert only that no id is reused.

task.body:
Task 258 landed the okx response slices and took the okx recorded-response gate from 7 passing / 32 failing to 10/29, but two of its own target cases stay red. Close both.

1. fetchCurrencies (`okx fetchCurrencies default #17`): OKX answers `asset/currencies` with ONE ROW PER CHAIN per currency (BTC-Bitcoin, BTCK-OKTC, BTC-Lightning, ...). ccxt-js groups those rows into a single unified Currency per code whose `info` is the LIST of chain rows and whose `networks` map carries per-chain fee/limits/deposit/withdraw. We currently emit one Currency per row keyed by `ccy`, so all but the last chain are lost. Author the grouping (the `networks` slot is generic — check whether other first-class venues need the same shape rather than overfitting to okx).

2. fetchAccounts (`okx fetchAccounts Fetch accounts #11`): the ONLY diff against the static fixture is that ccxt-js's parseAccount emits a `currency` key (undefined for okx) that `%CCXT.Account{}` has no field for. Do not add the field reflexively to match an `undefined` CCXT emits — run the confrontation step per docs/authored-specs.md: does an okx account have a currency in the venue's own semantics? Either add the field deliberately or register a DIVERGE carve saying our Account has no `currency` and why. Inheriting a CCXT key without confronting it is exactly what the carve register exists to prevent.

Reviewer evidence 2026-07-16 (harness run run-1784208240096-3fa5e0c5), live okx EEA demo `my.okx.com` with sandbox: true.

task.body:
Task 258 authored okx ticker vwap as `volCcy24h / vol24h`, faithfully mirroring ccxt-js safeTicker (quoteVolume/baseVolume). That is CORRECT AS COMPATIBILITY and the task asked for exactly it — but the carve was never confronted, and the number is domain-suspect.

Live okx demo evidence 2026-07-16 (harness run run-1784208240096-3fa5e0c5), BTC/USDT:USDT:

    last = 64092.8, open24h = 64950.2
    vol24h = 8444450.57 (CONTRACTS), volCcy24h = 849278.3743 (BTC)
    unified vwap = 0.01   <-- this is the contract size (ctVal), not a volume-weighted average price

A vwap of 0.01 for an instrument trading near $64,000 is not a price by any reading. For okx SWAP, volCcy24h is the BASE-currency volume and vol24h is a CONTRACT count, so the ratio collapses to ctVal. ccxt-js emits the same number, so a fixture/CCXT-anchored gate ratifies it green — the delta_calc trap surviving execution because CCXT is the shared wrong source on both sides (docs/authored-specs.md, "Compatibility != correctness").

Run the confrontation step against a TIER-1 oracle (okx API docs / official SDK semantics for vol24h vs volCcy24h per instType, plus the real API), across spot / linear swap / inverse swap, and decide deliberately: keep CCXT's number (CONFIRMED, documented as CCXT-compat with a known domain caveat) or compute a real vwap (DIVERGE)? Either outcome is acceptable — an unconfronted inherited carve is not. Check whether bybit/deribit/binance inverse contracts carry the same shape before overfitting to okx.

task.body:
Surfaced by the task 260 review (harness run run-1784213832864-182f1f59); out of that task's scope (it closed only the hostname component).

The authored htx sign_recipe omits the query auth params huobi's signing scheme requires. Observed against the real vendored spec via an offline plug on `private_get_account_accounts`:

    HOST=api.huobi.pro
    PATH=/v1/account/accounts
    QS=timestamp=2023-11-14T22%3A13%3A20.000Z&Signature=Jns0mIYEp9qhETobSzO4NfjkE%2F%2Bpp5LD0hUegSXUN34%3D

The signed query carries only a lowercase `timestamp`. Huobi/HTX documented signing requires four params present AND covered by the canonical payload: `AccessKeyId`, `SignatureMethod` (HmacSHA256), `SignatureVersion` (2), `Timestamp` (capital T, ISO-8601). `CCXT.Signing.HmacRecipe` injects declared params from `recipe["query_params"]`, which the htx recipe never declares, so nothing is injected and the venue would reject every private call as unauthenticated.

Confront the exchange's own docs for authoritative param names, casing, and timestamp format (whether the trailing `Z` and millisecond precision the current `iso8601` formatter emits are accepted), with CCXT JS `sign()` as one reference, never the arbiter. Author the slice for htx and its huobi/bittrade siblings.

task.title: Confront canonical query encoder space encoding (+ vs %20) against venue signing docs
acceptance_criteria: An offline test pins the encoding the canonical query emits for a param value containing a space, and asserts the documented form rather than the current behavior
The chosen encoding is confirmed against at least one affected venue's own API docs (not CCXT JS alone), with the doc reference recorded in the test or module docs

A live signed call against a provisioned testnet (bybit demo, deribit, binance, or okx demo) carrying a space-bearing param value authenticates successfully, or the task records the venue's real error proving the current encoding is rejected
Venues that legitimately require www-form encoding keep it, with the divergence registered as a deliberate per-venue carve rather than a silent global change

Array param encoding dialects (brackets vs repeat), covered by task 240
Provisioning htx/huobi testnet credentials
task.body:
Surfaced by the task 283 review (harness run run-1784216012617-6f61e80a); out of that task's scope, which closed only the four htx/huobi/bittrade auth query params.

The shared canonical query encoder builds signed query strings with Elixir's `URI.encode_query/1`, which renders a space as `+` (verified in this worktree: `URI.encode_query(%{"a" => "x y"}) == "a=x+y"`). CCXT JS's `urlencode` and the venue signing docs specify percent-encoding instead — Huobi's spot docs state query params are URL-encoded with uppercase hex values and show %20-style escapes. Any private call whose param value contains a space (or another character where www-form and RFC 3986 encoding diverge) would therefore sign and send bytes the venue re-canonicalizes differently, producing a signature mismatch the client surfaces as an auth failure rather than as an encoding bug.

This affects `CCXT.Signing.encode_query_pairs/2` and every recipe whose canonical string declares the `urlencode` encoder, so the blast radius is the whole authored catalog, not one venue. Confront each affected venue's own signing docs for the authoritative encoding rule (which characters, uppercase vs lowercase hex, space handling), with CCXT JS `sign()` as one reference and never the arbiter. Determine whether the divergence is real per venue before changing the shared encoder — some venues may genuinely accept www-form encoding.

Round-tripping every example in priv/specs/json/output/authored/deribit.json markets.patterns.{future,option} through from_exchange_id/3 then to_exchange_id/2 reproduces the original id exactly, including BASE_QUOTE-DDMMMYY futures and d-decimal strike options

task.body:
Task 236 closed Deribit's 1007-way BTC/USD:BTC symbol collision for the inverse (USD-quoted, base-settled) book. It did not cover Deribit's SECOND id grammar - the linear USDC book - because neither the :future_ddmmmyy nor the :option_ddmmmyy encoder models that shape.

Live testnet evidence (2026-07-16, deribit sandbox, gathered during the task 236 review): 3040 of 4961 markets carry the RAW instrument_name as their unified symbol, because neither from_exchange_id/3 nor to_exchange_id/2 classifies the shape, so the id passes through (uppercased) untouched. Ours vs CCXT-JS 4.5.65:

  AVAX_USDC-17JUL26        -> we emit "AVAX_USDC-17JUL26"      ; CCXT-JS "AVAX/USDC:USDC-260717"
  BTC_USDC-22JUN26         -> we emit "BTC_USDC-22JUN26"       ; CCXT-JS "BTC/USDC:USDC-260622"
  AVAX_USDC-22JUN26-5d5-C  -> we emit "AVAX_USDC-22JUN26-5D5-C"; CCXT-JS "AVAX/USDC:USDC-260622-5.5-C"

Two distinct carves are involved; both need confronting against Deribit's own naming (docs.deribit.com) with CCXT as one reference, per docs/authored-specs.md:

1. The linear USDC book separates base from quote with an UNDERSCORE (BTC_USDC-...), unlike the inverse book's base-only ids (BTC-22JUN26). The spec's own authored examples already record both shapes under markets.patterns.{future,option}.
2. USDC option strikes use `d` as the decimal point (5d5 == 5.5). These are exactly the 849 entries the spec currently parks in markets.patterns.option.anomalies.

Symbol uniqueness is NOT at risk today (raw ids are unique, so duplicates stay 0). The defect is that 61% of the deribit catalog is not on the unified symbol grammar, so those markets fail the CCXT compat oracle and cannot be addressed by a unified symbol on dispatch.

The round-trip is the real gate: to_exchange_id/2 must reproduce the exact instrument_name, since dispatch sends it as the instrument_name param.

task.title: Dead authenticated_sections entries designate no endpoint in 5 catalog specs
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 11 dead entries is classified vestigial (dropped) or missing-section (api tree corrected), with the reason recorded per venue

task.body:
Surfaced by the task 284 review (harness run run-1784218208291-57d312f4).

Task 284 fixed the generator so authored `authenticated_sections` entries match nested
section paths. Building the catalog-wide invariant for it surfaced an adjacent, distinct
condition: some specs author entries that designate NO endpoint at all, so the entry is inert.

Observed across all 110 compiled exchanges, post-284:

    alpaca, coinbase, coinbaseadvanced, coinbaseinternational => "private"
    tokocrypto => "dapiPrivate", "dapiPrivateV2", "fapiPrivate", "fapiPrivateV2",
                  "sapi", "sapiV3", "wapi"

The four coinbase/alpaca specs list a bare `private` alongside their real dotted entries
(`v2.private`, `market.private`, ...) but have no top-level `private` section. tokocrypto
lists binance-family section names its own api tree does not contain (likely inherited from
the parent spec at vendoring time).

This is NOT the 284 defect class and is currently benign: an entry designating nothing cannot
cause an unsigned dispatch — it signs nothing because there is nothing to sign. It is spec
hygiene, and it is load-bearing in exactly one direction: while these dead entries exist, the
catalog cannot enforce "every authored entry designates a real endpoint" as a CI invariant, so
a genuine TYPO in an authored entry (e.g. `contract.privat`) stays silent and leaves that
section unsigned — which is exactly the 284 failure mode, undetected.

Determine for each entry whether it is (a) vestigial and should be dropped from the authored
spec, or (b) evidence the api tree is missing sections it should have (check tokocrypto against
its CCXT JS parent). Then land the invariant so future typos fail loudly.

task.body:
Surfaced by the task 291 review (harness run run-1784220724237-ca926926).

Task 291 landed the invariant for one direction: every authored
`authenticated_sections` entry must designate at least one real endpoint (a dead
entry means a TYPO stays silent). The MIRROR direction is still unguarded and is
the one that actually causes the task 284 harm: an endpoint section that IS
private but has NO authored entry covering it materializes `authenticated: false`
and dispatches UNSIGNED, silently.

Observed post-291 across all 110 compiled exchanges (endpoints whose section path
contains "private", generated `authenticated: false`, matched by no authored entry,
on venues that DO have a non-empty authored list):

    kucoin, kucoinfutures => ["utaPrivate"]   (authored: broker, earn, futuresPrivate, private)
    coinspot              => ["v2","private"] (authored: private)

These three are the load-bearing cases: the venue has an authored auth slice, so
the omission looks like completed authoring rather than a gap. A further 15 venues
have an EMPTY authored list entirely — that is the documented public-data-only
frozen long-tail state, not this defect, and is out of scope.

All 7 first-class venues are clean (zero uncovered private sections) — verified at
291 review time, so this is long-tail hygiene, not a first-class correctness hole.

Determine for each of the three whether the section is genuinely authenticated by
reading the venue's CCXT JS `sign()` (kucoin's `utaPrivate`, coinspot's `v2.private`):
if it signs, author the missing entry; if it does not (i.e. the section is public
despite the name), record why the name is misleading. Then land the mirror invariant
so a future missing entry fails loudly the way a dead entry now does.

Note the invariant cannot simply key on the string "private" in the section path —
decide and document the rule that distinguishes "this section must be covered" from
"this section is legitimately unauthenticated", otherwise the 15 empty-list long-tail
venues make the invariant unlandable.

acceptance_criteria: Live binance testnet (sandbox: true, testnet.binance.vision creds): no-arg CCXT.fetch_markets returns the spot instrument set instead of {:error, -5000 'Path /dapi/v1/margin/allPairs ... is invalid'} — the whole call must not die on one fan-out wave whose section does not exist on the venue's testnet
The skip/degrade decision is confronted against CCXT-JS's own sandboxMode fetchMarkets behavior (which market types it fetches in sandbox) and registered as a carve outcome — never a silent hardcode

Investigate and record why the error names /dapi/v1/margin/allPairs on the SPOT sandbox host — margin/allPairs is a sapi path; if sandbox base-URL resolution maps the sapi section onto a wrong URL template, that is a second defect of this task (fix or register)
Live binance MAINNET public no-arg fetch_markets still returns the full multi-section set (~7800 rows observed 2026-07-17) — no regression on the non-sandbox path

task.body:
Orchestrator live finding 2026-07-17 during the task-227 landed-base verification:
CCXT.fetch_markets on binance with sandbox: true fails entirely with
{:error, %CCXT.Error{code: -5000, http_status: 404, message: "Path /dapi/v1/margin/allPairs,
Method GET is invalid"}} — one fan-out wave (margin pairs, a sapi section that does not exist
on testnet.binance.vision) kills the whole read. The same call on mainnet public succeeds
(12184 rows across binance+binanceusdm, 0 nil flags — task 227 verified live on that path).

Two suspicious facts to confront against reality: (1) CCXT-JS restricts fetchMarkets types in
sandboxMode — our fan-out set does not consult sandbox state; (2) the error path reads
/dapi/v1/... on the SPOT sandbox even though margin/allPairs is a sapi path — sandbox URL
template resolution for the sapi section may be mapping to the wrong host template.

Fail-loud vs degrade is a real design decision here: an empty margin wave on sandbox is venue
reality (the section does not exist there), not an error to propagate. Decide per CCXT-JS
compat + venue truth and register the outcome.

task.title: T-A/OKX: confront the greeks carve — coin-margined delta/gamma/vega/theta vs Black-Scholes *BS fields
acceptance_criteria: OKX's own API docs (not CCXT) are cited for what opt-summary delta/gamma/vega/theta vs deltaBS/gammaBS/vegaBS/thetaBS each denominate, and the citation is recorded in the task or carve register
A CONFIRMED or DIVERGE entry for the okx greeks carve exists in the carve register, naming which field family unified %CCXT.Greeks{} carries for okx and why
Live okx demo: fetch_greeks for a put returns a delta consistent with the documented meaning of the chosen field family — if the BS family is chosen, put delta falls within [-1, 0]
An offline regression pins the chosen field family through the okx greeks parse path against a real recorded opt-summary row carrying BOTH families, so a silent swap back is a red test
mix check.dispatch stays green; the static-fixture gate count does not regress from its pre-existing baseline
out_of_scope: The greeks response envelope and fetch_all_greeks symbol indexing (tasks 273/282 — landed)
Other venues' greeks field_maps, except to honor the cross-venue consistency requirement
Adding new unified Greeks struct fields to carry both families
task.body:
Surfaced while gating task 282 (reviewer, run run-1784223548618-dafc3b0e). The okx
authored greeks field_map copies OKX's coin-margined greeks (`delta`, `gamma`,
`vega`, `theta`) into the unified %CCXT.Greeks{} struct. OKX's public/opt-summary
returns BOTH families side by side, and they are not the same quantity.

Live OKX EEA demo (my.okx.com, sandbox: true), raw row observed 2026-07-17:

    instId: BTC-USD-261225-90000-P
    delta:   "-1.2051359955599346"     deltaBS: "-0.7904674450641715"
    gamma:   "3.2733454416584755"      gammaBS: "0.00001349022316429954"
    vega:    "0.0018957040866978078"   vegaBS:  "121.28278734752634"
    theta:   "-0.00028299440874938396" thetaBS: "-9.906365773126579"

A Black-Scholes put delta is mathematically bounded to [-1, 0]. The value we
currently surface as unified `delta` is -1.205 — outside that range — because
OKX's bare `delta` is expressed in coin/contract terms while `deltaBS` is the
Black-Scholes greek. Every consumer reading %CCXT.Greeks{} as BS greeks (the
unified struct's implied contract, and what a portable greeks abstraction has to
mean) is therefore reading a differently-denominated number without knowing it.

This is a CARVE question, not a value bug: decide what the unified Greeks struct
MEANS for okx, per the confrontation step in docs/authored-specs.md. CCXT-JS is
ONE reference (it likely copies the bare keys — matching it proves compatibility,
tier 2, not correctness); OKX's own API docs on opt-summary field semantics are
the non-CCXT semantic source that makes this tier 1. Record the outcome
(CONFIRMED or DIVERGE) in the carve register either way — a CCXT carve adopted
without a register entry is inherited, not confronted.

Note the cross-venue axis when deciding: whatever okx means by unified `delta`
should be the same quantity deribit/bybit mean, or the abstraction is not portable.

acceptance_criteria: Live binance SPOT testnet (sandbox: true, testnet.binance.vision): no-arg CCXT.fetch_markets returns the spot instrument set instead of dying on the same margin/allPairs wave (observed 2026-07-17: -5000 404 'Path /dapi/v1/margin/allPairs'); the skip/degrade decision is confronted against CCXT-JS sandboxMode fetchMarkets behavior and registered as a carve outcome

Live binanceusdm testnet: a far-from-market limit order lifecycle (create -> fetch by returned id -> cancel) succeeds with deterministic cleanup; completion evidence records the order ids
side (and type) casing normalization is authored and confronted against Binance's own docs with CCXT-JS as compatibility reference only; a lowercase caller-supplied side no longer yields -1117
An integration test pins the observed request shape and the real error semantics, tagged so it does not run in the offline gate

Coin-margined (binancecoinm) venue work
task.body:
Live-verified by the task-293 reviewer (run run-1784225001481-6a1cff20) against the real
Binance USD-M testnet. Two independent defects block any live order lifecycle on the
binance family; together they made task 293's live acceptance criterion unreachable.

1. `fetch_markets` on `binanceusdm` requests `/dapi/v1/margin/allPairs` -- a COIN-margined
   (dapi) path -- and the USD-M testnet answers `-5000 "Path /dapi/v1/margin/allPairs,
   Method GET is invalid"`. Markets therefore never load, the runtime symbols index stays
   empty, and every symbol denormalization fails. Observed live: `CCXT.fetch_markets(ex)`
   returns `{:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :exchange_not_available, code: -5000}}`. USD-M
   markets come from the fapi surface (`/fapi/v1/exchangeInfo`); confront the endpoint
   selection against Binance's own USD-M docs, not against CCXT's dispatch.

2. `side` reaches the wire in the caller's casing. Binance requires an uppercase enum
   (BUY/SELL); CCXT JS does `side.toUpperCase()`. Observed live on `binanceusdm`
   create_order: lowercase "buy" gives `-1117 "Invalid side."`, while uppercase "BUY"
   clears side validation and advances to the symbol failure from defect 1
   (`-1121 "Invalid symbol."`). The same normalization question applies to `type` and to
   binance spot.

Filed together because one session fixing the lifecycle fixes both: markets routing is
what makes the symbol resolvable, side casing is what makes the order acceptable, and
neither alone produces a green lifecycle.

Reviewer-observed environmental fact worth confirming, not assuming: the binance SPOT
testnet key reads fine (`fetch_balance` -> :ok) but every write returns `-2015 "Invalid
API-key, IP, or permissions for action"`, which points at a key lacking spot trading
permission rather than a signing defect.

Note 2026-07-17 (merge, update-beats-duplicate): task 294 (orchestrator filing, binance SPOT sandbox fetch_markets dying on the same margin/allPairs wave) is superseded into this task -- same root cause, one implement/review cycle. Its facets carry over: (a) the error names /dapi/v1/... on the SPOT sandbox host although margin/allPairs is a sapi path -- investigate whether sandbox base-URL template resolution maps the sapi section onto a wrong host template; (b) confront CCXT-JS sandboxMode (which market types it fetches in sandbox) before deciding skip-vs-degrade; (c) mainnet public no-arg fetch_markets (12184 rows binance+usdm observed 2026-07-17) must not regress.

task.body:
Convergence continuation of task 293 (reviewer run run-1784225001481-6a1cff20). Task 293
authored the order/trade/balance/position/ADL slices for the binance family and moved the
T-A recorded-response gates from 60/10 to 48/22 (binance) and from 30/4 to 20 passed /
14 failed (binanceusdm), with zero regressions verified by revert-to-parent set-diff. It
did not reach the zero-red criterion; this task owns the residual and is filed append-only
(293 stays untouched).

The remaining reds, clustered by the reviewer from the actual gate output:

- Request-shape `unresolved identifier_reference` raises (the authored-spec fail-loud from
  task 256), which abort the call before any response parsing: binance
  `fetchDepositAddress` param `coin` (8 tests), `withdraw` param `coin`, `fetchOrders`
  param `symbol`, `fetchConvertQuote` param `toAsset`; binanceusdm `fetchOrders`,
  `fetchOpenOrder`, `fetchMarginAdjustmentHistory`, `fetchADLRank` param `symbol`. These
  are request-build gaps that 293 scoped out, but the response slice cannot be proven
  green without them -- author them here.
- `parsed output mismatch` against the CCXT static fixture (22 binance tests): the
  fetchPositions family (linear with/without symbols, account endpoint, inverse),
  fetchOrder/fetchOrders spot, fetchCurrencies, fetchDeposits, fetchWithdrawals,
  fetchBorrowInterest, fetchMarginMode, fetchAllGreeks.
- `expected a map, got: [...]` on the papi balance rows (fetchBalance papi / linear papi)
  -- the portfolio-margin balance payload is a list where the slice expects a map.
- `unsupported nested query param "orders": list items must be scalars (got map)` on
  createOrders / editOrders -- the batch order request needs a JSON body or pre-encoding.
- binanceusdm `fetchPositionADLRank` -> `not_supported`.

Note that `fetchTicker public spot ticker` and `fetchTickers rolling tickers` are also red
and were ALREADY red before 293 (confirmed by the reviewer's revert-to-parent set-diff),
despite tickers nominally landing via 207/227/274 -- adjudicate them here rather than
assuming that chain covered them.

Per docs/authored-specs.md: CCXT-JS and its static fixtures are a tier-2 COMPATIBILITY
oracle, not correctness. For any field CCXT computes or branches rather than copies
(position notional/margin, papi balance aggregation, order cost), confront the carve
against Binance's own API docs and the live testnet and register the outcome in the carve
register. A deliberate divergence is registered as an expected-diff with rationale, never
silently tolerated.

task.title: Base-URL resolution silently rides an arbitrary host when a section has no sandbox URL
acceptance_criteria: A section with no base URL for the active environment fails with an error naming exchange + section + sandbox/mainnet, instead of silently resolving to an unrelated host
Reproduced live: binance sandbox routed to a sapi endpoint returns that explicit error rather than a -5000 for a /dapi/v1/... path it never requested
The nested (Gate/MEXC) and early-stop (BingX) base-URL patterns that find_any_url legitimately serves keep resolving -- pinned by tests
Full offline gate stays green; no previously-green fixture turns red
out_of_scope: Adding testnet hosts to any venue spec
The binance fetch_markets fan-out narrowing already landed in task 296
task.body:
`CCXT.Dispatch.resolve_base_url/2` ends in `navigate_sections(...) || find_any_url(base_urls) || ""`.
When a section has no entry for the current environment, `find_any_url/1` returns the FIRST string
URL anywhere in the map -- an arbitrary sibling section's host -- and the request is sent there.

Reproduced live 2026-07-17 (task 296 review): `binance` with `sandbox: true` resolves no `sapi` and
no `eapiPublic` base (both nil, because Binance publishes no margin/option testnet). A signed sapi
call for `margin/allPairs` therefore rode the coin-margined testnet host and the venue answered
`-5000 "Path /dapi/v1/margin/allPairs, Method GET is invalid"` -- a nonsense path naming a section
the caller never asked for. Task 296 removed the binance fetch_markets manifestation by narrowing the
no-arg fan-out to the surfaces CCXT declares, but the fallback itself is untouched: any other sandbox
call routed to a section without a testnet host still silently targets the wrong venue.

Silent-wrong-host is the failure class this repo's CLAUDE.md says to make LOUD rather than paper over
(see the `path_params` `source` invariant note). Decide the honest contract and encode it: an
unresolvable section should fail with an error naming the exchange, the section, and the environment
-- not fall through to whichever URL happens to sort first. Confront the `find_any_url` fallback
against the base-URL patterns it was actually written for (the nested Gate/MEXC and early-stop BingX
shapes documented in `CCXT.Dispatch`) so the legitimate uses keep working and only the
no-URL-for-this-section case turns loud.

task.body:
Discovered during task 287's full live Deribit catalog comparison. The USDC dated future/option grammar no longer accounts for the raw-symbol population, but 166 live markets still have symbols without a slash. The remaining examples are combo/future-spread instruments such as BTC-FS-17JUL26_PERP and BTC-FS-31JUL26_17JUL26. CCXT-JS 4.5.65 currently also returns these raw symbols, so this is not a task-287 compatibility regression; it is a separate carve decision that the all-market no-slash acceptance criterion made visible.

Do not overfit this as a parser bug before confronting Deribit's own combo semantics. The task is to decide and record whether raw symbols are the intended unified representation for these instruments, or whether ccxt_client should model a richer combo grammar and deliberately diverge/extend.

2026-07-17 (orchestrator): folds task 301 (REV combos raise FunctionClauseError in to_exchange_id — pre-existing, reproduced on the 287 base commit; parse_extended misclassifies the shape as option and :option_ddmmmyy converts the literal "REV" as an expiry). The REV combo carve is confronted against Deribit's own reversal/combo instrument naming (docs.deribit.com), with CCXT-JS 4.5.65 as a compatibility reference only, and the decision (unified grammar vs deliberate raw passthrough) recorded in the docs/authored-specs.md carve register

task.body:
Found by the task 287 reviewer via a live deribit testnet sweep (2026-07-17), and reproduced
on the task 287 BASE commit — this is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by 287.

7 live markets are Deribit REV (reversal) combos, e.g. instrument_name BTC-REV-18JUL26-65000.
They carry market type nil and get a mangled unified symbol that echoes the whole raw id on
both sides of the slash:

  id     => "BTC-REV-18JUL26-65000"
  symbol => "BTC-REV-18JUL26-65000/USD:BTC-REV-18JUL26-65000"

Calling CCXT.Symbol.to_exchange_id/2 on that symbol RAISES rather than returning the id:

  ** (FunctionClauseError) no function clause matching in CCXT.Symbol.convert_date/3
      convert_date("REV", :yymmdd, :ddmmmyy)
      lib/ccxt/symbol.ex:1055: CCXT.Symbol.apply_option_pattern/2

The symbol shape leads parse_extended to classify it as an option, so the :option_ddmmmyy
encoder unconditionally converts the "expiry" segment — which here is the literal "REV".

This is distinct from task 298 (FS combos passing through as RAW symbols): these do NOT pass
through, they produce a mangled symbol AND crash the encoder. Even if 298 decides combos stay
raw, this raise still has to become a graceful passthrough — a dispatch path that raises on a
symbol fetch_markets itself handed the caller is a fail-loud/robustness defect independent of
the combo grammar decision.

Confront Deribit's own combo/reversal naming before choosing between a unified grammar and a
registered deliberate passthrough. Do not paper the raise over with a rescue.

task.title: Symbol.from_exchange_id/3 silently corrupts Deribit combo ids instead of failing loudly

task.body:
Surfaced while gating task 299 (carve C27 — Deribit combo instruments retain native ids).

Task 299 fixed the market read path: CCXT.Unified.ReadParse retains a combo's
instrument_name before the symbol executor is consulted, so fetch_markets is correct.
But CCXT.Symbol.from_exchange_id/3 is public API, and calling it directly with a combo
id returns a plausible-but-wrong string rather than failing:

    from_exchange_id("DOGE_USDC-CS-28AUG26-0d1184_0d12", deribit, :option)
    #=> "DOGE_USDC-CS-28AUG26-0D1184_0D12"   # C24 d-encoded strikes uppercased

Verified live on deribit testnet 2026-07-17: this is a real live instrument, and the
option grammar partially matches the id and rewrites it. The corruption is silent — a
consumer gets a symbol that looks right and resolves to nothing.

This is the "make the day-it-changes failure LOUD" case from CLAUDE.md: an id the
grammar cannot faithfully represent should raise or return an explicit error, not a
mangled string. Decide the right contract for from_exchange_id/3 (and its ! variant)
when the id does not round-trip under the selected pattern — a raise, a tagged error,
or an explicit combo-aware clause — and confront it against Deribit's combo naming
rather than assuming the read-path guard is sufficient.

Do not simply duplicate the ReadParse combo guard into Symbol; the general defect is
that the pattern executor's partial match silently wins over an unrepresentable id.

9. fetch_position: contract_size stays nil for a linear perp; JS sets contractSize 1.

A caller who reads the aligned `add_margin(ex, symbol, amount)` will naturally write
`set_margin(ex, symbol, amount)` and silently ship `amount="BTC/USDT:USDT"`,
`symbol=1` — `maybe_denormalize_symbol/2` no-ops on a non-binary symbol, so nothing
fails client-side. 259's symbol pre-validation clause covers add_margin/reduce_margin
only, so set_margin does not get the fail-fast either.

Confront `set_margin`'s carve against the exchange's own semantics with CCXT as one
reference (CCXT is `setMargin(symbol, amount, params)`), decide ALIGNED or
CONFIRMED-as-ours, and register the outcome in the carve register. If aligned, extend

task.title: T-A/OKX: confront the currency-level fee/precision rollup semantics against a tier-1 oracle
acceptance_criteria: The currency-level `fee` rollup decision is recorded in the carve register with a non-CCXT semantic source (OKX docs or a production-key live call) cited as the oracle — not 'matches CCXT'
The `fee` and `precision` rollups are internally consistent about whether non-withdrawable chains contribute, or the inconsistency is explicitly justified in the carve entry
If the outcome is DIVERGE, a machine-readable contract is registered in divergence_contracts.json so the okx fetchCurrencies fixture case stays gated rather than silently red

other venues' currency rollups
task.body:
Task 277 authored the okx per-chain currency grouping and matched CCXT's currency-level rollups green against the static fixture. That gate is tier-2 (compatibility) only, and the rollup fields are COMPUTED, not key-copied — the exact category CLAUDE.md requires a tier-1 oracle for.

Observed in the recorded raw rows (priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/response/okx.json, fetchCurrencies default, 35 real rows): BTC has 7 chain rows. CCXT rolls the currency-level `fee` up as the MINIMUM across ALL chains, yielding fee = 0 taken from the `BTCK-OKTC` row whose `canWd` is false — i.e. a withdraw fee sourced from a chain you cannot withdraw on. Our authored slice reproduces this because it was authored to match CCXT. Note the same authored slice DOES filter `precision` by `canWd` (via `precision_enabled_key`), so the two rollups are internally inconsistent — evidence the CCXT behavior is incidental rather than intended.

Confront the rollup semantics against the exchange's own meaning (OKX asset/currencies docs and/or a production-key live call — demo answers 50038 per carve C17, so demo cannot verify this). Decide deliberately whether the currency-level `fee` should exclude non-withdrawable chains, and record the outcome (CONFIRMED or DIVERGE) in the carve register with its confrontation evidence.

task.title: Bybit request shapes: positional `params` slot read as a symbol crashes with FunctionClauseError
acceptance_criteria: Each affected bybit request-shape site either routes the positional `params` slot through symbol_param/2 or documents why its slot cannot carry a map
A unit test per fixed site passes an extra-params map in the positional slot and asserts a request map is built (no FunctionClauseError)

The unified methods backed by those sites (cancel_orders, set_position_mode, fetch_order/fetch_open_order/fetch_closed_order) are exercised live or error-compared against ccxt-js on bybit testnet with an extra-params map supplied

Non-bybit request-shape modules
Redesigning the positional params slot convention itself
task.body:
`CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Bybit` reads the positional `params` slot as a symbol with the bare
idiom `params["params"] || params["symbol"]`, then feeds the result to `native_symbol/2`
(guarded `is_binary`). When a caller supplies extra params as a MAP (the documented use of that
slot), the map flows into `native_symbol/2` and raises FunctionClauseError instead of returning
an error tuple or ignoring the map.

The module already has the correct helper — `symbol_param/2` — which only treats the slot as a
symbol when it is a binary containing "/". Two call sites use it; the rest do not.

Affected (verified by reading, 2026-07-17): `cancel_orders/2`, `position_mode_request/2`, and
`order_lookup/3`. Task 306 fixed the same defect in `order_trades_request/2` by routing through
`symbol_param/2`; this task generalizes that fix to the remaining sites.

Reproduced live 2026-07-17 on the (then-unfixed) order-trades path:
`RequestShape.apply(%{"id" => "123", "params" => %{"foo" => "bar"}}, exchange, "fetchOrderTrades")`
raised `FunctionClauseError no function clause matching in
CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Bybit.native_symbol/2`.

Confront each site against the real call signature before changing it: a site whose positional slot
can never carry a map needs no change, and that judgement should be recorded rather than assumed.

acceptance_criteria: fetchTransfers with an extra-params map in the positional slot no longer places that map in the `coin` request key — it either ignores it, merges it, or fails loudly

task.body:
Task 312 routed every bybit symbol path through `symbol_param/2`, so an extra-params map in the
positional `params` slot can no longer crash `native_symbol/2`. Two NON-symbol slots in
`CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Bybit` still read that slot bare, and because they feed `clean/1`
(which only rejects nil) a map survives into the request instead of raising:

- `build_general(params, "fetchTransfers", _)` — `"coin" => params["params"] || params["code"]`
- `build_general(params, "fetchConvertTrade", _)` — `"quoteTxId" => params["id"] || params["params"]`

Same defect family as 312, opposite failure mode: a silent wrong request rather than a
FunctionClauseError, so no crash or existing test surfaces it. `fetch_transfers` declares no
required positional args, which makes the bare read trivially reachable from ordinary opts usage.

Confirmed live on bybit testnet 2026-07-17 (reviewer, run run-1784255176779-2452778f):
`RequestShape.apply(%{"params" => %{"limit" => 5}}, exchange, "fetchTransfers")` returns
`%{"coin" => %{"limit" => 5}}` — the extra-params map lands in the `coin` query slot.

Confront each site against the real call signature and the exchange's own param semantics: decide
whether the positional slot can legitimately carry a value for that key at all, then either guard
it (the way `symbol_param/2` guards the symbol path) or document why the slot is safe. Prefer
failing loudly over building a request with a map-valued query param. Audit the other
request-shape modules for the same bare idiom on non-symbol slots while you are here.

Surfaced while gating task 295 (reviewer, run run-1784255168718-c3503053). Task 276 landed the
detection half of carve-id integrity (uniqueness of register headings + divergence_contracts
carve_id resolution) but left ids hand-typed and left every other reference to an id unchecked.

acceptance_criteria: A live bybit call (api.bybit.com, public, no creds) records lastPrice/volume24h/turnover24h for BOTH category=linear and category=inverse, and the unified vwap produced under the chosen carve is recorded next to each

task.body:
Task 279 registered carve C36 in docs/authored-specs.md as a SCHEMA-LEVEL rule: `vwap` is a
volume-weighted average PRICE, or nil — never contract size or an inverted scale. It implemented
that rule for okx only. bybit still violates it live.

`priv/specs/json/output/authored/bybit.json` maps the unified ticker `vwap` to a blind
`{"op": "div", "operands": ["turnover24h", "volume24h"]}`. For bybit LINEAR that ratio is
quote/base and IS a price. For bybit INVERSE, volume24h is USD contracts and turnover24h is BTC,
so the ratio collapses to ~1/price — not a price by any reading.

Live mainnet evidence, api.bybit.com, 2026-07-17 (reviewer of run run-1784256726499-747eeb91):

    category=linear  BTCUSDT: lastPrice=63473.40  volume24h=56045.9340   turnover24h=3598869742.8282
                     turnover/volume = 64212.86           <- a real VWAP, ~= last. Keep.
    category=inverse BTCUSD:  lastPrice=63409.00  volume24h=224851247.0  turnover24h=3506.4956
                     turnover/volume = 1.559473e-05       <- what we publish as vwap today. Not a price.
                     volume/turnover = 64123.9            <- the notional VWAP for inverse.

The mechanism does NOT transfer from okx: okx's fix used the new payload-gated `kind: "when"`
parser rule because okx ticker ROWS carry `instType`. The bybit v5 ticker row carries NO category
discriminator — `category` lives on the envelope (`result.category`); row keys are
symbol/lastPrice/volume24h/turnover24h/... So this needs either the context-driven
`kind: "discriminated"` rule (market flags already carry inverse/linear) or envelope access.
Confront the carve for bybit rather than porting okx's shape.

Record the outcome by EXTENDING the existing C36 entry — do not mint a parallel carve; C36 is
already the schema-level statement. Check binance COIN-M for the same class while here (C36's
cross-venue table flags `volume` contracts / `baseVolume` base as the same trap), but do not overfit.

task.title: T-A replay harness: load the CCXT static markets/currencies caches the response oracle itself used
acceptance_criteria: priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/{markets,currencies}/<id>.json are vendored for the 7 first-class venues at the same CCXT version as the response fixtures (priv/specs/json/ccxt/js/VERSION, currently 4.5.65), and registered as @external_resource
CCXT.RecordedResponseFixtures.build_exchange!/3 loads the markets + currencies caches into the replay exchange, mirroring CCXT initOfflineExchange

The parse layer can read a real market (at minimum precision.price and contractSize) for the symbol under parse; the symbol-shape-only %{inverse:, linear:} context is no longer the sole market context
binance fetchTicker 'public spot ticker' is green with average == 72775.46, or the tick truncation is registered as a carve with a written Binance-doc rationale for diverging
binance fetchDepositAddress 'with code' resolves currency == USDT from the request argument and network == ERC20 from the currencies contractAddressUrl match, or each is registered as a carve
A test pins that a cache-derived field (ticker average tick truncation) changes when the market precision changes -- proving the cache is actually consulted, not coincidentally matching
No previously-green fixture turns red: deribit (0 failed), bybit (0 failed) and okx (27 failed) gate counts are unchanged or improved

The live order lifecycle blockers (task 296)
The long-tail catalog -- first-class venues only
task.body:
Root cause found while gating task 297 (reviewer run run-1784260456631-141e0ea1). A large
fraction of the residual T-A recorded-response reds are NOT slice-authoring gaps -- they are one
harness gap, and every future "author the residual slice" task will hit this same wall until it
is closed.

CCXT's own static-response driver (ts/src/test/tests.ts -> initOfflineExchange) builds the replay
exchange as:

    const markets = this.loadMarketsFromFile (exchangeName);        // ts/src/test/static/markets/<id>.json
    const currencies = this.loadCurrenciesFromFile (exchangeName);  // ts/src/test/static/currencies/<id>.json
    const exchange = initExchange (exchangeName, { 'markets': markets, 'currencies': currencies, ... });
    exchange.currencies = currencies;

So every parsedResponse in our vendored fixtures was produced by an exchange WITH a loaded markets
+ currencies cache. Our CCXT.RecordedResponseFixtures.build_exchange!/3 builds an Exchange.new!/2
with credentials and options only -- no markets, no currencies. We vendored only static/request and
static/response; static/markets/ and static/currencies/ were never vendored (they ship in the CCXT
git repo, not the npm package).

Consequence: any oracle field CCXT derives from that cache is unmatchable by construction, and
looks like a slice bug. Two confirmed instances, both traced to ground truth:

  * binance fetchTicker "public spot ticker" -- the ONLY diff is average: oracle 72775.46 vs ours
    72775.465. Exchange.safeTicker computes average = Precise.stringDiv(stringAdd(open, close),
    '2', precision) where precision is 18 UNLESS market !== undefined && this.isTickPrecision(),
    in which case it is precisionFromString(market.precision.price). static/markets/binance.json
    gives BTC/USDT precision.price = 0.01 -> precision 2 -> stringDiv(145550.93, 2, 2) = 72775.46
    exactly. With no market we take the precision-18 path and publish the un-tick-truncated value.

  * binance fetchDepositAddress (4 cases) -- currency and network are both cache-derived.
    parseDepositAddress reads safeCurrencyCode(response['currency'], currency); the payload has no
    "currency" key (it carries "coin"), so CCXT falls back to the REQUESTED currency argument.
    network comes from getNetworkCodeByNetworkUrl(code, url), which scans
    currency.networks[*].info.contractAddressUrl and startsWith-matches the deposit url.
    static/currencies/binance.json gives USDT.networks.ERC20.info.contractAddressUrl =
    "https://etherscan.io/address/", and the fixture url is https://etherscan.io/address/0x437ef...
    -> "ERC20", exactly the oracle value.

The same cache dependency is expected to reach the fetchPositions family (contractSize), order
cost/amount precision, and the fetchAllGreeks/fetchTickers symbol-keyed reads.

Decide and implement the carve deliberately -- this is a schema/architecture decision, not a
mechanical port. The open question is whether tick-truncating a derived statistic like ticker
average is CORRECT (a price that cannot exist on a 0.01-tick market) or merely CCXT-COMPATIBLE.
Per docs/authored-specs.md a CCXT-derived value is a tier-2 compatibility oracle at best; confront
average and the depositAddress network derivation against Binance's own API docs and the live
testnet before adopting CCXT's shape, and register the outcome in the carve register.

Scope note: vendoring the fixtures is the cheap half. The load-bearing half is deciding whether
CCXT.Exchange grows a markets/currencies cache that the parse layer can consult at all -- today the
only market context that reaches CCXT.ResponseParser is %{inverse: bool, linear: bool}, inferred
from the symbol shape (read_parse.ex:980). There is no real market cache to read precision from.

Two things to settle, not one:

network derivation -- coordinate so the two do not author conflicting network-code carves.

task.body:
Split out of task 297's residual (reviewer run run-1784260456631-141e0ea1).

Task 297's acceptance criterion asserted that createOrders/editOrders should "encode the orders
list per Binance's documented shape (JSON body)". THAT CRITERION IS FACTUALLY WRONG and must not
be carried forward -- the observed wire shape is a JSON-encoded string carried in a QUERY param.

Ground truth, from the vendored CCXT static request fixture
(priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/request/binance.json, methods.createOrders[0].output):

    timestamp=1699382693405&batchOrders=[{"symbol":"LTCUSDT","side":"BUY",
    "newClientOrderId":"x-xcKtGhcub371e14dda9e4fda804421","newOrderRespType":"RESULT",
    "type":"LIMIT","quantity":"0.1","price":"60","timeInForce":"GTC"},{...}]
    &recvWindow=10000&signature=...

    url: https://testnet.binancefuture.com/fapi/v1/batchOrders

Confirm this against Binance's own USD-M futures docs for POST /fapi/v1/batchOrders (the
batchOrders parameter is documented as a LIST<JSON> sent as a request parameter) before authoring
-- the fixture is a tier-2 compatibility oracle, the doc is the semantic authority.

Today both methods abort at request build with:

    unsupported nested query param "orders": list items must be scalars (got map).
    Use a JSON body or pre-encode the value; ...

task.body:
Task 318 gave the T-A replay exchange the static markets/currencies caches CCXT's own
offline driver uses. To keep the oracle's input byte-faithful,
`CCXT.RecordedResponseFixtures.build_exchange!/3` writes CCXT's RAW market maps (string
keys: "symbol", "precision", "contractSize") into `%CCXT.Exchange{markets:}` via
`Map.put/3` -- but that field is declared `[CCXT.Market.t()] | nil` and is populated
everywhere else by `CCXT.load_markets/1` / `Exchange.put_markets/2` with real
`%CCXT.Market{}` structs.

Nothing is broken today: the only parse-layer reader (`ReadParse.market_context/2`)
accepts both shapes, and the one struct-shaped reader (`Unified.resolve_market_id_param`,
lighter `market_id` dynamic_construction) is unreachable for the seven first-class replay
venues. It is a landmine, not a live defect: the next reader that pattern-matches
`%CCXT.Market{}` on `exchange.markets` will work in production and break only under
replay -- or worse, read a raw map by atom key and silently get nil.

Decide the carve deliberately rather than mechanically converting. Either (a) give the
replay cache its own typed home so `:markets` keeps its struct contract, (b) widen the
declared type to the union both readers already accept and say so, or (c) convert the raw
maps to `%CCXT.Market{}` at load -- but (c) must prove the round-trip is lossless for the
fields the oracle actually consumed (`precision.price`, `contractSize`), since a lossy
conversion silently re-opens the exact unmatchable-oracle-field class task 318 closed.

Documented inline at `lib/ccxt/recorded_response_fixtures.ex` (`build_exchange!/3`
moduledoc warning), which should be removed/updated by whichever option lands.

task.title: Gate the T-A fixture-replay suite against a frozen failing-name baseline
acceptance_criteria: A single command reports fixture-replay failures absent from the committed baseline, exiting non-zero only for those
The committed baseline reflects the current base-branch failing set and is regenerable by a documented command
Adding an additive field to a unified struct is shown to fail the new check (reproduce the task 316 Position regression)

Adding fixture_replay to the default mix check.dispatch test run
task.body:
`mix check.dispatch` excludes the `fixture_replay` tag, so the T-A static fixture gate never runs in the per-run harness check. A change to a unified struct's field set can therefore regress fixtures across every venue while the dispatch check stays green.

Observed on the task 316 reviewer seat (2026-07-17): adding four additive fields to `%CCXT.Position{}` turned 8 previously-green position fixtures red (7 bybit, 1 deribit) because `do_equivalent/3` requires key-set equality and CCXT's golden carries no such key. `mix check.dispatch` passed (2787 tests, 0 failures) throughout; the regression only surfaced from a manual base-diff of the failing-name set.

The suite cannot simply be added to the gate: it is ~103/251 red on the base branch (known open defects). The invariant to encode is therefore delta-based, not absolute: freeze the expected failing-name set as a committed baseline artifact, and fail when a name appears that is not in the baseline. A newly-green name should prompt a baseline update, not a failure. Make it one command so a per-task reviewer can check "no fixture regressed" without hand-diffing two runs.

Per CLAUDE.md's rule that whole-surface invariants become CI failures rather than consumer discoveries.

acceptance_criteria: A successful hyperliquid transfer ack no longer surfaces as {:error, ...} — the unified transfer call returns {:ok, _} for {"status":"ok","response":{"type":"default"}}
The chosen return carve is justified against a NON-CCXT semantic source (hyperliquid API docs or official SDK), cited by URL — a CCXT fixture alone is not sufficient evidence

task.body:
Found by the reviewer of run run-1784267412270-bec119fb (task 328), 2026-07-17, on the landed base.

Hyperliquid's transfer endpoint answers a SUCCESSFUL transfer with a bare ack:

    {"status": "ok", "response": {"type": "default"}}

Our `:parse_transfer` read path maps that ack to an all-nil `%CCXT.TransferEntry{}`
(only `info` populated), which trips the read-path guard and returns
`{:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :exchange_error, message: "Unexpected response shape: parsed to an all-nil struct"}}`.
A successful transfer is therefore reported to the caller as a failure — the caller
cannot distinguish "transfer succeeded" from "transfer failed", which for a
money-moving call is the dangerous direction.

Reproduce (in-worktree; `mix run`, not tidewave):

    body = %{"status" => "ok", "response" => %{"type" => "default"}}
    ex = CCXT.RecordedResponseFixtures.build_exchange!("hyperliquid", %{})
    params = CCXT.RecordedResponseFixtures.params_from_input(:transfer, ["USDC", 5, "swap", "spot"])
    CCXT.Unified.ReadParse.parse(ex, ex.module, :transfer, "transfer", body, params, :parse_transfer, false)
    #=> {:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :exchange_error, message: "Unexpected response shape: parsed to an all-nil struct", ...}}

This is a CARVE question, not a field-map gap, which is why neither task 302
(response field-maps) nor task 328 (the response-gate seam) can reach it: the
exchange does not return TransferEntry-shaped data at all, so no field-map can
populate those slots. Decide what our `transfer` returns for a venue whose ack
carries no transfer detail — echo the request context (currency/amount/from/to)
into the entry with `status` derived from the ack, return the raw ack, or return
`{:ok, TransferEntry}` with only `status`/`info` set.

Per docs/authored-specs.md this needs a TIER-1 confrontation: hyperliquid's own API
docs / official SDK for the transfer-return semantics, plus a live testnet transfer
(HYPERLIQUID_TESTNET_API_KEY/SECRET are provisioned; the account is drip-funded).
CCXT's static fixture is tier-2 here and records `parsedResponse == httpResponse` —
it cannot tell you what the value MEANS. Register the outcome in the carve register
(task 181) as CONFIRMED or DIVERGE.

The two response-gate cases are held out of the replay gate by
`CCXT.Test.Generator.RecordedResponseReplay.response_exclusion/2`; if this task makes
them assertable, remove that exclusion entry and let them back into the gate.

2026-07-17: superseded — folded into task 331 (same hyperliquid transfer wire path; the
live-transfer evidence requires 331's :action builder, so one session lands both halves).

task.body:
Found by the reviewer of run run-1784267412270-bec119fb (task 328), 2026-07-17, on the landed base.

Task 328 established the seam: the `Hyperliquid signing requires :action in request params`
precondition is owned by the REQUEST-build/signing gate, not the response gate. This task
is that named owner — measured, it is red in exactly one place:

    mix test.json --quiet --include fixture_replay test/ccxt/signing_fixture_replay_test.exs
    # 9 cases fail with: Hyperliquid signing requires :action in request params

All 9 live in `test/ccxt/signing_fixture_replay_test.exs`; ZERO appear in the response gate
(confirmed by the reviewer's file-scoped breakdown). The failing set spans 5 methods, so this
is a request-build defect class rather than a transfer-specific quirk:

    hyperliquid cancelOrder    cancel order #1037, cancel hip3 order #1039
    hyperliquid cancelOrders   #1040
    hyperliquid createOrders   create limit orders #1077
    hyperliquid fetchCurrencies #1087
    hyperliquid transfer       spot->swap #1138, swap->spot #1139,
                               main->subaccount #1140, subaccount->main #1141

`CCXT.Signing.Hyperliquid` requires a caller-supplied `:action` in request params. CCXT JS
does not require its caller to pass an `action` — hyperliquid's `sign()` BUILDS the action
object from the method + args (an msgpack-serialized L1 action for order/cancel paths, a
user-signed action for transfer/withdraw paths) and then signs it. Our seam pushes that
construction onto the caller, so every fixture case that does not hand-feed `:action` cannot
sign at all.

Decide and implement the correct seam: the request builder should construct `:action` from
the unified method + params (mirroring hyperliquid's own action schema), leaving
`CCXT.Signing.Hyperliquid` to sign an action it is given. Confirm whether `:action` should
remain an accepted override for callers driving raw endpoints.

Authority: hyperliquid's own API docs / official SDK for the action schema per method
(tier-1); CCXT JS `sign()` is one reference, not the arbiter. The request static fixtures
(priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/request/hyperliquid.json) are the tier-2 gate that
pins byte-equality once the builder exists.

--- Absorbed from task 330 (superseded into this task 2026-07-17; coupling: the live
transfer evidence below REQUIRES this task's :action builder, and both halves sit on the
same transfer wire path — one session, one reviewer, one diff) ---

Hyperliquid answers a SUCCESSFUL transfer with a bare ack:

    {"status": "ok", "response": {"type": "default"}}

Our `:parse_transfer` read path maps that ack to an all-nil `%CCXT.TransferEntry{}` (only
`info` populated), trips the read-path all-nil guard, and returns
`{:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :exchange_error, message: "Unexpected response shape: parsed to an all-nil struct"}}`
— a successful money-moving call reported as a failure, the dangerous direction.

This half is a CARVE question, not a field-map gap: the venue returns no
TransferEntry-shaped data, so no field-map can populate the slots. Decide what our
`transfer` returns for an ack-only venue — echo the request context (currency/amount/
from/to) into the entry with `status` derived from the ack, or return `{:ok, TransferEntry}`
with only `status`/`info` set. Justify against hyperliquid's own docs/SDK (tier-1), then
prove it with ONE live testnet transfer (HYPERLIQUID_TESTNET_API_KEY/SECRET provisioned,
drip-funded account; spot->swap on our own account, reverse it in the same session).
Register CONFIRMED or DIVERGE in the carve register (task 181 shape).

The two response-gate transfer cases are currently held out via
`CCXT.Test.Generator.RecordedResponseReplay.response_exclusion/2` (task 328); if this task
makes them assertable, remove the exclusion entries and let them back into the gate.

task.title: Fix Hyperliquid L1 msgpack action field ordering
acceptance_criteria: The msgpack field order for every supported L1 action type is justified against Hyperliquid's official docs or SDK

task.body:
Found by the reviewer of run run-1784275482789-1cfca3d3 (task 331), 2026-07-17, with live
testnet evidence.

`CCXT.Signing.Hyperliquid.action_hash/4` msgpack-packs the L1 action with `Msgpax.pack!`
on a plain Elixir map. Hyperliquid's L1 signature is computed over msgpack bytes whose
FIELD ORDER must match the venue's own struct order (the server re-serializes and recovers
the signer). Elixir maps do not carry insertion order — Erlang flatmaps store keys in term
order and Msgpax emits them in REVERSE term order — so our bytes differ from the venue's
whenever reverse-alphabetical order != the venue's field order.

The module's `## Key ordering` moduledoc asserts "Elixir preserves insertion order for the
small maps these actions use". That is FALSE and is the root of the bug.

It survived because the only parity vectors in the suite happen to be order-immune:
`%{"type","orders","grouping"}` reverse-term-orders to exactly the JS insertion order. The
cancel row `%{"a","o"}` and the order row `%{"a","b","p","s","r","t"}` do NOT (they emit
`o,a` and `t,s,r,p,b,a`). The static request fixtures cannot catch it either — signature
is in `skipKeys`, so the tier-2 gate is green on a wrong signature.

Fix direction: make the L1 action packing order-explicit rather than map-iteration-derived
(e.g. author a per-action-type field order and pack via pre-ordered `Msgpax.Fragment`s, or
an ordered encoder). Author the order from hyperliquid's own docs/SDK, then prove each
action type live. Delete the false insertion-order claim from the moduledoc.

Task 339 supplies the live asset index and lands first. This task owns only the critical
signing seam: explicit per-action msgpack order, fail-loud action dispatch, coverage and
the live venue signature check.

Task 331 landed `CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Hyperliquid`, which resolves an L1 action's

market maps carry `baseId` = the asset index — but NOT live: `CCXT.load_markets/1` against

`base_id: nil` for every market (210 markets, verified live), so:

    CCXT.cancel_order(ex, "1", symbol: "BTC/USDC:USDC")
    ** (ArgumentError) hyperliquid action build: expected integer, got nil
        (ccxt_client) lib/ccxt/unified/request_shape/hyperliquid.ex:407: parse_int!/1
        (ccxt_client) lib/ccxt/unified/request_shape/hyperliquid.ex:82: build_cancel/5

The asset index is the position in the `universe` array from `/info {"type":"meta"}` (perps)
and `{"type":"spotMeta"}` (spot) — the live payload carries it, our fetchMarkets field-map
drops it. This is the fetchMarkets field-map gap (adjacent to task 302), surfaced as a hard
raise on the write path rather than a missing read field.

The implementation decision is explicit: add a dedicated `Market.asset_index` field.
Do not overload `id` or `base_id`; their existing market-identity semantics differ from
the venue's numeric signing index. Record this as a deliberate divergence from CCXT.

2026-07-17 correction: kept separate from task 338 because live-market parsing and
critical msgpack signing are independently reviewable seams. This task lands first;
task 338 consumes its asset-index result for live signing evidence.
