task.title: Hyperliquid order size/price string passthrough breaks the L1 signature (non-canonical wire format)
acceptance_criteria: A hyperliquid order with a non-canonical size string (e.g. 0.00020) produces the same L1 signature as the numeric-equivalent 0.0002 and reaches the venue with a recoverable signer
An offline unit test pins number_string wire canonicalization: trailing-zero and integer-valued strings normalize to hyperliquid's wire form
No silent wrong-signature path remains: a non-canonical numeric string is either canonicalized or rejected before signing

task.body: CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Hyperliquid.number_string/1 normalizes float and Decimal inputs through Decimal.normalize (stripping trailing zeros), but passes BINARY inputs through verbatim. Hyperliquid's server re-serializes the L1 action canonically (trailing zeros stripped) to recompute the EIP-712 connectionId; if the caller passed a non-canonical size/price string (e.g. amount '0.00020'), the signature is over different bytes than the venue reconstructs, so the recovered signer is garbage and the venue rejects with HTTP 200 status:err 'User or API Wallet 0x... does not exist.' — the exact signer-mismatch class that historically looked like an unregistered wallet. Observed live 2026-07-18 (testnet): create_orders with amount '0.00020' (string) -> signer recovered 0x59aa...3cae (not the real wallet 0x9fb7...3ff2) -> 'does not exist'; the identical order with amount 0.0002 (float, normalized by number_string) filled cleanly. Fix: canonicalize string number inputs to hyperliquid's wire form (route binaries through the same Decimal-normalize path) before msgpack packing, so a caller-supplied pre-formatted string cannot silently produce an unrecoverable signature. Confront against CCXT JS floatToWire / size-decimals rules; the failure is silent and signing-critical — a wrong format must be normalized or fail loudly, never signed as-is.

task.body:
Live finding 2026-07-18 (binance spot testnet, post-task-340 routing fix): CCXT.fetch_tickers(binance, symbols: ["BTC/USDT", "ETH/USDT"]) routes to the correct spot endpoint but returns 1373 rows keyed by MIS-normalized symbols — 894 of 1373 keys carry a settle suffix on a SPOT read ("BTCUSDT" -> "BTC/USDT:USDT", "BTCEUR" -> "BTC/EUR:EUR", and "BTCUSD" -> "BTC/USD:BTC" inverse-style), the rest pass through raw ("BTCARS", "BTCEURI"). The requested keys "BTC/USDT"/"ETH/USDT" are absent, so the caller cannot look up what they asked for. Singular fetch_ticker("BTC/USDT") is correct (echoes the request symbol); the defect is the multi-row response path, which classifies each raw id per-symbol-pattern without the endpoint's resolved market family — binance spot ids are ambiguous against the perp grammar, so the swap pattern wins.

Root-cause direction (verify, do not assume): thread the resolved market family / endpoint context of the call into multi-row response symbol denormalization so a spot endpoint's rows are classified as spot, instead of guessing per id. Confront against CCXT-JS parseTickers (which keys by market lookup, not pattern-guess) as compatibility reference and Binance's own exchangeInfo as the semantic source. If the fix is a general mechanism (market-family threading), verify okx/bybit multi-row reads do not regress.

Secondary contract fact (same method, same session): the symbols plural param is not sent server-side — the venue returns the full catalog (1373 rows) for a 2-symbol request. CCXT-JS binance sends symbols as a JSON-array query param. Fixing the keying is the hard requirement; server-side filtering is the natural companion while in the same code.

task.body:
Uncovered while reviewing task 356 (Binance spot multi-row ticker keying). The CCXT static
fixture `binanceusdm fetchTickers Inverse tickers` (cases #673 / #1001) is RED on the current
development base — reproduced with ALL of task 356's code reverted, so it is not caused by 356.
It was introduced by task 340 ("Unified endpoint selection ignores params symbols (plural) —
binance fetch_tickers routes to COIN-M dapi"), which landed with a stale fixture-replay baseline
(last refreshed for task 347, before 340). Task 356's reviewer added these two names to
test/fixtures/fixture_replay_failures.json to keep the delta-gate honest; this task FIXES the
underlying keying and then shrinks the baseline back.

Defect class: binanceusdm COIN-M (inverse) multi-row ticker reads mis-key their unified symbols.
Task 356 fixed the binance-SPOT analog (compact ids colliding with the perp grammar) by threading
the resolved endpoint family into response symbol denormalization, scoped to exchange.id ==
"binance" spot only. The COIN-M inverse path on binanceusdm is a distinct family (dapi / inverse
settlement) and needs its own confrontation: determine the correct unified key for an inverse
COIN-M ticker row and make the response keying produce it, WITHOUT re-introducing the
bybit/binanceusdm-linear regressions the generic section-name mechanism caused (carve C-T356 in
docs/authored-specs.md explains why section-name-only keying is unsound — public/v1 are shared
across venues and families).

Reality source (authority: live API > docs > CCXT-JS > assumptions): live binanceusdm COIN-M
testnet (testnet.binancefuture.com, /dapi/v1/ticker/24hr + /dapi/v1/exchangeInfo as the tier-1
semantic source); CCXT-JS binanceusdm parseTickers as tier-2 compatibility only; the static
fixture as the offline regression oracle.

2026-07-18 orchestrator live evidence (binanceusdm testnet, post-356 land): the keying class is
broader than COIN-M — linear fetch_tickers keys the dated future ETHUSDT_251226 by its RAW id
(every perpetual keys correctly as BASE/QUOTE:SETTLE). Same root cause family: ids outside the
perp grammar fall through symbol resolution. AC added above. Separately OBSERVED, explicitly NOT
this task's scope unless it falls out of the same seam: binanceusdm fetch_tickers(symbols: [..])
returns the FULL catalog (~500 rows) — the symbols filter is neither sent server-side nor applied
client-side (binance spot filters correctly post-356; CCXT-JS filters client-side via
filterByArray). If untouched here, file it as its own task at completion.

task.body:
Split out of task 366 at completion (366 fixed the COIN-M inverse / dated-future
KEYING seam; the symbols FILTER is a distinct seam and was left untouched).

Defect class: for binanceusdm, a caller-supplied `symbols` list on a multi-row
ticker read is neither sent server-side nor applied client-side, so the caller
gets the entire catalog back instead of the rows requested. Binance spot filters
correctly (task 356 wired the server-side `symbols` query param there), so this
is a per-venue gap in the same unified read path, not a missing capability.

Confirm the correct mechanism against reality before choosing one: Binance's
fapi/dapi `/ticker/24hr` may not accept a `symbols` array the way spot's
`/api/v3/ticker/24hr` does — if the venue has no server-side filter, the fix is a
client-side filter over the parsed rows (CCXT-JS does this via `filterByArray`).
Prefer whichever the live endpoint actually supports; do not assume parity with
spot.

Re-generalize rather than special-casing binanceusdm: check whether other venues
in the compiled set drop `symbols` on multi-row reads and fix the shared seam if
the defect is not venue-local.

acceptance_criteria: Live derive testnet (DERIVE_TESTNET_* env, api-demo.lyra.finance): public_post_get_time and private-path zero-param POSTs return the venue result (no -32700), matching ccxt-js output
A unit test pins that a zero-param POST on a JSON-body venue produces body {} (and that the signed path signs exactly the sent body); GET/query-param requests remain body-less

task.body: Live derive sweep 2026-07-18: when `params == %{}`, both the unsigned path (`CCXT.HTTP.build_request/5`, http.ex ~225: `body = if params == %{}, do: nil, else: encode`) and the signed path (`CCXT.Dispatch.prepare_signed_payload/3`) omit the request body entirely. Venues whose endpoints require a JSON body on every POST (derive: all-POST JSON-RPC style) reject the bodyless request with -32700 Parse error, while ccxt-js sends the literal `{}` and succeeds with real data. 11 derive endpoints live-verified red on our side / green on JS (get_time, get_all_currencies, get_latest_signed_feeds, get_liquidation_history, get_live_incidents, get_maker_programs, get_maker_program_scores, get_bridge_balances, get_vault_assets, get_vault_balances, get_vault_statistics); retry-proof: the same endpoint with one param succeeds identically on both sides. Also the transport half of derive unified fetch_markets failing (spec side tracked separately). Fix the general class: a POST/PUT/PATCH whose venue carries body-typed params must send an empty JSON object body when params are empty, not omit the body — confront how ccxt-js decides (it sends "{}" for implicit POST calls) and keep GET query behavior unchanged. Watch both code sites; the signed path must sign the body it actually sends.

task.body: Live testnet sweep 2026-07-18 (vs ccxt-js 4.5.65) found the hyperliquid unified read layer red beyond task 302's fixture-gate coverage (302 closed the recorded-response gate; these methods have no recorded fixtures, so the gate stayed green while live reads are broken): fetch_markets returns 210 swap-only rows with type/spot/swap/contract/active/id/quote/settle/base_id/quote_id/taker/maker/contract_size/precision.price ALL nil (JS: 1479 fully populated, 1252 spot + 227 swap); fetch_spot_markets and fetch_swap_markets CRASH with no-function-clause in CCXT.Unified.ReadParse.backfill_market_symbol/3; fetch_currencies raises 'Missing authored normalization.field_maps.currency slice'; fetch_tickers and fetch_funding_rates return {} where JS returns fully-populated symbol-keyed maps; fetch_ledger parses every semantic field nil (amount/currency/direction/fee/type/status); fetch_order_book omits the top-level symbol. Author the missing normalization slices per hyperliquid's own /info semantics (exchange docs are the authority, CCXT one reference), fix the backfill crash, and wire the error sentinel: the bare-body {"status":"unknownOid"} response must map to :order_not_found (spec errors.handle_errors.exceptions.exact is currently empty; JS raises typed OrderNotFound). Note the asymmetry to preserve: currencies raises loudly, most other slices silently no-op — silent field loss is the worse failure mode; missing slices should fail loud per the 237/256 convention.

task.title: Determine zero-param JSON body semantics across gated signing venues
acceptance_criteria: Enumerate the vendored venues whose body_encoding is json and whose current sign() gates the body on non-empty params, with source file:line evidence and the exact audited venue set

For at least two gated venues with usable credentials, live-exercise a zero-param signed POST both with and without a {} body and record the venue's actual response for each; when credentials are unavailable, record the exact missing variables and a durable production-verification-ledger entry rather than silently dropping the venue
If any venue rejects the {} body, the contract gains an authored value distinguishing always-json from json-when-present, set from observed behavior — not from an exchange id conditional
If no reachable venue rejects it, record that bounded finding and retain ledger entries for every unreachable authority rather than claiming catalog-wide proof

Response-side empty-body handling (task 255)
task.body:
Task 369 made a POST/PUT/PATCH on a venue whose request contract carries
body_encoding "json" always send a JSON body, emitting {} when params are empty.
That is correct for derive and hyperliquid, whose ccxt-js sign() does an
unconditional body = this.json(params) (verified in ccxt 4.5.57
js/src/derive.js:2645), and it is live-verified against api-demo.lyra.finance:
a bodyless POST returns -32700 Parse error, {} returns the result.

But body_encoding is a per-section contract meaning "when this section sends a
body, it is JSON" — it does not record whether the venue's ccxt-js sign() gates
the body on non-empty params. Roughly 70 vendored specs carry
body_encoding "json", and several gate it: ccxt 4.5.57 js/src/kucoin.js wraps
body = this.json(query) in if (!this.isEmpty(query)), so ccxt-js sends NO
body for a zero-param signed POST there while we now send and sign {}.

The signature stays self-consistent (we sign exactly what we send), so this is
not an auth break, and no fixture regressed (T-A gate delta was a single
newly-green derive fixture). The open question is whether any long-tail venue
rejects an unexpected {} body on a zero-param POST. Establish whether the
gating behavior needs to be a distinct authored contract value (e.g.
json_when_present vs json_always) rather than inferred, and back the answer
with live evidence rather than a read of ccxt-js.

Do not fix this by exchange-id string matching — the rule must stay contract-derived.

task.body:
An authored spec file with a duplicate top-level key silently loses a whole slice: the JSON decoder keeps one occurrence and the other is dropped with no warning. Observed during task 372's review — priv/specs/json/output/authored/derive.json was committed with two top-level `endpoints` blocks; the decoder kept the newly-added {handlers} block and silently discarded the pre-existing {request: {defaults}} slice, which held the instrument_name/wallet request mappings for fetchTicker/fetchTrades/fetchFundingRate/fetchBalance/cancelOrder.

Nothing in the loader caught it. The failure surfaced far from its cause as 8 red fixture-replay cases plus a request-shape unit failure, and was initially misattributed to unrelated pre-existing breakage. Any authored venue file is exposed to the same class.

Make the spec loader reject duplicate keys at load time, naming the offending file and key, so this is a loud load-time failure rather than a silent slice loss discovered downstream. Encode it as an assertion/CI check covering every authored spec file, not just the venue that happened to hit it.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): both Jason.decode!/1 and OTP :json keep the FIRST occurrence of a duplicate key (verified live: ~s({"a":1,"a":2}) -> %{"a" => 1}) — so in the derive incident the newly-added block survived and the pre-existing slice was dropped; the author should know first-wins is what survives. Neither decoder has a dup-detection knob, so the check needs a callback-based re-parse (e.g. OTP :json object_push) or equivalent. Scope decision for the implementer: the base priv/specs/json/output/*.json files ride the same decode path — cover them in the repo-wide check too (lower risk, machine-frozen, but same silent-loss class) or record explicitly why not. A jq --stream scan on 2026-07-18 found zero real duplicate key paths across all 8 authored files, so the regression fixture must be dedicated (AC 3 stands).

task.title: Audit and implement safeTimestamp coercion across the current catalog
acceptance_criteria: Before implementation, the merged runtime rule set is re-measured and the completion record reports the current safeTimestamp count and format distribution; stale filed counts are not reused
Every runtime field rule tagged safeTimestamp is resolved to behavior matching the venue's documented resolution for that field, with the venue authority named per rule
Parser-level tests pin seconds-to-milliseconds behavior, already-millisecond behavior and an unresolved-format failure that would catch the current passthrough
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate reports no regressions and any newly-green fixtures are committed as a shrunk baseline
Rules that cannot be resolved from venue documentation fail or remain explicitly ledgered rather than being silently scaled
out_of_scope: The binance epochMsOrDatetime coercion authored in task 335
Re-authoring unrelated slices of the affected specs
task.body:
`CCXT.ResponseParser.coerce/2` has no clause for the `safeTimestamp` coercion, so
every field rule tagged with it falls through to the passthrough clause and the
raw venue value is emitted unchanged. In CCXT, `safeTimestamp` means seconds ->
milliseconds; the x1000 happens nowhere in this codebase. `format` does NOT
supply it — `format_value/2` handles only `"hours"` and `"funding_interval"` and
returns every other value untouched, so `"format": "s"` is a descriptive
annotation with no runtime effect.

Surfaced while reviewing task 335 (harness run run-1784359761235-2fef9e29). That
task's binance capital-history slot needed an epoch-ms-or-datetime coercion and
was initially authored as `safeTimestamp`; it was renamed to `epochMsOrDatetime`
precisely so this gap stays visible instead of looking handled.

48 field rules across the catalog carry `"coercion": "safeTimestamp"`, the large
majority with second-resolution sources — e.g. kraken `order.timestamp` (`opentm`),
kraken `trade`/`transaction` (`time`), gate `transaction.timestamp`, indodax
`balance`/`ticker` (`server_time`), coincheck, bit2c, mercado, btcbox, coinmate,
whitebit `transaction.createdAt`, deepcoin `transaction.createTime`. Each emits a
value ~1000x too small for a ms slot, which silently dates every affected record
to 1970.

Confront each site against the venue's own docs before scaling: the coercion name
came from CCXT, so some rules may be mistagged and actually carry ms sources
(several already declare `"format": "ms"`). Decide per rule whether the fix is
the x1000, a retag to `safeInteger`, or a retag to `epochMsOrDatetime`; do not
blanket-multiply. Where a rule's source resolution cannot be established from
venue docs, say so rather than guessing.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): measured format distribution over the 48 safeTimestamp rules: 32 format 's', 11 'ms', 5 null — the 11 ms-format rules (gate liquidation/open_interest/settlement, whitebit funding_rate_history, deribit transfer created_timestamp, ...) are the do-not-blanket-multiply set. Live pinned evidence: indodax fetch_ticker returns timestamp 1784375095 with datetime 1970-01-21T15:39:35.095Z — raw seconds in the ms slot.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784416712681-b140824d, 4a984d2957a4c8694c7d319786fbe45917473f37).

inverse unified-symbol keying for `fetch_tickers` only; the same defect class is still open on
the other multi-row COIN-M reads, which key rows with the RAW exchange id instead of a unified
symbol.

    -> 40 rows keyed "SOLUSD_261225", "ETHUSD_260925", "ETHUSD_261225"   (raw dapi ids)

    CCXT.fetch_funding_rates(ex)                       # linear control

The linear control proves the parse path normalizes correctly for fapi; only the COIN-M family
is unkeyed. This is a parse/normalization gap, independent of endpoint selection — task 373
changed only `select_endpoint` and did not introduce it (pre-373 the inverse path already
reached dapi via the `hd(configs)` fall-through, since `infer_market_type` never read
`subType`).

Generalize rather than patching `fetch_funding_rates` alone: audit the multi-row COIN-M read
surface for the same keying class and fix it where the symbol is resolved, reusing the task-366
inverse grammar rather than adding a per-method branch. Confirm the dated-future grammar
(SOLUSD_261225 -> the unified dated inverse form) against /dapi/v1/exchangeInfo instrument
identity, with CCXT-JS as a tier-2 reference only.

2026-07-18 orchestrator live evidence (post-373 land, no-arg run): the linear control is NOT
fully clean — 59 of 728 fapi rows also key raw: linear dated futures (ETHUSDT_251226,
ETHUSDT_260925, BTCUSDT_250926, ...) and an index-style BTCUSD1. The defect class is
"dated/non-perp rows bypass symbol normalization on multi-row reads", not COIN-M-only —
fix both families where the symbol is resolved. BTCUSD1 has no obvious unified form;
list it explicitly if unmappable rather than silently passing it through.

REVIEW (2026-07-19, fresh live testnet verification): the inverse call still returns 40/40
raw keys, including perpetual rows such as FILUSD_PERP and ADAUSD_PERP as well as dated rows.
The no-arg linear call returns 728 rows; perpetual rows remain unified, while 20 keys are raw
dated/index-style identifiers in the current snapshot. Scope therefore includes the entire
inverse family plus dated/index-style linear rows, not dated rows alone.

task.title: Authored per-venue default-family spec slot — retire the venue-local hd(configs) clauses in CCXT.Unified
acceptance_criteria: A venue-level authored default-family slot exists in the owned schema and is honored by endpoint selection; no first-class venue default remains a hardcoded atom list in CCXT.Unified
All seven first-class venues are audited for multi-endpoint no-arg reads; every affected pair receives an authored default or a loud named failure when no default is semantically valid

The binanceusdm venue-local clauses added by tasks 368/373 are removed, and the routing they pinned is unchanged — proven live on binanceusdm testnet for linear defaults and an explicit inverse signal; the live call is the FIRST verification move
The count of first-class exchange x no-arg-read pairs resolving by bare hd(configs) is re-measured before and after using a named method set and predicate; the final first-class count is zero
The default-family carves are recorded in docs/authored-specs.md with task-scoped ids

out_of_scope: The ~200 long-tail (non-first-class) exchange/method pairs — public-data-only frozen specs
Symbol filtering (task 367) and COIN-M row keying (tasks 366, 377)
task.body:
Captures the architectural recommendation that task 373 was required to report. Recorded as a
task so it survives the run record rather than living only in a transcript.

Tasks 368 and 373 both fixed the same defect shape by adding venue-local clauses to
`CCXT.Unified.select_endpoint/5`: when a multi-endpoint unified read is called with no family
signal (no symbol, no type/subType), selection silently falls through to `hd(configs)` — which
for binanceusdm is the COIN-M dapi sibling rather than the correct linear fapi default. 368
pinned `fetch_tickers`; 373 generalized it to `fetch_positions`, `fetch_open_orders`,
`fetch_funding_rates`, and `fetch_time` via a preferred-path map keyed by method atom.

Both implementers reached the same conclusion, and the task-373 reviewer concurs: the
venue-local runtime clause is the WRONG long-term seam. It does not scale — measured on the
compiled catalog, 231 exchange x no-arg-read pairs have >1 endpoint config and no authored
`endpoint_selection` entry, so all of them resolve by arbitrary `hd(configs)` ordering; 24 of
those are on first-class venues. Growing one `CCXT.Unified` clause per venue per method is a
combinatorial dead end, and it puts venue judgment in runtime Elixir instead of the authored
spec — against this repo's authored-not-inferred doctrine.

The forward shape (as reported by task 373):

  1. A venue-level default-family slot in the owned schema (e.g. `default_family` /
     `defaultSubType: "linear"`), so the fall-through default is authored data rather than
     list ordering.
  2. Authored `endpoint_selection` per multi-endpoint method carrying the preferred path and
     the inverse rule — binanceusdm already authors exactly this for `fetchBalance`,
     `fetchOHLCV`, `fetchTicker`, and `createOrder`; the gap is the methods that lack an entry.

Deliver the schema slot and migrate binanceusdm off the venue-local clause first, proving the
runtime behaviour is unchanged. Whether to sweep the remaining first-class venues in the same
change or file follow-ups is the implementer's call, reported either way. Make the silent
default LOUD rather than merely correct: an unresolvable multi-endpoint selection on a
first-class venue should fail or warn, not quietly pick element zero.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): binanceusdm's authored endpoint_selection actually carries 8 entries (fetchBalance, fetchOHLCV, fetchTicker, createOrder, fetchTrades, fetchMarkets, fetchOrder, cancelOrder) — more existing coverage than the 4 named above.

REVIEW (2026-07-19, fresh live testnet verification): the no-arg funding-rate call still
selects fapi and returns 728 rows, while an explicit inverse signal selects dapi and returns
40 rows. This confirms the current behavior that the authored default must preserve.

The -32602 unknown-variant error no longer reproduces; order_type carries limit/market and instrument_name carries the venue id

Other Derive write families
Other venues
task.body:
Observed live 2026-07-18 (api-demo.lyra.finance, subaccount 144422), post-372 base:

    CCXT.create_order(ex, "ETH/USD:USDC", "limit", "buy", 0.1, price: 100, params: %{"subaccount_id" => 144422})
    -> {:error, %CCXT.Error{code: -32602, message: ~s(unknown variant `ETH-PERP`, expected `limit` or `market`)}}

The venue's validator read the INSTRUMENT NAME in the `order_type` field — the unified
create_order arg mapping for derive is shifted/misbound, so the whole unified write path is
unusable (raw private/order parity was clean in the sweep, so this is unified request-build,
not signing/transport; the EIP-712 signer and header-trio auth are live-verified).

Author the derive unified write request builds (createOrder and cancelOrder; editOrder and
cancelAllOrders are out_of_scope) against docs.derive.xyz order semantics (required fields incl. max_fee,
signature envelope threading, amount/limit_price as strings), CCXT-JS as tier-2 reference.
Diagnose where the positional args are bound to endpoint params and fix the binding where the
mapping is resolved — not with a derive-only special case in the shared dispatcher.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): offline plug capture shows the build is a wholesale mapping-resolution failure, not a single shifted binding — SEVEN endpoint params are bound to the symbol value (direction, limit_price, max_fee, nonce, order_type, signature_expiry_sec, signer all = "ETH-PERP") while unified keys (type, side, price, amount) ride through untranslated, and no EIP-712 order signature is threaded at all. Live tier-1 repro (2026-07-18, api-demo.lyra.finance, amount-0 error-compare): -32602 'unknown variant `ETH-PERP`, expected `limit` or `market`'. Response side also dead: a stubbed result parses to an all-nil %CCXT.Order{}.

REVIEW (2026-07-19, fresh live demo verification): an amount-zero create_order again reaches
api-demo.lyra.finance and returns -32602 with `unknown variant ETH-PERP, expected limit or
market`. No order can be created by this probe.

REVIEW (2026-07-19, task-review live confrontation): a create_order WITHOUT explicit
subaccount_id (price via opts, amount 0.1) dies earlier — edge 403 Forbidden JSON, never
reaching the -32602 validator; the same creds read green (fetch_open_orders with explicit
subaccount_id: 144422 → 1 open order). The observed venue error therefore depends on probe
shape (-32602 with subaccount_id, 403 without); implementer must not pin a single error code
as the pre-fix baseline. Defect class unchanged: unified write path cannot create orders.

task.body:
Task 336 closed the Binance spot order reads and scoped a no-padding carve to the documented
sparse spot ACK key set. Two adjacent values remain frozen at tier-2 CCXT compatibility because
correcting them needs a tier-1 oracle, and both are values CCXT MANUFACTURES rather than copies
from the venue:

1. Timestamp from a sentinel. Binance returns `workingTime: -1` on a spot create whose order is
   not yet working. CCXT adopts that -1 as the order's millisecond timestamp; our authored
   precedence (`time` -> `workingTime` -> `createTime` -> `transactTime`) reproduces it because
   the frozen `createOrder spot market buy order with trailingPercent` response fixture pins
   `timestamp: -1`. A negative epoch is not a real clock.

2. Fill padding outside spot. CCXT defaults `executedQty` to "0" for every row it parses as an
   order, so bare acknowledgements on non-spot surfaces (notably the binance-venue-file linear-swap
   conditional cancelOrder ACK fixture (there is no response/binanceusdm.json), whose body is only
   `algoId`/`clientAlgoId`/`code`/`msg`) report `filled: 0`
   — a fill fact the venue never stated. Task 336 diverged only for the documented spot ACK key
   set; the other surfaces still pad.

Confront both against Binance's own documentation and observed live responses, decide whether each
is a CCXT bug we should diverge from, and record CONFIRMED/DIVERGE in the Binance carve register.
Where a divergence is adopted, the affected frozen response fixtures become expected reds and need
carve entries naming the Binance authority.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): all claims confirmed against code (read_parse.ex:2097 precedence; binance_order_filled/2 padding at :2140), frozen fixtures (workingTime -1 alongside transactTime in the trailing spot fixture; algo-cancel ACK = algoId/clientAlgoId/code/msg only), and official docs (workingTime is an activation sentinel with documented -1; USDS-M Cancel-Algo-Order response schema has no fill info). Live recipe for the workingTime: -1 observation: place a far-from-market trailing/takeProfit spot order on testnet and cancel immediately — the create ACK carries workingTime -1 while pending.

LIVE (2026-07-19, orchestrator post-land check of task 341, binanceusdm testnet): third instance
of the invented-order-values class — CCXT.cancel_all_orders(usdm, symbol: "BTC/USDT:USDT")
returns {:ok, [%CCXT.Order{id: nil, symbol: nil, ...}]} while the venue actually answered the
bare ack {"code": 200, "msg": "The operation of cancel all open order is done."}. The parser
manufactures a phantom order row from an envelope containing no order data. Decide the unified
cancelAllOrders return against the venue ack schema (explicit ack pass-through or fail-loud),
never a fabricated struct.

task.body:
The task-339 live test `live load_markets stamps asset_index from meta universe order`
asserts the loaded asset_index set equals a contiguous `0..n-1`. That invariant is false
against the live testnet universe as of 2026-07-18: a live load returns n=1462 markets with
max index 11866 and zero duplicates — Hyperliquid indexes SPOT assets in a separate 10000+
range (10000 + spot index) while delisted/non-tradable perps leave gaps in the perp range
(e.g. 210-219 missing). The assertion therefore fails on healthy live data.

Decide the real invariant from Hyperliquid's own semantics rather than restating CCXT's:
perp indices come from `meta.universe` position, spot indices from the spot universe offset
by 10000. Assert what is actually true (uniqueness, correct range per market type, and that
a perp's index equals its universe position) instead of global contiguity.

Discovered while reviewing task 371; the test is network-tagged so it does not gate
`mix check.dispatch`, which is why it went unnoticed.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): live re-verified exactly (n=1462, max 11866, 0 dups) — but the gap MECHANISM above is corrected: the perp range is contiguous 0..209 today (meta.universe has 210 entries; 53 carry isDelisted:true and ARE loaded); indices 210-219 simply don't exist. The sparse range is SPOT (e.g. 10004 absent), since spot asset id = 10000 + spot-universe index with filtered entries. Official rule (hyperliquid docs, asset-ids): perps use meta.universe position; spot = 10000 + index; HIP-3 = 100000 + dex*10000 + index. The rewrite should also decide whether isDelisted perps load as active: false (currently indistinguishable).

REVIEW (2026-07-19, fresh live testnet verification): load_markets returns 1462 markets,
210 perps indexed 0..209 and 1252 spots indexed 10000..11866, with zero duplicate
asset_index values. The production parser is healthy; only the live assertion is stale.
task.implemented: Rewrote the task-339 live assertion to the real Hyperliquid invariant: per-type index ranges (perp = meta.universe position < 10000, spot >= 10000) with uniqueness asserted and gaps permitted; aligned the stale is_nil identity asserts to task 370's authored id/base_id (= universe index string, C-T370). Live-verified against api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz (10 tests, 0 failures).

task.title: Validate authored request-source contracts and repair known unresolved bindings
acceptance_criteria: RequestShape.apply/3 on fetchConvertQuote for binance and binanceusdm emits fromAsset and toAsset from unified from_code/to_code, with no unmapped snake_case keys left in the shaped params

Every authored source is represented as exactly one validated class: an emitted unified param, an explicit caller-native passthrough, or a defaulted/optional source; unknown sources fail loudly with venue, method and source

task.body:
Authored request bindings may only source unified params by the exact string key the unified
layer emits. `CCXT.Unified.build_params/3` stringifies required atoms verbatim
(`to_string(:from_code) == "from_code"`), so an authored `source` written in camelCase for a
param that is a *unified* argument silently resolves to nil, and `put_authored_reference/4`
then DELETES the native key instead of failing loudly.

LIVE (2026-07-19, orchestrator post-land check of task 341, binanceusdm testnet): a second
instance of the same class shipped in 341's authored mappings — setPositionMode sources
"hedged", but the unified layer emits the argument as "hedge_mode"
(`{:set_position_mode, "setPositionMode", [:hedge_mode]}` in method_defs). The source resolves
nil, the native key is deleted, and the live call fails with -1102 "Mandatory parameter
'dualsideposition' was not sent". Repair it under the same source-contract validation; the
validator must catch this instance too.

Reproduced on the task 341 dispatch base (2026-07-18, reviewer run):

    params = CCXT.Unified.build_params([:from_code, :to_code, :amount], ["USDC", "USDT", 3], [])
    #=> %{"amount" => 3, "from_code" => "USDC", "to_code" => "USDT"}
    CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.apply(params, CCXT.Exchange.new!("binance"), "fetchConvertQuote")
    #=> %{"fromAmount" => 3, "from_code" => "USDC", "to_code" => "USDT"}

`fromAsset` and `toAsset` are absent and the raw snake_case keys ride through unmapped, so the
outbound /sapi/v1/convert/getQuote request names neither asset. Affects binance and binanceusdm
(fetchConvertQuote.fromAsset <- "fromCode", .toAsset <- "toCode"). A repo-wide scan of authored
`source` values found these two are the only camelCase sources whose snake_case form is an
actual unified param name; posSide, reduceOnly, and trailingAmount are genuine caller-supplied
native passthroughs and are NOT part of this defect.

Fix the bindings against Binance's own Convert API semantics, and make the defect class
non-silent: an authored `source` naming no key present in params and carrying no `default` is
indistinguishable today from a legitimately-absent optional. Encode the invariant rather than
relying on review to spot the next one.

REVIEW (2026-07-18, orchestrator verification sweep): repro confirmed on HEAD for BOTH binance (authored/binance.json:1126) and binanceusdm (authored/binanceusdm.json:1099, added by 341 itself). Doc confrontation done: fromAsset/toAsset are MANDATORY on POST /sapi/v1/convert/getQuote and 'either fromAmount or toAmount' per developers.binance.com/docs/convert/trade. Second known instance for the invariant test: authored/deribit.json carries a garbage source string "async fetchVolatilityHistory (code: string, params = {})" — the invariant must therefore check 'source resolves to an emitted key or documented passthrough', not merely camelCase detection, and this deribit binding must be repaired under the same test.

REVIEW (2026-07-19, fresh live transport attempt): the provisioned Binance spot sandbox
cannot resolve a sapi base URL, so fetch_convert_quote fails locally with `No base URL for
section sapi on binance (sandbox)` before a venue call. Completion therefore requires the
production-verification-ledger path unless a reachable Convert host/key is supplied.

task.body:
Surfaced by the task-377 reviewer while discharging that task's Binance-family
audit criterion. Task 377 normalized the CONTRACT venues (binanceusdm fapi/dapi
and binancecoinm) by carving their compact contract ids. The SPOT venue is a
separate, larger instance of the same keying class and was deliberately left
out of 377's scope.

Live evidence (reviewer run 2026-07-19, public mainnet, no creds):

    {:ok, ex} = CCXT.Exchange.new("binance")
    {:ok, t}  = CCXT.fetch_tickers(ex)
    # 3652 rows, 1118 of them keyed with the RAW exchange id

    raw sample: 0GBNB, 0GTRY, 1000CATBNB, 1000CATTRY, 1000SATSTRY,
                1MBABYDOGETRY, 2ZBNB, 2ZTRY, AAVEBKRW, AAVEBNB, AAVEBRL,
                AAVETRY, LINKUSD1, BCHUSD1, REUSD1, TONUSD1, GRAMUSD1

Rows quoted in USDT/USDC/BTC key correctly; the failures are the long tail of
other quote assets (BNB, TRY, BRL, BKRW, USD1, ...). Spot ids are BASE+QUOTE
concatenated with no separator, so the quote boundary is NOT recoverable by
pattern alone -- 377's regex approach is the wrong tool here and must not be
copied. Resolve the split against the venue's own instrument identity
(/api/v3/exchangeInfo baseAsset/quoteAsset, or the already-loaded markets
index) so the carve is answerable to the exchange rather than to a guessed
suffix list.

Audit the other binance spot multi-row reads that share the symbol-backfill
path, not fetch_tickers alone.

mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate stays green on the unchanged base, and mix check.dispatch passes

Revisiting the C-T384b units verdict itself (tracked in docs/prod-verification-ledger.md)
task.body:
`test/fixtures/fixture_replay_failures.json` is a flat list of failing fixture
names with no reason attached. Two very different things now live in it and are
indistinguishable:

  * an open defect we intend to fix (the overwhelming majority), and
  * a fixture that is red **because we deliberately diverge from CCXT** and CCXT
    is the one that is wrong.

Task 384 created the first instance of the second kind:
`test hyperliquid withdraw withdraw from vault #1144` asserts CCXT's bare-dollar
`usd` for the `vaultTransfer` action, while our authored build correctly sends
1e6 micro-USD (carve C-T384b, grounded in the official Hyperliquid Python SDK
examples). Turning that fixture green would mean reintroducing a 1,000,000x
under-transfer money bug.

The hazard is concrete and mechanical: `mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate --update`
regenerates the baseline from whatever the code currently does, and the gate
also fails when a baseline-listed fixture *passes*. A future session that
"fixes" the divergence to chase a green fixture gets a green gate and a silent
money bug, with nothing in the baseline file to warn it. The only warning today
lives in the carve register and CHANGELOG, which the gate never reads.

Give the baseline a way to carry per-entry provenance — at minimum a reason
string, and a way to mark an entry as an intentional divergence that must NOT be
cleared by chasing a green fixture. Decide (and document) what the gate should
do when an entry marked as a deliberate divergence starts passing: that is
almost certainly a regression in our code, i.e. the opposite of the current
"a newly-green fixture just needs --update" prompt.

Keep the delta-based behaviour for ordinary open defects — this is about
annotating entries, not changing how the ordinary gate decides pass/fail.

acceptance_criteria: Loading any document consumed by a `use CCXT.Extract.JsonLoader` module raises when it contains a duplicate key at any nesting level, naming the file, the duplicated key and the object path

Changing the persistent_term caching or reload!/0 behaviour of JsonLoader
task.body:
Task 375 made CCXT.Spec fail loudly on duplicate JSON object keys, but only for the
documents that loader consumes (base specs, authored overlays, the manifest). Every
module built on `use CCXT.Extract.JsonLoader` still decodes with a bare
`File.read!() |> Jason.decode!()`, which keeps the FIRST occurrence of a duplicate key
and silently discards the rest — the exact failure that cost task 372 a re-dispatch.

This matters because at least one JsonLoader document is hand-edited, not machine-frozen:
`priv/extractor/ccxt_emulated_methods.json` gained `authored_delegate` entries by hand in
task 371. A duplicate key there silently drops emulation entries, and the symptom surfaces
far from the cause as a wrong-shaped request at dispatch time.

Reuse the validation CCXT.Spec already has rather than writing a second implementation —
it takes the file path, re-parses with the OTP `:json` callback decoder, and raises naming
the file, the duplicated key, and the object path. Decide where that helper should live so
both loaders share one copy, and keep malformed JSON reporting a `Jason.DecodeError` with a
byte position rather than an opaque `:json` `{:invalid_byte, _}`.

task.body:
Task 376 shipped resolution-aware `safeTimestamp` handling, but the defect it
originally missed — five rules carrying `"format": null` fell through a
key-presence guard and silently coerced to `nil` — was only caught by an ad-hoc
reviewer sweep over the merged runtime rule set, not by any test. The repo rule
is that whole-surface invariants become CI failures rather than consumer
discoveries (CLAUDE.md / critical-rules "Domain & Whole-Surface Defects").

Add a manifest-wide test that walks the merged runtime rule set
(`CCXT.Spec.load!/1` over every manifest id, after the authored-slice deep-merge)
and asserts that each field rule carrying a coercion resolves to a handled
`CCXT.ResponseParser.coerce/2` branch rather than the passthrough or a silent
`nil`. Feed each rule a plausible source value for its declared resolution and
assert the parsed output is non-nil and of the expected shape.

The generalized defect class is "a coercion tag whose runtime branch does not
exist, or whose guard does not match the shape the catalog actually emits" —
`safeTimestamp` was one instance; the test should cover the coercion vocabulary,
not just timestamps.

task.body:
Task 385 authored the OKX place/amend request bodies (instId/tdMode/ordType/side/sz/px,
newSz/newPx). It stringifies the caller's raw number verbatim — there is no market-precision
step. `CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.OKX.build/3` takes no `builder` argument at all, unlike the
bybit sibling, whose `_builder => "bybit_v5"` shape config threads a precision helper
(`precise_number_string/5`) into qty/price.

Consequence: a caller passing an amount or price that does not conform to the instrument's
`lotSz` / `tickSz` / `minSz` sends it through unrounded, and OKX rejects it at the venue with
its own business codes (51121 "Order quantity must be a multiple of the lot size", 51006
"Order price is not within the limit"). The request is well-formed, so the 385 fix and its
offline captures stay green — this defect only surfaces against a real instrument.

Plumb market precision into the OKX write builds the way bybit already does, and confront the
rounding mode against OKX v5 docs (OKX documents sz/px as strings conforming to the
instrument's lotSz/tickSz from /api/v5/public/instruments) rather than inheriting CCXT-JS's
Precise behaviour unexamined. Record the outcome in the okx carve register.

task.title: Route the recorded-fixture JSON reads through the strict duplicate-key decoder
acceptance_criteria: Both recorded-fixture decode sites go through CCXT.JsonDocument — no bare Jason.decode! on a fixture file remains in lib/
A duplicate key anywhere in a recorded-fixture document raises naming the file, the duplicated key, and the object path
Malformed recorded-fixture JSON still raises Jason.DecodeError with a byte position, not a bare ErlangError
A regression test pins duplicate-key rejection through the recorded-fixture read path with a dedicated fixture
mix check.dispatch stays green and mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate reports no regressions
out_of_scope: Re-recording or re-authoring any venue fixture corpus
Changing the fixture replay gate's baseline semantics
task.body:
Tasks 375 and 392 made CCXT.Spec and every `use CCXT.Extract.JsonLoader` module
decode through CCXT.JsonDocument, which rejects duplicate JSON object keys and
names the file, key, and object path. Two decode sites were left outside that
net and still use a bare `File.read!() |> Jason.decode!()`, which keeps the
FIRST occurrence of a duplicate key and silently discards the rest:
`CCXT.RecordedResponseFixtures` and the `mix ccxt.record_fixtures` task.

These read the recorded-response fixture corpus — machine-written by the mix
task but hand-tweaked in practice, which is exactly the condition that makes a
duplicate key plausible. A silently dropped fixture entry weakens the T-A
replay gate without reddening anything, so the loss surfaces as a fixture that
quietly stops covering a venue rather than as a failure.

Reuse CCXT.JsonDocument rather than adding a third decode path, and keep
malformed JSON reporting a Jason.DecodeError with a byte position instead of an
opaque `:json` `{:invalid_byte, _}`.

task.title: Reach CCXT.Order.Sanity from the unified create/edit dispatch path (currently dead code)
acceptance_criteria: A unified CCXT.create_order call with an amount below the loaded market's limits.amount.min returns a tagged {:error, _} without an HTTP request being issued, proven by an offline capture that asserts no request reached the plug
The behaviour is opt-in or opt-out via an explicit documented option, and the default is stated in the moduledoc with its rationale
Validation is skipped (not raised) when the exchange has no loaded markets, pinned by a test that calls create_order on an exchange without load_markets
A live EEA demo OKX order that violates only limits.amount.min is rejected locally, with the previously-observed venue error recorded for comparison
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate and mix check.dispatch pass
out_of_scope: Changing per-venue precision rounding carved in task 394
Adding new limit fields to CCXT.Market
WebSocket order entry
task.body:
`CCXT.Order.Sanity` implements client-side order validation — side, type, symbol-vs-market,
amount/price limits (`limits.amount.min|max`, `limits.cost.min`) and precision-increment
conformance. `CCXT.Order.Builder` is its only caller, and grepping `lib/` shows nothing
outside `lib/ccxt/order/` references either module: the unified `CCXT.create_order/6` and
`CCXT.edit_order/*` dispatch path (`CCXT.Unified.call/5`) never reaches them. Every venue's
unified write path therefore ships unvalidated orders and relies on the exchange to reject
them.

Task 394 surfaced this on OKX: applying `lotSz`/`tickSz` rounding to `sz`/`px` had to add its
own zero-guard for sub-lot amounts precisely because no pre-flight check rejects an amount
below one lot. That guard is venue-local; the underlying gap is client-wide.

Decide and implement how the unified path reaches this validation. Reaching it changes the
error contract (orders that previously round-tripped to the venue would now fail locally),
so the opt-in/opt-out semantics and the returned error shape are the substance of the task —
not merely inserting a call. If the conclusion is that the modules should be deleted rather
than wired, that is an acceptable outcome provided it is recorded with the reasoning.

task.title: Implement or retire the ten catalog coercion tags that fall through to the response-parser passthrough branch
acceptance_criteria: Each of the ten tags is either implemented as a coerce/2 branch or explicitly retired with a recorded reason
test/ccxt/response_parser_test.exs @coercion_ledger shrinks accordingly and the catalog coercion sweep stays green
For each newly implemented branch, a test asserts the coerced value against a real venue response shape rather than only a synthesised sample
mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Re-authoring venue spec slices beyond removing a retired coercion tag
Changing safeTimestamp semantics established by task 376
task.body:
Task 393's catalog-wide coercion sweep (test/ccxt/response_parser_test.exs, `@coercion_ledger`) ledgered ten coercion tags that appear in the merged runtime rule set but have no `CCXT.ResponseParser.coerce/2` branch, so the raw source value leaks into the unified struct unchanged: `parseNumber(parsePrecision(safeString))` (54 rules), `parseNumber(safeString)` (19), `member` (17), `safeIntegerProduct` (13), `parse8601` (11), `safeIntegerOmitZero` (6), `safeSymbol` (6), `safeStringLower2` (4), `parseNumber(omitZero(safeString))` (3), `safeTimestamp2` (1) — 134 rules total.

Concretely: a `parseNumber(...)` slot lands a string like "0.001" where the struct declares a number, `parse8601` lands an ISO-8601 string where `timestamp` declares an integer, and `safeTimestamp2` lands seconds where milliseconds are expected.

For each tag, decide from CCXT's own JS source what the runtime should do, then either implement the branch (moving the tag out of `@coercion_ledger` into `@coercion_samples` with its expected value — the sweep enforces that migration and fails while a ledgered tag is implemented) or, if the tag is an authoring artefact that should never have been emitted, record that finding and retire it under a separate authoring task.

Per CLAUDE.md the correctness oracle for a divergence-prone transform is the real exchange response plus a non-CCXT semantic source, not a CCXT fixture alone.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784432828832-428dd35e, 66d14464635360f947c639804129c0cf19df9cd1).

task.title: Make the iso8601 coercion honour its declared seconds resolution
acceptance_criteria: coerce/2 renders a format: "s" iso8601 rule from seconds, and a format: "ms" / absent-format rule from milliseconds
The {"iso8601", "s"} entry moves from @coercion_divergences to @coercion_samples with an exact expected value
A test covers deepcoin CreateTime and whitebit fundingTime specifically, citing the documented resolution for each
mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Changing safeTimestamp semantics established by task 376
Re-authoring the deepcoin or whitebit spec slices
task.body:
`CCXT.ResponseParser.coerce/2` implements `iso8601` as "epoch milliseconds -> ISO-8601 string" and ignores the rule's declared `format`. Two catalog rules declare `format: "s"` — deepcoin `CreateTime` and whitebit `fundingTime` — so a seconds epoch is read as milliseconds and renders an instant in January 1970.

Reproduced during task 393's review sweep: a rule `%{"coercion" => "iso8601", "format" => "s", "key" => "v"}` fed "1714923704" yields "1970-01-20T20:22:03.704Z" instead of "2024-05-05T15:41:44.000Z".

This is the same defect class task 376 fixed for `safeTimestamp`: a coercion whose guard does not match the resolution the catalog actually declares. Make `iso8601` resolution-aware the way `safeTimestamp` is, then move the `{"iso8601", "s"}` entry out of `@coercion_divergences` in test/ccxt/response_parser_test.exs into `@coercion_samples` with its exact expected value.

Confirm the seconds reading against each venue's own API documentation before committing to it — the field's real resolution is the authority, not the spec annotation alone.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784432828811-0a416491, 2840321b9454b5a29e8f59f3f5e02fc2aec07d81).

task.title: Binance fetch_tickers refetches the whole markets fan-out on every call when markets are unloaded
acceptance_criteria: Live binance (public, no creds): fetch_tickers on an exchange with no loaded markets still keys every currently-listed spot row unified -- task 390's behaviour does not regress
Live measurement shows the unloaded-markets fetch_tickers no longer issues the option (eapi) and coin-margined (dapi) requests, evidenced by a request-count or per-endpoint trace
Live timing comparison recorded in the task: unloaded-path latency is materially closer to the markets-loaded path than the 4442ms vs 969ms measured 2026-07-19
Offline test pins the request set issued by fetch_tickers on an unloaded binance exchange, so a future fan-out regression fails a check rather than only showing up as latency
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate reports no regressions and mix check.dispatch stays green
out_of_scope: The raw-id keying carve itself (task 390, landed)
A general cross-exchange markets cache for venues other than the binance family
Endpoint selection / default-family routing (tasks 368, 373)
task.body:
Surfaced by the task-390 reviewer. Task 390 made binance spot fetch_tickers resolve
raw compact ids against market identity: when the exchange struct carries no loaded
markets it calls fetch_markets inline. On binance that call FANS OUT to four
endpoints (spot exchangeInfo, fapi, dapi, eapi), and eapi alone returns ~1446 option
rows -- none of which can key a spot ticker.

The result is not cached anywhere: every fetch_tickers on an unloaded exchange pays
the whole fan-out again. Measured live 2026-07-19 (public mainnet, no creds):

    fetch_tickers, markets unloaded: 4442 ms
    fetch_tickers, markets loaded:    969 ms

A consumer polling tickers therefore pays ~4.6x latency and four extra heavy
requests per poll, and burns rate-limit weight on surfaces it never reads.

Resolve this so the identity lookup costs what it needs to and no more. Preloading
via CCXT.load_markets/1 already avoids the penalty, so the fix is about the
unloaded path: scope the inline load to the section that can actually answer the
lookup, and/or let a resolved index be reused across calls rather than refetched.
Decide where a cache belongs (or whether the honest answer is to make the inline
load narrow enough not to need one) -- do not add a cache layer speculatively.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784432828836-20ef1bfa, 54fb9e25c77c8ae53d72a091013a9f9023180378).

acceptance_criteria: Live binancecoinm (public, no creds): fetch_markets returns the venue's coin-margined instrument set with a row count matching its dapi exchangeInfo, not 4
Every returned market carries non-nil id, symbol and type; symbols match the exchange-reported baseAsset/quoteAsset/marginAsset identity
The endpoint and envelope path the parser reads are confirmed against binance dapi documentation or observed live traffic, not inferred from the existing code
Offline regression coverage pins the corrected row shape from a recorded dapi payload
binanceusdm and binance spot fetch_markets do not regress -- both still return 0 raw-id symbols live
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate reports no regressions and mix check.dispatch stays green
out_of_scope: binance spot ticker/market keying (tasks 390, 412)
binanceusdm fapi/dapi contract-id grammars (task 377, landed)
task.body:
Surfaced by the task-390 reviewer while establishing a contract-venue baseline; the
defect predates task 390 and is unrelated to its diff (measured identical before and
after).

Live 2026-07-19, public mainnet, no creds:

    {:ok, ex} = CCXT.Exchange.new("binancecoinm")
    {:ok, m}  = CCXT.fetch_markets(ex)
    length(m)  # => 4
    Enum.map(m, &{&1.id, &1.symbol, &1.type})
    # => [{nil, nil, nil}, {nil, nil, nil}, {nil, nil, nil}, {nil, nil, nil}]

Four rows, every field nil -- so the venue reports a markets set that is both the
wrong cardinality and devoid of instrument identity. For contrast, on the same run
binancecoinm fetch_tickers and fetch_funding_rates each returned 30 correctly-keyed
rows, so the venue's data is reachable; the markets read specifically is not
landing on (or not parsing) the coin-margined instrument surface.

Establish what the venue actually reports and make fetch_markets answerable to it.
Confront the endpoint selection and the response envelope shape against the
exchange's own dapi documentation -- the all-nil rows suggest the parser is walking
an envelope level that carries no instrument fields, which would mean the row set
being parsed is not the instrument list at all.

task.title: Hyperliquid action methods declare signer-owned natives (nonce/signature) as identifier_reference request slots
acceptance_criteria: Task 267's sweep re-run reports zero unresolved identifier_reference for hyperliquid

Live testnet evidence for at least one previously-raising reachable method (e.g. cancelAllOrdersAfter timer set+clear, or an invalid-params error-compare): the request reaches the venue and returns a venue business response instead of a local ArgumentError
Offline test pins the signed wire body shape %{action, nonce, signature} for at least one method of the class

The task-267 sweep becomes a tagged offline test: zero unresolved identifier_reference across all 7 first-class venues' shaped methods, with an explicit allowlist for entries still owned by open tasks (each entry names its task id); the allowlist may only shrink
No valid persistent mutation (createSubAccount/createVault/vault transfer) is executed against the venue
mix check.dispatch green; mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate reports no regressions
out_of_scope: The withdraw vaultTransfer branch (task 384, landed)
New unified method exposure for the 7 dormant actions
task.body:
Task 267's request-shape sweep (2026-07-19, base 497aece) found 12 hyperliquid
shaped methods raising `unresolved identifier_reference` for `nonce` or
`signature`. Those values are produced by the SIGNING pipeline
(CCXT.Signing.Hyperliquid builds the wire body %{action, nonce, signature}) —
request shaping runs before the signer, so declaring them as identifier_reference
natives makes the method raise before the signer ever runs. Same defect class as
the withdraw `signature` slot task 384 fixed for one method; this closes the class.

Unified-reachable and therefore non-functional today: cancelAllOrdersAfter,
cancelOrdersForSymbols, cancelTwapOrder, createSubAccount, createVault. Dormant
(shape entries exist but no unified method exposes them): approveBuilderFee,
enableUserDexAbstraction, modifyMarginHelper, reserveRequestWeight,
setAgentAbstraction, setRef, setUserAbstraction.

Author the slice so signer-owned natives are never shaping-required (drop them
from the request shape, or mark them signer-supplied) for the whole class, not
per-method. Read CCXT JS sign()/the exchange's action semantics as references;
the mutation-safety policy applies to live evidence (error-compare with invalid
params or reversible timer calls only — createSubAccount/createVault are
persistent mutations, SKIPPED_UNSAFE, prove them by shaping+signing to the wire
body offline plus a deliberately-invalid live rejection where feasible).

acceptance_criteria: deepcoin funding_rate_history.timestamp (CreateTime) and whitebit funding_rate_history.timestamp (fundingTime) declare format: "s"

Broader catalog re-audit of other safeTimestamp format annotations

task.title: Recover unified network codes from the live currency catalog before falling back to the frozen alias table
acceptance_criteria: With a loaded currency catalog, a chain id present in the catalog but ABSENT from the authored alias table resolves to the catalog's network code rather than nil
With no loaded catalog (the offline fixture-replay path), resolution still comes from the authored table and every currently-green fixture stays green
Where catalog and authored table disagree on a chain id, the resolution order is pinned by a test and the choice is recorded as a carve
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate and mix check.dispatch pass
out_of_scope: Re-authoring or expanding the frozen alias tables themselves
Request construction
Venues other than the authored first-class set
task.body:
Network-code resolution for deposit addresses (and any other read mapping a venue chain id to
a unified network) currently consults ONLY the authored `network_aliases` table frozen in the
spec. CCXT resolves the same fact against the LIVE currency catalog it just loaded
(`currency['networks']` indexed by chain id, then `networkIdToCode`), so a chain the venue
listed after our last authoring pass resolves there and not here.

Consequence today (carve C-T389c in docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md): a chain absent from the
frozen table resolves to `network: nil`, and the row is then dropped from
`fetchDepositAddressesByNetwork` and unreachable via `fetchDepositAddress`. That is
CCXT-compatible on a miss, but a newly-listed chain stays silently invisible until someone
re-authors the table by hand — an address the account genuinely has simply does not appear.

Make the live catalog primary: when `exchange.currencies` is loaded, resolve the chain id
through it and use the authored table only as the offline fallback (which is what keeps the
frozen fixture gates deterministic). Generalise beyond okx — the same limitation applies to
every venue whose networks are authored this way.

task.title: Replace inert flunk-inside-Req.Test-stub guards with assertions that survive the HTTP rescue
acceptance_criteria: Every flunk-inside-a-Req.Test-stub no-request guard is replaced with an assertion that fails when a request is issued, demonstrated by a recorded mutation run per converted site
A note in the test or test support explains why flunk inside the plug is swallowed, so the pattern is not reintroduced
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate pass
out_of_scope: Changing CCXT.HTTP's rescue behaviour
Converting flunk calls that are not inside a Req.Test stub callback
task.body:
Several tests guard "this code path must not issue an HTTP request" by calling
`flunk/1` inside a `Req.Test.stub/2` callback. That guard is inert: `CCXT.HTTP`
rescues exceptions raised inside the plug and converts them to
`{:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :network_error}}`, so the ExUnit assertion never
surfaces and the test passes even when the request WAS issued.

Verified live during the task 411 review: a test whose stub sent a message and
then called `flunk("STUB WAS CALLED")` reported 0 failures while the mailbox
proved the stub had run.

Known sites (confirm the list is complete rather than trusting it):
- test/ccxt/order/builder_test.exs:129
- test/ccxt/unified/request_shape_test.exs:408
- test/ccxt/unified/request_shape_test.exs:426

test/ccxt/unified_order_sanity_test.exs already uses the working pattern: the
stub sends `{:request_issued, method, path}` to the test process and the test
asserts with `refute_received/1`, which survives the rescue. Port that shape,
or another mechanism proven to survive, to the remaining sites.

Each converted guard must be mutation-checked: break the guarded behaviour and

task.title: Port networkIdToCode so catalog-resolved chains emit unified network codes, not raw network ids
acceptance_criteria: A catalog-only chain whose network id differs from its unified code resolves to the unified code, pinned by a test using the real string-keyed catalog shape
Network-id-to-code resolution is authored from CCXT source and shared across the first-class venues, not hardcoded per venue
Currency lookup applies the venue's currency aliasing before indexing the catalog, pinned by a test on a venue whose raw id differs from the unified code
Carve C-T421 is updated with the resulting ordering decision and its evidence

out_of_scope: Re-authoring or expanding the frozen network_aliases tables
Refreshing the vendored static response fixtures
Request construction
task.body:
Task 421 made the loaded currency catalog resolve deposit-address chains the frozen
`network_aliases` table never saw, so a newly-listed network surfaces instead of resolving to
nil and having its row dropped. That recovery is only half of CCXT's resolution.

CCXT does two steps (`js/src/okx.js` `parseDepositAddress`):
`indexBy(currency['networks'], 'id')` -> take `networkData['network']` -> `networkIdToCode(network, code)`.
The catalog supplies step one only, so its value is a network id. We currently emit that id
verbatim for a catalog-only chain — better than nil, but not guaranteed to be the unified code a
caller can match. Measured example: the vendored currencies cache resolves `USDT-Optimism` to
`OP`, while CCXT's unified vocabulary (and our alias table) says `OPTIMISM`.

Author the missing step: the venue's `options.networksById` plus whatever base-level alias
resolution `networkIdToCode` applies, read from CCXT source, and run catalog-derived network ids
through it. Generalise across the first-class venues rather than special-casing okx. With the
step in place, revisit carve C-T421's ordering — a fully-resolved catalog value would no longer
be strictly weaker than the frozen alias table.

Separately, `network_code_for_row/3` looks the currency up by the row's raw `ccy` id, while CCXT
applies `safeCurrency`/commonCurrencies aliasing first. On a venue whose raw currency id differs
from the unified code the catalog lookup silently misses. Fix that in the same pass.

Authored response transforms that synthesize unified rows before field-map parsing
(currently `market_fee_rows`, added by task 380) put the venue's raw object under an
`"info"` key of the synthesized row. The parser then sets the struct's `info` to the
whole synthesized row, so callers reach the exchange payload at `info["info"]` instead
of `info`.

per-transform inconsistency in a public struct field, not a venue quirk. Decide where the
raw payload should be carried for synthesized rows and make the runtime honor it uniformly
for any current or future transform `kind` — do not special-case `market_fee_rows`.

acceptance_criteria: A shared test-support helper exists for capturing a Req.Test plug's observed request and asserting on it after the call returns, and is used by the converted sites
No ExUnit assertion remains inside a Req.Test plug callback anywhere under test/ — verified by a repo-wide scan whose method is recorded in the PR description

task.body:
Tasks 422 and 425 removed the two *guard* classes of inert in-plug assertion — the
no-request guards and the unexpected-input diagnostics. A third, much larger class
remains: positive request-shape assertions written directly inside a Req.Test plug
callback (`assert conn.request_path == expected`, `assert query["symbols"] == ...`,
`refute Map.has_key?(decoded, "symbol")`, header/signature assertions, and so on).

These are inert for exactly the mechanism task 425 documented: CCXT.HTTP wraps the
transport in a rescue (lib/ccxt/http.ex), so an ExUnit.AssertionError raised inside
the plug is converted to {:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :network_error}}. The outer
assertion still fails, so there is no false green, but the diagnostic naming the
actual wrong path / param / header is destroyed and the failure reads as a network
error. Every one of these tests is a request-shape test whose entire value is that
diagnostic.

Measured 2026-07-19 on the landed base: 163 such assertions across 17 test files,
concentrated in test/ccxt/dispatch_test.exs (67), test/ccxt/unified_test.exs (30),
test/ccxt/http_test.exs (16) and test/ccxt/binance_authored_spec_test.exs (13).

Establish one reusable collector helper in test/support rather than open-coding an
Agent per stub, then convert the sites to it. Sites whose plug runs in a spawned
Task (the binance fan-out) need a cross-process collector; the rest may use the test
process mailbox. Prefer capturing the observed request into the collector and
asserting its shape after the call returns, so the assertion runs in the test
process and the diagnostic survives.
