task.title: Classify HTML-bodied 401 as an authentication error, not access_restricted
acceptance_criteria: An HTTP 401 with a text/html body classifies as :authentication_error (or a deliberate, documented alternative), with the HTML preview retained in the error's raw payload
HTTP 403 with an HTML geo-block/landing body still classifies as :access_restricted, and Cloudflare challenge detection is unchanged

A regression test pins the real recorded Alpaca nginx 401 body (already captured in test/ccxt/alpaca_authored_slice_test.exs) to the chosen classification, and that test is updated in the same change rather than left asserting the old behavior
mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Any change to Alpaca's authored spec slices or unified mappings
Broadening HTML detection itself (which bodies count as HTML)
task.body:
`CCXT.HTTP.Errors` routes any HTML-bodied response through `classify_html_response/3`,
which — absent a Cloudflare marker — returns `:access_restricted` regardless of status.
That is right for the case it was built for (geo/IP blocks, typically 403 + a vendor
landing page) but wrong for a plain 401.

Observed live 2026-07-19 (task 428 review): Alpaca's data edge rejects bad API keys
before the app layer, returning HTTP 401 with `content-type: text/html` and an nginx
`401 Authorization Required` body. Our stack reports that as `:access_restricted` with
hints suggesting a VPN, when the actual cause is a bad credential. A consumer retrying
through a VPN instead of fixing its key is following our hint away from the real fault.

Decide and implement the correct rule for an HTML body carrying a 401 specifically —
most likely: status 401 wins over the HTML branch and yields `:authentication_error`
(preserving the HTML preview in `raw`), while 403 keeps today's access-restricted
reading. Check whether any other venue in the catalog depends on a 401+HTML currently
classifying as access_restricted before changing it.
task.implemented: classify_html_response/3 branches on status: non-Cloudflare HTML 401 -> Error.authentication_error (HTML preview retained in raw.body_preview, credential-pointing hints); 403/other HTML stays access_restricted; Cloudflare markers still win. Alpaca slice + live integration pins flipped to :authentication_error; 3 new unit tests (401, 403, CF-over-401). Live-verified against real Alpaca edge (invalid creds -> 401 HTML -> :authentication_error); fixture_replay_gate: no regressions.

task.title: Author okx endpoint_selection for cancelOrders so stop/trailing/trigger reaches trade/cancel-algos
acceptance_criteria: cancel_orders with stop/trailing/trigger true posts to /api/v5/trade/cancel-algos with an algoId-keyed array body
cancel_orders without those flags still posts to /api/v5/trade/cancel-batch-orders with an ordId-keyed body
cancelOrdersForSymbols is confronted for the same defect and either fixed or shown correct with a test
The :known_defect tag is removed from the okx cancel-algos test and it passes in the default suite
Evidence recorded against the OKX demo account showing the algo cancel reaching cancel-algos, or a prod-verification-ledger entry if unreachable with current keys
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate pass
out_of_scope: The in-plug assertion mechanism conversion itself (task 433)
Other venues endpoint selection precedence
task.body:
OKX cancel_orders with stop: true (or trailing/trigger) builds the correct algo
array body -- [{"algoId" => ..., "instId" => ...}] -- but posts it to
/api/v5/trade/cancel-batch-orders instead of /api/v5/trade/cancel-algos. The body
and the path disagree, so the venue receives algo ids on the plain-order endpoint.

Root cause, read on the landed base 2026-07-19:
- priv/specs/json/output/okx.json authors raw.describe.options.cancelOrders.method
  = "privatePostTradeCancelBatchOrders" unconditionally.
- There is NO endpoints.request.endpoint_selection.cancelOrders slice authored.
- CCXT.Unified.configured_endpoint/3 honours the options.<jsName>.method string for
  okx, so the plain-order endpoint is chosen before any stop/algo branch is
  evaluated. CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Okx.build_cancel_orders/2 meanwhile keys the
  body on algoId whenever algo_cancel?/1 is true -- hence the mismatch.

cancelOrdersForSymbols carries the same shape and is very likely the same defect;
singular cancel_order is unaffected (it selects correctly today).

This was latent behind an inert in-plug assertion and surfaced by task 433's
conversion: the swallowed assertion became {:error, %CCXT.Error{type: :network_error}},
which satisfied the test's own assert {:error, %CCXT.Error{}}, so the suite was GREEN
on a wrong request. The test "stop cancel_orders selects trade/cancel-algos with
algoId array body" in test/ccxt/okx_authored_spec_test.exs now asserts the correct
path and is tagged :known_defect (excluded by default) pending this fix. Remove that
tag as part of this task.

Decide whether the fix is (a) authoring an endpoint_selection.cancelOrders slice with
stop/trailing/trigger cases, or (b) changing okx configured_endpoint precedence so
authored selection outranks options.method. Option (b) is cross-cutting for every okx
method relying on options.method -- confront it before choosing.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784537231378-a869d5d1, 472f626b1b0a486753f10964f59f13478c64d72b).

task.title: Adjudicate okx Optimism network code against the CCXT 4.5.65 oracle (alias OPTIMISM vs oracle OP)
acceptance_criteria: The okx Optimism unified network code is adjudicated against okx's own chain naming (exchange docs or a live/observed response), not against the CCXT fixture alone, and the evidence is recorded in the C-T421 carve entry

Either our resolution emits the adjudicated code and both okx replay fixtures go green, or they are annotated deliberate_divergence: true with the evidence, and mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate reflects that outcome
The interim reason annotations added by task 430 on those two baseline entries are replaced by the adjudicated outcome
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate and mix check.dispatch pass
out_of_scope: Re-freezing any vendored static fixture directory to a new CCXT vintage
The retained upstream bybit OP/OPTIMISM cross-fixture skew
task.body:
Task 430 re-froze priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/response/ to CCXT 4.5.65 so the
currencies cache and the response oracle share one vintage. That surfaced a behavioural
divergence it was not allowed to fix: for okx's Optimism chain, the 4.5.65 oracle resolves the
unified network code to `OP`, while our alias table (carve C-T421, alias-first ordering) yields
`OPTIMISM`.

Two replay fixtures are red on this and were baselined with an explicit `reason` rather than
adjudicated: `test okx fetchDepositAddressesByNetwork fetch deposit addresses by network` and
`test okx fetchCurrencies default` (see test/fixtures/fixture_replay_failures.json).

Decide which code is right and make ours match that decision. This is a CARVE question, not a
mechanical one: `OPTIMISM` may still be the better unified code even though CCXT 4.5.65 emits
`OP` — in which case the correct outcome is a `deliberate_divergence: true` baseline annotation
with evidence, NOT a change to our tables. Per the repo's tier rules, a CCXT fixture is a tier-2
compatibility oracle and cannot settle correctness on its own; confront okx's own documented
chain naming (exchange docs / live response) before choosing.

Note that the sibling skew recorded in the same sweep — bybit's `OP` chain, where CCXT 4.5.65
contradicts itself between its own currencies cache and response oracle — is upstream's
inconsistency and is deliberately retained, not in scope here.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784537236253-8572eca7, c7622730cd0bfa9dd4456ba39edeb0084fb61544).

task.title: Adjudicate the residual replay reds absorbed by the 4.5.65 response re-freeze
acceptance_criteria: The okx fetchCurrencies #17 entry is adjudicated on both residual axes: per-network `active` (nil in the oracle, bool in ours) and numeric rendering (fee/limits as float vs int)
The numeric-rendering axis is first checked for a SHARED root cause with the binance and bybit fetchCurrencies entries below before being scoped to any single venue

Each of the eight baseline entries carrying task 430's 'Not adjudicated as correct-or-not' reason is adjudicated: either our parse is corrected and the fixture goes green, or the entry is annotated deliberate_divergence: true with the evidence that our value is right and CCXT's is wrong
No baseline entry is left carrying the interim 'Not adjudicated' wording
Each adjudication names the semantic source it was decided against (exchange docs, official SDK, or an observed live response), not the CCXT fixture alone
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate and mix check.dispatch pass
out_of_scope: The okx Optimism NETWORK-CODE question, settled by task 441 (the residual `active`/numeric axes of the same fixture ARE in scope here)
The retained upstream bybit OP/OPTIMISM cross-fixture skew, which no CCXT release resolves
Re-freezing any vendored static fixture directory to a different CCXT vintage
task.body:
SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-07-20 (orchestrator, after task 441 landed). Task 441 settled okx's Optimism
network code and brought `test okx fetchCurrencies default #17` to network-key parity with the
4.5.65 oracle (28 keys each, `op` both sides). It stayed RED on two axes that 441 could not
touch and that task 430's baseline reason had wrongly attributed to Optimism alone:

  1. per-network `active` is nil in the oracle and true/false in ours (all 28 networks). CCXT's
     okx parseCurrency leaves it undefined; we derive it. Deriving may be the better unified
     contract -> deliberate_divergence: true with the reasoning in the okx carve register; else
     align. Confront okx's own semantics, not the tier-2 fixture.
  2. numeric rendering: fee 0.0 vs 0, limits.withdraw.min 0.0/1.0/2.0 vs 0/1/2, max 500.0 vs 500.

Axis 2 is why this landed here rather than in its own task: it is almost certainly a coercion
artifact in the shared currency parse path, and THIS task already owns the binance (x2) and
bybit fetchCurrencies reds. Check for one root cause across all four before scoping to a venue.
Evidence: the task-441 reviewer diffed expected-vs-actual on #17 in full; neither residual can
be caused by 441's four alias-string edits.

Task 430 re-froze priv/specs/json/ccxt/ts/src/test/static/response/ from CCXT 4.5.65 so the
response oracle and the currencies cache share one vintage. That refresh changed recorded
parsedResponse values and turned eleven replay cases red. Two are okx network-code cases and
are tracked by task 441. The review of task 430 fixed one of the rest — deribit's
`percentage`, which CCXT computes in base-class `safePosition` and our deribit slice left
unauthored — because `mix check.dispatch` gates deribit's replay directly and was red on it.
The remaining EIGHT were absorbed into
test/fixtures/fixture_replay_failures.json with an honest but interim annotation: "the recorded
parsedResponse changed with the vintage; our parse did not. Not adjudicated as correct-or-not."

The affected cases span four venues and three read paths:

- binance fetchCurrencies default (x2)
- bybit fetchCurrencies default
- bybit fetchPositions (linear position, hedged mode, realisedPNL)
- bybit fetchStatus
- derive fetchPositions

The deribit fix is the worked example for the rest: CCXT's `safePosition` computes
`percentage` from `unrealizedPnl / initialMargin` (truncated to 4 dp, then ×100) for EVERY
venue, so a missing `percentage` is the likely root cause of the bybit and derive
`fetchPositions` reds too — check that before treating them as separate defects. The op is
already implemented as `pnl_percentage` in `CCXT.ResponseParser`; those venues need the
authored slot, not new mechanism.

Honest baselining was the right call for task 430 — it refused to claim a green it had not
earned. But an unadjudicated entry is a parked question, and the delta gate cannot distinguish
"upstream changed its interpretation and we should follow" from "our parse has a real defect
that the old vintage happened to mask". Decide each one.

Per the repo's oracle tiering, a CCXT fixture is a tier-2 COMPATIBILITY oracle: matching it
proves we match CCXT, never that CCXT is right. Where the delta touches a divergence-prone
computed field rather than a straight key copy — the fetchPositions cases especially, which is
where inverse-vs-linear and PNL sign conventions live — confront the venue's own documented
semantics or a live response before adopting CCXT's new value.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784690256705-9aa1499a, 295eb7330447762cc64670744ad1410865a5f7af).

task.title: Make fixture-replay baseline drift visible to dispatch-scale runs
acceptance_criteria: A diff that changes a first-class venue's request shaping, endpoint selection, or response parse cannot land with a stale or regressed fixture baseline without a dispatch-visible check going red

The signal works in a COLD harness worktree within the dispatch-scale time budget (the existing deribit slice is the cost reference; the full gate is ~50s and the broad fixture suite is permanently red on the long tail by design)

The existing --only exchange_deribit line in check.dispatch is generalized rather than duplicated per venue, and its file-path + bare-tag shape is preserved (an --include fixture_replay ORs the filters and pulls in the whole suite)
A deliberate_divergence baseline entry going green still fails loudly rather than prompting --update
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate pass
out_of_scope: Adjudicating any individual red fixture (tasks 442 and its siblings own that)
Introducing a broad all-venue fixture gate that is permanently red on the unauthored long tail
task.body:
mix check.dispatch gates fixture replay for exactly ONE venue -- deribit, via a
`--only exchange_deribit` line with a comment explaining why it was not made broader.
For the other six first-class venues there is no dispatch-scale signal at all, so an
implementer changing okx or derive request shaping never sees a red when the fixture
baseline drifts. The gate that would catch it, mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate, runs only
because CLAUDE.md tells the reviewer in prose to run it.

Observed twice in one wave on 2026-07-20: task 441's implementer removed a baseline
entry assuming its fix made it green (it did not) and reported the gate as passing;
task 440's implementer never completed the gate and shipped a stale baseline after the
fix turned four okx cancelOrders fixtures green. Both times check.dispatch was green
throughout and only the reviewer caught it.

This is the repo's own "encode it as a criterion or CI, not as prose someone remembers"
rule applied to itself. Derive the venue scope from the diff's touched paths (an authored
spec under priv/specs/json/output/authored/<venue>.json, a lib/ccxt/unified/request_shape/
<venue>.ex, a venue carve doc) and run the venue-scoped gate for exactly those venues --
generalizing the deribit line rather than adding a permanently-red broad gate. A
count-only comparison of baseline entries for touched venues is an acceptable cheaper
alternative if the full per-venue replay does not fit the cold-worktree budget; state
which you chose and why.

task.title: Derive option instrument ids do not carve into unified symbols on read paths
acceptance_criteria: A Derive option order read back through fetch_open_orders carries the unified symbol, not the raw instrument id, verified live on api-demo.lyra.finance
The carve works in BOTH directions (normalize and denormalize) and option rows round-trip
The YYYYMMDD-vs-YYMMDD expiry mismatch is reconciled with the existing write-path alias in RequestShape.Derive rather than duplicated
The wrong-but-observed pin in derive_authored_integration_test.exs (assert_order_lifecycle/5, expected_read_symbol) is flipped to the unified symbol
Positions/trades/greeks option rows are checked for the same leak and either fixed or shown unaffected
The carve is recorded in docs/authored-spec-carves/derive.md; mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate pass
out_of_scope: Perpetual symbols, which already round-trip correctly
The derive editOrder request build
Other venues' option symbol grammars
task.body:
CCXT.Symbol.from_exchange_id/3 cannot parse Derive's option instrument grammar
BASE-YYYYMMDD-STRIKE-C/P (e.g. ZEC-20260925-800-P), so it returns the native id
unchanged. Every read path that backfills a symbol from the venue payload therefore
leaks the raw instrument id into %CCXT.Order{}.symbol, and the same very likely applies
to positions, trades and greeks rows for options.

Verified live 2026-07-20 on api-demo.lyra.finance during task 379's review: a created
option order read back through fetch_open_orders carried symbol "ZEC-20260925-800-P"
instead of "ZEC/USDC:USDC-260925-800-P". Perpetuals are unaffected (ETH-PERP ->
ETH/USD:USDC works). Offline reproduction: CCXT.Symbol.from_exchange_id("ZEC-20260925-800-P",
ex, :option) returns its input.

Note the expiry-format asymmetry before authoring: CCXT denormalizes to a SHORT YYMMDD
expiry while Derive lists the full YYYYMMDD date. The write path already bridges this via
an alias in RequestShape.Derive -- reconcile the general carve with that alias instead of
adding a second, divergent mapping.

The task-379 integration test currently pins the WRONG-but-observed value with a comment
naming this gap (the implementer had weakened it to `assert is_binary(parsed_symbol)`,
which passes on any string; the reviewer restored a real assertion against market.id).
Flipping that pin to the unified symbol is part of this task.

acceptance_criteria: The derive editOrder request build binds each unified key to its own venue field; the CCXT static request fixture no longer shows direction/limit_price/nonce all carrying the instrument name
The EIP-712 order signature is threaded through editOrder, reusing RequestShape.Derive.build_create_order/3's order-envelope path rather than duplicating signing logic

Zero resting orders before and after the live test

The option symbol read-path carve
Turning any deliberate_divergence baseline entry green

Task 379 fixed derive createOrder and cancelOrder and explicitly left editOrder out of
scope. editOrder still exhibits the identical defect: the CCXT static request fixture
replay shows direction, limit_price and nonce all bound to the instrument name
("LBTC-USDC") while the unified keys ride through untranslated, and no EIP-712 order

task.title: Carve registers can assert a weaker evidence tier than the ledger records; the consistency gate does not catch it
acceptance_criteria: The carve-register consistency test cross-references each carve id against docs/prod-verification-ledger.md and fails when a register entry's evidence tier contradicts a closed ledger entry for that id, naming the venue, carve id and both claimed tiers

The gate fails on an OVERSTATED claim: a carve asserting CONFIRMED/tier-1 without both observed or recorded venue behavior and a provider-owned semantic source is reported; official documentation alone, a ledger status alone, or CCXT evidence can never upgrade a carve to tier 1

A supersession mechanism exists that does not rewrite append-only history - a later dated status entry for a carve id is read as authoritative over earlier *Verification:* lines and exposes semantic_source, observed_evidence, compatibility_reference, and resolved_tier

Deliberate-divergence fixture-baseline entries and divergence contracts resolve through a registered carve and its current machine-readable evidence tier rather than carrying an ungrounded correctness claim
The alpaca C-T428a/b/c entries resolve to their true live-verified tier through that mechanism (the audit's hand-appended closure note is replaced by or expressed in the machine-checkable form)

Every existing register is swept once and any other tier contradiction found is either corrected via the supersession mechanism or recorded as a known gap with its reason; future entries do not use an unqualified Oracle label
The gate runs in the default offline suite (not behind an excluded tag), and mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Re-verifying any carve against a live venue - this task reconciles recorded evidence claims, it does not gather new evidence
Changing the append-only rule for carve registers
The ledger's own entry format and the prod-verification-ledger template
Fixture-gate output labels and tier wording - owned by Task 459
task.body:
Found during the post-merge audit of a8c8eac4 (range 4c7c19be..a8c8eac4).

A carve register entry states its evidence tier in a `*Verification:*` line, and
the registers are append-only - so once a carve is written as
"documentation-anchored; the live probe has never run - no credentials", nothing
updates that line when the credential gap later closes and the venue IS observed.
The register then understates the evidence tier indefinitely, while
`docs/prod-verification-ledger.md` carries the true, closed state.

Observed instance (fixed by hand in the audit commit, so it is evidence, not an
open red): `docs/authored-spec-carves/alpaca.md` carried a reviewer banner reading
"None of them is live-verified: no ALPACA_API_KEY/ALPACA_API_SECRET is provisioned
in any environment this repo has run in", and each of C-T428a/b/c said "has never
run - no credentials". The ledger's alpaca entry had already closed on 2026-07-20
("authored stocks slice live-verified (task 428, C-T428a/b/c/d; closed
2026-07-20)") with 3/3 green live integration tests against `data.alpaca.markets`
and real recorded 200 bodies frozen into `alpaca_authored_slice_test.exs`. The
audit appended a closure note; the per-carve lines are still stale by the
append-only rule.

`test/ccxt/carve_register_consistency_test.exs` already gates ids, uniqueness,
task-scoping and dangling prose references, but it never reads the ledger and
never looks at the `*Verification:*` lines - so this class passes every check.

Both directions of drift matter, and the second is the dangerous one:
- Understated (the observed instance): the register claims tier 2/3 when the
  ledger closed at tier 1. Wastes future work re-verifying, and misleads a
  reviewer into thinking a slice is weaker than it is.
- Overstated: a register claims CONFIRMED/tier-1 with no closed ledger entry and
  no live evidence behind it. This is the failure the whole oracle-tier doctrine
  exists to prevent (CLAUDE.md: "DO NOT treat a green CCXT-fixture gate as
  verified against reality"), and it is currently unenforced.

The provider-owned contract is the authority. Tier 1 therefore requires two
separate facts: observed or recorded venue behavior, plus the venue's own
documentation, specification, or SDK establishing semantic meaning. CCXT runs,
fixtures, and source remain compatibility/reference evidence only. Carry that
provenance explicitly through register supersessions, divergence contracts, and
the fixture baseline instead of letting a bare `Oracle:` label imply correctness.

Note the doctrinal constraint: registers are append-only, so the fix is NOT to
rewrite stale `*Verification:*` lines in place. Design the mechanism so a
supersession is expressible and machine-checkable - e.g. a dated closure/status
entry the gate reads as authoritative over earlier lines for the same carve id.
Decide the shape by reading the existing registers and the ledger format; the
audit's hand-written alpaca closure note is one candidate shape, not a mandate.

task.body:
Promote Binance Coin-M into the ten-venue runtime contract using the generic promotion gate. Produce one complete self-contained owned spec and confront its DAPI public, authenticated and trading semantics against the live Binance API and Binance's own documentation. Use CCXT and the completed Binance-family defect tasks as references, not as runtime inheritance or correctness oracles.

The venue is promotable only when the required public reads, private account/order reads and a safe order lifecycle are live-green and every remaining method is explicitly supported or unsupported. Preserve the inverse COIN-M ontology rather than copying spot or USD-M assumptions. Run with Codex GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh reasoning effort.

Unblocked 2026-07-25 — the COIN-M demo wallet is funded and the full lifecycle was
observed live. Do not re-derive these facts; confront and extend them.

Environment: BINANCE_FUTURES_TEST_API_KEY / _API_SECRET authenticate COIN-M.
The authored spec's `testnet.urls` MUST use the demo hosts
(`https://demo-dapi.binance.com/dapi/v*`, `https://demo-fapi.binance.com/fapi/v*`),
matching authored binance.json and binanceusdm.json. Today's runtime resolves
`https://testnet.binancefuture.com/dapi/v1` only because binancecoinm still loads the
frozen CCXT-derived sibling — there is no authored/binancecoinm.json yet, which is this
task. This is a consistency requirement, not an open confrontation: Binance's own
COIN-M docs name demo-dapi as the testnet base, and both hosts returned byte-identical
account/balance payloads for the same key, so they are one account, not two
environments.

Funding: COIN-M and USD-M are separate wallets in that one account. The UI faucet
credits USD-M only (observed: fapi wallet BTC 0.01 / USDT 4999.76 / USDC 5000 while
dapi read 0 across all 52 asset rows). The dapi wallet was funded separately and now
holds BTC 0.01 plus ~50 other coins. There is no API faucet and, with no spot/sapi
wallet in this environment, no API transfer into COIN-M — a drained COIN-M wallet is
re-funded through the UI, so the integration test must not assume it can top itself up.

Account shape: `dualSidePosition: true` (Hedge Mode). Orders therefore REQUIRE an
explicit `positionSide`; omitting it fails -4061 "Order's position side does not match
user's setting." An order beyond available margin fails -2019 "Margin is insufficient."
Both are real, pinnable error observations — use them for the required error evidence
instead of manufacturing an invalid-parameter error. `/dapi/v1/account` reports 96
position slots while `/dapi/v1/positionRisk` returns 144 rows; that asymmetry is
unexplained and is a carve to confront, not to normalize away silently.

Observed lifecycle (BTCUSD_PERP, 1 contract = 100 USD notional, limit BUY at 50% of
mark 63915.14, positionSide LONG, GTC): create -> orderId 3378350551 status NEW price
31957.6 origQty 1 executedQty 0 pair BTCUSD; fetch by orderId -> NEW, avgPrice 0.00;
delete by orderId -> CANCELED; 0 open orders after; `DELETE allOpenOrders` returns
`{"code":200,"msg":"The operation of cancel all open order is done."}` even with
nothing resting, so it is a safe idempotent cleanup hook.

Known adjacent defect, out of scope here: -2019 currently classifies as
`:exchange_not_available` (a transient-looking retry class for a permanent business
error) because `error_codes` loads only the top-level `exceptions.exact` map and never
the market-type-scoped `inverse`/`linear`/`option`/`spot`/`portfolioMargin` sub-maps.
Do not paper over it inside this promotion; assert the class you actually observe.

to native `after=T` with an exclusive boundary. Do not follow CCXT's omission of
`until`, and do not approximate the contract by filtering only the newest page.

- https://my.okx.com/docs-v5/en/#rest-api-account-get-positions-history
- https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/trick_en/#pagination

EEA-demo success/error evidence. Preserve Task 454's existing local `since`
contract; global pagination design remains out of scope. The Sol pin is deliberate
because this is live-semantics and regression-critical work.

task.body:
The signing/request side has no reality oracle at all: the replay gates assert
our built request against CCXT's static request fixtures (vintage 4.5.57,
VINTAGES.md) — pure tier-2, blind to a shared CCXT bug, and the venue_compare
sweeps that DO prove live request parity persist nothing (out/ is gitignored).
For auth, the only real authority is acceptance: the exchange verified the
signature over these exact bytes.

Design and freeze an exchange-acceptance request oracle: capture the request our
signer produced when the live testnet/demo accepted it, scrub secrets, and gate
offline by deterministic re-signing (the timestamp/nonce override hooks the
fixture-replay harness already honors). Signing is 95%-coverage-tier critical
code; raise coverage first where below. Where an acceptance golden contradicts a
CCXT static request fixture, the golden wins and the divergence is registered —
that is the point of the task.

The repo vendors exactly one API corpus: CCXT itself (priv/specs/json/ccxt/).

artifact anywhere under the repo), so tier-1 sources are not re-runnable and
every session re-fetches ad hoc. Fix the asymmetry: vendor each first-class
venue's own artifacts with full provenance, structurally parallel to (and above)
the CCXT tree.

Authority ranking per venue is a judgment call — prefer first-party
machine-readable specs, fall back to pinned docs snapshots; record what was
chosen and why in the manifest. Respect upstream licensing: reference-by-hash

task.body:
Error semantics currently flow one way from CCXT: authored error_codes maps were
read out of CCXT JS handleErrors, and nothing checks them against the venues'
own published error tables (binance errors doc, okx/bybit error-code pages,
deribit RPC error list, derive JSON-RPC codes). A code CCXT mislabels — or that
the venue has since retired or repurposed — stays wrong invisibly, the exact
shared-bug class the tier doctrine exists to catch.

Vendor the official enumerations as authority artifacts, then make the authored
mappings answerable to them by test. Where the vendored table and CCXT disagree,
the table wins and the divergence gets registered; where our sweep evidence
already recorded live error parity (venue_compare mutation error-compares),
cite it instead of re-probing.

Closing this needs a populated body: a discounted testnet or production account, whose raw extended summary is retained and compared field-by-field against every parsed %CCXT.TradingFee{}. task.title: Make vacuous-on-empty private replay assertions self-declaring
acceptance_criteria: A populated fixture that re-captures as empty causes a visible signal (failure or explicit downgrade note), not a silent green
Every populated list-returning fixture asserts at least one value binding against its raw wire row
Empty-body cases emit an explicit 'shape-only evidence' marker in test output or manifest
task.body:
CCXT.PrivateRecordedResponseReplayTest's assert_private_shape!/3 for :fetch_open_orders / :fetch_positions / :fetch_my_trades uses `is_list` plus `Enum.all?(parsed, &struct-match)`, which passes VACUOUSLY when the captured body is empty — Enum.all?([], _) is true. 10 of 21 list-returning private fixtures currently hold empty bodies (empty testnet accounts), so those cases assert only that the parser returned a list. That is honest given account state, but it is indistinguishable in the gate output from a populated case that genuinely bound values, so corpus coverage reads stronger than it is.

Make the distinction mechanical: have each fixture's manifest (or a derived helper) record whether its body is populated, assert value bindings whenever it IS populated, and emit an explicit 'empty-body: shape-only evidence' note otherwise — so a fixture that silently goes empty on re-capture cannot quietly downgrade a tier-1 cell to tier-0 while staying green.

Evidence: measured during task 457's review (run run-1784675193786-6a57550e): of 21 list-returning private fixtures, 10 have max body array length 0. Related but distinct from task 459 (oracle-tier labels in gate output).

task.title: Lighter test helper crashes with :epipe on normal Port teardown, polluting every check run
acceptance_criteria: A full `mix check.dispatch` run contains no `Writer crashed (:epipe)` line, no `ErlangError ... :terminated` stacktrace originating in test/support/fixtures/lighter_helper.exs, and no stray `Usage: elixir` banner

The existing Lighter Port tests (test/ccxt/signing/lighter_test.exs, lighter_native_test.exs, lighter_protocol_test.exs) still pass unchanged, including the helper-crash-does-not-kill-the-VM and restart-on-next-request cases
A write failure that is NOT a closed-port teardown still surfaces as a loud error rather than being swallowed; a test pins that distinction
out_of_scope: Any change to CCXT.Signing.Lighter, its Protocol, Worker, or Supervisor production code
Changes to the real C helper in native/lighter_signer
task.body:
The fake Lighter signer helper used by the Port tests writes a response frame to stdout after the owning port has already closed, so an ordinary teardown raises and dumps a crash report into the output of every `mix check.dispatch` run:

    [error] Writer crashed (:epipe)
    ** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :terminated
        (elixir) lib/io.ex:308: IO.binwrite/2
        test/support/fixtures/lighter_helper.exs:28: CCXT.Test.LighterHelper.handle_operation/5

followed by a spurious `Usage: elixir [options] ...` banner. Observed independently in the check.dispatch logs of runs run-1784675195760-6368f864 (task 456) and run-1784675197779-f3a02219 (task 445), and by the post-merge audit agent. The suite is green and the exit status is 0 — this is output noise, not a failing assertion, which is exactly why it is corrosive: a reviewer scanning a check log for `error` hits a stacktrace that means nothing, and a real crash in the same helper would be indistinguishable from the routine one.

Make the helper treat a closed port as an ordinary end-of-stream and exit quietly, while keeping genuine write failures loud. Do not silence the crash by swallowing all errors from the write path — a helper that can no longer report a real protocol fault would be worse than the noise.

acceptance_criteria: The docs.derive.xyz /private/order schema is cited for whether label is accepted on create

Any other unified write field
Promoting Derive beyond its current authored scope
task.body:
`CCXT.Unified.RequestShape.Derive.put_label/1` copies a unified `clientOrderId` into Derive's native `label` field, but `build/4` applies it only on the `"editOrder"` branch. The `"createOrder"` branch never calls it, and `build_create_order/3` rebuilds a fresh params map copying only known keys — so a `clientOrderId` supplied on create is silently dropped and never reaches the wire. The same unified field round-trips on edit but vanishes on create, so the two write paths disagree about one identifier.

Confront Derive's own contract before choosing the fix. Read the docs.derive.xyz `/private/order` body schema — the authority for whether `label` is accepted on create and any length/charset constraint — and confirm live against `api-demo.lyra.finance` whether an order created with `label` reads that label back through `fetch_open_orders`. Two legitimate outcomes: `label` is valid on create (apply it there too and pin the round-trip), or it is replace-only (narrow `put_label/1`'s comment to the replace body and make create fail loudly rather than discard a caller-supplied identifier). Silent drop is not an acceptable end state either way.

Note `put_label/1` also leaves `clientOrderId` in the params map after copying it; it does not reach the wire today only because `build_create_order/3` allowlists keys. That latency is in scope to tidy while here.

Dispatch trigger: requires live external-system evidence against the Derive testnet plus the provider-owned body schema, on a write-path request-shape contract.

Discovered during the post-merge audit of 9592d3b7 (task 445's landed range).

task.title: Lighter native signer is unbuildable for Hex consumers and its C helper layer is unverified by the default check
acceptance_criteria: A consumer-facing doc states the Go toolchain and mix ccxt.build_lighter_signer prerequisite, or the helper build is resolved without manual steps
Attempting a private Lighter call without a built helper fails with a message naming the exact build command
The verification story for native/lighter_signer/csrc/helper.c is written down: what the Go golden test covers and what the C framing/parsing layer needs beyond it
The C helper's parsing and framing paths have test coverage commensurate with the 95% critical tier, or a recorded rationale for why the Go golden test suffices
mix check.dispatch passes and the lighter-signer workflow still builds every declared target
out_of_scope: Changing the wire protocol in CCXT.Signing.Lighter.Protocol
Promoting Lighter as an authored venue (task 451)
Shipping a prebuilt binary in the Hex package
task.body:
Task 146 landed the `:lighter` signing pattern behind an external Go helper process. Two gaps in its build and verification story remain, both on the same surface.

Distribution: `CCXT.Signing.Lighter.default_helper_path/0` resolves `priv/native/lighter_signer/<target>/ccxt_lighter_signer`, but `mix.exs` ships only `native/lighter_signer` (source) in the package files and `.gitignore` excludes the build output. A consumer installing from Hex therefore gets `{:lighter_signing, :helper_unavailable}` at first private call, and no README or CLAUDE.md text states that `mix ccxt.build_lighter_signer` (plus a Go toolchain) is a prerequisite. Decide and document the intended contract: either the prerequisite is stated where a consumer will hit it, or the build is wired to run on demand. Do not ship a prebuilt binary in the package as the fix.

Verification: `native/lighter_signer/csrc/helper.c` is ~561 lines of hand-written C on a signing-critical path, and the only things exercising it are the Go golden test and `test/ccxt/signing/lighter_native_test.exs`, which is tagged `:native` and default-excluded — so it runs in `.github/workflows/lighter-signer.yml` but never in `mix check.dispatch`. Per the repo's coverage tier, cryptographic and wire-encoding code sits at the 95% bar; today the C parsing layer is the least-covered surface in the signer. Establish what that layer's verification story is: which cases the Go golden test genuinely covers, what the C framing/parsing layer needs beyond it, and whether the native test can join a check that actually gates merges on machines with the toolchain present.

Discovered during the post-merge audit of 9592d3b7 (task 146's landed range). Distinct from task 451, which promotes Lighter as an authored venue and explicitly puts the signer out of scope.

task.title: OKX request shape carries an unregistered -USD option hardcode and silently passes through unmapped timeframes
acceptance_criteria: OKX's v5 documentation is cited for the option underlying/settlement families and for the period enumeration on the affected endpoints
A non-USD option underlying no longer silently produces a -USD request; it either resolves correctly or fails with a message naming the input
An unmapped timeframe fails locally with a message naming the supported values instead of passing through to the venue
Both assumptions are recorded as carve entries in docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md with assertions that fail if the premise breaks
mix check.dispatch passes and no previously-green OKX fixture turns red
out_of_scope: Adding OKX option trading support beyond current authored scope
Changing the position or balance request builds
task.body:
Task 434's OKX request builds landed two venue assumptions that are correct today but fail silently rather than loudly when they stop being correct.

`option_underlying/1` appends `"-USD"` to any underlying that carries no dash, so a non-USD option family would be requested against a wrong underlying with no local error. The carve text describes the assumption but nothing asserts it, so OKX listing a USDC- or USDT-settled option family would surface as a venue-side rejection or, worse, an empty result read as "no options".

`normalize_period/1` maps only `"1d"`/`"1D"` to the venue default and passes every other unified timeframe through unchanged. An unmapped timeframe therefore reaches OKX's `period` verbatim and fails at the venue instead of locally, which is the failure mode the repo's fail-loud doctrine exists to prevent.

Confront both against OKX's own contract: the v5 instruments/underlying listing for which option settlement families actually exist, and the documented `period`/`bar` enumeration for the affected endpoints. Then make each assumption explicit — either a registered carve with an assertion that fails when the premise breaks, or a mapping that rejects an unmapped value with a message naming the supported set. Do not widen either behavior speculatively; the point is that a wrong input stops being silent.

task.title: .sobelow-skips accumulates stale line-pinned entries, so any edit above a skip silently re-reds the gate
acceptance_criteria: Stale .sobelow-skips entries whose pinned line no longer matches a live finding are removed
Every surviving entry is confirmed a genuine false positive against the operator/CLI-derived-path bar
mix sobelow --skip --format compact reports zero findings after the prune
CLAUDE.md's Sobelow section records that line shifts invalidate skips and states the prune/re-mark cadence
mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Suppressing any finding that is not already an established false positive
Changing Sobelow configuration in .sobelow-conf
task.body:
`.sobelow-skips` pins each suppression as `FindingType,file:line,HASH`. The line number is part of the identity, so deleting or inserting lines *above* a suppressed finding invalidates its entry and the finding re-appears — even though the code at fault never changed. The remedy (`mix sobelow --mark-skip-all`) only appends, so the invalidated entry stays behind forever.

The file already shows the accumulation: `lib/ccxt/fixture_replay_baseline.ex` now carries three separate generations of the same three Traversal findings (lines 47/63/65, 78/101/103, and 68/91/93), of which only the last generation is live. This audit added the third generation while removing a dead function from that file — a five-line deletion cost a re-mark and left two dead entries.

Prune the stale entries and decide whether the file should be regenerated wholesale rather than appended to. Regeneration is the judgment step, not a mechanical one: deleting `.sobelow-skips` and re-running `mix sobelow --mark-skip-all` re-suppresses whatever is outstanding at that moment, so it is only safe once every current finding has been confirmed a genuine false positive (operator/CLI-derived paths, fixed-dir plus content-hash reads — never untrusted input). Confirm each surviving entry against that bar before regenerating, then record the pruning cadence in CLAUDE.md's existing Sobelow section so the next session does not rediscover the trap.

Kept human/inline per the routing gate: one file, no dispatch trigger, and the judgment about which suppressions are legitimate is exactly what should not be delegated blind.

Discovered during the post-merge audit of 9592d3b7.
task.implemented: Pruned .sobelow-skips wholesale (57 entries -> 8 live + 1 inline-comment suppression; 48 stale generations removed) after confirming all 9 outstanding findings as false positives (compile-time atom creation from vendored specs, operator/CLI paths); mix sobelow --skip reports 0; documented line-shift invalidation + regen cadence in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Sobelow section.

The existing FieldMaps-derived struct check remains green and is subsumed or preserved by the generalized mechanism

task.body:
CCXT.FixtureReplayScope.@global_scope_paths is a hand-maintained literal list of ~50 shared module paths. Task 467 existed because two real modules (recorded_response_fixtures.ex and its capture.ex) were missing from it, and 467's review found a THIRD omission (test/fixtures/responses/_manifest.json) in the very diff that fixed the first two — the same failure mode recurring inside its own fix. The list already has one self-verifying member class: the 'every governed unified response struct' test derives its paths from FieldMaps.parse_types() and asserts each resolves globally, so a new struct cannot be silently omitted. Generalize that pattern to the rest of the shared surface so membership is derived or asserted rather than remembered. Candidate approaches (author's judgment): assert every module under a set of shared-surface directories is either global-scoped, venue-regex-matched, or on an explicit reviewed allowlist; or drive the list from a module attribute/behaviour the shared modules declare. A silent-omission failure must be a red test, not a gate that skips itself.

task.title: Give authority-corpus drift checks an independent signal per artifact
acceptance_criteria: For each of the 7 venues, an upstream change reports as drift naming the artifact and its expected-vs-actual pin, distinct from a corrupted-fetch error
Covered by an offline test with a stubbed fetcher so the assertion does not depend on network
task.body:
In Mix.Tasks.Ccxt.AuthorityCheck, artifacts whose drift.url equals fetch_url have a tautological drift comparison: fetch_and_verify!/1 has already raised on any hash mismatch, so check_drift!/2 re-hashes identical bytes — true for 5 of 7 venues (deribit, derive, hyperliquid, okx, binanceusdm). Drift is still caught (via the fetch-verification error), but reported as a manifest-verification problem rather than upstream drift, misleading the reader about what changed. Only binance (pinned commit vs mutable master) and bybit (git_head vs pinned commit) exercise a genuinely independent drift signal.

Make the two signals distinct: either give every artifact a mutable drift target separate from its pinned fetch target (as binance/bybit already have), or restructure so pinned-fetch verification and mutable-upstream comparison are reported as separate, separately-named outcomes. Routing: human/inline — bounded two-file reporting change, no dispatch trigger.

Evidence: 460's review (run run-1784681237997-e25bc59a), reading check_drift!/2.
task.implemented: Restructured Mix.Tasks.Ccxt.AuthorityCheck upstream check: drift (mutable target vs pin, named expected-vs-actual) and pinned-fetch corruption are separately-named outcomes; injectable :fetcher/:git_head enable offline stubbed tests covering all 7 venues (12/12 green).

acceptance_criteria: Each of the 19 modules is either in the global scope set or on the reviewed allowlist with a one-line evidence-backed rationale recorded in the test/allowlist
The 477 guard covers lib/ccxt/*.ex non-recursively: a new unclassified top-level module fails a test naming it

task.body:
Task 477 made the shared-surface subtrees (recorded_response_fixtures, signing, unified, test/fixtures/responses) self-verifying, but the top-level lib/ccxt/*.ex surface is still membership-by-memory: 19 of 69 modules resolve to no venue scope (application, circuit_breaker, credentials, defaults, dispatch, emulation, error, exchanges, http, json_document, mcp, multi, rate_limiter, registry, response_transformer, spec, telemetry, testnet, ws). Several sit directly on the request/response path the fixture gate exercises (dispatch.ex, http.ex, response_transformer.ex, spec.ex, error.ex) — a change there can redden or silently green a venue without the diff-scoped gate running any replay.

Make a per-module decision for each of the 19: add it to CCXT.FixtureReplayScope's global scope set, or place it on the explicit reviewed allowlist with a one-line rationale. Then extend the task-477 guard to treat lib/ccxt/*.ex (non-recursive) as a shared-surface root so a new top-level module cannot ship unclassified. Ground each decision in evidence rather than intuition (e.g. mutate the module and observe whether any first-class venue's replay changes, or cite the concrete data flow) — wrongly allowlisting a replay-relevant module reintroduces exactly the silent-skip failure 477 eliminated. Resolve the named tension explicitly: over-globalizing blunts task 443's diff-scoping (a full 7-venue replay is ~50s), so the goal is an evidenced split, not a blanket sweep.

Routing: dispatch — CI/check-infrastructure and a repo-wide invariant (the same trigger as task 477). Evidence: task 477's review (run run-1784684303747-c1a0eda5) enumerated venues_from_paths/1 over all 69 top-level lib/ccxt/*.ex files; 19 return [].

task.title: Make deribit fetchTradingFees fail loudly on the nested fee contract instead of silently returning an empty map
acceptance_criteria: An offline test feeding a response whose `fees` matches the pinned OpenAPI nested shape yields a CCXT.Error naming deribit, the observed key shape, and carve C-T380a — not an empty map
The absent-`fees` branch still returns {}: the live network-tagged deribit authored suite stays green (flunks loudly on missing creds, never skips)
If market_fee_rows is shared by other venues, their legitimate empty results are unaffected (evidence named in the diff)
mix check.dispatch passes and no previously-green deribit fixture turns red
out_of_scope: Rewriting the transform to parse the nested contract (blocked on a real populated body; tracked in docs/prod-verification-ledger.md)
task.body:
Task 468 hash-pinned Deribit's own contract (priv/authority/deribit manifest, OpenAPI 2.1.1): private/get_account_summary returns `fees` as index_name -> instrument_type -> {default:{type,taker,maker}, block_trade?}, while the authored C-T380a transform (kind=market_fee_rows) reads a flat `fees[]` list keyed on instrument_type with maker_fee/taker_fee. The transform finds no matching rows, so a discounted account yields `{}` — byte-identical to the correct answer for an undiscounted account; the divergence is unobservable at the call site.

Make the divergence non-silent without waiting on a populated body: when `fees` is present but no row matches the authored carrier shape, return/raise a CCXT.Error naming the venue, the observed key shape, and carve C-T380a instead of degrading to an empty map. Absent `fees` must keep returning `{}` — that branch is live-verified correct on testnet. This is a public-contract change on the unified read path (error semantics on fetch_trading_fees), hence dispatched. Distinct from the prod-verification-ledger entry, which tracks OBTAINING a populated body; this makes the current parser's wrong answer detectable the first time one appears. Rewriting the transform to the nested contract stays out of scope until a real populated body exists.

Evidence: task 468's review (run run-1784684293060-dc4321cb) fetched the provider OpenAPI (sha256 matches the manifest pin) and read the authored transform keys — they cannot match the documented nested object; the live testnet account returns neither `fees` nor `fee_group` (15/15 network suite green).

task.title: Unify or explicitly justify the per-venue currency `active` rollup semantics (OR vs AND)
acceptance_criteria: A single documented rule governs how currency-level active derives from per-chain status for every first-class venue: either one rollup applied uniformly, or an explicitly declared per-venue authored decision with no silent default

Each venue's rollup choice is confronted against that venue's own documented chain-status semantics (okx canDep/canWd, bybit chainDeposit/chainWithdraw, binance depositEnable/withdrawEnable) and recorded in the owning carve register
A cross-venue test fails when a first-class venue's authored currency map neither declares nor inherits the documented rule - a new venue cannot silently pick up a default
Existing carves C-T442a/b/f remain true or are superseded via the dated status mechanism, never rewritten
mix check.dispatch passes and the fixture-replay gate shows no regression
out_of_scope: Changing the per-network deposit/withdraw booleans themselves
Long-tail venues - the rule and test cover the first-class set
Re-litigating task 442's deliberate_divergence entries against CCXT
task.body:
CCXT.ResponseParser.currency_network_summary/3 rolls a currency's `active` up from its
chains as `deposit OR withdraw` by default (lib/ccxt/response_parser.ex:482), but binance
and okx set `active_requires_both: true` in their authored specs and roll up as
`deposit AND withdraw`. Bybit's authored currency map simply omits the flag and inherits
the OR default, so the divergence is implicit rather than chosen. A consumer reading
`%CCXT.Currency{active: true}` gets a different guarantee depending on which venue produced
it, with nothing in the type or docs signalling the difference.

Decide the unified contract and make it explicit rather than incidental. Either (a) pick one
rollup rule, apply it to all first-class venues, and record the per-venue confrontations for
any venue that must diverge, or (b) keep the split but make it a declared, per-venue authored
decision with no silent default - require the flag to be present in every first-class authored
currency map so the OR case is chosen, never inherited. Either way, add a test asserting the
rule holds across all first-class venues so the next venue cannot pick up the default by
accident. Confront each venue's own documented chain-status semantics (okx canDep/canWd,
bybit chainDeposit/chainWithdraw, binance depositEnable/withdrawEnable), not the CCXT
fixture - CCXT leaves per-network `active` undefined entirely at 4.5.65 and cannot arbitrate.

Evidence (task 442 review, run-1784690256705-9aa1499a): C-T442b describes bybit's rollup as
"active when at least one funding direction is usable" while C-T442a/C-T442f describe binance
and okx as "active only when both directions are available" - the reviewer confirmed the split
at response_parser.ex:482 against the active_requires_both flags in binance.json:1955 and
okx.json:1893.

Dispatch trigger: public unified-contract semantics change plus a repo-wide cross-venue
invariant test. depends_on 481 because recorded confrontations append to the carve registers
481 is sweeping.

task.body: Task-224 convergence audit (2026-07-22) found 20 unexplained OKX request-gate reds in one defect class: order-domain request builds are unauthored beyond the write side (385/387 covered create/edit/cancel only). Clusters: (1) fetchOpenOrders sends raw `symbol` on the wire instead of renaming to `instId` (#144/#145) and passes CCXT's unified stop/trigger/trailing params through to plain orders-pending instead of routing to orders-algo-pending with the matching `ordType` (#146-#148); (2) fetchClosedOrders (#120-#126) omits `state=filled` and the algo/archive routing (trigger/trailing/stop -> orders-algo-history + ordType; archive-endpoint case #124); (3) fetchCanceledOrders (#189-#193) omits `state=canceled` and the same algo routing; (4) fetchOrder with an algo id (#228) is not routed to trade/order-algo; (5) createMarketBuyOrderWithCost/#88 and createMarketSellOrderWithCost/#100 return from dispatch WITHOUT any HTTP request - diagnose the short-circuit and author the cost-driven build. OKX ignores unknown query keys (C-T385e), so the raw-symbol and missing-state requests are silently over-broad, the same silent-drop class C-T385e fixed for fills. task.body:
Post-merge audit of range d810fbdf..e2c2d37e found 31 landed tasks (146, 323, 382, 434, 437-438, 442, 445-448, 452-454, 456-457, 459-460, 462, 466-470, 473, 475, 477, 479-482) with zero CHANGELOG entries, and backfilled them by hand.

This is the CLASS, not the instance: `git log --grep 'audit('` shows at least ten prior audits doing the same manual sweep (de424dc7 filled 2, 4f3902ae filled 29, 6bb2c6c5, 4c7c19be, eb4c17c9, 8f063f12, ac4a9719, e73234b0, 021b501f, bb158c8f). The structural cause is sound and should NOT be reverted: harness deliberately excludes CHANGELOG.md from delivery commits so a run diff carries only code, which means nothing in the implement -> review -> land loop ever writes the entry. The gap is therefore invisible until a human-or-audit sweep notices it, and CLAUDE.md's own rule ("A task isn't complete until affected docs are updated ... CHANGELOG.md") has no mechanical enforcement behind it.

Encode the rule instead of re-discovering it: a repo-wide invariant check that cross-references roadmap task status against CHANGELOG.md headings, wired into `mix ci`. Per the project's own doctrine, a finding caught twice by hand is a missing test — this one has been caught ten times.

Design is yours; the constraint is that the check must be mechanical (count facts: which done-task ids lack a heading), not interpretive — it asserts presence of an entry, never judges entry quality. Keep it out of `mix check.dispatch`, which is the per-run implementer gate: a missing CHANGELOG entry is not the implementer's fault under the harness exclusion, exactly as the AGENTS.md freshness gate is already scoped to `mix ci` only.

task.title: Gate CLAUDE.md's mechanical claims against the tree so doc drift fails loudly
acceptance_criteria: A check fails when CLAUDE.md names a CCXT.* module, a Mix.Tasks.Ccxt.* task, or a repo-relative file/directory path that does not exist in the tree; it passes on the current tree

The check covers the Key Modules tables, the Quick Commands / Running Tests command blocks, and the Toolchain check-command table, and reports every stale reference in one run rather than failing on the first

Counted claims that already have a machine-readable source are verified rather than trusted: the CCXT.Signing pattern count/list is cross-checked against CCXT.Signing's own dispatch clauses, and the CCXT.Application supervised-children claim against the actual child list
The check is wired into mix ci (and mix check.dispatch only if fast enough not to redden cold reviewer worktrees), alongside the existing AGENTS.md freshness gate rather than replacing it
Prose, rationale and doctrine sections are explicitly out of scope, and the implementation documents which CLAUDE.md regions it parses so a future edit knows what is gated

Deliberately-unlisted surfaces do not red the gate: the check distinguishes 'CLAUDE.md names something that does not exist' (fail) from 'the tree has something CLAUDE.md does not mention' (not a failure)
out_of_scope: Grading prose quality, doctrine, or whether a documented rule is good
Auto-fixing or auto-generating CLAUDE.md content
Changing the AGENTS.md generation/freshness mechanism (task 471 owns its unattended-firing gap)
The CHANGELOG landed-task invariant (task 486)
task.body:
CLAUDE.md is the reviewer-facing contract: AGENTS.md is generated from it, and the
cross-family reviewer grades against that generated copy. `mix ci` already gates AGENTS.md
FRESHNESS (does AGENTS.md match CLAUDE.md), but nothing checks whether CLAUDE.md's mechanical
claims are still TRUE of the tree. So a landed diff that deletes a module, renames a mix task,
or adds a signing pattern leaves CLAUDE.md asserting the old world, AGENTS.md faithfully
regenerates the stale assertion, and the reviewer grades against it.

This is the CLASS, not one instance. The post-merge audit of range d810fbdf..bc15602f found ten
drifted claims in one sweep, five caused by that very range: the CCXT.Signing row said "12
patterns" and omitted :lighter while the module's own @moduledoc (which CLAUDE.md itself calls
authoritative) already listed it; the CCXT.Application row omitted the newly-supervised
CCXT.Signing.Lighter.Supervisor; four new CCXT.Signing.Lighter.* modules had no Key Modules
rows; the venue_compare section described a two-way harness after the official-SDK third seat
landed; three new mix ccxt.* tasks were undocumented. Five were older drift the same sweep
caught: a dead docs/superpowers/... design-spec path, a FixtureReplay row still naming the
retired ccxt-distill/fixtures/signing/*.json source, a :known_defect note claiming an occupant
that no longer exists, and a "DO author" bullet pointing at the base spec path rather than the
authored/ overlay.

Prior audit commits show the same manual sweep recurring (b4362fe5 "correct stale mapping
source docs", 6bb2c6c5 "fix stale fixture-gate doc command"). A finding caught repeatedly by
hand is a missing test.

Build the check as a test or mix task wired into the CI gate. Scope it to claims that are
MECHANICALLY decidable from the tree - do not try to grade prose. The audit sweep that
motivated this verified ~188 paths by hand, which is exactly the automatable part.

Dispatch trigger (routing gate Q6): repo-wide invariant + CI/check infrastructure.

task.body: Task 486 introduced mix ccxt.changelog_check with a shrink-only baseline (test/fixtures/changelog_gap_baseline.json, 113 numeric ids + v4-adopt) whose stated purpose is to freeze debt that PREDATES the gate. It did not only freeze history: task 486 landed mid-wave, and the baseline it generated froze 38 tasks that landed in the SAME commit range (de424dc..HEAD, audited 2026-07-22): 146, 323, 382, 434, 437, 438, 442, 445, 446, 447, 448, 452, 453, 454, 455, 456, 457, 458, 459, 460, 461, 462, 463, 465, 466, 467, 468, 469, 470, 473, 474, 475, 477, 479, 480, 481, 482, 483. Only the 5 landing after the gate (484, 486, 487, 489, 490) fell outside the baseline and required real entries; those were written by the post-merge audit of this range. Consequence: 38 tasks' worth of shipped behavior has no CHANGELOG record and, being frozen, never will - the shrink-only rule means the gate will never ask for them. That is the 'ignore list absorbs real gaps' outcome the shrink-only design exists to prevent; it happened once, at baseline-creation time, because the snapshot was taken against a tree whose own wave was undocumented. Work: write entries for these 38 from their delivery commits (the 'harness: agent delivery - task N' commits and reviewer-fix follow-ups carry the substance), then mix ccxt.changelog_check --update to shrink the baseline by exactly those ids. Human/inline rather than dispatched: 38 judgment calls about what each landed diff means, driven off git history, no positive dispatch trigger; can be done incrementally since the baseline shrinks one id at a time.

task.title: Decide and encode the unified order-precision contract when markets are not loaded
acceptance_criteria: The contract is encoded, not documented-only: an order build on the real dispatch path without usable instrument precision either loads markets or fails loudly with a CCXT.Error naming the symbol and missing precision - it never silently sends an unrounded value
The same contract applies to bybit, okx, derive, and hyperliquid request shapes (no venue-local patch)
Offline request-shape unit tests that construct builds against a market-less exchange still pass, and a test pins the distinction between unit construction and the guarded dispatch path

Live evidence on at least one venue (bybit demo): an order call without loaded markets surfaces the encoded behavior (auto-load or loud error), and the normal path still produces venue-accepted grid-snapped values
mix check.dispatch green; touched request-shape modules hold the 95% critical-coverage tier
out_of_scope: Changing precision derivation itself (task 489's tickSize model stands)
Non-first-class venues
task.body:
Task 489 moved Bybit order precision from a hardcoded table to instrument metadata, which introduced (and task 489's review documented) a fail-open fallback in a money path: when `exchange.markets` is empty, the symbol is not found, or the market carries no precision, `precise_number_string/5` silently sends the unrounded value and the venue rejects it at order time (Bybit 170134). The same silent-fallback shape already exists in the okx, derive, and hyperliquid request shapes — this is the venue-agnostic contract question, not a bybit patch (dispatch trigger: order-building/money path with a public unified-API contract implication).

Decide the intended contract and encode it: either (a) unified order methods ensure markets are loaded before request shaping for venues whose precision is instrument-derived, (b) the precision path fails loudly with a CCXT.Error naming the symbol and the missing precision, or (c) the load-markets prerequisite is asserted at the unified-call boundary. A blanket raise would break the many offline unit tests that legitimately build orders against a market-less exchange, so the chosen answer must distinguish a genuine order dispatch from request-shape unit construction.

Evidence (from task 489's review, run run-1784712931983-dbed2e16): lib/ccxt/unified/request_shape/bybit.ex `precise_number_string/5` `else -> number_string(value)` swallows every miss; the new offline unit tests building against a market-less exchange return unrounded values without error; pre-489 the hardcoded table rounded spot:LTCUSDT / linear:LTCUSDT / linear:ADAUSDT regardless of market state, so those three pairs are a narrow behavioral regression.

task.title: Make Sobelow blocking and eliminate dynamic fuse atoms
acceptance_criteria: mix sobelow --skip exits non-zero when an unsuppressed finding exists (demonstrate with a temporary finding, or by removing one skip entry and observing the failure)
mix precommit and mix check.dispatch still pass green on a clean tree

The inline `# sobelow_skip` comment in lib/ccxt/circuit_breaker.ex is removed, and the DOS.BinToAtom finding is either fixed in code or carried as a hash-based .sobelow-skips entry after its false-positive status is confirmed
mix sobelow --no-skip --format compact finding count equals the .sobelow-skips entry count, so no finding is silently unaccounted for
.sobelow-skips contains no stale generations (every entry maps to a currently-reported finding)
out_of_scope: Re-triaging the pre-existing suppressed findings beyond confirming that every skip still maps to a live finding
Adding sobelow to mix ci separately (it already runs inside check.dispatch)
task.body:
The sobelow check in `mix precommit` / `mix check.dispatch` cannot fail. `.sobelow-conf`
carries `exit: false` (present since the initial project setup commit a7f0d229, i.e. an
inherited generator default rather than a deliberate choice), so `mix sobelow --skip` prints
findings and always returns success. Every sobelow finding is therefore advisory, and a new
one -- including a genuine `String.to_atom` on untrusted input, which is Iron Law #1 in
CLAUDE.md -- would land silently.

The gap is not theoretical; it is already masking a live miss. `lib/ccxt/circuit_breaker.ex`
attempts to suppress its `DOS.BinToAtom` finding with an inline `# sobelow_skip
["DOS.BinToAtom"]` comment. CLAUDE.md's sobelow section documents that inline comments do NOT
suppress under this host's invocation -- only the hash-based `.sobelow-skips` file does. So
the finding was unsuppressed at filing time: `mix sobelow --no-skip --format compact` reported
9 findings while `.sobelow-skips` held 8 entries, and circuit_breaker was the unaccounted one. Nobody noticed
precisely because `exit: false` means the gate never reddens.

Fix the class, not just the instance: make the gate able to fail, then make the outstanding
set honest. Confirm each currently-outstanding finding is a genuine false positive before
suppressing it (CLAUDE.md forbids regenerating skips while an unconfirmed finding is
outstanding), and remove the inert inline comment so it cannot be mistaken for working
suppression by a future reader.

PREMISE TO CONFIRM before suppressing: `fuse_name/1` interpolates an exchange id that appears
to come from the compile-time registry rather than user input, which would make the
BinToAtom finding a bounded-set false positive. Verify that the id cannot be attacker-supplied
on any reachable call path before adding a skip entry; if it can, fix the code instead.
task.implemented: Landed in commit 8c76149a: .sobelow-conf exit low (gate reddens on any unsuppressed finding), inline sobelow_skip comment removed, fuse names resolved via CCXT.Registry.module_for/1 (compile-time module atoms, no dynamic atom interpolation), .sobelow-skips regenerated to exact 11/11 parity with live findings

task.title: Unify order-precision market resolution so a passing guard provably implies a rounded wire value
acceptance_criteria: A public contract test enumerates every guarded venue/method pair from the production precision matrix and asserts a guard-passing build never emits price or amount off the resolved instrument grid; the test does not reach into a private module attribute
A bybit linear perp edit with no explicit category rounds on the LINEAR grid; a test pins spot-vs-linear disambiguation for the same exchange id with distinguishable steps
Live evidence on the bybit demo host: at least one grid-snapped order accepted through the unified path after the change (existing bybit_order_lifecycle_integration_test suite green)
OrderPrecision and every request-shape module actually mutated by the implementation meet the 95% critical-coverage tier
out_of_scope: Changing precision derivation itself (task 489's tickSize model stands)
Non-first-class venues
Widening the guard's field-key lists (@price_keys etc.) beyond what the shared resolution requires
task.body:
Money-path dispatch trigger: order precision on the four precision-shaping venues (bybit/okx/derive/hyperliquid) is order-building money handling.

CCXT.Unified.OrderPrecision.guard_dispatch!/4 (task 494) and each venue request shape resolve the market INDEPENDENTLY. When the two disagree, the guard passes and the shape silently skips rounding — exactly the fail-open class 494 closed one instance of (bybit editOrder without category: guard green, qty/price shipped unrounded; found and fixed in 494's review). The structural hazard remains, and its root cause is that Unified.build_final_params/5 denormalizes the unified symbol to the bare exchange id BEFORE RequestShape.apply runs, so category-sensitive venues re-derive the market from a lossy id: verified by probe in 494's review, a bybit LINEAR perp edited via bare id with no explicit category resolves to "spot" and rounds on the spot grid (amount 0.55 / price 9050 against spot 0.000001/0.01 vs linear 0.1/100 steps returned the spot-grid result) — still off the linear grid, still rejectable (the 170134 class).

Fix the CLASS, not another instance: make guard and shape share ONE market-resolution path, and thread the market-type context (or the resolved market itself) from the unified layer into the shape layer so the resolution is not re-derived from the denormalized id. Options named by the reviewer: guard consults the venue module's own resolver, or the shape reports which fields it actually rounded and the guard asserts on that report. Both probes above are reviewer-verified evidence from harness-run:run-1784719780534-4c847b50 (verdict concerns/proposals), not hypotheses.

The implementation should touch only the venue shapes required by the shared resolution design. The 95% critical-coverage gate applies to every module actually mutated; it does not require changing Hyperliquid merely to raise unrelated coverage.

task.title: Re-derive the promotion method inventory from the pinned reference at check time
acceptance_criteria: A test that deletes a method from BOTH the candidate support maps and the report's capability items is refused with a distinct gap code
The gate verifies the reference file's bytes against report.reference.sha256 and fails loudly on mismatch or missing reference
Promotions completed concurrently with this fix, including Tasks 429, 450 and 451, are rechecked against the reference-derived inventory before the runtime cutover
The existing end-to-end promotion test passes unchanged
out_of_scope: Existence-checking author-attested semantic_authority/provenance references (recorded 449 concern, separate surface)
Changing the evidence tiers or report schema beyond the reference pin
task.body:
CI/check-infrastructure dispatch trigger: this closes a hole in the repo's venue-promotion gate (task 449).

mix ccxt.promote_venue --check and --promote currently accept only --candidate and --report. Evidence.method_inventory_gaps/3 enforces that the candidate's capabilities.has and endpoints.unified key sets match the method inventory, but it derives the expected inventory from the REPORT's own capability:* items rather than from the pinned CCXT reference, and the report's pinned reference.sha256 is never re-read during the gate. Consequence: an author who deletes a method from the candidate's two support maps AND from the report's capability items produces a self-consistent pair that passes the gate, silently dropping that method from the "every method is explicitly supported or unsupported" contract. Task 449 closed the candidate-only half (:method_inventory_mismatch); the both-sides deletion remains open. Evidence (449 reviewer, run-1784726132125-d60cc97d): lib/ccxt/spec/promotion/evidence.ex:127-146 compares against capability_methods(report), not the reference; lib/mix/tasks/ccxt.promote_venue.ex:62-74 passes only candidate and report; no --reference switch exists in @switches; the existing test "candidate cannot drop a method from the prepared reference inventory" mutates only the candidate side.

Let --check/--promote take --reference (or resolve it from the report's pinned path), verify the reference bytes match report.reference.sha256, re-derive the method inventory from that reference, and fail with a distinct gap code when the candidate OR report inventory has drifted from it.

task.title: Decide the spec-driven trigger for static public trading fees instead of a hardcoded venue list
acceptance_criteria: A venue whose owned spec carries the authored static-fee signal populates market maker/taker without any lib/ venue-id edit
A venue without the signal keeps nil maker/taker (regression proving the absent direction)
binance/binanceusdm behavior unchanged (existing task-164 tests green)
out_of_scope: Authoring or verifying any additional venue's fee values
Private account-tier fee endpoints
task.body:
Task 164's reviewer fix narrowed CCXT.Unified.ReadParse.apply_static_trading_fees/2 to `when id in ["binance", "binanceusdm"]`. The function body is already fully venue-generic (reads exchange.fees from the authored spec, selects spot/linear/inverse by the market's own type flags) — only the guard is venue-specific. Consequence: authoring another first-class venue's public fee schedule into its owned spec is NOT sufficient to make it take effect; the values are silently ignored until someone edits the guard. That silent-wrong shape is the class the "author it explicitly — don't infer it at runtime" kernel targets. Evidence: post-merge audit of 4d61ce87 (.audit/4d61ce87.md § 2, commit aa917d45 — the audit intended to file this as task 496 but its roadmap write never reached tasks.toml; this task is that filing, under a fresh id).

Decide the CONTRACT: what in the owned spec signals "this venue publishes a static public fee schedule that should populate market rows" (presence/shape of the fees block, or an explicit authored flag), then replace the id-list guard with that signal. Per-venue fee-value correctness is out of scope — this is the trigger decision only.
task.implemented: Authored fees.static_market_fees as a required boolean contract, preserved it through Exchange construction, and replaced the Binance venue-id guard with the spec signal; Bybit positive/negative schema and parser tests plus Binance regressions passed.

Each symbol-scheme decision is confronted against OKX's own instrument-naming semantics with CCXT-JS as one reference; carve outcomes recorded in docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md

out_of_scope: Other venues' symbol schemes

task.body:
Live tidewave evidence (2026-07-23, okx demo via sandbox: true): OKX's unified-margin instId renaming (`_UM` infix) is not carved. All 1680 option markets carry the RAW instId as their unified symbol (e.g. symbol == id == "SOL-USD_UM-260731-48-C" — no unified grammar at all), and dated futures mis-parse `USD_UM` as a currency: "SOL-USD_UM-260724" becomes symbol "SOL/USD_UM:USD_UM-260724" (quote and settle = "USD_UM"), with "USD_UM_XPERP" appearing as a quote currency on DOGE rows. Swaps are unaffected ("DOGE/USD:DOGE"). No carve register entry exists for the OKX derivative symbol scheme — the state is inherited, not confronted (C-T398b/C-T397b cover Greeks/quantity only; tasks 257/269 built the fan-out but not identity).

This is a public-contract change (market identity / unified symbol grammar — the dispatch-trigger for agent routing): symbol-addressed unified calls on OKX options are only possible via raw instIds, cross-venue canonical addressing is broken, and the OptionSurface (task 398) joins on whatever the market carries.

Author the OKX derivative identity carve against OKX's OWN instrument-naming documentation (public instruments endpoint semantics, the `_UM` unified-margin migration notes) — confront base/quote/settle/expiry/strike/type extraction from the `_UM` grammar. CCXT-JS 4.5.x is compat reference only; premise unverified — confirm during confrontation what symbols CCXT-JS currently emits for `_UM` instIds before adopting its shape. Deribit precedent: the T-D/Deribit dated-instrument identity task (1007-way collision) defines the pattern — expiry/strike/type encoded in the unified symbol, resolving back to the correct instId on dispatch.
