acceptance_criteria: Live (www.okx.com demo, OKX_INTL_* creds, sandbox: true): every _UM market including the 2 swaps produces a canonical unified symbol with no USD_UM in quote or settle, and canonical symbols are collision-free across the full derivative+swap set (absorbs the reviewer proposal from run-1784797067322-8cfc9abd)

Pattern fallback (no loaded markets) pins in symbol_test.exs: BTC/USDT:USDT-260327 -> BTC-USDT-260327; SOL/USD:USD-260724 -> SOL-USD_UM-260724; BTC/USD:BTC-260626 -> BTC-USD-260626; EWJ/USD:USD -> EWJ-USD_UM-SWAP; HOME/USDT:USDT -> HOME-USDT-SWAP; DOGE/USD:DOGE -> DOGE-USD-SWAP
Carve register entry records the USD-family attachment condition against OKX's own USDs-contract documentation; mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate --from-diff green (tier-2 compatibility)
out_of_scope: Re-carving other venues' suffix grammars
Any change to loaded-market exact resolution (correct as landed)
task.body:
Convergence finding on landed task 503 (live tidewave verification against the www.okx.com intl demo, 2026-07-23). Two defects, one root cause: the _UM quote-settled-suffix attachment condition is mis-scoped.

(a) SWAP family missed: the live set lists EWJ-USD_UM-SWAP and SLX-USD_UM-SWAP (tokenized-equity linear perps, settleCcy USD). Their unified symbols leak the native quote: EWJ/USD_UM:USD_UM. The authored swap symbol_pattern carries no quote_settled_suffix and the swap reverse/forward paths never strip/reconstruct it.

(b) USDT-future pattern-fallback regression: native_quote_currency/2 appends the suffix whenever settle == quote, but the live grammar has 14 plain -USDT- dated futures alongside the 53 _UM ones. Without loaded markets, BTC/USDT:USDT-260327 renders BTC-USDT_UM-260327 (wrong; verified live 2026-07-23 — loaded-market resolution masks this, only the no-markets fallback misfires).

Per OKX's own USDs-contract grammar, _UM attaches ONLY to the USD-quoted unified-margin family: plain -USD- ids are coin-margined, -USDT-/-USDC- ids never carry the suffix. Author that attachment condition into the carve (extend C-T503a or add a sibling entry in docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md, confronted against OKX's USDs-contract FAQ — tier-1 semantic source), extend the swap symbol_pattern with the suffix, and fix reverse/forward so EWJ-USD_UM-SWAP round-trips to EWJ/USD:USD while USDT/USDC contracts stay untouched. Live-evidence figures above are attested by the orchestrator session; re-observe live rather than trusting them blindly.
task.implemented: Landed by harness run run-1784800268547-e5377815 (codex/gpt-5.6-sol): native_quote_currency/2 attaches _UM only when quote == USD == settle; apply_swap_pattern routes through it so USD-settled swaps gain -USD_UM-SWAP; swap reverse strips _UM via unified_quote_currency; authored okx.json swap pattern gains quote_settled_suffix; C-T503a carve extended against OKX USDs FAQ (tier-1); six fallback pins + live task_504 integration test (collision-free, no USD_UM leak, exact round-trips).

task.title: OptionProposal preflight: make the live self-fetch path usable — negative-age staleness and inverse-hedge price sourcing
acceptance_criteria: Live (Deribit testnet, DERIBIT_TESTNET_*): a preflight whose leg and hedge candidate carry only exchange: + symbol (module fetches market, greeks, quote itself) reaches quote/greeks check :ok with DEFAULT observed_at and a sane max_age_ms, and completes with a feasible sized inverse-perp hedge (BTC option leg + BTC/USD:BTC candidate) or a named non-freshness rejection
Clock-skew fail-closed intent preserved: a timestamp ahead of observed_at beyond a bounded, documented tolerance still rejects; pinned by a test

Inverse hedge sizing honors a caller-supplied candidate price/quote ahead of the market.info fallback; candidate typespec + docs updated; a test pins sizing on an inverse perp Market whose info carries no price keys
Existing option_proposal suite stays green; touched Hedge/Checks logic holds >=95% coverage (critical risk-math tier)
out_of_scope: Strategy or auto-hedge decisions
Task 401 saga execution
task.body:
Convergence finding on landed task 400 (live tidewave verification, Deribit testnet, 2026-07-23). Two defects making the module's own live-fetch path structurally unusable:

(a) Negative-age staleness: preflight defaults observed_at at call start (option_proposal.ex:63), then fetches greeks/quotes itself for exchange:-bearing legs; the fetched source_timestamp is necessarily NEWER than observed_at (fetch latency), and stale_timestamp?/3 treats age < 0 as stale (checks.ex:626). Result: every self-fetch preflight rejects with :stale_or_missing_greeks and :stale_or_missing_quote regardless of max_age_ms. Verified live: same proposal with observed_at set 15 s in the future turns both checks :ok. The age<0 guard is legitimate clock-skew fail-closed for CALLER-supplied data; module-fetched data needs either a bounded skew tolerance or comparison against fetch-completion time — implementer judgment, documented in the code.

(b) Inverse hedge price sourcing: inverse_price/1 reads only market.info keys (mark_price/markPrice/index_price/indexPrice/last/price, hedge.ex:151). A Deribit inverse perp Market from fetch_markets carries no price in info, and a candidate-level price: field is ignored (not in the candidate typespec), so :inverse_hedge_requires_price is unavoidable for the natural candidate shape. Verified live: BTC/USD:BTC candidate with price: 65753.5 still failed.

Positive dispatch trigger: risk-math/hedge-sizing surface (money-adjacent) and it blocks task 401's live evidence (an approved fresh preflight is 401's entry condition).

task.title: Pin reach.check's graded surface so check.dispatch grades the same set cold and warm
acceptance_criteria: The cold-environment red is REPRODUCED first and the environment delta is named in the completion note: a fresh worktree with no _build/deps produces reach.check findings that the warm main checkout does not, and the note states WHY the graded surface differs (scope resolution, source-vs-BEAM frontend, or reach falling back to scanning test/ when no compiled artifacts exist)

reach.check's graded surface is pinned explicitly — in .reach.exs or the mix alias, not left to reach's environment-dependent default — so the same file set is graded in a cold harness worktree and on a warm checkout

mix reach.check --arch --smells --strict and mix check.dispatch both exit 0 in a COLD worktree (no _build, no deps, bootstrap first) and on the warm checkout, and the two runs report the same graded surface

If pinning brings test/support genuinely into scope, each String.to_atom/1 site there is resolved by a validated name->atom map, a guarded String.to_existing_atom/1 with a fail-loud path, or a justified documented suppression — never a blind to_existing_atom swap that can raise on valid generator input
No test behavior changes; the probe/generator suites still enumerate the same cases, and --strict is not relaxed nor the reach step removed
out_of_scope: The lib/ atom-safety work already tracked separately (Emulation.to_method_atom, Symbol structs)
Adding new probe/generator coverage
Relaxing --strict or removing the reach.check step from check.dispatch
Refactoring the test/support generators when pinning scope resolves the red without touching them — the environment delta is the defect, the generators are only a symptom
task.body:
`mix check.dispatch` (the harness check_command) currently exits non-zero at its
final `reach.check --arch --smells --strict` step: reach reports 40 smell
findings, all in `test/support/*` (test generators and probe helpers), the bulk
being `String.to_atom/1 on dynamic input` atom-exhaustion smells. Evidence: cold
post-merge audit run 2026-07-23 on `development` (audit of range
f0408726..042aa90e); full finding list in that run's check log. None of the
findings are in application code — they are pre-existing test-infrastructure
debt (files untouched by the option-readiness tasks that prompted the audit),
so the gate step has been red independent of recent feature work, and every
harness reviewer has to hand-distinguish these pre-existing smells from any new
ones a diff introduces.

Heaviest files: test/support/test_generator/raw_endpoint_probe.ex (11),
unified_method_integration_probe.ex (6), plus symbol_public_endpoint_probe.ex,
signature_helper.ex, request_builder.ex, public_endpoint_probe.ex,
invalid_creds_probe.ex, and others. These generators legitimately turn
runtime-derived endpoint/method names into atoms, so a blind
String.to_existing_atom/1 swap can raise on valid input (the same trap
documented for the CCXT.Emulation.to_method_atom fix, task id 151). Resolve the
class: per site, use an explicit validated name->atom map, a guarded
existing-atom lookup with a clear failure path, or a justified reach suppression
where the input is genuinely a fixed compile-time set — then the gate step is
green without weakening it. Confirm whether reach.check should scope to lib/
only or keep scanning test/; if test-support is intended to be graded, it must
be clean.

Adjudication note (orchestrator, 2026-07-24): premise does NOT reproduce on the
main checkout — `mix reach.check --arch --smells --strict` exits 0 (arch OK, no
smells) on the landed base that includes the audited range, and every harness
reviewer's `mix check.dispatch` across tasks 505-509 was green including the
reach step. The red is so far observed ONLY in the audit agent's cold
environment. FIRST step of this task is reproducing the red and identifying the
environment delta (reach version / scope resolution / cold-worktree state);
if the graded surface differs per environment, the fix may be pinning scope in
.reach.exs rather than touching the generators. premise unverified — confirm
before building on it.

Reshape note (orchestrator, 2026-07-25): the adjudication above is re-confirmed and the task is
re-pointed at the real defect. Evidence today on the landed base (`eb334e63`): `mix reach.check
--arch --smells --strict` exits 0 — "Architecture Policy OK", "Cross-Function Smell Detection (no
issues)" — and both harness runs landed this session (tasks 511, 514) reported check.dispatch exit 0
including the reach step. So the generators are NOT the defect: `.reach.exs` is literally `[]`, i.e.
the graded surface is never pinned and reach resolves it from the environment. The same command
therefore grades a different file set in the audit agent's cold worktree (no `_build`/`deps`) than on
a warm checkout — that non-determinism is the bug, because it makes the harness check_command's
verdict depend on where it ran, and forces every reviewer to hand-separate pre-existing smells from
new ones. Fix the determinism (pin the scope), and only touch the generators if pinning legitimately
brings `test/support` into scope.

Routing changed human -> codex for the same reason: a harness run executes in a fresh worktree with
no `_build`, which IS the cold environment where the red appears — the implementer gets the repro
for free, where a warm main-checkout session cannot reproduce it at all. Dispatch trigger:
CI/check-infrastructure and a repo-wide gate invariant.

task.body:
Live-observed 2026-07-24 (orchestrator session, deribit testnet): a marketable option order
(private_get_sell ETH-28AUG26-1950-C at the bid, and again on the close buy) returns the
synchronous response with order_state "speed_bumped" and an EMPTY trades array; the fill lands
asynchronously ~1-2s later (order history then shows filled @ the limit). A cancel raced against
it returned 11044 not_open_order. Same behavior observed twice in one session.

The authored deribit order-status enum_map covers only cancelled/filled/open/rejected — the
class defect is: authored status enum_maps cover the common states and silently pass venue-
documented transient states through unmapped, so unified consumers (Order status predicates,
OptionSaga submission classification, OptionReadiness collector lifecycle polls) see a raw or
nil status for a live order.

Scope the fix as the CLASS, deribit-first: (1) confront Deribit's provider-owned order_state
enumeration (docs.deribit.com, the provider is the authority; CCXT is reference only) against
our authored enum_map, add every missing state with correct unified semantics (speed_bumped is
live/transient -> open-equivalent) and record each CONFIRMED/DIVERGE in the deribit carve
register; (2) encode the general unmapped-order-status policy at the shared parser/schema
boundary (fail-loud by default, explicit passthrough only when authored — never a silent nil)
and close every first-class status-map gap the new guard exposes in this same task; (3) verify OptionSaga
resume/classification and the readiness collector treat a transient synchronous state as
live/reconcilable, never as a definite failure and never as a fill (the empty-trades synchronous
response is not the truth — order history/positions are).

Dispatch trigger: live external-system semantics needing independent evidence + authored public
contract change (spec enum_map + unmapped-status policy).

task.title: OptionProposal: base-currency numeraire risk targets + covered-call preflight mode
acceptance_criteria: A numeraire option on the proposal contract selects quote-terms (default, byte-compatible with today's results — existing tests green unchanged) or base-terms accounting; the base-terms residual-delta math is pinned by hand-computed unit cases for a coin-settled short call and an inverse-perp hedge leg

A covered short-call proposal (short calls + sufficient held base balance, zero hedge candidates) preflights to approved with the coverage recorded in the result; insufficient coverage yields a named violation, not an approval and not a hedge-sizing crash

Live deribit testnet evidence: one preflight over a real ETH covered-call proposal with live greeks/balances reaches approved, and one deliberately under-covered variant yields the coverage violation (credentials fail loudly when missing)
Cross-venue and USDT-settled paths are untouched by the base-numeraire branch; margin-impact and hard-limit checks run in both modes
Touched modules at coverage tier; mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Automatic strike/instrument selection or roll scheduling (caller strategy)
OptionReadiness short-side evidence cells (separate task)
Fee/cost estimation in preflight
task.body:
Operator-requested (2026-07-24 session): the portfolio numeraire is the base coin (pure-ETH PM),
not USD. Today OptionProposal projects exposure and sizes hedges toward quote/USD-terms delta
targets; a base-numeraire caller needs the mirrored math: in base-currency accounting the base
coin itself is flat and the QUOTE leg is the risk, so "delta-neutral" flips.

Add an explicit numeraire axis to the proposal contract (default preserves today's quote-terms
behavior unchanged): (a) base-terms exposure projection for coin-settled options (position value
C/S in base units; residual base-delta of a short call is delta_usd - C/S per contract) and for
inverse perps (1/S payoff — its own convexity, funding in base); (b) a covered-call shape: a
proposal whose short calls are fully covered by held base balance passes preflight WITHOUT hedge
candidates — the hedge requirement is waived exactly when coverage holds (balance >= short call
amount, from the snapshot/portfolio input), margin and hard-limit checks still run; uncovered
remainder is a named violation, never silently approved. Strategy stays with the caller: the
library projects and checks, it never picks instruments or submits.

Authority: provider-owned settlement semantics (docs.deribit.com — coin-settled options and
inverse perp contract specs); CCXT is reference only. Live evidence from this session: ETH
covered-call cycle on deribit testnet 2026-07-24 (sell ETH-28AUG26-1950-C 1x @ 0.0455 ETH against
584 ETH balance, IM delta ~0.115 ETH, buyback, zero residual).

Dispatch trigger: public API/contract change on the option-proposal surface.
task.implemented: Superseded 2026-07-24 before implementation. The original task incorrectly coupled settlement coverage to risk-target approval: covered does not mean delta-neutral and must not waive an explicit target. unwind). Short-side capability — sell order acceptance, short-option margin path, buyback close,
zero residual — is a distinct venue capability the matrix cannot express today, though it is now

BTC-14AUG26-65000-C 0.01 @ 2430 with 122 USDT IM visible mid-cycle, buyback, zero residual;
deribit testnet BTC-28AUG26-65000-C 0.1 sell cycle and ETH-28AUG26-1950-C covered call 1x,
both zero residual).

Extend the evidence model with a short-side group injected through the existing run(evidence: ...)
channel (mutate: false default unchanged): sell fill, short-margin observation, buyback close, and
baseline-relative cleanup. Surface it as an ORTHOGONAL capability/side-status; do not add another
winner to VenueRow's single scalar status precedence, because a venue may be both buy-fill-ready
and short-fill-ready. Mechanical validation stays in code; degraded/broken judgments remain
AI-only via apply_judgment.

Evidence must carry enough provenance to prevent a timestamp-only map from certifying the wrong
venue, environment, instrument, or lifecycle, and cleanup must compare against the pre-cycle
baseline rather than demand a globally empty account.

Deribit's transient speed_bumped order state (task 511) means synchronous sell responses may carry
an empty trades array. This task consumes reconciled order-history/position evidence; task 511 owns
polling/parser behavior, so the write-sets remain independent. Numeraire/coverage math lives in

task.title: Make %CCXT.OrderBook{} level arity a real contract, and confront okx's count-or-id column
acceptance_criteria: FIRST verification move is a live call against the real okx API plus at least one venue whose rows carry no third column (bybit); the completion note records the actual calls and the observed raw row shapes

The %CCXT.OrderBook{} @doc, typespec, and struct validators agree with what the parser actually emits — a consumer written strictly against the documented level shape works on okx, bybit, binance, deribit, and hyperliquid live, with no silent fall-through

The okx count-or-id column question (CCXT's index-2 deprecated liquidated_orders vs index-3 num_orders) is confronted against OKX's official v5 order-book documentation and recorded as a CONFIRMED or DIVERGE entry in docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md, citing the live row as evidence

If the chosen contract diverges from CCXT's parseBidAsk output, the divergence is registered: the fixture_replay baseline entry carries deliberate_divergence: true naming the carve id, so a future session cannot clear it by chasing a green fixture
A regression test pins level shape per first-class venue from captured raw envelopes, and a level carrying unexpected extra columns fails loudly rather than silently reaching the consumer

mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate is green for the touched venues (or its baseline is updated with an annotated reason); mix check.dispatch green; touched parse/struct modules meet >=80% coverage before mutating
out_of_scope: WebSocket order-book frames and delta application
Order-book depth/limit request-param semantics
Level-shaped fields on other unified read paths (trades, OHLCV)
Wholesale fixture re-capture via mix ccxt.record_fixtures
Fixing quantex's own level parsers (consumer-side hardening is already in flight there)
task.body:
Reported by quantex (BUGS.md 2026-07-25) as "okx leaks 3-element levels". Re-verified live by the
orchestrator 2026-07-25 — the symptom is real but the reported root cause is WRONG, and the fix is
not an okx patch. Two coupled defects, one diff:

(1) CONTRACT DISAGREEMENT (ours, unambiguous). `lib/ccxt/order_book.ex` documents bids/asks as
`[price, amount]` pairs and types them `[[number()]]`, while the order-book parse deliberately keeps
up to three elements per level. Doc and code disagree, so a consumer pattern-matching the documented
pair shape silently falls through on any venue whose rows carry a third column. Decide the contract
and make doc, typespec, parser, and validators agree — either normalize every level to exactly
`[price, amount]` and park extra columns in `:info`, or keep CCXT's variable arity and document it
with a pair accessor consumers can rely on. Justify the choice against the venue contract, not
convenience, and state it in the carve register.

(2) INHERITED CARVE (okx, tier-1). Live raw okx row is `[price, sz, liquidated_orders, num_orders]`
(observed 2026-07-25: `["64070.7","866.05","0","35"]`). CCXT JS `parseBidAsk` defaults
`countOrIdKey = 2` and okx.ts calls `parseOrderBook` with the defaults, so CCXT — and therefore we —
surface okx's DEPRECATED always-zero `liquidated_orders` as the third element and discard the
meaningful order count at index 3. bybit is 2-element only because bybit.ts overrides the side keys
and its rows have no third column. Copying CCXT's index choice here is inherited, not confronted:
confront it against OKX's own v5 order-book documentation (see priv/authority/okx/manifest.json) and
record CONFIRMED or DIVERGE in the okx carve register with the live row as evidence.

Consumer impact, live-probed by quantex: the failure is SILENT, not loud — `Orderflow.imbalance`
returns a plausible neutral `0.0`, `heatmap_points` returns `[]`, `dom_level` raises
FunctionClauseError, and `Execution.split_order` reports `:unfillable` against a 600+ unit top level.
A bot would trade on the neutral reading.

Generalize past okx: audit level arity across the first-class venues so the answer is a
whole-surface contract, not a per-venue special case, and make an unexpected level shape fail
loudly instead of passing extra columns through to consumers.

Dispatch trigger: public contract + typespec change on a unified struct every venue flows through,
plus a tier-1 confrontation that needs live venue evidence and provider-owned docs.

task.title: Error classification silently drops market-type-scoped exception sub-maps
acceptance_criteria: A spec-driven test asserts that for every authored first-class venue, every error code declared anywhere under errors.handle_errors.exceptions is reachable by classification for at least one market type — an unreachable code fails the test naming venue, sub-map and code, so a future authored spec cannot add a dead sub-map silently

Classification selects the scoped sub-map by the market type the request was issued against, and the scoped entry wins over a conflicting top-level entry; a code present only in a scoped map resolves to that map's class

The conflicting-class cases are pinned by offline tests: -2019 resolves to insufficient-funds under inverse and linear but to the portfolioMargin class under portfolioMargin; -4061 resolves differently under option vs portfolioMargin — no test asserts a single flattened class for a code the spec scopes

Live on the COIN-M demo host (BINANCE_FUTURES_TEST_API_KEY/_SECRET, sandbox: true): an oversized far-from-market order returns -2019 and classifies as a permanent non-retryable class, NOT :exchange_not_available; the assertion in test/ccxt/binancecoinm_promotion_integration_test.exs is updated to the corrected class in the same change

The chosen class for each confronted code is justified against Binance's own error-code documentation or priv/authority/<venue>/errors.json — not against CCXT's mapping alone — and the confrontation outcome is registered in the carve register as CONFIRMED or DIVERGE
The deribit flat-map shape ({"11051": "OnMaintenance"} with no exact key) stays reachable — a regression test pins it
The binance / binanceusdm decision (lift the scoped maps into the authored errors slice, or deliberately declare them out of the authored contract) is made explicitly and recorded, not left implicit
mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate and mix check.dispatch pass; no previously-passing error-classification case turns red — prove by diffing the failing-name set against the base commit
out_of_scope: Redesigning CCXT.Error's 17 error types or the class hierarchy — the mapping TARGET is unchanged, only which spec entries feed it
Re-transcribing or extending the vendored authority error enumerations (task 461 territory) — this task consumes them, it does not author them
The market-type-scoped http_exceptions / error_code_fields slices, unless the same selection mechanism covers them for free
Hedge-mode -4061's own semantics beyond its classification — the positionSide requirement is documented and already pinned by task 450
task.body:
`CCXT.Exchange.exceptions_section/2` (lib/ccxt/exchange.ex:1604) reads only the
top-level `exact` / `broad` sections of an authored spec's
`errors.handle_errors.exceptions`. When a spec ALSO declares market-type-scoped
sub-maps, every code in them is silently unreachable — no warning, no gate, no
test. Classification then falls through to a default class, so a permanent
business error can present as a transient retry class.

Measured on the landed tree 2026-07-25, authored binancecoinm declares five
scoped sub-maps that classification never reads:
`inverse.exact` (46 codes), `linear.exact` (24), `option.exact` (77),
`portfolioMargin.exact` (~125), `spot.exact` (~78) — roughly 350 mappings
dropped, against 107 that are loaded.

The observed symptom, pinned live on the COIN-M demo host: an oversized order
returns `-2019 "Margin is insufficient"`, a PERMANENT business error, and
classifies as `:exchange_not_available` — a transient-looking retry class that
invites a caller to retry an order that can never fill. `-2019` is genuinely
absent from top-level `exact` and present only in the scoped maps. Task 450's
integration test deliberately asserts the wrong-but-observed class rather than
papering over it, so that assertion must be corrected here.

A naive merge is WRONG and would be a second defect: the scoped maps disagree
with each other on purpose. `-2019` is `InsufficientFunds` under `inverse` and
`linear` but `OperationFailed` under `portfolioMargin`; `-4061` is
`ExchangeError` under `option` and `InvalidOrder` under `portfolioMargin`. The
correct class depends on which market type the request was issued against, so
selection — not flattening — is the deliverable.

Scope this as the CLASS invariant, not as a binance patch. Two shapes exist in
the tree today and both must be handled or explicitly rejected: authored
binancecoinm carries the scoped maps inside `errors.handle_errors.exceptions`,
while authored binance and binanceusdm carry only `exact` there and keep their
scoped maps in the frozen `raw.describe.exceptions` projection (299 spot / 169
portfolioMargin / 163 option / 90 linear / 46 inverse). Decide deliberately
whether the authored slice must be lifted for those two, and register the
outcome — do not leave one venue's codes reachable and another's dead by
accident.

Confront the intended class against Binance's own error-code documentation and
the vendored authority enumeration in `priv/authority/<venue>/errors.json`, not
against CCXT's mapping alone — CCXT is one reference here, the venue's table is
the authority (tier-1 pairing per docs/authored-specs.md). Pin the corrected
classification with a real live error, not a fixture.

Note the shape that is already correct and must not regress: a spec whose
`exceptions` map has NO `exact` key (deribit: `{"11051": "OnMaintenance"}`) is
read via the flat-map fallback and IS reachable today.

task.title: Author each supported venue's oracle profile instead of inferring graded sets from exemption lists
acceptance_criteria: Every supported venue carries an authored oracle declaration naming whether the tier-2 CCXT static corpus, the private real-recordings corpus, and live tier-1 evidence grade it, with a recorded reason for each declined oracle
The spec schema validates the declaration and fails with a named per-venue gap when it is missing or incomplete
A test fails when any supported venue declares zero grading oracles
The fixture-replay gate's graded-venue set and its uncovered-venue announcement derive from the declaration, with no filesystem probing and no exemption constant
The private-capture floor derives from the declaration, so excluding a venue from the tier-2 gate no longer removes it from the private-recordings floor
Removing alpaca's tier-2 declaration still yields exactly one uncovered-venue announcement and no empty --only exchange_alpaca replay run
mix check.dispatch passes and the fixture-replay baseline is byte-unchanged
out_of_scope: Adding tier-2 CCXT static-corpus coverage for alpaca or any venue that currently declines it
Promoting an eleventh venue
Adding or changing any oracle implementation
Editing the frozen reference corpus
task.body:
Which oracles grade a venue is currently INFERRED from file existence plus two
hand-maintained subtraction lists, which contradicts this repo's authored-not-inferred
doctrine and makes promoting venue eleven a scavenger hunt across three files.

Three orthogonal facts are collapsed into one derived list today:

1. runtime-supported (the runtime-support manifest — the single source task 173 established)
2. graded by the tier-2 CCXT static corpus
3. ships a private tier-1 real-recordings corpus

`RecordedResponseFixtures.first_class_venues/0` computes (2) as "supported venues that
have a static response fixture on disk, minus a `@no_static_gate` constant" — alpaca is
excluded there because its 41 vendored cases are CCXT's crypto reading of an equities
broker and were never a graded oracle for us. The fixture-replay gate then reads that
same list for its uncovered-venue bucket. Fact (3) lives somewhere else entirely: a
`-- ["lighter"]` subtraction inside a test. So one list silently drives two gates, and
excluding a venue from the tier-2 gate also drops it from the private-capture floor.

Replace the inference with an authored per-venue oracle declaration — the venue states
which oracles grade it, and every consumer reads that declaration instead of probing the
filesystem or subtracting a constant. Where the declaration lives (the authored venue
document vs the runtime-support manifest) is the implementer's call; what matters is that
it is one authored fact per venue, validated by the spec schema, with each `false` carrying
its reason.

The payoff is the invariant this makes expressible and enforceable: no supported venue may
be graded by zero oracles. That is a real correctness floor the current shape cannot state,
and it is exactly the kind of whole-surface rule that has to be CI rather than prose.

task.title: No signing pattern may exist that no supported venue routes to
acceptance_criteria: `mix ccxt.classify_signing` still reports all ten supported venues resolving to a pattern, and the reported pattern set is exactly the set the signing layer declares
The four unreachable patterns are absent from `lib/ccxt/signing.ex` (moduledoc table, `@type pattern`, recipe pattern list, `sign/4` heads) and their modules are deleted

A test fails when a declared signing pattern is routed to by zero venues in `priv/specs/json/runtime_support.json`, and fails when a supported venue resolves to a pattern the layer does not declare — demonstrated by temporarily reintroducing one orphan and one unknown pattern
The CLAUDE.md `CCXT.Signing` row and pattern list name only the surviving patterns, and `mix ccxt.claude_check` (which gates that list and its count) passes
Signing modules stay at the 95% critical-tier coverage gate
`mix check.dispatch` green
out_of_scope: Changing how any surviving pattern signs, or touching `CCXT.Signing.HmacRecipe`'s executor semantics
Adding or promoting a venue
Pruning WS subscription or WS auth patterns (task 463 covered the subscription side; WS auth is untouched here)
task.body:
The ten-venue cutover (task 173) closed runtime support, and four of the twelve declared signing patterns are now unreachable: `:hmac_sha256_passphrase_signed` (was kucoin), `:hmac_sha512_nonce`, `:hmac_sha512_gate` (was gate), `:hmac_sha384_payload`. Verified 2026-07-26 with `mix ccxt.classify_signing`: all ten supported venues resolve across only eight patterns (`:hmac_sha256_query` x3, plus `:hmac_sha256_headers`, `:hmac_sha256_iso_passphrase`, `:api_key_secret_headers`, `:deribit`, `:derive`, `:hyperliquid`, `:lighter` x1 each).

Prune the four unreachable patterns from every surface that declares them — the `@moduledoc` pattern table, the `@type pattern` union, the recipe-executor pattern list, the `sign/4` dispatch heads, their four modules under `lib/ccxt/signing/`, and the tests and generator helpers that enumerate them. Signing is a critical-tier surface: a pattern nobody can reach is untested reachable-looking code in exactly the place where dead branches are most expensive to reason about.

Then encode the invariant so it cannot silently recur: a test asserting that every pattern the signing layer declares is resolved to by at least one venue in the runtime-support manifest, and (the other direction) that every supported venue resolves to a declared pattern. Today the correspondence is prose in a doc table; the next promotion or removal should redden a test, not drift.

This is the signing sibling of task 463, which pruned the WS subscription patterns left without a hand base by the same cutover. Same disposal rule applies: re-adding a venue re-vendors its pattern shape from git history or `ccxt_client_bak` — deleting now costs nothing a promotion cannot recover.

Note the shared-file constraint: `lib/ccxt/exchange.ex` carries the `signing_pattern` typespec reference and is also the write target of task 515, so these two must not run in the same parallel wave.

task.title: Author the error-classification market scope instead of inferring it from base-URL text
acceptance_criteria: The exception scope for a request is read from the authored spec, not derived from base-URL path segments or host labels; `error_scope_for_url/1` and both `@error_scope_*` module attributes are gone from `lib/ccxt/exchange.ex`

A supported venue that authors no scoped exception sub-map resolves to no scope for every one of its base URLs — asserted for all seven non-binance-family venues, so the alpaca/bybit/derive/hyperliquid false-positive 'spot' scope measured on the landed tree cannot recur

`CCXT.Spec.Schema` fails with a named per-venue gap when a venue declares a scope for which it authors no exception sub-map, and when it authors a scoped sub-map no declaration routes to — demonstrated by temporarily breaking each direction

Live on the COIN-M demo host (BINANCE_FUTURES_TEST_API_KEY/_SECRET, sandbox: true): an oversized hedge-mode limit order on BTCUSD_PERP still returns -2019 and still classifies as `:insufficient_funds` with `retry_class: :non_retryable`; the offline tests pinning -2019 as `:operation_failed` under portfolioMargin and the -4061 option-vs-portfolioMargin split stay green
Deribit's flat exception map (codes at the top level, no `exact` key) still classifies unchanged — the existing regression test stays green
`mix ccxt.fixture_replay_gate` shows no baseline delta, and `mix ci` (check.dispatch plus dialyzer) is green
out_of_scope: Changing which class any error code maps to, or the scoped sub-maps' contents — this task moves WHERE the scope comes from, not what it resolves to
The market-type-scoped http_exceptions / error_code_fields slices, unless the same declaration covers them for free
Adding scoped sub-maps to a venue that has none today
task.body:
Task 515 fixed the real defect — market-type-scoped exception sub-maps were
unreachable, so binancecoinm's `-2019 "Margin is insufficient."` classified as a
transient retry class. The fix is live-verified (see acceptance criteria). But the
MECHANISM it introduced selects the scope by parsing the base URL, and that
contradicts this repo's authored-not-inferred doctrine in the one module that is
supposed to be venue-agnostic.

`CCXT.Exchange` now carries two Binance-shaped constants — `@error_scope_by_api_prefix`
(`api`/`sapi`/`dapi`/`eapi`/`fapi`/`papi`) and `@error_scope_host_suffixes` — and
`error_scope_for_url/1` derives the scope from a URL's first path segment or host
label. Venue judgment lives in a hardcoded table in shared runtime code, not in the
authored spec, which is exactly the class of inference tasks 173 and 516 removed
elsewhere.

Measured live on the landed tree 2026-07-26 by resolving every supported venue's
base URLs through `error_scope_for_url/1`: four non-Binance venues already resolve
to a scope they never declared — alpaca (`https://api.alpaca.markets`) -> "spot",
bybit (`https://api.bybit.com`) -> "spot", derive and hyperliquid
(`api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz`) -> "spot". Their classification is unaffected TODAY
only because none of them authors a `spot` exception sub-map, so the lookup returns
an empty map. The moment any venue authors a sub-map whose key collides with one of
the six Binance scope names, a Binance URL-naming heuristic silently selects it —
and error classification is precisely where a silent wrong selection is expensive,
because it decides retry-vs-permanent for a caller.

Replace the inference with an authored declaration: the venue states which
exception scope each of its API sections/base URLs classifies under, the schema
validates that every declared scope names a sub-map the venue actually authors
(and vice versa), and the runtime reads that declaration. Then delete the two
hardcoded tables and `error_scope_for_url/1`. Deribit's flat code map and every
venue with no scoped sub-maps must keep resolving to no scope.

The three binance-family specs are the only venues that need a non-empty
declaration; the other seven declare none.

task.body:
Doctrine pivot (operator decree): the only verification oracle is frozen reality; CCXT JS is
authoring reference only. Step one is making provenance COMPUTED instead of declared, so it can
never be forgotten (binancecoinm was skipped by hand-tagging in task 464) and so venue eleven
acquires provenance the moment recordings land, with or without CCXT data.

Rewrite CCXT.OracleProvenance as a derivation. The mechanical chains exist in-tree:
js_method -> CCXT.Unified.method_atom_for_js_name/1 -> descriptor return_type -> parse_type
(@parse_types_by_return_type / FieldMaps.parse_types/0) -> normalization.field_maps.<parse_type>;
js_method -> endpoints.unified -> endpoint config sections -> auth.sign_recipe.<section>;
fetch_markets recordings + RecordedResponseFixtures.infer_market_type/1 -> markets.patterns.<type>.
Known partiality (handle explicitly, never silently): the relation is many-to-one (one populated
fetch_ticker must not bless fetchTickers/fetchMarkPrice — hence contributing-methods reporting
and method-level evidence for critical slots), parser_plan returns :none for write/order-book
methods, and some venue field_maps keys are outside the struct vocabulary (hence the extension
map). The vocabulary is binary verified/unverified — the tier 1/2/untagged triple does not
survive into the new gate's output.

Keep the surviving OracleProvenance functions the ledger conflict check needs
(open_ledger_entries/tier_one_ledger_conflicts adapted to the binary+host-class model).
The old percentage ratchet stays alive in parallel until the gate flip task retires it.

task.body:
Three venues have zero-to-one recordings (alpaca 0, lighter 0, binancecoinm 1) and the other
seven have critical-slot holes. Under the computed-provenance model this is the wave that earns
the verified claims: capture profiles + live recordings via the existing mix ccxt.record_fixtures
/ mix ccxt.record_accepted_requests machinery, using the provisioned testnet/demo credentials

requires positionSide and the demo faucet funds USD-M only).

The authority ladder applies: live venue behavior is the truth; recordings freeze it; provider
docs give fields their meaning. A venue whose evidence is genuinely unreachable with our keys
gets an honest open ledger entry, not a silent gap.

This wave also feeds task 157 (scheduled drift lane = re-record + diff on this corpus).

SCOPE AMENDED (2026-07-26, orchestrator, from wave-2 review evidence): (1) The landed
critical_slot? marks EVERY safely-recordable exact code in the 8 safe error classes as

task.title: Decide the client's remaining vendored reference slice: recorded seeds or documented carry
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.ReplayExchange seeds its market and currency caches from manifest-registered recordings, or priv/reference_cache/ is documented as a deliberate vendored slice with the reason it cannot be a recording — one or the other, decided and written down, not left implicit

Whatever stays vendored is reachable from a fresh clone with no extra step: the offline suite (mix test.json, no network tags) and mix ci are green on a clean checkout, proving no tracked test path depends on a gitignored directory

task.body:
Rescoped 2026-08-05 — the repository split delivered most of this task's original body as a
side effect, and the part that survived changed shape.

As filed (2026-07-26) this task targeted one repository and asked to evict `priv/specs/json/ccxt/`
behind a manifest-pinned fetch. That directory now exists in both repositories with opposite
meanings: in the workbench it is the 110-document reference corpus the repository exists to hold,
so evicting it there is incoherent; in the client it is already gitignored and untracked, holding
only the two upstream pin files, so the eviction criterion is already satisfied there. The two
authored-spec tests named in the original criteria no longer read it — only comments mention it —
and `Bourse.ReplayExchange` (the former `build_exchange!`) now seeds from a purpose-built ~1 MB
slice under `priv/reference_cache/`, not from the CCXT static caches.

What genuinely remains is a smaller and more honest question the split exposed. The client still
tracks 19 MB of reference documents under `priv/specs/json/output/` plus `reference_corpus.json`
plus the 1.1 MB `priv/reference_cache/`, and none of them carries a written reason for being
vendored rather than fetched. Decide each, and make the decision legible: a recording-backed seed
where a recording can carry the semantics, an explicit documented carry where it cannot. The
answer may well be "keep it vendored" — an offline suite that needs no network is worth 20 MB —
but that has to be a recorded decision rather than an accident of the move.

One invariant the split makes load-bearing: the client's slice and the workbench's corpus pin the

task.body:
`Bourse.fetch_ohlcv/3-4` has no working call shape on alpaca. The bare call returns
`{:ok, []}`, and the documented `since` option returns HTTP 400
`"unexpected query parameter(s): since"` because it is forwarded to the venue unmapped.

The defect is in the authored request slice, not the parse layer: alpaca returns HTTP 200
with an empty bar set when no window is given, so task 256's "empty collections are
success" invariant is behaving correctly — we are asking for nothing. Author the
`fetchOHLCV` request slice so the unified time-window and pagination options map onto the
parameters alpaca actually accepts, in the same spirit as the bybit `category` injection
authored under task 171.

Authority is Alpaca's own market-data documentation for the bars endpoint (what `start`,
`end`, `limit`, and `timeframe` mean, their formats, and the default behaviour when a
window is omitted) plus observed live responses; CCXT's alpaca implementation is reference
material only. Confront the carve rather than inheriting one: decide deliberately whether a
window-less `fetch_ohlcv` should synthesise a default lookback, or should fail loudly
instead of returning an empty success — a silent `{:ok, []}` that can never be non-empty is

register.

task.title: Whole-surface unified-read contract guard: no raw envelopes, no collapsed multi-row responses, no un-normalized symbol keys
acceptance_criteria: A suite-wide test walks every venue's __unified_endpoints__ read methods and asserts the returned value is a unified struct or a list of them — never a bare map carrying the venue's own envelope keys (code/msg/data, jsonrpc/result, retCode/result)

A static coverage assertion fails the suite when any venue declares capabilities.has == true for a read method that has no endpoints.handlers.parse slice — the absence of a parse slice must be loud at test time instead of silently returning the transport envelope at runtime
The same guard asserts a venue response containing N rows does not reduce to a single row, and that symbol-keyed results are keyed by unified symbols rather than venue ids
The guard runs against manifest-registered recordings so it gates offline, and mix ccxt.oracle_gate stays green

The coverage assertion's exclusion list is written out per venue as the authoritative enumeration of the gap — 246 method-venue cells measured at filing — and every entry names task 550 as its tracking task
Live spot-check on at least two venues confirms the guard's verdict matches real API behavior, not just the recordings
out_of_scope: Authoring the missing parse slices the coverage assertion enumerates — task 550 owns draining that pool, venue by venue
Fixing the individual violations the runtime guard surfaces — those are the sibling class tasks 537, 538 and 539
Write/mutation response shapes (task 358 owns the transport-envelope contract for writes)
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04 (ten venues, ~400 unified fetch_* calls against real sandboxes) found the raw-envelope leak class alive on okx (fetch_deposit, fetch_withdrawal, fetch_open_interests return {"code","data","msg"}), deribit (fetch_liquidations, fetch_status return the JSON-RPC envelope) and binanceusdm (fetch_positions_risk returns bare %{"brackets" => [...], "symbol" => ...} maps).

This class has been patched venue-by-venue at least five times already — tasks 200, 239, 258, 380, 485 — and keeps coming back because nothing asserts the contract across the whole surface. Two adjacent shapes belong to the same guard: binance fetch_bids_asks returns ONE ticker where the venue returns 1373 (verified live: GET /api/v3/ticker/bookTicker on testnet.binance.vision is a 1373-element array; we hand back the first, a test-coin row), and binance fetch_last_prices keys its result by raw exchange ids ("BTCUSDT") instead of unified symbols.

Build the guard so the sixth venue-specific patch is impossible: a unified read either returns typed structs or fails the suite. Per critical-rules, a defect class caught twice by hand is a missing test.

Note 2026-08-04 — the scale of the pool, measured before dispatch. Taking the set difference between each authored spec's capabilities.has == true keys and its endpoints.handlers.parse keys gives bybit 47, binance 44, okx 43, binanceusdm 42, hyperliquid 30, deribit 22, derive 13, binancecoinm 3, lighter 2 — 246 method-venue cells declared supported with no parse slice, alpaca the only venue at parity. Measured from the loaded specs, not estimated: comparing bare counts understates it, because several venues carry parse handlers for methods they do not declare (binancecoinm shares the binance parse table), which masks their own misses. The three venues the sweep caught are samples from that pool, and so were tasks 200, 239, 258, 380 and 485. This changes what the task delivers: the guard must fail on missing parse coverage statically, not only on the runtime shapes the recordings happen to exercise, because a cell with no recording is exactly the cell that leaks. It also means the exclusion list this task writes is large by construction and is not a defeat — it is the enumeration nobody has had until now. Draining it is task 550; do not attempt it here, and do not shrink the guard to make the list small.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via coalesced run run-1785800307483-5b7e01ab; reviewer-approved (c2683e7531231b6010d6925c934e40c479783bb1). 533: static parse-coverage guard (79 read cells enumerated, all tracked to 550) + manifest-replay runtime contract guard. 537: un-carved read path returns a typed %Bourse.Error{} instead of raising.

acceptance_criteria: Endpoint selection picks the candidate whose section ranks highest in the market-type priority list, not the first entry in the config list — pinned by a test using a venue whose config order and priority order disagree

A manifest-wide test asserts no mapped unified method is unreachable by construction: for every venue and method, at least one documented param combination resolves an endpoint, or the method is not mapped at all

Methods that legitimately need a disambiguating param produce an error naming a param set that actually works — an error asking for type/subType/symbol when no value of those resolves is itself a failure
out_of_scope: Adding new unified method mappings (sibling coverage tasks own that)
Plural-symbols routing, which task 340 already closed
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04. Selection takes the first matching config in the endpoint-config list rather than the first section in priority order, so binanceusdm fetch_positions_risk, fetch_account_positions and fetch_leverages all resolve to fapiPrivate_get_leveragebracket and return leverage brackets. Verified live: fetch_positions_risk returns %{"brackets" => [...], "symbol" => "KAVAUSDT"}. /fapi/v1/positionRisk is mapped and never reached.

Second face of the same defect: @spot_sections lists only public and v1, omitting the private and sapi sections that spot's authenticated endpoints actually use — so six binance spot methods refuse with "ambiguous multi-endpoint selection" even when the caller passes type: "spot". A/B evidence from the sweep: the same call with type: "swap" resolves cleanly to fapiPrivate. Spot callers cannot reach those methods at all today.

Third face: binanceusdm fetch_open_interest_history and fetch_long_short_ratio_history map only to fapiData/dapiData sections, which appear in no branch of the market-type table — no param combination can ever resolve them, while the error message advises passing type/subType/symbol. bybit fetch_option_markets and okx fetch_positions_for_symbol fail the same way.

task.title: Funding cadence must come from observed venue data, not an authored constant — deribit reports 8h for an hourly venue
acceptance_criteria: Deribit fetch_funding_rate reports the venue's real cadence, derived from provider-owned data rather than a literal default in the field map
The correction is registered in docs/authored-spec-carves/deribit.md with the measured evidence and the authority cited
A test asserts no authored funding field map supplies interval as a bare literal default for any venue — the cadence is answerable to venue data or explicitly carved with evidence
Live verification: the reported interval matches the observed spacing of the venue's own funding history rows, for deribit and for at least one venue whose cadence differs
deribit normalization.field_maps.funding_rate_history stops being null: rows parse to typed structs instead of raising
out_of_scope: Rewriting funding math for venues whose cadence is already correct (hyperliquid reports 1h correctly today)
Historical funding-payment reconciliation
task.body:
Measured live 2026-08-04, directly against the venue: GET /api/v2/public/get_funding_rate_history on test.deribit.com over a 12-hour window returns 12 rows, every gap exactly 60 minutes, each row carrying both interest_1h and interest_8h. Deribit publishes hourly.

Our authored spec sets normalization.field_maps.funding_rate.field_map.interval to the literal {"default": "8h"} and fetch_funding_rate duly reports "8h" for every deribit call. The 8h figure traces to CCXT's own averaging window for computing a snapshot rate, which was carried over as if it were the venue's cadence. A consumer annualizing from interval is off by roughly a factor of eight.

This is the domain-ground-truth failure mode critical-rules names explicitly: the constant is internally consistent, fully covered by tests computed from the same constant, and therefore ratified rather than caught. The same spec has normalization.field_maps.funding_rate_history set to null, so history rows stay raw maps and the read path raises KeyError when it tries to backfill the symbol.

Fix the deribit value, and encode the invariant so the next venue cannot inherit a cadence constant unchallenged.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1785808429317-c512b1d8, 1ac7174012903ee018b7ccd6ead57c56032ce328).

acceptance_criteria: fetch_canceled_orders returns only orders the venue reports as canceled; fetch_closed_orders returns only filled/closed ones — asserted against a live account holding both
The filter is applied for every venue whose spec routes these methods to a shared all-orders endpoint, not special-cased for one venue
Live evidence: a real venue response containing a mix of canceled and filled rows, with the unified results asserted to partition it correctly
A test pins that the three methods do not return byte-identical result sets when the underlying account has mixed order states
out_of_scope: Venues that expose genuinely separate canceled/closed endpoints and already partition correctly
Order write paths
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04 against binance USD-M demo. fetch_canceled_orders, fetch_closed_orders and fetch_orders all resolve to the same all-orders endpoint family with no status post-filter. Verified directly: all three return 28 identical rows with raw status frequency %{"CANCELED" => 6, "FILLED" => 22}. A caller asking for canceled orders gets 22 filled ones.

The same class was found on binance spot in the same sweep. Task 435 fixed the mirror-image defect on derive (open orders returning canceled ones), so the vocabulary and unified Order status predicates already exist — this is the filter step, applied where the venue hands back one undifferentiated list.

task.title: Unified read parsing raises instead of returning a typed error on legitimate venue responses
acceptance_criteria: okx fetch_funding_rate_history no longer raises KeyError :symbol — it returns typed structs or a %Bourse.Error{}
binanceusdm fetch_position_adl_rank handles the venue's documented empty-object no-data response without raising
A venue response the parser cannot map yields {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} naming the venue and method — never an escaping exception from a public unified call
Live evidence per case: the real venue response that triggers each raise, pinned by an integration test
The all-nil-struct detection stays intact — this task must not turn a loud parse failure into a silent empty result
out_of_scope: The response-shape extraction defects owned by the unified-read contract guard task
Changing which endpoint a method selects
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04. Three raises escaping public unified calls:

okx fetch_funding_rate_history("BTC/USDT:USDT") raises KeyError: key :symbol not found in %{"instId" => "BTC-USDT-SWAP", ...} — the backfill step assumes a struct where the parse produced a plain map.

binanceusdm fetch_position_adl_rank raises "Unexpected response shape: parsed to an all-nil struct" on GET /fapi/v1/adlQuantile returning HTTP 200 with body {} — a legitimate no-positions answer for an account holding none.

deribit fetch_funding_rate_history raises through the same symbol-backfill path once the venue returns real rows, because that venue's funding_rate_history field map is null (owned by the funding-cadence task).

A public unified read must fail as data, not as an exception. The fail-loud design is right; the failure mode is that it fails as a raise on inputs that are not errors.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via coalesced run run-1785800307483-5b7e01ab; reviewer-approved (c2683e7531231b6010d6925c934e40c479783bb1). 533: static parse-coverage guard (79 read cells enumerated, all tracked to 550) + manifest-replay runtime contract guard. 537: un-carved read path returns a typed %Bourse.Error{} instead of raising.

task.title: Authored enum slices reject real venue values — an unmapped order status kills four hyperliquid read methods
acceptance_criteria: hyperliquid fetch_orders, fetch_closed_orders, fetch_canceled_orders and fetch_canceled_and_closed_orders succeed on an account whose history contains a min-notional-rejected order
The authored order status enum covers every status the venue's own documentation lists, with the doc citation recorded
A test asserts each venue's authored enum slices cover the venue-documented value set, so a missing arm fails at test time rather than on a consumer's account
The fail-loud behavior on a genuinely unknown value is preserved — the fix is completing the enum, not adding a permissive fallback
Live evidence: the real order history that triggers the current failure
out_of_scope: Other venues' enum slices unless the same test surfaces a documented gap
Relaxing fail-loud into silent mis-mapping
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04 against hyperliquid testnet. Four unified order-read methods fail with: Unmapped authored order status for venue "hyperliquid", field "status", raw value "minTradeNtlRejected".

The authored order.field_map.status.enum_map covers canceled, cancelled, filled, marginCanceled, open, rejected and triggered. Hyperliquid documents further statuses — minTradeNtlRejected (order rejected for not meeting the minimum trade notional) and selfTradeCanceled among them — and a real historical order on the test account carries the first. Any account with such an order cannot read its order history at all through those four methods.

Failing loudly on an unknown enum value is the correct design and must stay. The defect is that the authored slice was completed against a sample rather than against the venue's documented value set, so the test suite cannot tell a covered enum from an under-covered one.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1785804601743-f2c3711e, 000a042837707eac4402c131b168981cb2f01b68).

task.title: Field maps present but inert: populated venue fields arrive nil, and one scalar parse takes the year off a timestamp
acceptance_criteria: binanceusdm fetch_ledger populates amount, currency and type from the venue's income rows instead of returning them nil
binanceusdm fetch_funding_intervals reports the interval the venue supplies rather than nil
alpaca fetch_time returns epoch milliseconds parsed from the venue's ISO-8601 clock timestamp
derive fetch_canceled_orders maps the venue's order list instead of parsing the whole envelope into one all-nil struct
A test asserts that when a venue response carries a value for a mapped field, the unified struct is not nil for that field — the assertion covers the four cases above and generalizes across venues
Live evidence per case: the real venue response alongside the parsed struct
out_of_scope: Fields the venue genuinely does not supply — those stay nil and are registered as carves where the distinction matters
Response-shape extraction, owned by the contract-guard task
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04, each verified directly.

binanceusdm fetch_ledger returns LedgerEntry with amount, currency, type, direction, before, after, status and account all nil, while the same struct's info carries %{"asset" => "USDT", "income" => "-0.05096864", "incomeType" => "COMMISSION"}. The field map for this slot is effectively a no-op.

binanceusdm fetch_funding_intervals returns interval nil while the venue's fundingInfo response supplies fundingIntervalHours: 8.

alpaca fetch_time returns {:ok, 2026}. Ground truth fetched directly from paper-api.alpaca.markets: {"timestamp":"2026-08-03T19:07:12.706593732-04:00"}. The parse takes the leading year digits instead of converting to epoch milliseconds, so the value is four digits where every other venue returns milliseconds.

derive fetch_canceled_orders parses the whole JSON-RPC envelope into a single Order with every field nil, though the body carries 52 real orders under result.orders.

The pattern is one class: a mapped field that stays nil while the payload carries it. Assert that, rather than fixing four instances and waiting for the fifth.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1785800307483-5b7e01ab, c2683e7531231b6010d6925c934e40c479783bb1).

task.title: Time-window request params must reach the venue on every venue, not one at a time
acceptance_criteria: A caller passing since to a unified read reaches the venue with the venue's own time parameter, for every venue that documents one — asserted by a cross-venue request-shape test, not a per-venue fix
binance order-history reads accept since and limit and return the venue's filtered result; live-verified with a real success
Optional params that are nil are omitted from the request rather than serialized as empty values
A request-shape test asserts no unified read emits a query parameter with an empty value
Accepted-request goldens registered for the venues covered, and mix ccxt.oracle_gate green
out_of_scope: Pagination cursors and continuation tokens
Timeframe mapping for OHLCV, which is already authored per venue
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04 against binance spot testnet. Two coupled defects on the same path.

Passing no limit to the filtered-order reads produces -1105 "Parameter 'limit' was empty": the emulated handlers build the param map unconditionally and a nil serializes to a literal empty query value. Supplying both since and limit then produces -1104 "read 4 but sent 5", because since is never renamed to Binance's startTime — the binance request-shape module has no since handling, unlike the bybit and hyperliquid modules which do. Any binance caller passing since hits this, including plain fetch_orders.

Task 532 just closed the same class for alpaca fetchOHLCV alone. Filing the third venue-specific patch would guarantee a fourth; the deliverable here is the cross-venue assertion that a documented time window reaches the venue, with binance as the failing case that proves it.

Lighter write paths

Live sweep 2026-08-04. Bourse.fetch_open_orders on lighter fails with our own guard, "lighter requires a known market symbol to resolve market_id", before any request is built. Lighter's own API reference documents market_id as optional on the account-active-orders endpoint, defaulting to all markets, and the raw call confirms it: private_get_accountactiveorders with only account_index returns 200 with the order list.

We are stricter than the venue contract, for no reason the venue imposes. Task 531 covers the probe-side symptom and explicitly excludes product changes to unified dispatch, so the product-side loosening is unowned.

task.title: WebSocket private path never authenticates — the auth layer has no caller from the public API
acceptance_criteria: A private WebSocket subscription authenticates before subscribing — live-verified on at least two venues with different auth patterns, each showing a venue-acknowledged login rather than an auth error
watch_orders on a credentialed exchange either streams the account's order events or returns a typed error — it never opens a private channel unauthenticated
The eight authored auth pattern modules are reachable from the public API; a test asserts every WS-configured venue with an auth pattern can complete its handshake
A venue that rejects the auth frame surfaces that rejection to the caller rather than leaving the socket silently unusable
Missing credentials fail loudly with the env vars needed, never a silent skip
out_of_scope: Authoring new WS slices or the cassette harness — task 175 owns those
Venues without a WS config at all, owned by the sibling coverage task
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04. Bourse.WS.watch_orders against okx with valid demo credentials returned an :ok handle and the venue answered 60011 "Please log in" — the private channel was opened without authenticating. deribit answers no_channel_templates, and bybit and binance reject the call for a missing symbol on an account-wide order stream.

Root cause is structural, not per-venue: Bourse.WS.Adapter is where pre_auth/3 and build_auth_message/3 are invoked, and grep over lib/ finds no production caller of that module — lib/bourse/ws.ex, the public facade, never references it. Eight auth pattern modules with tests exist behind an entry point nothing calls.

This is the gap the "Early" label on the WebSocket surface was hiding. The public read path streams live on seven venues; the private path is an unwired layer.
task.implemented: Hand-built inline across three commits in the bourse repo: c7c63c0 (facade calls the handshake; a rejected handshake closes the socket), 35f85c2 (binance family — spot re-authored onto ws-api under the new :ws_api_signature pattern after Binance retired the spot listen key 2026-02-20; binanceusdm listen key issued pre-connect, authenticate: false refused with {:auth_not_optional, :listen_key}), 1843ce1 (binancecoinm on dstream with its own dapiPrivate_* key). Live differential evidence on six venues across five auth patterns: each private subscribe is accepted authenticated and rejected/silent unauthenticated. RESIDUAL: derive authors no auth_pattern although the venue has a WS login, so its private section still connects without a handshake — split out as its own task.

task.title: WS subscribe reports success when the venue rejects the subscription, and its return shape varies by venue
acceptance_criteria: A subscription the venue rejects yields an error to the caller rather than :ok — live-verified with a real venue rejection on at least two venues
Bourse.WS.subscribe/3 has one documented return shape across venues; the current mix of :ok and {:ok, envelope} is resolved either way, and the choice is pinned by a test
A rejection that arrives asynchronously as a frame rather than a synchronous reply is still surfaced to the caller
The subscription pattern modules accept a consistent channel shape, or reject a wrong one with a named error instead of building a malformed frame
scripts/ws_sweep/ws_probe.exs reproduces both the pass and the rejection case
out_of_scope: Private authentication, owned by the sibling WS auth task
Adding WS support for venues that have no config
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04 via scripts/ws_sweep/ws_probe.exs. Three venues accepted a subscribe call and reported success while the venue rejected it:

derive returned :ok; the venue replied that the ticker channel is deprecated in favour of ticker_slim. hyperliquid returned :ok; the venue replied with a JSON parse error. deribit returned {:ok, envelope} where the envelope carried error 13778, raw_subscriptions_not_available_for_unauthorized — so the rejection was at least visible there, but through a different return shape than the other two.

That inconsistency is the second half of the defect: a caller cannot write one correct handling of subscribe across venues, because bybit, binance, derive and hyperliquid answer :ok while deribit answers {:ok, envelope}.

Separately, the hyperliquid subscription pattern accepts only a string channel; handed a map it double-wraps into {"type":{"type":"allMids"}} and the venue rejects the frame. Sibling patterns accept both shapes, so the caller contract differs per pattern with nothing naming the difference.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1785808436828-1e5dbbb5, c443ea58731ce14c17969526ff857fe9ff25d88e).

Bourse.WS.connect on a supported venue lacking WS support returns an error distinguishable from the error for a genuinely unsupported exchange

Unified WS event normalization
binancecoinm — delivered inline by bourse 1843ce1
task.body:
Live sweep 2026-08-04. Bourse.WS.Config.supported_exchanges/0 returned seven venues against ten runtime venues; alpaca, binancecoinm and lighter had no WS config, and Bourse.WS.connect on them returned {:error, :unsupported_exchange} — the same term Bourse.Exchange.new/2 uses for a venue we genuinely do not support, though all three construct fine as exchanges. A consumer cannot tell "this venue has no WebSocket here" from "this venue does not exist here".

NARROWED 2026-08-07: binancecoinm is done, delivered inline by bourse 1843ce1 — hosts dstream / demo-dstream.binance.com, listen key from dapiPrivate_*, live-verified with an order placed and cancelled on the COIN-M wallet while a decoy-key socket received nothing. Configured venues are now eight; alpaca and lighter remain. The error-distinguishability criterion was never addressed and still stands for both.

Both remaining venues do publish WebSocket APIs, so the likely outcome is adding config rather than recording an absence; confirm against each provider's own documentation before deciding.

fetch_leverage_tiers, fetch_open_interest, fetch_trading_fees, fetch_ledger and fetch_adl_rank map to their existing raw endpoints and return typed structs

Response slices authored from the provider contract with evidence registered; mix ccxt.oracle_gate green

Write methods

Also unmapped with endpoints available: dapiPrivate_get_leveragebracket and dapiPrivateV2_get_leveragebracket (leverage tiers), dapiPublic_get_openinterest and dapiData_get_openinteresthist (open interest), dapiPrivate_get_commissionrate (trading fees), dapiPrivate_get_income (funding, realized PnL and transfers — a direct fit for the LedgerEntry type), dapiPrivate_get_adlquantile (ADL rank), dapiPrivate_get_forceorders (liquidation history).

acceptance_criteria: Every venue reaches parity between capabilities.has == true and an authored response parse slice — the coverage assertion introduced by task 533 passes with an empty exclusion list for that venue

boundary first. Before implementation begins, the

Every read method reachable with the provisioned testnet/demo credentials gains a recording captured through the existing mix ccxt.record_fixtures pipeline, and each is replayed through 533's runtime contract guard (no raw provider envelope, no N-to-1 row collapse, unified symbol keying)
Each newly graded method is asserted on domain meaning, not merely shape — a populated struct with the venue's real values, never is_map or a non-empty body alone

The coverage file only shrinks: a test fails if a venue's ungraded count grows, so a newly authored slice cannot enter the surface ungraded

endpoints.handlers.parse slice" and "79 do not" split rests on the same dead field task 533's
static guard measures. No runtime code reads endpoints.handlers.parse; parsing resolves through
Unified.parser_plan/2 and ReadParse's normalization.field_maps. Re-measured on 2026-08-08
against that path: 63 real gaps, only 14 of them in the 79-cell list, 65 listed cells phantom,

derived from it — must be recomputed after 564 lands. The okx fetchOpenInterests repro recorded
below is unaffected and is in fact the sharpest evidence for 564: it carries a handlers.parse
key, so the static guard passes it, while the live call returns the raw envelope.

ROADMAP REFRAME (2026-08-04): This row is a coverage tracker, not one dispatch unit. Tasks
555–556 must establish the provider-versus-authored inventory and direct live-REST capture
boundary first. Before implementation begins, the
orchestrator must turn the remaining findings into vertical venue-and-contract-section tasks,
folding them into an existing venue task when the work belongs in one session. Do not dispatch
this tracker wholesale; keep it pending until every child gap is adjudicated.

For Deribit, deduplicate those vertical tasks against tracker 557 instead of filing parallel
raw and unified recording work for the same provider section.

Task 533 landed two guards and they are both honest, but between them sits the hole this defect class has been escaping through for six tasks (200, 239, 258, 380, 485, 533).

Measured live on the landed base 2026-08-04, across the ten venues:

  392 declared read methods (capabilities.has == true, fetch*)
  313 of them have an endpoints.handlers.parse slice
   79 do not                      -> enumerated by 533's guard, owned by task 550
  246 of the 313 have NO recording -> graded by NOTHING
   84 recorded venue/method pairs exist in total

(The 246 here is a different set from the 246 in tasks 533/550, which counted reads plus writes. Coincidence of arithmetic, not the same gap — do not conflate them.)

533's STATIC guard measures declaration: does a declared read have a slice? 533's RUNTIME guard measures behavior — no raw provider envelope, no N-to-1 row collapse, unified symbol keying — but it only replays manifest-recorded methods, so it sees 84 pairs. A method that is declared, sliced, and never recorded passes both guards while being arbitrarily broken at runtime.

Live proof on the landed base: okx fetch_open_interests has a parse slice, is capabilities.has == true, and is NOT in 533's exclusion list — yet the live call still returns {:ok, %{"code" => ..., "data" => ..., "msg" => ...}}, the raw provider envelope reported as success. This is the exact invariant task 239 declared closed ("a unified read method with a wired slot never leaks the raw HTTP envelope"). It was never measurable, so it reopened.

The work is to make the runtime guard's coverage enumerable and shrinking, the same way 533 made the slice gap enumerable: every declared+sliced read is either recorded and replayed through the contract guard, or it appears in a written-out coverage gap list with a tracking reference. Nothing may be silently ungraded. Capture through the existing pipeline (mix ccxt.record_fixtures / RecordedResponseFixtures.capture_targets) — do not build a second capture mechanism.

task.title: enum_passthrough silently exempts a venue from the status-coverage test — enumerate it or drop it
acceptance_criteria: A live lighter call against the testnet host establishes the venue's real order-status values, recorded in the completion note — this is the FIRST verification move and decides which fix applies

lighter order status is either authored as an explicit enum_map covering the venue-documented vocabulary, or kept as a deliberate passthrough with a docs/authored-spec-carves/lighter.md entry stating the venue's vocabulary and why passthrough is correct

Every venue using enum_passthrough on any field appears in a written-out exemption list, each entry naming the reason and a tracking reference, asserted by a test with exact equality so the list reddens on drift in either direction
The status-coverage test from task 538 fails for a venue that has neither a covering enum_map nor a registered exemption entry — proven once by removing an entry and observing the red, then restored
The fail-loud behavior on a genuinely unknown status is preserved for every venue that does not hold a registered exemption — no permissive fallback is added to make the test pass
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Authoring missing parse slices — task 550 owns that pool
Recording coverage for read methods — task 551 owns that
Relaxing fail-loud into silent mis-mapping on any venue
task.body:
Task 538 landed a coverage test asserting each venue's authored order-status enum covers the venue's documented value set. It has an escape hatch nothing tracks.

Bourse.Spec.Schema.validate_order_status_rule!/2 accepts "a non-empty enum_map OR explicit enum_passthrough == true", and in ResponseParser.enum_fallback/3 the enum_passthrough clause is matched BEFORE the Bourse.Order status fail-loud clause. So a venue that sets enum_passthrough passes the new coverage test with zero enum arms, and every venue-native status value flows through unmapped into Order.status — the exact opposite of the fail-loud behavior 538 was filed to preserve.

Measured on the landed base 2026-08-04: lighter has enum_map arms = 0 and enum_passthrough = true for order.field_map.status. The other nine venues carry between 7 and 30 arms with no passthrough. The lighter setting predates 538 (present since the 182 rename); 538 did not introduce it, but 538's test is now the thing that would have caught it and does not.

UNVERIFIED and to be settled in this task: whether lighter's real status vocabulary actually diverges from the unified one. This session could not reach lighter live (the running BEAM has no LIGHTER_TESTNET_* credentials), so the consumer impact is asserted as a possibility, not a fact. Establish it live before deciding the fix: if lighter's venue statuses already equal the unified vocabulary, the honest fix is an explicit identity enum_map plus a carve-register entry, not a passthrough. If they diverge, Order.status and the Order status predicates are wrong for lighter today and the enum must be authored.

The general rule this task installs: an exemption is allowed to exist, but never to be invisible. Same shape as task 533's exclusions file and task 551's coverage file — the exemption set is written out, each entry names why and what tracks it, and it may only shrink.
