task.title: since is still dropped on binance spot reads — assert the returned window, not the absence of an error
acceptance_criteria: binance spot fetch_ohlcv, fetch_trades and fetch_my_trades accept since and return the requested window — verified live against the binance spot testnet, with the -1104 responses recorded as the before-state

A test enumerates every unified read that accepts a time window, per venue, and asserts the venue HONORED since: the first returned row sits at the requested boundary rather than at the latest bar — an assertion that only checks for the absence of an error is explicitly insufficient and must not be used

That test covers the venues which fail silently (bybit, okx, deribit, hyperliquid, derive), not only the venue that fails loudly, so a future lost translation reddens instead of silently returning the wrong window
Reads that genuinely cannot be window-probed with our credentials or hosts are named in a written-out exclusion list with a tracking reference, never silently skipped
until is covered on the same terms as since wherever the venue supports an end bound
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green; FIRST verification move is a live call recorded in the completion note
out_of_scope: Parse-slice coverage (task 550) and recording coverage (task 551)
binance sapi-section reads, which have no sandbox host and correctly error today
Re-fixing binanceusdm, which already honors since on all four probed methods
task.body:
Convergence on task 540, measured live on its own landed base (4996a4b263a3, 2026-08-04, binance spot testnet + binance USD-M demo).

540 wired since/until into endpoints.request.defaults for exactly one method — fetchOrders — and left the sibling time-windowed reads on the same venue broken, under a title that reads "on every venue, not one at a time".

Live, binance spot, since = now - 3d:

  fetch_orders    since+limit -> 5 orders                    OK (the method 540 patched)
  fetch_ohlcv     since+limit -> -1104 read 3 but sent 4     since never becomes startTime
  fetch_trades    since+limit -> -1104                       same
  fetch_my_trades since+limit -> -1104 read 4 but sent 5     same

The same four calls on binanceusdm all succeed, so this is binance-spot-specific, not a client-wide regression.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE FOUR METHODS. Binance rejects an unread parameter loudly with -1104, which is why this is visible at all. Every other venue silently ignores an unknown parameter: measured live the same day, bybit / okx / deribit / hyperliquid all HONOR since on fetch_ohlcv (first candle lands 0.1h after the requested since rather than at the latest bar), so they are correct today — but if any of them ever lost its since translation, the call would still return {:ok, rows} and the caller would silently receive the wrong time window. A test that asserts "the call did not error" would pass straight through that.

So the guard must assert the WINDOW, not the absence of an error: request a since well in the past, then assert the first returned row actually sits at that boundary rather than at the latest bar. That assertion is what makes the class closeable instead of patchable, and it is what this task installs. The four binance methods are its first customers, not its scope.

A static count is not a substitute for it: counting spec entries suggested 107 unmapped time-windowed reads across the ten venues, but the live probe showed most of those venues translate since in the Elixir request-shape path instead, so the static number was wrong by an order of magnitude. Measure behavior.

acceptance_criteria: All ten venue manifests enumerate the first-party contract artifacts confirmed by the implementation-time provider audit, or record a source-specific reason an identified candidate is rejected; every relied-on artifact has URL, immutable pin where available, retrieval date, byte count, SHA-256, license handling, and explicit freshness/expressiveness/scope/authority metadata

The verified 2026-08-04 source candidates are reconciled: Deribit current/upcoming OpenAPI, current/upcoming AsyncAPI, and llms.txt; Binance-family official OpenAPI/Postman/docs; Alpaca official repository OpenAPI documents; Bybit official Postman/docs; Hyperliquid official docs plus SDK sub-specifications; Lighter SDK OpenAPI; Derive llms index; and OKX official docs

task.body:
Task 460 created the ten venue manifests and fetch/drift machinery, but it explicitly excluded contract conformance. The corpus is also incomplete as a source index: the online 2026-08-04 provider-source audit found first-party artifacts not represented by the current manifests, including Deribit's upcoming OpenAPI, current and upcoming AsyncAPI, and llms.txt; Alpaca's repository OpenAPI documents; Bybit and Binance-futures Postman collections; and Hyperliquid SDK sub-specifications. Reconfirm each source at implementation time; the provider-owned upstream is authoritative and the manifest is only the local provenance index.

Make the corpus enumerate every first-party artifact we actually rely on, with separate machine-readable facts for freshness, expressiveness, authority, and scope. Current REST, upcoming REST, current WebSocket, upcoming WebSocket, and documentation indexes are separate contract surfaces. An official artifact may be partial, stale, internally inconsistent, or untyped; record that limit instead of promoting it to a completeness source. Third-party OpenXAPI material may be noted as discovery/reference input but never as semantic authority or a completeness gate.

The offline authority command currently passes while Deribit's mutable OpenAPI has moved from the pinned 1,369,497 bytes to 1,385,649 bytes. Offline validation cannot observe reference-only remote drift. Wire the cheap offline corpus/error consistency checks into the dispatch gate and extend the existing `.github/workflows/live-drift.yml` weekly lane with contract-artifact drift, preserving its summary and artifact evidence instead of creating a second workflow. Review and record a semantic diff of the moved current-REST artifact before refreshing its pin. Upcoming OpenAPI, both AsyncAPI documents, and llms.txt enter as separately scoped initial baselines, not as drift claims; never update a hash merely to restore green.

task.title: Compare provider-owned contracts with authored specs across the ten supported venues
acceptance_criteria: The comparator consumes byte-verified artifacts from the provider-authority corpus and emits deterministic per-venue inventories with artifact provenance; mutable remote content is never compared without first entering the corpus through task 554 controls

The normalized operation inventory captures path or channel, transport method, authentication, parameters, requiredness, available types, response schemas, and examples only when the first-party source actually supplies each fact; absent source detail remains unknown rather than inferred
Current REST, upcoming REST, current WebSocket, and upcoming WebSocket are separate denominators and reports; upcoming operations never count as missing from the current authored runtime

Each venue report separates provider-only, authored-only, and shared operations plus field-level differences, and states source limitations such as partial repository coverage, prose-only semantics, untyped Postman collections, missing authentication metadata, unsafe or non-paired examples, and internally inconsistent message references

The Deribit proof reproduces the current-REST counts recorded by task 554 for the exact source SHA or revision in its semantic-diff report; the dated pre-refresh 178 provider / 123 authored / 116 overlap / 62 provider-only / 7 authored-only measurement remains a regression fixture for that historical pin, not the post-refresh gate, and upcoming REST plus current/upcoming WebSocket baselines bind to their own revisions

The Deribit proof preserves the observed provider-source limits: 10 OpenAPI paths tagged WebSocket Only are not executable REST coverage, absent OpenAPI security metadata remains unknown, provider examples are documentation rather than reality, and the AsyncAPI send/receive message-reference inversion is reported rather than normalized away
All ten supported venues produce either a comparable report or an explicit source-capability limitation; no report claims full coverage from a partial or untyped source

Every operation in the union of provider and authored inventories has independently validated axes for relation (shared/provider_only/authored_only), runtime scope (unified/raw_only/carved/not_implemented/unknown), evidence (verified/unverified), reachability (safe/unsafe/unreachable/unknown), and contract scope (current_rest/upcoming_rest/current_websocket/upcoming_websocket). The comparator carries forward only registered facts, defaults missing evidence to unverified and missing judgment to unknown, and never collapses these axes into one disposition enum
Semantic changes require later provider confrontation; the tool never deletes, authors, executes, files follow-up tasks, or marks an operation verified automatically

Tests cover OpenAPI JSON and YAML, Postman, AsyncAPI, partial/prose source declarations, source omissions, independent-axis validation, and deterministic output; mix check.dispatch and mix ci are green
out_of_scope: Mutating authored runtime specs or generated exchange modules
Deciding semantic equivalence between provider operations and unified methods
Executing provider calls or capturing live evidence — tasks 556–558 own the REST proof boundaries
Treating provider examples, empty-list calls, or CCXT error parity as live semantic verification
Using CCXT or OpenXAPI as authority
Filing per-venue implementation tasks automatically
task.body:
Task 460 established the provider-authority manifests but explicitly excluded mechanical OpenAPI-versus-authored conformance. Task 554 makes that source index complete and freshness-visible. Build the missing read-only meta-layer after 554: one reusable comparator that exposes what the provider contract says, what the authored spec declares, and where they differ without pretending that syntactic equality proves semantic correctness.

Parse mechanical facts only to the degree each first-party artifact supports them. OpenAPI, Postman, AsyncAPI, SDK fragments, llms indexes, and prose pages have different expressive power; provenance, source defects, and unknown fields must survive normalization. Current REST, upcoming REST, current WebSocket, and upcoming WebSocket are different contract surfaces. Third-party OpenXAPI and CCXT may help discover candidates but may not establish semantics or completeness.

Deribit is the proof case because its pre-refresh official current OpenAPI and our authored inventory produced a dated baseline: 178 provider paths, 123 authored raw paths, 116 shared, 62 provider-only, and 7 authored-only. Task 554 records the exact source revision and its semantic-diff counts before moving the pin. Reproduce the counts belonging to the selected revision instead of hardcoding the historical baseline as a post-refresh gate; upcoming REST and WebSocket use their own initial baseline revisions. Extend the same mechanism across all ten venues, reporting honest partiality where no complete machine-readable first-party contract exists.

This task measures two-way contract coverage; it does not repair venue behavior. Its output feeds task 556's capture mechanism plus trackers 557/558's read-evidence and mutation-safety work, followed by vertical tasks by venue and contract section. Relation, runtime scope, evidence, reachability, and contract scope remain independent facts: absent evidence is `unverified`, absent judgment is `unknown`, and a missing operation is a finding to adjudicate rather than an automatic deletion or implementation order.

task.title: Build provider-operation reality capture and prove it on Deribit public REST
acceptance_criteria: The capture boundary consumes task 555's exact-revision operation inventory and preserves its independent axes; source revisions, OpenAPI paths tagged WebSocket Only, and absent security metadata remain explicit rather than guessed or collapsed into one disposition

A representative Deribit public proof set covers a parameter-free success, a parameterized success with populated domain data, and a relevant real invalid-parameter error against the official test environment without passing through unified response parsing

Each proof stores and manifest-registers the exact scrubbed raw request, raw response, HTTP status, host, capture time, operation id, and provider-artifact revision; an empty success can prove reachability but never row-field semantics

Provider examples are request seeds only and are never executed blindly; the mechanism requires an explicit reviewed reachability/safety decision and refuses private, mutating, unclassified, upcoming, unsafe, and WebSocket-only operations in this proof task

The existing recording, manifest, and mix ccxt.oracle_gate machinery is extended rather than duplicated; a provider operation becomes evidence=verified only from its registered live capture, never from an OpenAPI response example or CCXT parity
The mechanism is venue-reusable without generating runtime code from a provider contract and produces the per-operation evidence inputs that trackers 550/551/557/558 can consume
Tests prove an out-of-scope or unclassified operation cannot execute, a source-revision mismatch fails, and deleting a registered capture reddens the oracle; mix check.dispatch and mix ci are green
out_of_scope: Exhaustively capturing Deribit's public or private read inventory, owned by tracker 557
Mutating operations and their safety adjudication, owned by tracker 558
Changing authored runtime specs, generated exchange modules, or unified mappings
Capturing the other nine venues in this task
Executing upcoming REST operations
WebSocket capture or subscription behavior, which remains with the WS roadmap and scripts/ws_sweep
Treating provider examples as observed behavior or generating runtime code from OpenAPI
task.body:
Tasks 554 and 555 establish what provider-owned contracts publish and how that surface differs from the authored inventory. They deliberately do not establish what the live API actually returns. Task 551 records already-declared unified reads, so provider-only raw operations remain outside its denominator. Build the missing reusable live-REST evidence boundary and prove it against Deribit's public current-REST surface before private or mutating calls enter scope.

Online provider audit on 2026-08-04 against https://docs.deribit.com/specifications/deribit_openapi.json: 178 current paths, 170 JSON-RPC request examples, 173 documented response examples, 47 public and 131 private operations. Ten paths are tagged WebSocket Only despite appearing as GET paths. The document declares no security scheme or operation security, so private examples are not executable authenticated evidence. The published private/buy example is a real market-order request and its response example does not correspond to that request. A harmless documented public/get_time call was executed against test.deribit.com and returned live successfully, but its response differed from the documentation example. These observations make provider examples useful request seeds and semantic documentation, never reality fixtures.

Carry task 555's independent facts into the capture boundary and prove the mechanism with a small public set spanning the materially different request/response cases above. Do not turn safety judgment into verb-name heuristics or automatically execute provider examples. Tracker 557 drains the complete read inventory through later section-sized tasks, tracker 558 owns mutation adjudication, and WebSocket-only methods remain with the WS roadmap rather than curl.

This task earns a full dispatched review cycle because it changes live external-system evidence and the oracle/CI contract.

task.title: Drain Deribit current-REST read evidence by provider contract section
acceptance_criteria: The exact-revision Deribit current-REST inventory is confronted with provider-owned semantics and partitioned into one-session vertical tasks by coherent provider contract section; authentication and mutation class are not inferred from the OpenAPI HTTP verb or absent security metadata

Every provider-documented public or non-mutating private operation reachable on testnet gains a direct raw call and a scrubbed, manifest-registered request/response fixture carrying operation id, provider revision, host, HTTP status, and capture time

Each vertical task includes populated success evidence where the testnet state permits and a relevant real provider error; assertions pin domain meaning rather than generic status, map shape, or empty success

Operations needing unavailable state, roles, instruments, orders, positions, or identifiers remain in the inventory as unverified with a dated prod-verification-ledger entry naming the blocker and unblock path
Private-task credentials and sensitive response fields are redacted without destroying semantic replay; missing credentials fail loudly with exact setup instructions and never skip

The aggregate tracker closes only when every current read operation has registered evidence or an explicit unverified blocker and all resulting oracle/check gates are green

The provider-operation evidence machinery classifies the response shapes the inventory actually contains before the first array-returning section is drained: array-shaped and scalar result payloads gain row-field or reachability evidence semantics (Capture.row_fields_populated? and the validate_observation! row-field branch are map-only as landed by 556), and the JSON-RPC-specific envelope assumptions (result/error keys) are confronted per section rather than assumed venue-universal

Treating empty successful responses as field-semantic verification
task.body:
TRACKER — DO NOT DISPATCH WHOLESALE. Task 556 establishes the reusable direct-provider capture path with a bounded Deribit public proof. Once task 555's exact operation inventory exists, the orchestrator partitions the read surface by coherent provider contract section into tasks that fit one implementation/review session. The source OpenAPI omits security metadata, so deciding which methods are private reads requires provider-semantic confrontation; a GET-shaped JSON-RPC declaration is not evidence that a call is safe or unauthenticated.

Each child task calls the real testnet API and stores the raw response as a manifest-registered fixture before it changes or grades authored/unified behavior. Merge its work with 550/551 or an existing venue task whenever the same provider section belongs in one session; do not create parallel raw-capture and parser tasks for one slice. Preserve every inventory member: reachable reads gain registered reality, while role- or state-blocked reads remain visible and unverified with an actionable ledger entry. This tracker does not send mutations.

Keep this tracker human-routed. Its section-sized child tasks earn dispatched review when they handle live authenticated traffic, credential redaction, or verification-oracle evidence.

UPDATE 2026-08-12 (ARC pass on landed 556): two boundary limits of the shipped capture machinery become blockers on this tracker's first sections and are folded in as the final acceptance criterion rather than filed as siblings. (1) Row-field evidence only accepts a map-shaped JSON-RPC result (capture.ex row_fields_populated?; provider_operations.ex validate_observation!) — public/get_instruments, get_book_summary_by_currency, get_order_book and most of the read surface return arrays, so the very next section hits a raise. (2) The envelope keys (result/error.code) are JSON-RPC hardcodes; fine for Deribit, but any reuse claim beyond it (556 AC6) needs the shapes confronted, not assumed.

task.title: Circuit-breaker fuses leak across test modules, so the offline suite reports a rotating set of flaky failures
acceptance_criteria: A test that melts a venue's circuit cannot affect any other test: the offline suite runs clean across at least five different seeds with zero entries in the runner's flaky[] array, not merely zero confirmed failures

The isolation is structural rather than per-victim — a newly added test that melts a fuse must not be able to leak into an unrelated module, and the mechanism that guarantees this is named in a moduledoc or the shared case template

Bourse.CircuitBreaker's production behavior is unchanged: fuse naming, melt thresholds, and the reset API behave identically outside the test environment, pinned by the existing circuit_breaker_test assertions
A regression test proves the isolation: melting a venue's fuse in one test leaves a subsequent test in another module seeing a closed circuit
mix ci is green, including the reality oracle
out_of_scope: Changing circuit-breaker thresholds, melt classification, or which errors melt
The rate limiter and any other shared global state, unless the same mechanism turns out to cover them
Converting async: false modules back to async as part of this fix
task.body:
Measured 2026-08-05 on a clean tree, three offline runs of `mix test.json --quiet --exclude integration`:
each reported 0 confirmed failures but a **different** set of tests in the runner's `flaky[]` array —
seed A gave `Bourse.DispatchTest` + `Bourse.ExchangeAcceptanceFixturesTest`, a later run gave
`Bourse.OptionProposal.MarginImpactTest` (twice), `Bourse.OrderStatusFilterTest` and
`Mix.Tasks.Ccxt.OracleGateTest`. The victim set rotates with the seed, which is what identifies this
as shared-state leakage rather than a defect in any one test.

The mechanism: `Bourse.CircuitBreaker.fuse_name/1` returns `Bourse.Registry.module_for(exchange_id)`,
a single global atom per venue, and `:fuse` keeps that state in application-global storage for the
lifetime of the node. Any test that drives a venue into enough transport errors to melt its fuse
leaves it open for every later test using that venue, in every module, for the rest of the run.

The obvious hypothesis is wrong and worth stating so nobody re-tests it: this is **not** an
`async: true` race. Both victims in the first run — `dispatch_test.exs` and
`exchange_acceptance_fixtures_test.exs` — are already `use ExUnit.Case, async: false`, and ExUnit runs
async:false modules after every async module has finished. The leak crosses the async/sync boundary
because nothing ever resets the fuse; marking more modules `async: false` cannot fix it and only makes
the suite slower.

`Bourse.CircuitBreaker` already exposes `reset/1` and tracks `installed_fuses/0`, so the pieces for a
structural fix exist. Decide between scoping fuse names per test and resetting installed fuses between
tests, and put the chosen guarantee somewhere a future test author will read it — the failure mode of
the per-victim fix is that the sixth victim shows up two months later with the same symptom and no
memory of this task.

The runner's auto-retry currently heals these into `flaky[]` so the suite still exits 0. That is
containment, not a fix: it hides an isolation defect behind a green gate, and the same leak in a
non-retried context (the new CI workflow's package job, a consumer running the suite) reads as a real
failure.
task.implemented: config/config.exs disables the circuit breaker for the whole :test environment, so no test can install or melt a fuse by default; the three modules that assert breaker behaviour (circuit_breaker_test, http_test, fixture_gate_isolation_test) opt back in through the new test/support/circuit_breaker_control.ex, whose enable!/1 removes every installed fuse on exit. Regression cover in test/bourse/test/circuit_breaker_leak_test.exs: one module blows a fuse and proves the cleanup closes it, a second proves a module that never enables the breaker cannot melt at all — each meaningful alone, so neither depends on ExUnit module ordering. Root cause pinned by direct repro rather than inference: blowing the bybit fuse makes Bourse.Order.Builder.submit return {:error, %Bourse.Error{type: :circuit_open}} with the Req.Test stub never invoked, which is exactly the reported 'expected the plug to observe exactly 1 request, got none'. Production behaviour untouched — the config guard is config_env() == :test only.

task.title: Derive ticker maps high/low/change/percentage from a stats object the venue does not publish
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.fetch_ticker/2 on derive no longer advertises coverage it cannot resolve: the four fields sourced from the absent stats object are either sourced from a field the venue actually publishes or recorded as null
The decision is registered as a carve-register entry for derive citing the provider's own get_ticker reference, so a later session cannot re-inherit the mapping from a CCXT sample
Evidence for the absence is live and from both hosts, not documentation alone: the demo and mainnet get_ticker responses are shown to carry the same key set with no stats member
The BUGS.md entry that reported this carries a dated status pointing at the fix
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and the offline suite stay green
out_of_scope: Emulating derive's last-traded price from public/get_trade_history — the venue publishes no last field on this endpoint and populating it is a design decision, not this repair

task.body:
Live on 2026-08-05, `public/get_ticker` for `BTC-PERP` returned 36 result keys on BOTH
`api.lyra.finance` (mainnet) and `api-demo.lyra.finance` (demo) — and neither carries a `stats`
member. The authored derive ticker field map nonetheless sources four unified fields from it:
`high` <- `stats.high`, `low` <- `stats.low`, `change` <- `stats.percent_change`, and
`percentage` <- `stats.percent_change` scaled by 100. All four are therefore permanently nil.

No wrong number is produced — the fields are honestly nil — but the map advertises coverage that
cannot resolve on any host, which misleads consumers reading the spec and future authoring
sessions reading the map as evidence the venue publishes those values.

The `stats` shape appears only in the CCXT-derived descriptor's embedded sample under
`endpoints.descriptors.fetchTicker.source`, whose sample timestamp is 1736140984000 — January
2025. This is an inherited carve that was adopted from CCXT and never confronted against the
venue's own contract, exactly the confrontation step the doctrine requires. Derive's official
get_ticker reference documents the same key set the live hosts return.

task.title: Bourse.Testnet exits the calling process when unsupervised, aborting a consumer's entire test suite
acceptance_criteria: Calling a Bourse.Testnet function when the registry process is not running returns a typed error the caller can match on, instead of exiting the calling process
The registry stays out of Bourse.Application's children — a sandbox credential registry has no place in a consumer's always-on supervision tree, and the 0.1.0 decision to remove it is preserved
Every public Testnet function that reaches the process is covered, not only the one the consumer happened to call: a caller cannot find a second function that still exits
The moduledoc states that the caller starts the process and what the functions return when it is absent
Tests prove both paths: the started registry behaves as before, and every public function against an absent registry returns the typed error rather than raising or exiting
Bourse.Testnet coverage is at its tier before the change lands
out_of_scope: Re-adding Bourse.Testnet to the application supervision tree
Changing the env-var convention or which venues register_all_from_env/1 reads
Auto-starting the process on first use — a credential registry that silently starts itself hides the same problem
task.body:
Reported by trading_dashboard on 2026-08-05 (BUGS.md). A consumer calling
`Bourse.Testnet.register_all_from_env/1` from its own `test_helper.exs` gets an
`(exit) exited in: GenServer.call(Bourse.Testnet, ...)` / `no process` — which aborts the ENTIRE
test suite before a single test runs, because an exit in test_helper takes the run down with it.

The cause is not a bug in the registry: `Bourse.Testnet` is a GenServer owning an ETS table, and it
was deliberately removed from `Bourse.Application`'s children in 0.1.0 on the grounds that a
sandbox-only credential registry does not belong in a consumer's always-on tree. That decision
holds. `Application.ensure_all_started(:bourse)` does not help — the app starts fine, the child is
simply not in the tree.

What is wrong is the failure mode. A credential-registration helper that exits the caller when its
process is absent gives the consumer no way to detect the condition, no message naming what to
start, and takes down the surrounding process. Return a typed error naming the absent registry
instead, and say in the moduledoc that the caller starts it. Cover every public function that
reaches the process, not only register_all_from_env/1 — the reporter found one entry point, and a
consumer who works around that one should not discover the next.
task.implemented: Writes (register/3, register_from_env/3, register_all_from_env/1, unregister/2, clear/0) return {:error, :not_started}; reads (creds/2, creds!/2, registered?/2, registered_exchanges/0, exchanges_with_creds/0) raise ArgumentError naming Bourse.Testnet.start_link([]) rather than an opaque ETS badarg; started?/0 added. The registry stays out of Bourse.Application's children, so the 0.1.0 decision holds. Reads deliberately keep raising: their nil/false/[] returns already mean 'not registered'. Exit reproduced live via Tidewave before the fix; 8 new tests cover every public function against a stopped registry.

task.title: Per-field maps cannot address envelope-level keys, so every bybit ticker is unstamped
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.fetch_ticker/2 on bybit returns a non-nil timestamp and the datetime derived from it, live against the testnet and against the committed recording

The mechanism is general, not a bybit special case: a field map can address a key on the response envelope rather than only on the extracted row, and the vocabulary for doing so is documented where an authoring session will read it
At least one other venue whose response stamps at the envelope is checked against the same mechanism, so the carve is confronted rather than fitted to one venue
A regression test uses the existing recording — the captured envelope already contains the value the parser could not reach, so no new capture is required
The oracle gate's blind spot is closed for this class: a green gate over a recording that carries a field the parser drops no longer reads as coverage
mix ci is green
out_of_scope: Re-capturing bybit fixtures — test/fixtures/responses/bybit/fetch_ticker.json already preserves the whole envelope including body.time
Any other nil field on any other venue's ticker, unless it turns out to have the same envelope-level cause
Changing how response_envelopes extracts the row
task.body:
Live on bybit testnet 2026-08-05: `Bourse.fetch_ticker(bb, "BTC/USDT:USDT")` returns
`timestamp: nil` and `datetime: nil` on every call, while every other field populates. Not a crash
and not a wrong number, but every bybit ticker is unstampable — a consumer cannot tell a fresh
quote from a stale one, or order two tickers in time. Deribit stamps correctly from the same
unified call, so the blast radius is bybit and any other venue that stamps at the envelope.

The authored field map asks for the right key: ticker `timestamp` maps to `time` with a ms format.
But `normalization.response_envelopes.ticker.fetchTicker` extracts `result.list`, so the parser is
handed a LIST ELEMENT, and `time` sits one level up on the envelope. Verified live against
`public_get_v5_market_tickers`: `body` carries `time`, and the list element carries only
`deliveryTime` / `nextFundingTime`, both unrelated. `datetime` is nil downstream of `timestamp`.

This is a mechanism gap in the parse path, not a spec edit — there is no per-field way to reach the
envelope. Note the mechanism exists next door at a different level:
`response_envelopes.time.fetchTime` uses `fallback_keys: ["result.timeNano", "result.timeSecond",
"time"]` and does reach the envelope root. A bybit-only special case would be the wrong shape;
scope the vocabulary before implementing.

Worth stating plainly because it is the CLAUDE.md failure this repo warns about: the reality
evidence for the fix is ALREADY COMMITTED. `test/fixtures/responses/bybit/fetch_ticker.json`
(captured 2026-06-20) preserves the whole envelope with `body.time == 1781993749592`, and the list
element again carries no `time`. `mix ccxt.oracle_gate` is green over a recording that CONTAINS the
value the parser cannot reach — coverage ratifying the bug. Whatever closes this should also close
that blind spot, or the next envelope-level field will pass the gate the same way.

acceptance_criteria: derive's authored websocket.auth slice carries a real auth_pattern, or the absence is registered as a carve in docs/authored-spec-carves/derive.md with the provider evidence that the venue has no WS login
Bourse.WS.connect(exchange, :private) on derive either completes a venue-acknowledged handshake or returns the venue's rejection — it never returns an open unauthenticated socket
Live-verified differentially against api-demo.lyra.finance: a private subscription is accepted on the authenticated connection and rejected or silent on authenticate: false

Unified WS event normalization
task.body:
Residual split out of task 542, which wired the private handshake into the facade and live-verified it on six venues across five auth patterns. derive is the one WS-configured venue left where the handshake cannot run: its authored slice sets no auth_pattern, so Bourse.WS.connect(exchange, :private) opens the socket and returns it unauthenticated. The venue does have a WS login, so this is a missing slice rather than a correct nil.

The failure mode is the one 542 was filed against: a private subscription on an unauthenticated derive socket is not an error, it is an empty stream that surfaces much later as missing data.

Known trap before anyone probes this. Derive's edge proxy verifies auth BEFORE the app, so a wrong signer gets HTML 403 from nginx with no JSON body to parse. The signer must equal X-LyraWallet or be a session key registered for it: DERIVE_TESTNET_API_KEY is the Derive smart-contract wallet, DERIVE_TESTNET_API_SECRET is a registered Admin session key's private key, and the owner EOA is NOT auto-registered on UI onboarding. Budget the probe for a 403 that looks like a network failure.

Kept inline (assignee human) rather than dispatched: the load-bearing step is an exploratory live confrontation against a venue whose auth surface we have not yet observed, so the acceptance criteria cannot be written ahead of the answer. Re-route once the handshake shape is known.

task.title: The parse-coverage guard measures a dead CCXT descriptor field: 65 of its 79 tracked cells are phantom and 49 real leaks are invisible
acceptance_criteria: The static coverage assertion derives its denominator from the runtime parse path — the parser slot resolved from the method descriptor's return type, plus the venue's normalization.field_maps entry for that parse type — and never from endpoints.handlers.parse, which no runtime code reads

Two named cases pin the metric in both directions and fail the suite if either flips: fetchTime on bybit and deribit is NOT a gap (read_parse.ex hard-wires it to :parse_time and it parses to an integer), and okx fetchOpenInterests IS a gap (task 551 records the live raw-envelope repro)

Parse types whose do_parse/8 clause bypasses field maps entirely (time, order_book, volatility_history, and the binanceusdm fetchPositionADLRank clause) count as covered; that set is derived from the module rather than hand-copied into the test, so a new special clause cannot silently desync the guard
test/fixtures/unified_read_parse_coverage_exclusions.json is regenerated from the corrected measurement with exact-equality assertion, so the list reddens on drift in either direction
Every entry records WHICH failure it is — no resolvable parse type versus no authored field map for a resolved type — because the two need different fixes and are owned by different follow-up work
The completion note states the corrected per-venue counts and the delta against the 79-cell list this task replaces; mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Authoring the missing parse slices or field maps the corrected list enumerates — tracker 550 owns that drain
The runtime contract guard's recording-replay half and its grading coverage — tracker 551 owns that
Write and mutation response shapes — task 358 owns the transport-envelope contract for writes
Weakening or deleting task 533's runtime guard; this task corrects the static half's denominator only
task.body:
Task 533 shipped the static parse-coverage assertion and wrote test/fixtures/unified_read_parse_coverage_exclusions.json as "the authoritative enumeration of the gap" — 79 method-venue cells, all tracking task 550. Measured against the runtime on 2026-08-08, that enumeration is not the gap.

THE DEFECT. The assertion computes supported_reads -- parsed_reads, where parsed_reads comes from the authored spec's endpoints.handlers.parse. Nothing in lib/ reads that key: exchange.ex:2059 reads endpoints.handlers.error and that is the only handlers consumer. handlers.parse is a CCXT-descriptor artifact whose values are CCXT helper names ("parseMarkets", "parseNumber", "parse8601"). The actual runtime path is Unified.parser_plan/2, which resolves a parser slot from the descriptor's return_type via @return_type_aliases and @parsers_by_parse_type, and then ReadParse.do_parse/8, which reads normalization.field_maps for that parse type. So the guard measures the presence of a key that has no runtime effect.

THE MEASUREMENT. Re-deriving the denominator from parser_plan resolution plus field_maps presence, over the ten authored specs and every declared read (capabilities.has == true):

  63 real gaps, against 79 listed
  14 of the 79 listed cells are real
  65 are phantom — listed, but they parse
  49 real gaps are invisible to the guard

Per venue (real / phantom-listed / missed-by-guard): alpaca 0/0/0, binance 16/8/13, binancecoinm 1/2/0, binanceusdm 19/8/16, bybit 9/18/8, deribit 3/3/2, derive 0/5/0, hyperliquid 3/10/2, lighter 0/0/0, okx 12/11/8.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE CONFIRMED, not inferred. Phantom: fetchTime is special-cased in read_parse.ex to :parse_time regardless of any spec key, and parses to {:ok, 1785772800000} on bybit and on deribit — yet it is listed as a gap on eight venues. derive's entire five-cell listing is phantom. Missed: okx fetchOpenInterests carries a handlers.parse key, so the guard passes it, and task 551 already records the live repro of it returning {:ok, %{"code", "data", "msg"}} — the raw provider envelope reported as success. That is the exact class the guard was built to make impossible, escaping through the guard.

WHY THE SHAPE OF THE REMAINING WORK CHANGES. The 63 real gaps split into two kinds that need different fixes and different task shapes. Roughly three quarters are :no_parse_type — the descriptor return type resolves to no parser slot at all, so the read falls through to raw passthrough. These repeat across venues (fetchStatus on 6, fetchDepositWithdrawFees on 5, fetchPositionMode on 4, fetchSettlementHistory on 4, fetchLeverageTiers and fetchMySettlementHistory on 3 each) and some are a missing @return_type_aliases entry rather than a missing unified type. That is shared-module work, not venue-vertical work: six venue tasks each inventing a status parse type is the cross-module collision CLAUDE.md warns about. The remainder are no-field-map cases where the type is already wired and only the venue's slice is absent (binanceusdm conversion and currency, bybit conversion, binance funding_history and margin_modification, okx margin_modification, hyperliquid funding_history) — those are genuinely vertical.

Recording the failure kind per entry is therefore load-bearing: it is what lets the orchestrator cut 550 into the right tasks instead of ten venue tasks against a list that is 82 percent noise.

Build the corrected measurement, regenerate the file, and stop there. Draining the corrected list stays with 550 and 551, which cannot be cut into child tasks until this lands.

acceptance_criteria: Every declared read whose descriptor return type resolves to no parser slot is resolved one of three ways, and which way is recorded per method: aliased to an existing unified struct via Unified's return-type alias table; given an explicit non-struct return contract the way fetchTime already has one; or flipped to capabilities.has = false with a carve-register entry naming the venue-side reason

Building net-new unified structs; this task enumerates them, the sibling builds them

task.body:
First child of tracker 550, cut on 2026-08-08 from the corrected measurement in task 564. Of the 63 real parse gaps, 51 are of this kind: Unified.parser_plan/2 resolves the descriptor's return_type through the return-type alias table and the parser table, finds nothing, and the read falls through to raw passthrough — the caller gets the provider's transport envelope inside an ok tuple.

Per venue: binance 14, binanceusdm 14, okx 11, bybit 6, deribit 3, hyperliquid 2, binancecoinm 1. alpaca, derive and lighter have none.

THE POINT OF THIS TASK IS THAT IT IS NOT VENUE-VERTICAL. The same methods recur across venues — fetchStatus on 6, fetchDepositWithdrawFees on 5, fetchPositionMode on 4, fetchSettlementHistory on 4, fetchLeverageTiers and fetchMySettlementHistory on 3 each, and fetchAccountPositions, fetchOptionPositions, fetchPositionsRisk, fetchLastPrices, fetchMarginModes, fetchMyDustTrades, fetchTransactionFees, fetchIsolatedBorrowRates and fetchOpenInterests on 2 each. Cutting this class venue-by-venue would have six worktrees each independently invent a status parse type, which is exactly the cross-module collision the orchestrator seat exists to prevent. One diff owns the resolution table.

Expect the cheap majority to be alias entries rather than missing types: several tokens are plural or variant spellings of structs that already exist and already have parser slots (fetchOpenInterests against OpenInterest, fetchDeposit and fetchWithdrawal against Transaction, fetchLiquidations against Liquidation, fetchMarginModes against MarginMode, fetchIsolatedBorrowRates against BorrowRate, fetchLeverageTiers against LeverageTier). Confirm each against the venue's own response before aliasing — an alias that maps a token onto the wrong struct is a silent mis-parse, strictly worse than the raw passthrough it replaces.

The residue is genuinely new unified surface (venue status, position mode, deposit and withdraw fee schedules, settlement history). Enumerate it, do not build it here.

acceptance_criteria: Every method the sibling resolution task enumerated as needing a net-new unified type is decided under the three-fact model task 570 establishes: the type is built and wired through the existing parser-slot mechanism, or the method keeps its venue-support fact and stays callable as a labelled raw read with its mapping recorded incomplete. A method left unmapped stays in the parse-coverage obligation, so this task's coverage delta reflects only types actually built — the backlog may not shrink by withdrawing declarations

Each new type is authored from the provider-owned contract in priv/authority/<venue>/, and its shape is justified against at least two venues that return it — a type carved from one venue's response is a venue field map wearing a unified name

task.body:
Second child of tracker 550, cut 2026-08-08. Sequenced after the return-type resolution repair because only that task can say which of the 51 unresolvable reads genuinely lack a unified type versus which merely lack an alias entry. Filing it now so the residue has an owner instead of becoming a completion-note footnote.

The expected residue, from the 2026-08-08 measurement, is the reads with no plausible existing struct: fetchStatus (binance, binanceusdm, bybit, deribit, hyperliquid, okx), fetchDepositWithdrawFees (binance, binanceusdm, bybit, deribit, okx), fetchPositionMode (binance, binancecoinm, binanceusdm, okx), fetchSettlementHistory and fetchMySettlementHistory (binance, binanceusdm, bybit, okx), plus venue singletons such as okx fetchUnderlyingAssets and fetchMarketsByType and bybit fetchDerivativesOpenInterestHistory. Treat that list as a prior, not as the spec — the sibling task's enumeration is authoritative.

NOT EVERY UNMAPPED READ NEEDS A STRUCT INVENTED AROUND IT — BUT THAT IS NOT A REASON TO WITHDRAW THE DECLARATION. A venue that answers a scalar mode string does not need a unified struct; under task 570's model it stays callable as a labelled raw read, with the venue-support fact true and the mapping recorded incomplete, and it stays in the coverage obligation until a mapping lands. This paragraph previously said the opposite — that flipping capabilities.has to false with a registered reason is the honest outcome. That was written before 570 separated venue support from mapping completeness from verification, and it is superseded: withdrawing a declaration is now reserved for a provider contract showing the venue does not offer the operation at that surface, which is a claim about the venue and not about our effort.

task.title: Five of the seven C-exposed Lighter signing operations are pinned only by shape, so a dependency bump cannot be verified
acceptance_criteria: cancel_order, cancel_all_orders, modify_order, update_leverage and update_margin each have a deterministic Go vector asserting the exact signature bytes and the exact serialized tx_info, built with the existing fixedSigner nonce injection rather than a new mechanism
update_margin's vector covers a negative usdc_amount, the conversion the current shape-only assertion cannot distinguish from a sign-flipped or truncated one

Each vector's expected bytes are justified in the test or a comment by what produced them — a recorded venue-accepted request, or a run of the pinned upstream library at a named revision — never by re-running the code under test and pasting its current output, which would pin the bug as the golden

Reverting native/lighter_signer/go.mod to go-ethereum v1.15.6 and gnark-crypto v0.14.0 either leaves every new vector green (proving the bump was signature-neutral) or reddens a named one; the outcome is recorded in the completion note either way
The Elixir Port test keeps its shape assertions and gains no duplicate byte assertions — the exact vectors belong on the Go side where the nonce can be fixed
go test ./... green in native/lighter_signer, and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: auth_token and create_order, which already carry exact vectors
Changing any signing behaviour, serialization or dependency version — this task adds evidence for what the code already does
The randomized-nonce production path; fixing the nonce is a test-only affordance that already exists
Signing for the other two DEX venues, hyperliquid and derive
task.body:
The Lighter signer exposes seven operations across the C boundary. Only three carry deterministic evidence: TestTask198PrimitiveVector, TestTask198AuthTokenVector and TestCreateOrderVector in native/lighter_signer/golden_test.go pin exact bytes using the fixedSigner type at golden_test.go:25, which injects a fixed nonce. The remaining five — cancel_order, cancel_all_orders, modify_order, update_leverage, update_margin — are exercised only by the Elixir Port test at test/bourse/signing/lighter_native_test.exs:63, which asserts tx_type > 0, that tx_info is valid JSON, and that tx_hash is a binary. Any correctly shaped 80-byte signature satisfies that, including one the venue would reject or, worse, accept as a different transaction than intended.

This became concrete rather than theoretical: go.mod was bumped (go-ethereum 1.15.6 to 1.17.0, gnark-crypto 0.14.0 to 0.18.1) to clear dependabot alerts on the signing path, and the only verification available for those five operations was a live testnet request returning 200 OK for an unrelated operation. The reason given at the time — that randomized Schnorr signatures make byte goldens impossible — is wrong: fixedSigner already exists precisely to remove that randomness, and three operations already use it. The determinism was on the shelf and went unused.

update_margin is the sharpest case. Its Port test case passes usdc_amount: -10, and negative-value field conversion is exactly the kind of serialization detail a field-element library bump can change silently — a sign flip or a truncation still produces valid JSON, a positive tx_type and a well-formed hash.

Verified before filing: the fixedSigner type and its three call sites, the three Test functions in golden_test.go, and the shape-only assertions plus the seven-entry operation_cases list in the Elixir test. What is NOT verified and must be established by this task is whether the recent bump actually changed any of the five signatures — nobody has measured it.

Dispatched rather than kept inline because this is the signing surface: a wrong signature is either a rejected order or an order the venue reads differently than the caller wrote it.

task.title: One field carries three independent facts, so a raw unmapped read is either silently mislabelled as normalized or deleted outright — separate them and label raw as raw
acceptance_criteria: The three facts are recorded separately in the authored specs, each with one owner field and a stated meaning: (1) the VENUE offers this operation, (2) bourse implements the mapping completely, (3) the implementation has been verified against the venue. No single field may answer more than one of them

Fact 1 is derived from and cited to the provider-owned contract in priv/authority/<venue>/, never from whether our credentials could reach the endpoint. A method the venue documents and serves records fact 1 as true even when facts 2 and 3 are false

Fact 3 is the ONLY fact sandbox or demo-account reachability may influence. An unreachable confrontation produces a dated docs/prod-verification-ledger.md entry and leaves fact 3 unverified; it may never change fact 1 or fact 2

An operation the venue offers stays CALLABLE even when its mapping is incomplete, and returns the provider payload in a form the caller cannot mistake for a normalized result — a distinct labelled shape carrying at minimum the raw payload, the venue, the method and the verification state. The defect being fixed is not that raw data reaches the caller; it is that today raw data arrives as a bare {:ok, map} indistinguishable at the type level from a parsed struct. Consumers of this client are agents and can use a labelled raw payload intelligently; they cannot defend against an unlabelled one

Deleting a WRONG MAPPING and removing a METHOD are two different acts and the task must never let one imply the other. A field map or endpoint wiring shown to point at the wrong surface is deleted as soon as it is shown wrong, whether or not the venue offers the operation — deribit fetchLiquidations wired to public/get_last_settlements_by_instrument is wrong and goes on those grounds alone, because that endpoint returns settlements

Removing a METHOD from the exposed surface is the stricter act and is permitted ONLY when the provider contract shows the venue neither serves the operation natively nor exposes primitives sufficient to derive it. deribit fetchLiquidations must be RE-ADJUDICATED under that test rather than inherited: Deribit's public trades carry an optional liquidation field, so the venue does expose the primitive and the honest disposition is likely emulated-from-trades with a stated boundary (recent trade window, no historical backfill). Whichever way it lands, the reason cites the provider contract for the operation, never the wrongness of the previous wiring

The three-value vocabulary is preserved and stated: the venue-support fact keeps true, false and "emulated" as distinct values — Bourse.Spec.Schema.validate_support! already enforces exactly these three (lib/bourse/spec/schema.ex:513) and deribit already ships "fetchCurrenciesWs" => "emulated". CRITICALLY, "emulated" is a statement about the PROVIDER and not about us: it means the venue exposes no native endpoint for the operation but does expose primitives sufficient to derive it. Whether bourse actually performs that derivation is fact 2. So fact 1 "emulated" with fact 2 false — a venue that could be emulated and a mapping we have not built — is a legal and expected state, not a contradiction. Defining "emulated" as "bourse synthesizes it" would re-commit the exact conflation this task exists to end

The parse-coverage obligation is computed from fact 1 AND NOT fact 2 — every operation the venue offers whose mapping is incomplete — so neither deleting a method nor labelling one raw can shrink the backlog. Regenerating the fixture under this definition states the new count and the delta against the current 37 (38 before task 568 closed the binance funding-history cell)

The eight flips resting on test-rig reach are RESTORED to callable — binance and binanceusdm fetchMyDustTrades, fetchIsolatedBorrowRates and fetchOptionPositions; okx fetchDeposit and fetchWithdrawal — each recording fact 1 true, its real fact 2 state, fact 3 unverified, and a dated prod-verification-ledger entry naming what is unreachable. None of them may be made to fail merely because our sandbox cannot verify them

The seven flips resting on the venue's own contract are re-expressed in the three-fact form rather than assumed correct: binance and binanceusdm fetchAccountPositions and fetchPositionsRisk record fact 1 true and fact 2 false (the venue serves the data; our mapping needs a two-response join), and bybit fetchDerivativesOpenInterestHistory and binance fetchMarginModes likewise. deribit fetchLiquidations is the only open question and is decided by the re-adjudication criterion above, not pre-declared here

The task-565 carve-register entries in docs/authored-spec-carves/binance.md, binanceusdm.md and okx.md are rewritten, not supplemented: they currently assert sandbox absence as evidence that the venue lacks the method, and claim a verification tier from negative rig evidence

While regenerating the fixture, the failure kind recorded per cell is re-derived rather than carried over, because at least two entries are known wrong: binanceusdm fetchConvertTrade and fetchConvertTradeHistory are labelled no_field_map but fail earlier at endpoint resolution with an ambiguous multi-endpoint selection error and never reach the field-map layer. A cell blocked by more than one thing states the blocker the caller hits FIRST, or is split so each blocker is tracked

A test asserts the separation directly: no spec state may encode fact 1 as false with a reason citing sandbox or demo-account reachability, and no change to fact 3 may alter the exposed surface or the coverage obligation

The correction sweeps every venue rather than the enumerated cells, because the conflation predates task 565: binancecoinm records fact 1 false for fetchFundingHistory and fetchMarginAdjustmentHistory while both raw endpoints answer HTTP 200 on the demo host. Every operation recording fact 1 false whose own raw endpoint is generated and reachable is re-adjudicated against the provider contract, and the audit states how many such cells existed and how each was resolved

The public-surface consequences of the split are decided EXPLICITLY, not inherited (codex review 2026-08-10): today has = "emulated" both generates a unified method and makes Exchange.has?/2 answer true (lib/bourse/exchange.ex supported_unified_methods/2 and has?/2), so redefining "emulated" as a provider-only fact is a public-contract change. The task states which fact(s) drive method generation, Exchange.has?/2 and describe/2, records the compatibility decision (breaking vs preserved, and for whom) in the carve register, and guarantees a fact-1 "emulated" with fact 2 false can never generate a method that dispatches nothing
mix check.dispatch green

The task-549 derive capability-confrontation invariant is generalized repo-wide under the new fact model: for every venue, a capability declared unsupported with wired unified routes fails the suite, and one declared unsupported while a matching raw endpoint exists requires a registered carve — ARC wave-4 finding: the 549 test is a hand-listed 4-entry derive table, so a fifth capability or another venue escapes it

A raw parse_<slot>/2 for a slot the venue does not offer answers with the unsupported-operation fact rather than :no_field_map. The deribit parse_order_list/2 consumer report is the worked case: :no_field_map states fact 2 (our mapping is incomplete) for a surface where fact 1 is false, and the consumer read it as a bourse gap and special-cased the response locally
out_of_scope: Authoring the missing mappings themselves; this task makes the obligation visible and correctly counted, tracker 550 owns the drain
Reaching the prod-only endpoints; the ledger entry records the blocker, it does not have to close it
The ten cells task 565 closed by actually authoring a parser — those are live-verified and stand
Fixing the endpoint-resolution blocker behind the two misclassified binanceusdm convert cells; this task corrects the classification, tracker 550 owns the repair
task.body:
Found by the orchestrator's whole-surface pass over the task 565 landed base on 2026-08-08, after mix ci was green and the per-task reviewer had approved. It is the domain-ground-truth class CLAUDE.md describes: internally consistent, fully tested, and wrong about the world.

WHAT LANDED. Task 565 reported closing 25 of the 51 no-parser cells. Ten were closed by authoring a parser and are live-verified (hyperliquid and okx fetchOpenInterests, okx fetchMarketsByType and fetchPositionsForSymbol, binance and binanceusdm fetchLastPrices, binance and binanceusdm fetchLeverageTiers, binanceusdm fetchMarginModes, bybit fetchLeverageTiers). The other fifteen — ten distinct methods across five venues — were closed by flipping capabilities.has from true to false. The reviewer disclosed this plainly and wrote carve-register entries for each, so nothing was hidden; the disagreement is with the disposition, not the reporting.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS NOT THE FLIPS, IT IS THE FIELD. capabilities.has is one field answering three independent questions at once: does the VENUE offer this operation, does bourse IMPLEMENT the mapping completely, and has that implementation been VERIFIED against the venue. It is not a boolean — Bourse.Spec.Schema.validate_support! accepts true, false or "emulated" (lib/bourse/spec/schema.ex:513), and deribit already ships "fetchCurrenciesWs" => "emulated" — so the three-value vocabulary is real and must survive the split rather than be flattened by it. "emulated" belongs to the venue-support fact: it says the venue offers the data and bourse synthesizes the unified shape from other endpoints. Because all three questions collapse into this one field, a correct decision about one of them silently overwrites the other two. That is what happened here, and it will happen again to whoever touches this next, whatever they decide about these fifteen cells.

WHAT TASK 565 CORRECTLY REACTED TO. A declared read with no parse mapping returns the raw provider envelope inside an ok tuple, at a type indistinguishable from a parsed struct. That is success-shaped garbage and the worst failure mode this client has. The reaction was right; the remedy was too blunt.

THE REMEDY, DECIDED 2026-08-09. Raw data is not the problem — raw data PRETENDING TO BE NORMALIZED is. This client's consumers are agents, and an agent handed a clearly labelled raw provider payload can use it intelligently; what it cannot do is defend against a raw payload wearing a parsed result's shape. So an operation the venue offers stays callable with its mapping incomplete, and returns a distinct labelled shape carrying the payload, the venue, the method and the verification state. Deletion is reserved for a mapping PROVEN WRONG — deribit fetchLiquidations wired to a settlements endpoint. Incompleteness is a backlog entry, never a deletion, and never a synthetic failure.

WHAT REMOVAL GOT WRONG. It also erased the fact that the venue supports the operation, and it shrank the coverage obligation. Eight of the fifteen flips cite our test rig, not the venue: binance and binanceusdm fetchMyDustTrades, fetchIsolatedBorrowRates and fetchOptionPositions because the SAPI and EAPI surfaces have no sandbox host; okx fetchDeposit and fetchWithdrawal because the demo account holds no deposit or withdrawal history to name an identifier with. All are documented and served in production. Sandbox reachability is evidence about verification and nothing else — it may not decide what the venue offers, and it may not decide whether we owe a mapping.

THE MEASUREMENT CONSEQUENCE. The coverage guard in test/bourse/unified_read_contract_test.exs counts only has == true reads, so a flip erases the obligation instead of discharging it. The headline 63-to-38 shrink is therefore part measurement and part declaration. Under the corrected definition the obligation is every operation the venue offers whose mapping is incomplete, so removing a broken method from the exposed surface leaves the backlog entry exactly where it was — which is the whole point.

THE REMOVAL IS STRUCTURAL, NOT COSMETIC. An independent cross-family adjudication on 2026-08-08 established that capabilities.has = false mechanically drops the method from the generated unified mappings in lib/bourse/exchange.ex, so the consumer cannot call it at all. It also noted the three specs still carry non-empty native routes for the eight disputed cells, so the wiring already contradicts the declaration — further evidence that one flag is being asked to mean too much.

THE SEVEN CONTRACT-BASED FLIPS ARE A SEPARATE QUESTION AND MOSTLY DO NOT STAND EITHER. deribit fetchLiquidations was the one cell that looked like genuine absence, and on re-examination it is not settled. Its wiring to public/get_last_settlements_by_instrument is certainly wrong — that endpoint returns settlements. But Deribit's own contract for public/get_last_trades_by_instrument documents an optional liquidation field on the trade object, "M" when the maker side was under liquidation, "T" when the taker was, "MT" when both (verified against the provider documentation 2026-08-09; a 2000-row live production sample of BTC-PERPETUAL and ETH-PERPETUAL contained no liquidation-marked trades, which is consistent with the field being rare and is NOT evidence of absence). So the venue does expose liquidation data, and the honest disposition may well be "emulated" — filter trades on the marker — with a stated boundary that it covers only the recent trade window and offers no historical backfill. Re-adjudicate it against the provider contract for the OPERATION; do not inherit a fact-1-false conclusion drawn from the wrongness of our own wiring. THE REST ARE INCOMPLETENESS, NOT ABSENCE. binance and binanceusdm fetchAccountPositions and fetchPositionsRisk need two responses joined, and selecting either alone fabricates positions — the venue serves the data, so fact 1 is true and fact 2 is false. bybit fetchDerivativesOpenInterestHistory authors no complete request binding and binance fetchMarginModes declares incompatible account routes — again fact 2, not fact 1. Re-express each rather than assuming the flip encoded the right fact.

THE CONFLATION PREDATES THE TASK-565 FLIPS — LIVE EVIDENCE FROM THE 568 LANDED BASE. The orchestrator's whole-surface pass on 2026-08-09 found the same collapse in cells no recent task touched, which means fixing only the fifteen 565 flips would leave the class intact. On binancecoinm, capabilities.has records fetchFundingHistory = false and fetchMarginAdjustmentHistory = false. Both operations are served: a signed call to dapiPrivate_get_income with incomeType FUNDING_FEE returned HTTP 200, and dapiPrivate_get_positionmargin_history for BTCUSD_PERP returned HTTP 200 (both on demo-dapi.binance.com, 2026-08-09, both with an empty list because the COIN-M demo wallet carries no history — the UI faucet credits USD-M only). An empty 200 proves routing and authentication, so it establishes fact 1 and says nothing about facts 2 or 3; that is precisely the distinction this task exists to make. Sweep for this pattern rather than fixing the enumerated cells alone: any venue recording fact 1 false for an operation whose own raw endpoint is generated and reachable is the same defect, and binancecoinm is the proof it was not introduced by task 565.

ORDERING. This must land before task 566. 566 builds or retires the net-new return types for the remaining no-parser cells, and its input set is exactly the coverage obligation this task redefines. Building 566 against today's numbers means rebuilding it afterwards.

NOTE 2026-08-10 (orchestrator QA pass over the task 573-575 landed base): while in the shared parser, harden empty-string compute operands. Safe.string("") returns "" (lib/bourse/safe.ex:69), which is not nil, so a computed field-map rule like {"op": "sub"} reaching Decimal.new("") raises Decimal.Error (verified 2026-08-10). okx can return an empty nextFundingTime, and its new interval rule is the fourth "sub" on okx, so the exposure is live-plausible. The honest result for an empty operand is the same as for a missing one: the computed field is nil. Fix in the same pass as the raw/normalized separation — the parser surface is already this task's write-set.

2026-08-19 facet (consumer report, ../bourse/BUGS.md). Bourse.Deribit.parse_order_list([], symbol: instrument) answers {:error, :no_field_map}. Verified against the authored spec and the capability set: deribit carries a field map for "order" and none for "order_list", and declares no fetchOrderList / fetchOrderLists / fetchOpenOrderLists capability at all, so the venue has no OCO order-group surface. The honest answer is fact 1 false, while :no_field_map answers fact 2. The consumer read the error as an incomplete bourse mapping and special-cased the empty raw response in trading_dashboard instead of calling parse_order/2, which deribit does support. Folded here rather than filed as a sibling: the raw parse_<slot>/2 boundary is the same one-field-answers-two-questions conflation this task exists to end.

task.title: Bulk list reads return venue-native symbols in unified structs, so a consumer cannot join them to any other unified result
acceptance_criteria: Every unified struct carrying a symbol field carries the UNIFIED symbol, whatever the read shape — a symbol-argument call, a symbol-keyed map, or a bulk list with no symbol argument at all

The backfill path that produced the defect is fixed at the class rather than per parse type: requested_symbol/2 in read_parse.ex falls back to the venue-native string when the caller passed no symbol, and it feeds leverage_tiers and liquidation alike

Denormalization resolves the market family from the row itself where the venue supplies it — the bybit rows carry info.category, which is what disambiguates 0GUSDT as linear 0G/USDT:USDT rather than spot 0G/USDT — and a row whose family cannot be resolved fails loudly instead of silently keeping the native string
A suite-wide guard asserts the invariant over the declared read surface, so a parse type added later cannot reintroduce native symbols without reddening the suite
Verified live on at least binanceusdm and bybit against their own sandboxes, with the recordings registered — both are confirmed defective today and are the regression cases
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: The request-binding gap that makes bybit fetch_leverage_tiers error without an explicit category — a sibling task owns it; this task may pass category to obtain a response
Adding parse slices for methods that have none — tracker 550 owns that
Symbol normalization on write and mutation responses
task.body:
Found live by the orchestrator's whole-surface pass on 2026-08-08 against the task 565 landed base, using real testnet calls rather than fixtures.

OBSERVED. Bourse.fetch_leverage_tiers on binanceusdm returns 6714 %Bourse.LeverageTier{} rows whose symbol reads KAVAUSDT. The same sweep on bybit, with category linear supplied, returns 407 rows whose symbol reads 0GUSDT. In the same session Bourse.fetch_open_interests on okx returned %Bourse.OpenInterest{} with symbol 2Z/USDT:USDT and binanceusdm fetch_margin_modes returned %Bourse.MarginMode{} with symbol OBOL/USDT:USDT. So the unified surface is internally inconsistent: some reads normalize and some hand back the venue's own string.

CAUSE. read_parse.ex defines backfill_leverage_tier_symbol/2 as symbol: requested_symbol(params, row.symbol), and requested_symbol/2 returns the caller's symbol param when there is one and the native symbol otherwise. A bulk call passes no symbol, so every row keeps whatever the venue wrote. backfill_liquidation_symbol/2 is built the same way, so liquidation carries the same defect wherever a bulk liquidation read exists.

CONSUMER IMPACT. The symbol is the join key across the unified surface. A consumer that fetches leverage tiers and markets and tries to pair them by symbol matches nothing, because one side says KAVAUSDT and the other KAVA/USDT:USDT. This is silent — no error, no nil, just an empty join — which is why it survived the per-task gate.

WHY THE CLASS AND NOT THE METHOD. Patching backfill_leverage_tier_symbol alone leaves liquidation defective and leaves the next bulk parse type free to repeat it. The durable form is the invariant plus a guard over the declared read surface: a unified struct's symbol is the unified symbol. That is what stops this from spawning a sibling task per parse type.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1786357805500-1bf4652b, 25233e860b1f06010ffc0660073497bfe7dc544d).

task.title: Bybit authors 59 unresolved category defaults, so declared reads that pass every coverage gate still fail live with error 10001
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.fetch_leverage_tiers on bybit succeeds with no caller-supplied category, verified live against the venue's own sandbox with the recording registered — it errors 10001 Illegal category today

The 59 request defaults in the bybit authored spec whose category is marked unresolved are adjudicated rather than left as a marker: each is either authored with the value or derivation the provider contract requires, or its method is dispositioned with a carve-register entry naming why no single category can serve it

Category derivation is authored into the spec rather than added as another per-method Elixir branch — the ad-hoc injection that makes fetchTicker and fetchOrderBook work is what let fetchLeverageTiers ship declared and unusable

A test asserts the class invariant across the declared bybit read surface: a declared read whose request contract requires category either resolves one or is dispositioned per the task-570 three-fact model — the venue-support fact stays provider-derived and is never flipped to false over an implementation gap; callability reflects the implementation fact — so a resolvable parse slot can never again certify a read that cannot be called

Methods whose category genuinely depends on caller intent, and which cannot be defaulted, state that in the carve register and surface a typed error naming the required param rather than the provider's raw 10001

Non-bybit venues; the unresolved-default pattern may exist elsewhere but this task is scoped to the venue with measured evidence
Write and mutation request shapes; this task covers declared reads
task.body:
Found live by the orchestrator's whole-surface pass on 2026-08-08 against the task 565 landed base.

OBSERVED. Bourse.fetch_leverage_tiers on bybit returns {:error, %Bourse.Error{type: :bad_request, code: 10001, message: "Illegal category"}}. The same call with an explicit category linear returns 407 %Bourse.LeverageTier{} rows. The method is declared capabilities.has = true, resolves a parser slot, has a field map, and appears in no exclusion list — so every gate in the repository reports it covered while a consumer cannot call it.

THE MEASUREMENT. This is not one method. The bybit authored spec carries a category request default on 66 methods. Seven are authored literals — fetchAllGreeks, fetchGreeks, fetchOption, fetchOptionChain, fetchOptionMarkets and fetchVolatilityHistory take option, fetchSpotMarkets takes spot. The remaining 59 are marked unresolved, with reason conditional_value or identifier_reference and a null value. fetchLeverageTiers has no request-defaults entry at all, which is why nothing is injected for it.

WHY THE WORKING CASES MISLEAD. fetchTicker's category default is also unresolved, yet the call succeeds — because category injection for it lives in Elixir in the unified layer, not in the spec. So the spec's unresolved marker is not a reliable signal of brokenness, and the Elixir injection is not a reliable signal of coverage. The two disagree, and the coverage guard reads neither: it measures parse resolution, which is a response-side property, while this is a request-side failure. That is the structural reason this class survives every check.

PRIOR ART IN THE INBOUND QUEUE. BUGS.md already carries bybit category reports against fetch_ticker, fetch_order_book, fetch_funding_rates and fetch_ohlcv, fixed one at a time. fetchLeverageTiers is the fourth site of the same class. Fixing it as a fifth one-off guarantees a sixth; the acceptance criteria therefore require the derivation to be authored and the invariant asserted across the declared read surface.

NOTE ON SCOPE. Task 565 met the same class from the other side and chose has = false for fetchDerivativesOpenInterestHistory, whose carve records that the venue requires category, intervalTime and a native symbol while the declared method authors no complete request binding. That disposition and this task must agree on one rule rather than deciding per method.

task.body:
BUGS.md 2026-08-10, three coupled defects on binance USD-M futures (sandbox, testnet.binancefuture.com), all live-observed by trading_dashboard; real-money-relevant.

(1) create_order silently drops documented unified opts. time_in_force never reaches the wire in any spelling (-1102 "Mandatory parameter 'timeinforce' was not sent"; workaround params: %{"timeInForce" => "GTC"} works). trigger_price + reduce_only are discarded: an order meant as a stop went out as type=MARKET, no stopPrice, reduceOnly=false — filled immediately and OPENED a -1.28 ETH position. stop_loss_price equally dead, and a "type" override via params is clobbered by the unified type, so conditional orders are currently unbuildable on binance through the unified surface. All four opts are listed in create_order's Descripex contract docs. Root-cause split is open — determine whether the opts→param mapping is a missing binance request slice or a unified-layer mechanism gap (check whether the same opts reach the wire on bybit/okx before deciding the shape; premise unverified).

(2) Provider contract moved: binance rejects conditional orders on POST /fapi/v1/order with -4120 "use the Algo Order API endpoints" — POST /fapi/v1/algoOrder with algoType=CONDITIONAL + triggerPrice. Live-verified 2026-08-10; authority developers.binance.com/docs/derivatives/usds-margined-futures/trade/rest-api. The binance mapping needs the new endpoint regardless of where the opts fix lands.

(3) set_margin_mode(ex, "isolated", "ETH/USDT:USDT") never sends symbol: every arg variant returns -1102 "Mandatory parameter 'symbol' was not sent" while the raw POST /fapi/v1/marginType?symbol=ETHUSDT&marginType=ISOLATED succeeds with the same keys.

(4) cancel_all_orders(ex, symbol: ...) feeds the venue's {"code":200,"msg":"...done."} confirmation through the order parser and returns {:error, "parsed to an all-nil struct"} — AND the underlying call cancelled nothing (3 resting limit orders survived; fetch_open_orders confirmed). The raw DELETE /fapi/v1/allOpenOrders?symbol=ETHUSDT both returns 200 and actually cancels, so the unified call likely hits the wrong product endpoint; verify the routing, don't just fix the parse.

Sibling of task 553 (read-side: since dropped on binance spot) — same defect class, params silently not reaching the wire. 553's lesson applies: assert what was SENT/EXECUTED, not the absence of an error.

task.body:
Found by the orchestrator's whole-surface QA pass over the task 573-575 landed base (run run-1786327329346-148b8b33, 2026-08-10). Task 574 fixed the CREATE side of the conditional-order surface: stops now route to POST /fapi/v1/algoOrder. But Binance keeps conditional orders in a separate book with dedicated endpoints, and the read/cancel side still routes linear to the regular book (fapiPrivate_delete_order, fapiPrivate_delete_allopenorders, fapiPrivate_get_openorders). Net effect observed in the landed diff itself: the acceptance fixture's cleanup has to drop to the raw Bourse.Binance.fapiPrivate_delete_algoorder/2 (lib/bourse/exchange_acceptance_fixtures.ex, algo cleanup) because no unified path can cancel what the unified path just created. A consumer creates a stop, cancel_all_orders returns {"code":200} success, and the stop stays resting — the same reports-success-nothing-happened class task 574 was fixing, re-created on the other side.

Second gap, same surface: the algoOrder selection rules key only on trigger_price and stop_loss_price. take_profit_price is a first-class unified param (lib/bourse/order/builder.ex, lib/bourse/order.ex) and selects nothing — create_order(ex, symbol, "market", "sell", qty, take_profit_price: X) routes to /fapi/v1/order as a bare MARKET sell, the exact naked-market-sell bug of the original BUGS.md report, in the take-profit direction. Binance's New Algo Order contract accepts STOP, STOP_MARKET, TAKE_PROFIT, TAKE_PROFIT_MARKET, TRAILING_STOP_MARKET. The spec already carries fapiPrivateDeleteAlgoOrder, fapiPrivateDeleteAlgoOpenOrders and fapiPrivateGetOpenAlgoOrders in endpoints.unified, unselected by any rule — the endpoints exist, only the selection is missing.

Authority: Binance USD-M Algo Order contracts (developers.binance.com — New/Cancel/Cancel All/Current All Algo Orders). Live demo evidence required per the reality doctrine. Account state note: the futures demo account runs One-way mode (verified live 2026-08-10, GET /fapi/v1/positionSide/dual returned dualSidePosition=false) — orders need no positionSide.

Scope this as the CLASS invariant, not three endpoint patches: every venue where create_order can select a distinct order book must route the matching read/cancel methods to that book. fetch_open_orders merging both books (regular + algo) needs a carve decision: one merged list vs a named divergence.
