task.body:
Found by the orchestrator's whole-surface QA pass over the task 573-575 landed base (2026-08-10). The BUGS.md entries were titled binance USD-M, and the consumer-facing fix landed on the GENERIC binance spec's fapi section — but the dedicated binanceusdm and binancecoinm venues, which a consumer reasonably reaches for by name for USD-M/COIN-M work, still carry the original defects: (a) no algo routing and no endpoint_overrides for createOrder, (b) createOrder defaults without timeInForce/reduceOnly so time_in_force and reduce_only are still silently dropped, and (c) binanceusdm setMarginMode is kind unresolved/identifier_reference, which resolves marginType through identifier_value's :symbol-in-required fallback (lib/bourse/unified/request_shape.ex) — it sends the symbol string as the margin type. binancecoinm has no setMarginMode entry at all. The dedicated venues read as fixed when they are not.

Also folds in the coverage regression from the same QA pass: the binance spot fetch_balance accepted-request golden (api/v3/account @ testnet.binance.vision, captured 2026-07-22) was REPLACED by the swap golden in the landed diff because Bourse.ExchangeAcceptanceFixtures keys goldens strictly on venue+method (fixture_path -> venue/method.json, one profile per method). Nothing live-pins the spot route anymore, while the carve claims the golden prevents a silent return to the spot wallet. The profile-scheme extension belongs in this task because the usdm/coinm goldens touch the same machinery.

Depends on task 576: 576 completes the conditional-order pattern (algo cancel/fetch routing, take_profit_price selection) on the generic spec; porting before it lands means porting the incomplete pattern. Account state note: the futures demo account runs One-way mode (verified live 2026-08-10, dualSidePosition=false).

Authority: Binance USD-M and COIN-M trade REST contracts (developers.binance.com); live demo-fapi/demo-dapi evidence per the reality doctrine.

ARC wave-2 fold-in (2026-08-10): the whole-surface review verified C-T576's carve against Binance's own docs (the 2025-12-09 conditional-order migration to the Algo service is real — derivatives change-log, error -4120 on /fapi/v1/order) but found two defects this task now carries: (1) the both-legs selection defect on the generic spec (TAKE_PROFIT* cases ordered before STOP* while triggerPrice.fallback_sources tries stop_loss_price first — priv/specs/json/output/authored/binance.json, first-match-wins in lib/bourse/unified/request_shape.ex), which must be fixed before the pattern is ported; (2) the false binanceusdm exclusion rationale in the task-576 distinct-order-book invariant test. The read-side class (lifecycle reads seeing the algo book) is task 580, depends_on this one.

Live-QA fold-in (2026-08-10, post-577 landing, orchestrator testnet probe): two additional opts-drop instances verified LIVE, both -1102. (1) GENERIC binance SPOT create_order on testnet.binance.vision returns -1102 'timeInForce was not sent' although the caller passed timeInForce: "GTC" explicitly (test/bourse/binance_authored_integration_test.exs 'spot ACK remains sparse' red live) — so the 574/575 generic-spec fix does NOT hold for spot; the out_of_scope assumption is corrected accordingly. (2) binanceusdm set_position_mode returns -1102 'dualsideposition was not sent' on demo-fapi — the unified write drops the required param entirely ('position mode reaches business validation' red live, expected -4059). Mechanism hypothesis (premise unverified — confirm before building on it): RequestShape venue builders rebuild the wire body and lose pass-through opts; build_final_params pipes every selection path through RequestShape.apply.

task.title: Authority drift lane cries wolf: split --online drift semantics by artifact class (typed contract fails, prose churn warns)
acceptance_criteria: A typed-contract artifact with a sha256 mismatch still fails mix ccxt.authority_check --online; a prose/docs artifact mismatch warns, records drift_detected with checked_at, and exits green while acknowledged — both behaviors pinned by tests
An acknowledged prose drift older than the bounded staleness window re-fails the run; the window and its rationale are documented in the manifest schema notes
The live enumeration evidence is reproduced as a test-level distinction: artifact class (typed vs prose) comes from the manifest role/expressiveness fields, not from URL heuristics

The VPS lane decoupling (authority rc not gating the healthcheck alarm) is removed in the same change: the lane's script contract is documented so the operator host folds authority rc back into the alarm; the GH manual-only fallback behaves identically
mix check.dispatch green; first verification move runs --online against the real upstreams and shows the warn-vs-fail split on the currently-drifted set

The authority axis discriminates (ARC W2, folded 2026-08-10): semantic_authority is no longer constant-true — a validator rule ties it to freshness/coverage so a known_stale or index_only artifact cannot claim semantic authority (concrete cases: alpaca trading-openapi-repository and market-data-openapi-repository are provider-disowned as outdated yet carry semantic_authority: true; deribit/derive documentation_index artifacts are coverage: index_only); manifests updated and the rule pinned by a test
out_of_scope: Refreshing the 10 currently-drifted prose pins (each needs its own semantic review; they quiesce as acknowledged drift under the new semantics)
Changing the offline authority_check behavior in the dispatch gate
task.body:
Found by the orchestrator running the task-554 landed lane live (2026-08-10): mix ccxt.authority_check --online raises on the FIRST sha256 mismatch, and an enumeration of all 18 mutable sha256-pinned artifacts found 10 already drifted within 18 days of their pins — alpaca trading-api-create-order/stock-bars-single/crypto-snapshots/crypto-bars, binancecoinm+binanceusdm developer-docs-full (llms-full.txt), deribit error-codes, derive error-codes, hyperliquid docs-full, okx api-v5-docs. Every drifted artifact is a rendered docs page or llms-full aggregate; every stable one is a typed contract (spot-openapi, deribit openapi/asyncapi x4, lighter rest-openapi, docs-index llms.txt). Hash-pinning prose pages means the weekly lane is red nearly every week from upstream docs edits — alarm fatigue that buries the one drift that matters (a typed contract change). The alpaca postorder drift is already honestly marked freshness.status=drift_detected in the manifest, yet --online still raises on it, so an acknowledged drift keeps re-alarming with no way to quiesce except a pin refresh.

Split the drift semantics by artifact class: a typed-contract artifact (openapi/asyncapi machine spec roles) drifting fails the run as today; a prose/docs artifact drifting emits a visible warning plus a durable per-run drift report line and flips freshness.status=drift_detected with checked_at, but does not fail the lane while the manifest already acknowledges the drift. A drift_detected acknowledgment must carry its date; define how an acknowledgment goes stale (e.g. re-fail if acknowledged longer than a bounded window without semantic review) so warn-and-track cannot become warn-and-forget. Keep 'never refresh a pin merely to restore green' — refresh still requires the recorded semantic review, per the deribit current-rest-drift-2026-08-10.json pattern (for storage=reference_only artifacts the review compares the CURRENT page against the authored slice, since old bytes are not retained).

task.body:
Convergence finding on the landed task 577 (orchestrator live probe, 2026-08-10). Task 577's endpoint_selection correctly routes inverse symbols on the GENERIC binance client to the DAPI family, but the request still carries the wrong symbol FORM: Bourse.Symbol.to_exchange_id("BTC/USD:BTC", binance) yields "BTCUSD" (the pair), while binancecoinm yields "BTCUSD_PERP" (the contract). Binance DAPI premiumIndex answers the pair form with HTTP 200 + [] — silently empty, no error — so Bourse.fetch_funding_rate(binance, "BTC/USD:BTC") returns {:ok, []} (verified live 2026-08-10; raw dapiPublic_get_premiumindex with symbol=BTCUSD_PERP returns the populated row). Root cause class: the generic multi-family binance client's authored markets.symbol_patterns are keyed by market type only (:swap/:future/:spot/:option), and the :swap pattern produces the linear form (BTCUSDT) — it cannot express that an INVERSE swap needs the _PERP contract form (and an inverse delivery future needs the _<yymmdd> form). Confront the symbol forms against Binance's OWN dapi contract (developers.binance.com COIN-M docs) — the dedicated binancecoinm patterns are the in-repo reference for the expected output, not the authority.

Authority: Binance COIN-M REST contract (developers.binance.com); live dapi evidence per the reality doctrine. First verification move is a live call.

The offline case 584 added was green against the stub, which is exactly the blind-stub AC below. Decide the dedicated-venue semantics against the provider contract: either binanceusdm denormalizes inverse to the contract form and serves the dapi read, or an inverse symbol on the USD-M venue refuses loudly (:bad_symbol / unsupported family) — {:ok, []} is the one wrong answer.

ARC wave-[571/584] folds (2026-08-10): (a) INBOUND is broken the same way: read_parse.ex binance_contract_symbol is guarded id in [binanceusdm, binancecoinm], so the generic binance client cannot parse any contract-form native id inbound — Symbol.from_exchange_id("ETHUSDT_260925", binance, _) returns the id verbatim, which is why fetch_funding_rates(binance) keys that row natively while binanceusdm leverage tiers unify the analogous form. Minimal change: add "binance" to that guard while keeping binance_linear_perpetual_symbol (the USD1|U branch) scoped to binanceusdm; dated (USDT|USDC)_(yymmdd) and USD_(PERP|yymmdd) grammars cannot collide with spot ids (spot symbols carry no underscore). (b) binanceusdm's fetchFundingRate/fetchFundingRates market_family "future" selection routes settle-less dated LINEAR symbols (BTC/USDT-250627 family, which live on FAPI) to DAPI — family_from_symbol yields "future" only for expiry-without-settle. Same dedicated-venue decision; resolve both against the provider contract.

After task 646 landed, the same defect reproduces on the umbrella client and is now AUDIBLE rather than silent: Exchange.new!(binance, sandbox: true) with no loaded markets, fetch_funding_rate for BTC/USD:BTC hits 646's unservable refusal instead of the old {:ok, []}, because the outbound id is still the compact pair form and dapi premiumIndex does not list it. task.body:
ARC whole-surface finding on the landed task 577 (2026-08-10, verified against live venue data — the @funding_periods_per_day class: internally consistent, fully tested, wrong, because the offline stub covers only perpetuals).

FundingInterval.enrich applies @binance_default_interval "8h" to ANY row absent from fundingInfo. Binance's own default statement is scoped to PERPETUALS (FAQ 360033525031: 'The default funding interval is every 8 hours' — a perpetual-contracts page). Live reality 2026-08-10: dapi premiumIndex returns 30 rows of which 10 are DATED DELIVERY FUTURES (BTCUSD_260925 etc.) with nextFundingTime: 0 and no funding history — dapi fundingInfo is [], so a third of every binancecoinm plural funding read carries a fabricated interval: "8h" for contracts that never fund. fapi: 857 rows, 135 absent from fundingInfo; 4 are TRADING quarter contracts (nextFundingTime: 0), 127 are SETTLING perps — a 45-symbol sample of the defaulted set showed 30 whose real measured cadence (consecutive fundingRate.fundingTime gaps) was 4h, not 8h.

Fix direction: gate the 8h default on the instrument being a funding perpetual (e.g. nextFundingTime > 0, or contract-type from the row), leave interval nil (or a typed no-funding marker) otherwise; add a dated-delivery-future row to the plural stub so coverage stops ratifying the constant.

Fold-ins from the same ARC pass:
(1) Citation fix — carve C-T573a and the funding sections cite binance.com announcement 6d707b1f7ae34f419621b4c807464ab1 as the source of the 8h default; fetched, that page is a TREEUSDT-specific 1h→4h notice and states no default. The provider-owned citation is FAQ 360033525031. Correct the carve register and any doc that repeats it.
(2) binanceusdm selection asymmetry — 577 gave binanceusdm fetchFundingIntervals a market_family inverse → dapiPublic_get_fundinginfo rule but fetchFundingRate on that venue still resolves by market type to fapiPublic, so an inverse symbol on binanceusdm would read fapi premiumIndex while joining the dapi interval list. Off-label reach, but the two selections disagree by construction — author the matching fetchFundingRate rule or carve the exclusion.

ACCEPTED TRADEOFF (do not 'fix'): enrich propagates a fundingInfo failure as the failure of the whole plural read and costs one extra weighted request per plural call — failing loud over silently degrading to nil is this repo's doctrine (ARC reviewed and accepted 2026-08-10).

Authority: Binance USD-M/COIN-M REST contracts and the provider FAQ named above; live fapi/dapi evidence per the reality doctrine. First verification move is a live call.

task.title: Unified boundary accepts structurally invalid arguments and crashes in the signing layer — validate param value shapes before dispatch
acceptance_criteria: The reported call — set_margin_mode(ex, "isolated", symbol: ...) — returns {:error, %Bourse.Error{type: :invalid_parameters}} naming the offending argument; no raise, no signing-layer crash (regression test)

A class test sweeps unified entry points with non-encodable param values (keyword list, tuple, struct) and asserts a typed refusal — no exception escapes a public function (task 185's invariant extended to the param-value layer)

mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Changing any method's positional signature
Coercing misplaced opts into the intended positional arg (guess-free refusal only)
task.body:
Consumer report (BUGS.md 2026-08-10, live demo-fapi evidence): Bourse.set_margin_mode(ex, "isolated", symbol: "ETH/USDT:USDT") — symbol is positional arg 3, and the misplaced keyword list flowed through dispatch into Bourse.Signing.HmacRecipe.encode_query_pairs, crashing with a Jason tuple-encode error whose stack points nowhere near the caller's mistake.

Class precedent: task 185 (done) established the invariant that public unified functions never raise — it covered the opts ENVELOPE (:params extraction, map-opts coercion). This instance is one layer deeper: a param VALUE that is not query/JSON-encodable (keyword list, tuple, arbitrary struct) survives the boundary and detonates in the signer. Scope the fix as the class, not the instance: at the unified boundary, refuse any param whose value cannot reach the wire, with a Bourse.Error :invalid_parameters naming the offending param and its expected shape. Where the misuse is recognizably a positional-arg mistake (a keyword list in a binary slot), the message names the positional convention.

The suite-wide NativeSymbolParser guard grows a non-bybit venue case and a symbol-keyed-map case so map KEYS are covered, not only struct fields
mix check.dispatch green; mix dialyzer.json clean (the resolver region already burned one dead-clause warning this wave)
out_of_scope: The generic-binance inbound contract-form grammar (task 583 owns binance_contract_symbol)
Re-keying semantics beyond the guard coverage (existing behavior stays)
task.body:
ARC whole-surface finding on the landed task 571 (2026-08-10). The class-wide native-symbol backfill's fail-loud branch ({:error, {:unresolved_unified_symbol, ...}}) fires only when native_market_type/3 returns nil, and exactly one clause can produce nil: the authored %Exchange{id: "bybit"} fallback (read_parse.ex:1073). Every other venue reaches the binary catch-all (read_parse.ex:1075-1077), which always answers :spot or :swap — so for nine venues an unresolvable native id silently passes through as the struct's symbol. Live 2026-08-10: fetch_leverage_tiers(binanceusdm) returns 6714 rows with "BNXUSDTSETTLED", "OPENUSDT_SETTLED", "ICPUSDT_SETTLED_4" passing through native. Both tests pinning the error branch are bybit-only and pass BECAUSE of the bybit nil clause — they ratify the implementation, not the class.

The passthrough branch cannot distinguish a dead instrument (settled/delisted placeholder — arguably fine to pass through, and failing a 6714-row read over junk rows would be worse) from a live instrument the resolver merely failed to carve (the 583 inbound gap had exactly this shape). Make the outcome EXPLICIT: an authored per-venue dead/unlistable-id grammar (e.g. binance *SETTLED*) that passes through BY NAME with a recorded carve, while every other unresolved id is loud on every venue — not just where an authored nil-clause happens to exist.

Folds ARC F6 (latent): unified_symbol?/1 accepts any string containing "/" as proof of unification (read_parse.ex:829-830), so a degenerate resolver output like "/USDT:USDT" (Symbol.from_exchange_id("USDT", venue, :swap) — empty base) counts as unified and is written into the struct. With the allowlist removed, nine new parse types entered scope, three of which document symbol as nil-for-cross-margin (borrow_rate, borrow_interest, margin_loan) — a currency code landing in symbol would be rewritten to "/USDT:USDT" instead of left alone. Add a base/quote-non-empty sanity check to unified_symbol?.

Sequencing: depends_on 583 because both rewrite the same resolver region of read_parse.ex (583 widens binance_contract_symbol inbound; this task restructures the fail-loud/passthrough decision around it). Never fan out together.

Authority: the venues' own instrument catalogs define which ids are live; the dead-id grammar is authored per venue with provider-doc/observed citations in the carve register. First verification move: the live binanceusdm leverage-tiers read — SETTLED rows resolve per the authored grammar, and a synthetic unresolvable id on a non-bybit venue is loud.

task.title: Emulated configuration reads answer {:ok, nil} when the plural has no row — a config read refuses or errors, it never hands back nil
acceptance_criteria: The four configuration handlers (trading_fee, leverage, margin_mode, market_leverage_tiers) error on a missing row — {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} naming the symbol, never {:ok, nil}; unit-pinned per handler
fetch_position's nil-for-flat stays, recorded as an explicit decision with a test asserting {:ok, nil} for a flat symbol
The offline repro flips: fetch_leverage(binancecoinm, unknown symbol) is a loud error (stub test); a live coinm probe with a well-formed unknown symbol is recorded as evidence
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Changing the plural reads' row sets
The leverage-0 sentinel semantics (sibling task)
task.body:
ARC whole-surface finding on the landed task 586 (2026-08-11), filed as the CLASS invariant. Five emulation handlers use the {:ok, pick_symbol_entry(rows, symbol)} idiom, which returns {:ok, nil} when the plural read carries no row for the symbol: handle_fetch_trading_fee (emulation.ex:356), handle_fetch_position (:368), handle_fetch_leverage (:467), handle_fetch_margin_mode (:483), handle_fetch_market_leverage_tiers (:501). Three siblings in the SAME module already do it right — require_symbol_result errors on a miss (handle_fetch_funding_rate :519, handle_fetch_funding_interval :537, and :406). Verified offline: Bourse.fetch_leverage(binancecoinm, "DOGE/USD:DOGE") -> {:ok, nil}.

The idiom is pre-existing but task 586 newly activated it for the binance futures family, and it is aggravated on binancecoinm where the symbol is consume'd off the wire — the selection is purely client-side against whatever the account payload happens to carry, so a typo'd or delisted symbol silently answers {:ok, nil} instead of an error.

The invariant: a CONFIGURATION read (leverage, margin mode, trading fee, leverage tiers) whose venue answer contains no row for the requested symbol surfaces a loud error naming the symbol. fetch_position is the one deliberate exception — flat IS an answer — and that exception gets recorded as an explicit decision (comment + test), not left as an accident of shared idiom.

Authority: client-boundary contract; no external authority needed. First verification move: the offline repro above, then a live coinm read with an unknown-but-well-formed symbol.

task.title: Binance futures leverage/margin carve completion: coinm cannot read the margin mode it can set, and leverage 0 ships as a multipliable number
acceptance_criteria: binancecoinm fetch_margin_mode/fetch_margin_modes are callable and answer the isolated-flag-derived mode — live demo evidence, before-state (has=false) recorded
The coinm singular fetch_leverage carries margin_mode from the same row — the live nil observed 2026-08-11 becomes "cross"/"isolated"
annotate_binance_margin_mode gains the leverage parse-type wiring and a list-payload case; both unit-pinned

leverage "0" rows normalize to long/short nil with raw 0 in info, on both venues — pinned against the committed 47-row coinm recording (46 nil, BTCUSD_PERP 3) and a usdm stub; carve-register entries record the sentinel on both venues plus coinm marginMode
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: The {:ok, nil} missing-row idiom (sibling class task)
Replay-set inclusion of the coinm recording (task 582)
task.body:
ARC whole-surface findings on the landed task 586 (2026-08-11), two coupled gaps in the same field-map region.

(1) binancecoinm declares fetchMarginMode/fetchMarginModes false while setMarginMode is true — a consumer can SET coinm margin mode but not READ it. The venue serves the data: every position row in the committed recording (test/fixtures/responses/binancecoinm/fetch_leverages.json) carries "isolated": false. The derivation exists and is correct — annotate_binance_margin_mode/1 (read_parse.ex:3232-3241) maps isolated true/false -> "isolated"/"cross" — but it is wired only for parse_type "margin_mode" (read_parse.ex:2986), coinm's field_maps.leverage.marginMode is null, and the annotator's %{} = row head lets a LIST payload fall through unannotated (:3243). Consequence today: the coinm singular fetch_leverage answers margin_mode nil (live 2026-08-11) although the wire row carried the fact. Carve doctrine: C-T586b confronts leverage/symbol but records no CONFIRM/DIVERGE line for marginMode — a field left null without a register entry is an unconfronted carve.

(2) leverage 0 is Binance's "never configured on this account" sentinel, not a leverage. The committed coinm recording has 46/47 rows at "leverage": "0" and exactly one at "3" (the operator-configured BTCUSD_PERP); live usdm symbolConfig showed 731 rows mostly 0. Binance's own symbolConfig example (developers.binance.com USD-M Symbol-Config) documents no zero case. %Bourse.Leverage{long_leverage: 0} is a plausible number a consumer will multiply by — the @funding_periods_per_day precedent exactly: internally consistent, fully tested, wrong at the consumer. Ship nil with the raw 0 retained in info, and record the sentinel carve in both venues' registers.

Authority: Binance USD-M/COIN-M account REST contracts (developers.binance.com); the committed recordings are the observed evidence. First verification move: live coinm fetch_margin_mode before-state (:not_supported) and after-state, live usdm plural spot-check that a configured symbol keeps its number while an unconfigured one is nil.

task.title: binancecoinm wires plural fetchTradingFees to the symbol-mandatory commission-rate endpoint - move to singular fetchTradingFee and retire the shared parse compensation
acceptance_criteria: fetch_trading_fee (singular) dispatches on binancecoinm and is live-verified against demo-dapi.binance.com with a real success
capabilities.has no longer claims a plural fetchTradingFees that cannot dispatch without a symbol: the plural is either absent or wired to a genuine all-symbols venue read
a symbol-less unified trading-fees call on binancecoinm no longer surfaces the raw venue -1102
the venue-agnostic fetchTradingFees single-struct compensation clause in read_parse.ex is removed and the full suite stays green
carve C-T545b amended (or a successor carve added) recording the singular-vs-plural confrontation
out_of_scope: Trading-fee coverage for other venues
A computed all-symbols fan-out client-side
task.body:
ARC pass on landed task 545 (2026-08-11), cross-session finding. Bourse.Unified documents fetch_trading_fees (plural) as "fetch trading fees for all symbols" with no required params, but binancecoinm wires the PLURAL to dapiPrivateGetCommissionRate, whose contract mandates symbol - live probe: Bourse.fetch_trading_fees(ex) surfaces the raw venue -1102 "Mandatory parameter 'symbol' was not sent". This is the exact inverse of binanceusdm (singular fetchTradingFee -> commissionRate, plural empty) and diverges from binance spot, whose plural maps a genuine all-symbols source. Carve C-T545b is silent about the per-symbol read living under the plural name, and the new integration test never exercises the symbol-less call.

The delivery also compensates in the SHARED parse layer: read_parse.ex shape_parsed_result wraps a single %TradingFee{} into a one-entry map keyed by the requested symbol whenever js_name == "fetchTradingFees". That clause is venue-agnostic, and requested_symbol falls back to the parsed native symbol - nil for coinm (trading_fee.symbol authored null) - so any future venue whose plural fee read parses to one struct silently yields a map keyed by nil.

Fix class is SINGULAR, not fan-out: flip coinm to fetchTradingFee wired to the commission-rate endpoint (matching usdm and the endpoint arity). If a real plural is wanted, wire it to a genuine all-symbols source the way binance spot does (account feeTier); per-symbol fan-out over ~hundreds of COIN-M symbols is a rate-limit hazard and still not a single authored read. Retire the read_parse plural-compensation clause with the rewiring and amend carve C-T545b with the confrontation.

Provider authority: COIN-M Commission Rate contract (developers.binance.com, pinned in priv/authority/binancecoinm/). Require one live success (singular, demo-dapi.binance.com) and confirm the symbol-less plural path can no longer surface a raw -1102.

task.title: binance-family ledger enums are incomplete and undirected - add the missing income-type arms, sign_direction, and a documented-set coverage guard for ledger_entry.type
acceptance_criteria: binancecoinm and binanceusdm ledger_entry.type enum_maps cover every provider-documented incomeType, including INSURANCE_CLEAR and AUTO_EXCHANGE where documented
a documented-set coverage guard for ledger_entry.type exists in the suite, registering provider citations per venue that authors a ledger type enum_map, and fails on any missing documented arm
the guard's documented sets cite the full venue contract (endpoint doc plus FAQ or change log where applicable), not a single enum page
binance-family ledger_entry.direction is authored via the sign_direction recipe and pinned by offline typed-parser tests off signed income fixtures
carve registers record the confrontations for the new arms and the direction recipe

the guard's scope generalizes to required-source nil slots: a unified enum-or-currency slot authored null while the provider contract marks its source field required is a suite failure, and the lighter transaction/transfer instances are fixed under it - transaction.currency resolves from the required asset_id via the venue's asset mapping, transaction.type carries the per-endpoint deposit/withdrawal literal, and transfer currency/fee stop parsing to silent nil
out_of_scope: Ledger coverage for non-binance venues beyond registering their documented sets in the guard
Changing the unmapped-enum fallback semantics globally (tracked separately if needed)
task.body:
ARC pass on landed task 545 (2026-08-11), cross-session finding, class-scoped. The COIN-M Get Income History contract documents incomeType TRANSFER, WELCOME_BONUS, FUNDING_FEE, REALIZED_PNL, COMMISSION, INSURANCE_CLEAR, DELIVERED_SETTELMENT; the authored binancecoinm ledger_entry.type enum_map covers all EXCEPT INSURANCE_CLEAR (binanceusdm additionally documents AUTO_EXCHANGE, also unmapped there). An unmapped enum value without enum_default parses to nil SILENTLY (response_parser.ex enum_fallback), so a liquidation-clearance row ships as a typed LedgerEntry with type: nil. Unlike order status, no whole-surface coverage guard exists for ledger types - the gap is invisible until a consumer account holds such a row.

Second half of the same surface: ledger_entry.direction is authored null across the binance family, while bybit and okx both author the sign_direction recipe off the signed amount. Binance income is signed (the offline coinm test pins -0.00000375), so the existing recipe applies verbatim - the binance-family ledger is strictly less joinable than bybit/okx for no venue reason.

Class rule this task encodes (taught by the EXPIRED_IN_MATCH fix, carve C-T545d): a venue's documented enum set must be derived from the venue's FULL contract - endpoint contract plus FAQ and change-log-documented values - never from a single enum page, because those pages go stale while the venue ships new values. The coverage guard mirrors test/bourse/authored_order_status_coverage_test.exs: register each venue's provider-documented ledger-type set with citations and assert the authored enum_map covers it (defensive extra aliases stay allowed).

Provider authority: COIN-M and USD-M Get Income History contracts (developers.binance.com, pinned under priv/authority/). Offline evidence suffices for the enum arms (no live income rows are guaranteed on the demo account); direction is pinned by offline typed-parser tests off the signed income fixtures.

UPDATE 2026-08-11 (folds ARC-546 F4, live-verified): the same silent-nil class ships on lighter today - a REAL 10000 USDC deposit parsed live to Transaction{type: nil, currency: nil}, and the transfer map leaves currency/status/fee null, although the provider contract marks DepositHistoryItem.asset_id, TransferHistoryItem.asset_id and TransferHistoryItem.fee required and the venue's Asset operation maps asset_id to symbol (the identical id space the account assets slice already consumes). type is endpoint-determined (deposit/withdrawal literal per method), never the venue's WithdrawHistoryItem.type (secure|fast - a different vocabulary). The fixture ratifies the nils (fetch_deposits.json rows carry asset_id 1/2/3, nothing asserts currency or type). Hence the added criterion: the guard covers required-source nil slots generally, with the lighter transaction/transfer instances as the proof cases alongside the binance ledger arms.

acceptance_criteria: Bourse constructs coinbaseexchange and fetch_ohlcv + fetch_ticker succeed live against api.exchange.coinbase.com for ETH-USD (public, no credentials) — one real success recorded as reality evidence per the client's manifest/oracle-gate mechanism
One relevant live error pinned (e.g. an unsupported granularity value returns the venue's own error, asserted on the venue's error semantics, not just non-200)

The authored spec/docs record the venue quirks: numeric granularity set {60,300,900,3600,21600,86400}, max 300 rows per call, response ordering and absence/presence of the forming bucket as OBSERVED live (consumer-reported newest-first + missing forming bucket are premises unverified — confirm before encoding), start/end windowed pagination for >300-row histories works through the client

The vendored reference slice gains coinbaseexchange.json byte-identical to the workbench corpus copy under the same upstream pin

task.body:
Add coinbaseexchange (api.exchange.coinbase.com, ex-GDAX/Pro) to the client as its first deliberately public-only venue: GET /products/{id}/candles and GET /products/{id}/ticker, nothing else. Demand signal is concrete: a consuming app structurally depends on Coinbase ETH-USD spot — seeded IndicatorSettings name it as source, and two of its roadmap tasks (quarterly lines needing full daily history, TradingView datafeed needing exactly these candles) consume this source; symbol routing, the 300-row pagination window, and the ordering/forming-bucket quirks belong documented in the lib instead of rebuilt three times in the consumer.

Follow the mix ccxt.promote_venue flow (--check/--promote with candidate + report), passing the reference document from the workbench corpus. The corpus reference confirms the endpoint (public.get.products/{id}/candles) and timeframes 1m/5m/15m/1h/6h/1d matching the numeric granularity seconds. Consumer-observed behavior (newest-first ordering, max 300 rows, forming bucket absent) is premise unverified — confirm live during reality recording before encoding it in the spec. Authority: live api.exchange.coinbase.com traffic + Coinbase's own Exchange API docs; the CCXT extraction is authoring reference only.

Public-only is not a contract break: authored specs are already per-venue subsets (alpaca ships 5 endpoints) and capabilities.has declares the surface honestly — the promotion gate enforces that every method is explicitly supported or unsupported.

Dispatch trigger (routing): live external-system semantics needing independent evidence, plus a public-surface addition to the client (new venue in Bourse's supported set).

task.title: Confront the unit of every authored rate-like slot against venue-owned arithmetic
acceptance_criteria: Every authored fundingRate, funding-rate-history rate, interest/borrow rate, percentage and fee-rate slot across the ten venues has a recorded unit confrontation: a carve-register line naming the venue's unit (fraction vs percent vs bps) and the arithmetic or provider statement that established it - a verbatim copy with no unit note is a review failure
Any slot found mis-scaled is fixed with its goldens and offline expectations recomputed from the corrected unit, never by adjusting the assertion to the shipped value

For at least the funding-rate slots, the confrontation uses venue-owned cross-field arithmetic (e.g. funding value = mark price x rate under the venue's stated unit) or an explicit provider unit statement, cited per venue
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.oracle_gate are green
out_of_scope: The lighter fundingRate instance - already fixed and carve-recorded as C-T546g in bourse commit 0bb9b3f
Inventing new unified rate slots; this task confronts existing authored ones
task.body:
ARC pass on landed task 546 (2026-08-11), class-scoped from a live-proven instance. Lighter published funding rate in PERCENT while the authored slice copied it verbatim as a fraction, shipping values 100x too large (0.0012 instead of 1.2e-5, i.e. ~1051% APR instead of ~10.5%) - and the golden ratified it because it was computed with the same assumption. The proof was venue-owned arithmetic: for every live market, funding value == mark_price x rate / 100, so the fraction reading implied a $639 BTC that the venue's own order book refutes.

The class: any rate-like number a venue publishes (funding, interest, fee, percentage) carries an implicit unit that CCXT-derived references and verbatim copies get wrong silently, and per-venue goldens cannot catch it because they inherit the authoring assumption. The confrontation is cheap where the venue publishes a cross-field identity (funding value, fee amounts on fills) or an explicit unit statement in its docs; where neither exists the register line honestly records the unit as unverified rather than assumed.

Provider authority: each venue's own API docs and cross-field arithmetic on live or recorded rows. CCXT's scaling choices are compatibility reference only - agreement with CCXT proves nothing about the unit.

task.title: Lighter account and history slice fidelity against a funded, active testnet account
acceptance_criteria: Position, trade and liquidation symbol slots resolve to the unified market symbol (e.g. BTC/USDC:USDC) from the venue's market_id against loaded markets, never the raw id string; live-verified with an open position

Balance free derives from the venue's own available_balance (or an explicitly confronted equivalent), not total minus locked - verified with an open position where margin_balance is non-zero, where the shipped carve overstates free
A flat position row (position 0.00000, venue sign 1) does not report side long; side is suppressed or derived from signed size, confronted against the provider's sign semantics

Trade rows carry side, taker_or_maker, fee and order resolved from the venue's ask/bid account and fee fields against our own account_index; the venue's trade classification enum (trade|liquidation|deleverage|market-settlement) does not pollute the unified order-type slot
TransferEntry from/to carry the counterparty account identity, with the spot|perps route explicitly dispositioned (info or a confronted slot) as a recorded DIVERGE

The empty my_trades/withdrawals/transfers/liquidations recordings are re-captured populated from real testnet activity (a :dangerous-tagged fill and a transfer with cleanup) and the manifest body_populated flags flip to true

The C-T546 carve entry is amended to honest per-method evidence status (which recordings are populated vs shape-only, which slices remain unverified) with explicit DIVERGE lines for the symbol, free-balance and transfer-route decisions

A stub-honesty guard exists for lighter: hand-written test stubs for provider schemas with required fields must carry every required field, so a stub can never omit a field that decides a parse branch (the shipped position stub omitted the REQUIRED symbol field, which is exactly what hid the raw-id symbol bug)

The re-capture records the params the harness auto-resolves (l1_address, account_index, market_id) into caller_params so the task-596 congruence gate re-derives them through the runtime builder on the real fixtures; the exemption registry shrinks to genuinely non-reproducible params (auth_deadline), and the real fetch_deposits recording goes red under the gate if the builder ever drops l1_address again
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.oracle_gate are green
out_of_scope: The funding-rate unit fix (shipped in bourse 0bb9b3f) and the cross-venue unit sweep (task 594)
The transaction.currency/type nil fix (folded into task 592's required-source guard)
deposit/history l1_address handling (shipped in bourse 0bb9b3f, carve C-T546h)
New unified methods beyond the eight task 546 mapped
task.body:
ARC pass on landed task 546 (2026-08-11), cross-session because every fix needs live evidence the current flat, inactive testnet account cannot produce: an open position, at least one real fill, and a transfer. The shipped slices are internally consistent and fully green precisely because the recorded account is empty - the canonical flat-account-ratifies-everything failure.

Live-proven defects: Position.symbol parses to the raw market_id string ("1") because the authored map is symbol = safeString(market_id) and the read_parse backfill branch is defeated by the venue's REQUIRED AccountPosition.symbol field carrying the base asset ("BTC") - native != symbol so backfill_symbol? is false and loaded-market resolution never runs. The unit stub hid this by omitting that required field. Trade and liquidation symbol slots share the same map shape (untested live, empty recordings). Balance free = total - used counts margin_balance as spendable the moment a position opens, while the venue publishes available_balance and collateral directly. A flat position reports side long off sign=1. Trade rows leave side/taker_or_maker/fee/order null although ask/bid_account_id, is_maker_ask, taker_fee/maker_fee and ask_id/bid_id are all resolvable against our account_index, and the venue's trade classification enum is mapped into the unified order-type slot (unrelated vocabularies; the liquidation classification is also how a forced fill would be recognized). TransferEntry from/to map to from_route/to_route (spot|perps) so an L2 transfer between two accounts can show from == to == perps and the counterparty vanishes; the declared account-index fallbacks never fire because the route key is always present - and the 546 capture scrub redacts account indexes from recordings, so decide the carve deliberately.

Provider authority: the pinned lighter OpenAPI (priv/authority/lighter/manifest.json artifact rest-openapi, revision 6957dd8a) - AccountPosition.symbol and sign, DepositHistoryItem/TransferHistoryItem required lists, Trade type enum and account/fee fields. Evidence discipline: fund and activate the account (limit fill via the existing signed create path, far-from-market ladder or crossing limit as the venue allows; transfer with cleanup), re-capture, manifest-register, then confront each slot against populated rows.

UPDATE 2026-08-12 (folded from the task-596 reviewer proposal, run run-1786511901415-57da5051): the landed congruence gate blanket-exempts the three lighter methods because their fixtures record caller_params {} - so the gate skips shape derivation on exactly the real recordings and a l1_address re-regression would stay green there (caught only by the synthetic pin and the runtime raise). Since this task re-captures those fixtures anyway, record resolved caller_params during capture (capture.ex) and shrink the exemption registry - see the new acceptance criterion. Reviewer evidence: Unified.request_param_shapes forwards account_index/auth_deadline/market_id/l1_address when supplied, so all are runtime-reproducible from caller inputs.

task.title: Request-shape / recorded-request congruence gate: a recording captured with params the runtime builder cannot produce is red
acceptance_criteria: A suite-level gate asserts, for every manifest-registered private recording that carries request params, that the venue's request-shape path (unified builder plus authored request slices) reproduces the recorded param set from the recorded caller inputs - any capture-only param that the runtime cannot emit fails the gate with the param named

The gate caught-class is pinned by a regression case reconstructing the lighter fetch_deposits shape: a capture harness that injects a param (l1_address) the builder omits must be red under the gate as it stood before bourse commit 0bb9b3f

Capture-harness bespoke param injection (recorded_response_fixtures/capture.ex) either disappears in favor of the runtime builder producing the same request, or each remaining injection is a registered, reasoned exemption that the gate enumerates exactly
mix ccxt.oracle_gate or check.dispatch runs the gate so a divergent capture cannot land green

The provider-operation oracle path re-applies the safety classification: ProviderOperations.validate!/1 (what oracle_gate consumes via binary_reports!) runs Capture.authorize-equivalent checks against every manifest operation and validates the plan against its Task-555 inventory report, so a post-hoc plan edit relabeling a private or mutating op as public/read/safe cannot yield green verified evidence

The manifest evidence vocabulary is honest per observation: evidence = verified is derived from the observation class (an error-only or reachability-only proof is not stamped identically to populated row-field semantics) instead of being set unconditionally from the plan in manifest_operations/1
mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Re-capturing recordings; the gate grades congruence of existing artifacts
Public accepted-request goldens - they already pin request shapes for public reads; this task covers the private recording side
task.body:
ARC pass on landed task 546 (2026-08-11), class-scoped from a live-proven instance. The lighter fetch_deposits recording was captured with l1_address injected by a bespoke lookup inside the capture harness (capture.ex ran its own public_get_account round-trip solely to satisfy the provider's required param), while the runtime request builder omitted it - so the shipped method could never succeed live (venue 20001), yet the oracle stayed green because oracle replay verifies recorded BODIES through the parser and never re-derives the request. The implementer discovered the requirement, satisfied it in the evidence path, and left the runtime broken; no existing gate can see that divergence.

The invariant this task encodes: reality evidence must be reproducible by the runtime. A recording whose request the client cannot re-issue is not evidence of the client working - it is evidence of the harness working. The congruence check turns that into a mechanical suite failure instead of a live-probe discovery.

Depends on 556 because that task is currently extending the same capture/manifest/oracle machinery for provider-operation captures; land this gate on top of its boundary rather than in parallel against the same files.

bourse has no Coinbase coverage today. A consumer (trading_dashboard's calibrated oscillator pipeline, documented in its docs/tito_trading_tests.md) needs exactly two read-only public surfaces from Coinbase Exchange spot and currently calls them raw via Req: GET /products/<id>/candles and GET /products/<id>/ticker on api.exchange.coinbase.com. Observed live semantics (verified 2026-08 by the consumer session; re-verify, don't trust): unauthenticated but requires a User-Agent header (403 without); candles granularity in {60,300,900,3600,21600,86400} seconds, max 300 rows per call, newest-first, rows as [time,low,high,open,close,volume] with unix-second timestamps; the currently forming bucket is NOT returned; /ticker carries the live spot price. Authority: Coinbase's own Exchange API documentation (docs.cloud.coinbase.com / docs.cdp.coinbase.com Exchange section) — CCXT's coinbaseexchange implementation is reference material only, never the semantic authority.

Scope is deliberately read-only public market data — no auth, no trading, no account endpoints. How it lands (authored spec vs. hand adapter) is the implementer's call within bourse's architecture.

Remaining work is the consumer-side switch of trading_dashboard from raw Req to bourse, which belongs in that repo's roadmap.

ARC pass on landed task 592 (2026-08-12, run run-1786511899426-5b1aec9e ARC seat). The durable mechanism (final AC): eliminate the silent-nil fallback for ledger types. With a loud unmapped path, registry staleness becomes a runtime discovery instead of an invisible gap, and the registry stops being the only defense. task.title: One unit per unified rate-like field: cross-venue unit invariant (margin percentage, implied volatility, lighter coverage, extras-carried rates)
acceptance_criteria: A manifest-wide test asserts a single unit per unified rate-like field (margin percentages, IV, funding/interest rates, fee rates, ticker percentage) across ALL runtime venues, with the venue list derived from the runtime-support set, never hardcoded

Bourse.Position and the greeks struct docs name the unit for every rate-like field; the deribit margin-percentage scale and the lighter margin/percentage passthroughs emit that unit, with goldens and offline expectations recomputed from the corrected unit — never assertions adjusted to shipped values

IV units are confronted per venue against provider-owned docs with CONFIRM/DIVERGE carve entries; venues publishing percent points carry authored scales; the IV keys are in the confrontation guard's rate-key set
lighter has a rate-unit confrontation block covering its rate-like slots and the guard covers every runtime venue
extras-carried unified rate slots are inside the guard's derivation; the dead income field maps are deleted or corrected (derive's carries the funding-cashflow-as-rate bug in its extras sibling)
Live evidence: deribit and bybit IV probed live and recorded next to the chosen unified unit in the carve register
out_of_scope: Wiring the income parse slot (stays unwired; only the dead maps are cleaned)
Funding-period markers on fraction units (covered by C-T535a)
task.body:
Task 594 confronted each venue's rate units against itself but never confronted the venues against each other; the ARC pass on commit 8354d03 (2026-08-12) found the unified surface carries contradictory units. Evidence, all verified in that pass:

1. Position.initial_margin_percentage / maintenance_margin_percentage is a FRACTION on binance, binancecoinm, binanceusdm, bybit and okx (e.g. 0.1 = 10%), PERCENT POINTS on deribit (authored `initial_margin / size_currency` with `"scale": 100`, so 10 = 10%), and lighter passes `initial_margin_fraction` through as the string "5.00" — a third convention. `Bourse.Position` docs never pin a unit, so no per-venue review could refute either side. Pick ONE unified unit (recommendation: fraction — the five-venue majority), fix the deribit and lighter outliers with goldens recomputed from the corrected unit, and document the unit on the struct fields.

2. Implied volatility is live-inconsistent TODAY and sits outside the guard's @rate_keys: deribit `mark_iv` 63.29 (percent points; live test.deribit.com public/ticker BTC option, 2026-08-12) vs bybit `markIv` "0.7567" (fraction; bybit v5 tickers doc). okx `markVol`, binance `markIV`, derive `option_pricing.iv` are bare safeNumber passthroughs with no scale and no confrontation. Confront IV per venue against provider-owned docs, author scales where the venue publishes percent points, and add the IV keys (impliedVolatility, markImpliedVolatility, askImpliedVolatility, bidImpliedVolatility) to the guard.

3. The confrontation guard hardcodes @venues to the ten venues task 594 touched; lighter (a supported runtime venue with 10 rate-like slots, zero confrontation, and the repo's only proven percent-source rate, C-T546g scale 0.01) is structurally exempt, as is any future venue. Derive the venue list from the runtime-support set like every other venue-wide test (mix_project_test, live_drift_test, registry_test, spec_test), and author lighter's confrontation block — including `ticker.percentage <- daily_price_change` (recorded raw 1.3548) and the margin fraction string above.

4. extras-carried rates escape the slot derivation (collect_field_map_paths matches map KEYS; an extras entry carries rate-ness in unified_key): bybit, hyperliquid and derive each author `income.extras[0] -> rate`, and derive's maps the same dollar cashflow to rate that task 594 just fixed in funding_history. Mitigating: "income" is not in @parse_slots, so all three are dead slices today. Extend the derivation to extras and delete the dead income maps (or fix derive's before it can be wired).

5. Guard robustness folds: the register split reads only the FIRST C-T594 block (later amendments invisible; literal prefix collides with a future C-T5940), File.read! runs once per path, and the absent-direction cross-check is one-way only (a null slot must claim absent, but a shared prose row prevents the reverse check at line granularity — per-slot markers would enable it).

The real deliverable is item 0 underneath all of these: a manifest-wide test asserting ONE unit per unified rate-like field across all runtime venues. The per-venue registers cannot catch cross-venue divergence by construction; only a whole-surface invariant can. Dispatch trigger: repo-wide invariant + public unified-contract semantics change.

task.title: Ledger vocabulary is route-blind: scope the type registries per routed endpoint and make the unified type contract honest
acceptance_criteria: fetch_ledger on OKX's asset/bills route emits the funding-account vocabulary (deposit/withdrawal/transfer arms per OKX's own asset-bills documentation), never the account-bills reading of the same codes; a routed-row confrontation test pins one row per route

The type registry is scoped per routed endpoint where the venue publishes distinct vocabularies (OKX account-bills vs asset-bills; binance income vs options bills), and the coverage guard asserts each scope against its own provider set

binance options ledger rows no longer hard-fail on unenumerated types: the options bill route carries passthrough or its own branch, and C-T592c states honestly that the provider documents type as a free string (shape evidence, not literal enumeration)
Passthrough venues assert documented-set SUPERSET coverage instead of two-way equality; the identity no-op enum padding is removed from bybit/okx/hyperliquid specs
The OKX bill-type enumeration is a manifest-registered recording that mix ccxt.oracle_gate covers; the guard's citation assertion is restored to String.starts_with?("https://")

The unified type carve is decided and recorded per venue as CONFIRM or DIVERGE against the documented unified vocabulary — translating OKX's enumerated code->name semantics or documenting the divergence, never recording passthrough of known-translatable codes as CONFIRM
The derivation note assertion is load-bearing: stated count equals the registry set size
Live evidence: one populated OKX asset/bills row (a real demo deposit/transfer) or, if unreachable, a prod-verification-ledger entry naming the exact blocked call
out_of_scope: Translating bybit/hyperliquid passthrough literals into unified values (their vocabularies are venue-idiomatic; only the carve decision is required)
Wiring the income parse slot (task 600 territory)
task.body:
The ARC pass on commit 3aaa75a (task 598, 2026-08-12) found the new ledger type registry is exact for four provider sets but route-blind and dishonest at two edges. Evidence, all verified in that pass:

1. SERIOUS — OKX maps ledger types account-bills-only, but fetchLedger also routes GET /api/v5/asset/bills (authored endpoint 46, reachable via type/method selection), where the SAME type codes mean different things: on the asset-bills vocabulary 1 = Deposit and 2 = Withdrawal (corroborated via the sibling docs-v5 engine; confirm against okx.com's own asset-bills section before authoring), while the flat map emits them as "transfer" and "trade" — silently, on a reachable route. The guard's two-way equality assertion now FORBIDS adding the funding-route arms to the same flat map, cementing the route-blindness. Needed: a per-route branch or a second field map, plus a split registry (account-bills set vs asset-bills set), and the routed-row-shape confrontation 598 did for binance applied to OKX.

2. SERIOUS — binance options FEE is a CCXT-docstring value wearing a provider citation: the cited AccountFundingFlowResponseInner.md at pin a13868d0 documents type as a free String ("(fees)"), enumerating nothing; the pinned "provider-shaped options row" is byte-identical to the CCXT source blob's example row inside the spec itself. Meanwhile binance/binanceusdm ledger type has NO enum_passthrough, so any eapi/v1/bill row with type != FEE now hard-fails fetch_ledger(type: "option") with {:error, {:unmapped_ledger_type, ...}} — the venue's most OPEN vocabulary got the STRICTEST treatment while the three enumerated vocabularies got passthrough. Restate C-T592c's options evidence honestly (the provider doc gives shape, not literals) and author passthrough or a route branch for the options bill route.

3. MODERATE — the two-way equality assertion forces open-vocabulary specs to carry identity no-op padding (bybit 90/101, okx 21/32, hyperliquid 12/14 entries are runtime no-ops under enum_passthrough), and raw venue literals ("ADL", "CUSTODY_UNLOCK_REFUND", bare "12"/"250", inconsistent casing "Prize" beside "trade") flow into a unified field. OKX's account/subtypes response IS a type->name mapping, so the semantics for the 21 unmapped codes were in hand and discarded — recorded as CONFIRM where it is a DIVERGE from the documented unified vocabulary. Decide the carve honestly (translate the OKX codes, or accept documented divergence), and let passthrough venues assert SUPERSET instead of equality so the no-op padding goes away. (The public docs were already aligned to current behavior in 3001f5b; this item decides whether the behavior itself is the contract.)

4. MODERATE — the OKX registry's sole evidence is an unregistered ad-hoc live call: no account/subtypes recording is committed anywhere, so CI cannot re-derive the 32 values and enumeration drift is undetectable; and the guard's citation gate was weakened from String.starts_with?("https://") to String.contains? specifically to admit that prose entry. Capture and register the subtypes response as a manifest-registered recording, then restore starts_with?.

5. MINOR fold — assert the derivation string's stated count equals MapSet.size(values) so the derivation note is load-bearing.

Provider authorities: OKX API v5 docs (funding-account asset/bills vs trading-account bills vocabularies; GET /api/v5/account/subtypes), binance-connector-java pin a13868d0 (IncomeType.md for USD-M/COIN-M — already exact), binance options Account Funding Flow doc (shape only). Write-set overlaps task 600 on the authored binance-family specs — the dispatcher serializes; no logical dependency. Dispatch trigger: public unified-contract semantics + repo-wide guard change + live external-system evidence (OKX demo recording capture).

task.title: The rate-unit invariant grades declarations, not emissions: make it falsifiable and fix the three unit bugs it certified green
acceptance_criteria: The invariant test is falsifiable: seeding one venue with a deliberately contradictory unit (mutation check in the test module or a negative fixture) turns it red; the expected-unit table is derived from or asserted against the public struct docs, not restated from the specs

An emitted-value check exists: for every authored scale, the guard asserts the declared source unit is consistent with the scale arithmetic (the fc5e570 check restored and generalized), and at least one golden per corrected slot pins a provider-shaped raw value through the parser to the unified unit

binance-family OptionData.percentage emits percent points (scale 100 on the eapi route) with a provider-cited carve amendment and an emitted-value golden; the binance fetchTicker eapi route's percentage unit is confronted and recorded

deribit margin percentage is correct per instrument kind: inverse stays fraction, linear is branched or restricted with the carve claim softened to what the provider contract supports; a linear golden or a prod-verification-ledger entry exists
hyperliquid Position.percentage is signed (loss emits negative), pinned by a golden recomputed from the corrected arithmetic
The confrontation-section regex matches any C-T-numbered rate-unit block (no task-number pin) and supersession between conflicting unit rows follows date, not file position
recorded_venue observed-evidence kinds at every tier require a registered frozen body; the derive/okx C-T600 trailers are restated honestly or upgraded with captured recordings
mix check.dispatch green; the rate-unit guard and carve_register_consistency stay green on the corrected corpus
out_of_scope: Translating passthrough ledger vocabularies (task 601)
New IV work beyond what 600 landed (deribit/bybit scales are verified live and stay)
task.body:
The ARC pass on commit 95d8d88 (task 600, 2026-08-12) proved the new cross-venue unit invariant cannot fail and found three real unit bugs it certified green. Evidence, all verified in that pass:

GUARD MECHANISM (the root cause):
- The "one unit per unified field" grouping assertion is mathematically vacuous: expected_unit!/1 and unified_field/1 are both pure functions of the same (rate_key, parse_slot) pair, and every entry already passed unit == expected_unit! — so Enum.uniq() over a group can never exceed length 1. The only real gate is the hand-written @fraction_keys table, which restates the specs instead of deriving from the public struct contract.
- The guard validates DECLARED units from carve tables, never EMITTED values; the one emitted-value cross-check (scale 100 => must claim percent points, added in fc5e570) was deleted, and the surviving 0<scale<1 arm accepts either unit, constraining nothing.
- @confrontation_section is pinned to C-T(?:594|600) — the next task's confrontation blocks are invisible to the guard (recurring exemption; 600 already had to widen 594's pin). Match any C-T\d+ block carrying a rate-unit marker instead.
- Supersession is by file position (reversed concatenation, last match wins), while docs/authored-specs.md:286 mandates supersession by date. A 594-suffixed amendment appended later would silently flip the graded unit.

THE THREE BUGS IT MISSED (fix with emitted-value goldens, never assertion-adjusted):
1. SERIOUS — binance-family option.percentage: fetchOption routes eapiPublicGetTicker whose priceChangePercent is a DECIMAL FRACTION (provider example: priceChange -16.2038 / lastPrice 1000 = priceChangePercent "-0.0162"), authored with no scale while the carve declares percent points citing the SPOT 24hr-ticker doc — and deribit emits genuine percent points (price_change 10.23 = 10.23%) into the same unified OptionData.percentage. ~100x apart. Author scale 100 on binance/binancecoinm/binanceusdm option.field_map.percentage, cite the eapi contract, pin an emitted-value golden from a provider-shaped eapi ticker row. Also confront the fetchTicker route: binance fetchTicker lists eapiPublicGetTicker too, so Ticker.percentage is percent points for spot/futures and a fraction for option symbols within one venue.
2. MODERATE — deribit margin percentage: dropping scale:100 is right for INVERSE instruments (initial_margin 0.000197283 / size_currency 0.006687487 = 2.95% fraction) but unevidenced-to-wrong for USDC/USDT LINEAR instruments (margin is denominated in the stablecoin per Deribit's linear-perpetual docs, size_currency in base coin — the divide is price-scaled, emitting ~6000 for a 0.1 fraction). The registered fetch_positions recording has all-zero margins and the new golden is synthetic. Branch on instrument kind/settlement or restrict the divide to inverse, soften the carve's "same-currency" claim, and pin a linear-instrument golden (live if a demo position is reachable, else prod-verification-ledger entry).
3. MINOR — hyperliquid Position.percentage is computed as Decimal.abs(unrealized)/margin_used*100 (read_parse.ex ~4945), so a losing position reports positive PnL percent — contradicting the newly authored "percent points (10 = 10%)" signed doc; okx and binance/alpaca are signed. Drop the abs.

EVIDENCE HONESTY (folds):
- derive C-T600g and okx C-T600j set observed_evidence.kind "recorded_venue" for hand-authored parser goldens (docs/authored-specs.md:281 defines the kind as a frozen venue body) while their own known_gap_reason admits no registered row exists. Tighten the kind vocabulary at tier 2/3 in carve_register_consistency_test, or capture live derive/okx option tickers (derive demo was reachable during the run).
- okx C-T600j cites the bare docs root for the markVol/pxVol=fraction claim; deep-link the actual option market-data section or capture the value live.

Provider authorities: Binance options API GET /eapi/v1/ticker (priceChangePercent example row), Deribit public/ticker (price_change percent points) and linear-perpetual margin documentation, hyperliquid clearinghouseState. Dispatch trigger: repo-wide invariant + public unified-contract semantics + live external evidence.

task.title: InvalidNonce is terminal: split nonce/timestamp drift from credential rejection in the retry contract
acceptance_criteria: An error resolving through the InvalidNonce class name yields a dedicated error type whose retry_class is retryable (should_retry?/1 true), while :authentication_error and :permission_denied remain :auth with should_retry?/1 false

At least one venue's provider-owned doc statement on nonce/timestamp errors is cited as the authority for the retryable classification (URL in carve/commit or test), and any venue error codes currently mapped through InvalidNonce still resolve consistently — mix ccxt.error_authority green
Moduledoc, Descripex error docs and the retry-collapse comment no longer fold invalid nonce into authentication_error; the compatibility class mapping table reflects the new type
Classification unit tests pin the new type and both directions of the split (nonce retryable, credential rejection terminal); no existing assertion weakened; full offline suite green
out_of_scope: Updating the BUGS.md entry status (orchestrator does this post-land)
Consumer-side changes in trading_dashboard
Re-classing other collapsed edges (bad_request, exchange_not_available) — they keep their documented resolution
task.body:
Consumer bug (BUGS.md entry 2026-08-12, reporter: trading_dashboard): lib/bourse/error.ex maps the
"InvalidNonce" class name to :authentication_error (name map, ~line 260), and :authentication_error
carries retry_class :auth (@retry_class_by_type, ~line 186) — should_retry?/1 false, "do not retry
without intervention". The collapse comment (~lines 169-171) documents this as a deliberate lossy
resolution: the upstream per-venue retry_classification tables class InvalidNonce as :network
(transient), but the Elixir-side collapse picked :auth as the "dominant/safer" bucket. Verified by
reading lib/bourse/error.ex at those lines, 2026-08-12.

The consumer case shows :auth is the WRONG side for the money path: nonce/timestamp-window errors
(client clock skew, concurrent signers racing a nonce, venue recv-window jitter) succeed on retry
after re-sync, but trading_dashboard's OrderLifecycle treats retry_class :auth as a DEFINITE
rejection — a transient nonce blip while placing a protective stop marks the order :rejected
terminal and strands the guarding ladder while the position is live.

Fix shape: give the InvalidNonce class its own error type (e.g. :invalid_nonce) with a retryable
retry_class (:network), keeping genuine credential rejection (AuthenticationError, PermissionDenied)
at :auth. This is a public contract change on Bourse.Error (error_type union grows; the moduledoc
line ":authentication_error - API key/secret rejected or invalid nonce" must be corrected; Descripex
docs and the 34-class compatibility mapping updated; the resolved edge removed from the collapse
comment). The per-exchange errors.retry_classification tables preserved verbatim on Bourse.Exchange
are class-name-keyed and should NOT need spec edits — if an authored spec edit turns out necessary
for a binance-family venue, note that task 603 (in flight) touches those spec files.

Authority: the venues' own docs on nonce/timestamp errors win (e.g. Binance -1021 "Timestamp for
this request is outside of the recvWindow" is documented client-clock drift, retryable after
re-sync). CCXT's taxonomy (InvalidNonce under NetworkError/OperationFailed) is reference material
only, cited in the BUGS entry as practice signal, never as the authority. Reconcile with
mix ccxt.error_authority; check whether recorded exchange errors for timestamp drift already exist
before recording new ones.

Positive dispatch trigger: public error-contract change on a money-path classification surface,
consumer-reported live defect.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1786533021068-d9b8f637, 1a3a386b1418e23e8ad8fcd6576bc0d46593bc7d).

task.title: Register one cross-venue ledger type taxonomy: same economic event, same unified value, doc enumerates the set
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.LedgerEntry moduledoc + Descripex doc enumerate the registered unified type set and state the two-class contract (registered values; venue-specific snake_case labels for events outside the registry; venue literal always in info)

The same economic event maps to the same registered value on every mapped venue: OKX bill type 8 and binance FUNDING_FEE both emit funding_fee; binance REALIZED_PNL no longer flattens to trade; OPTIONS_PREMIUM_FEE no longer shares a label with funding
A registry test asserts every mapped venue enum_map value is registered-or-declared-venue-specific, and fails on a new unregistered label; existing per-scope registries stay green
Every remapped code carries a carve-register entry citing the venue's own event table (account_subtypes recording for OKX, provider income docs for binance family); no CCXT-as-authority language
Full offline suite + mix ccxt.oracle_gate green; recorded fixtures updated only where parsed output legitimately changed
out_of_scope: Passthrough venues (bybit, hyperliquid, okx asset-route unknowns keep venue literals per the landed 601 contract)
New live recordings (the OKX populated-bills gap stays with the open prod-verification-ledger entries)
LedgerEntry struct shape changes (no new fields)
task.body:
Convergence finding on task 601 (ARC pass 2026-08-13): the landed LedgerEntry doc still names the
unified five ("trade, fee, deposit, withdrawal, transfer") for mapped venues, but the mapped venues
emit far beyond it, and the SAME economic event now gets DIFFERENT labels per venue. Verified by
reading the authored specs on main (post-601):

- okx account/bills enum_map: venue-faithful snake_case of OKX's own typeDesc table (29 values:
  funding_rate, margin_transfer, auto_token_conversion, adl, settlement, ...), verified against the
  manifest-registered account_subtypes recording.
- binance/binanceusdm/binancecoinm income enum_map: a coarse taxonomy beyond the five (cashback,
  commission, rebate, referral, settlement) BUT with CCXT-era flattenings kept: FUNDING_FEE,
  OPTIONS_PREMIUM_FEE and POSITION_LIMIT_INCREASE_FEE all -> "fee"; REALIZED_PNL -> "trade".

Concrete consumer failure: filtering entries by type == "fee" for funding cashflows matches binance
rows but silently misses every OKX funding row (emitted as "funding_rate"); nothing errors.

The architect decision (encoded here, not open for redesign): unified `type` is a REGISTERED coarse
taxonomy of economic event classes — one label per event class across all mapped venues. The
venue's own label is always recoverable from `info` (raw passthrough), so no venue detail is lost.
Confront each venue's own event table (OKX bills typeDesc via the committed account_subtypes
recording; binance IncomeType via the provider's income docs) and register the set. Expected shape:
the five, plus event classes both venue tables share as first-class events — funding_fee (OKX 8
"Funding rate" AND binance FUNDING_FEE land here; a funding payment is a cashflow, distinct from
trading fees), realized_pnl (binance REALIZED_PNL out of "trade"), liquidation, settlement,
interest, rebate, commission, cashback, referral, conversion, and a venue_specific remainder policy:
codes with no cross-venue event class keep a venue-faithful snake_case label and the doc says so
explicitly (two-class contract: registered values + venue-specific labels for events outside the
registry). Record every mapping decision as CONFIRMED/DIVERGE entries in the venue carve registers
(docs/authored-spec-carves/) citing the venue's own table.

The per-scope registries built by task 601 in authored_ledger_contract_coverage_test.exs are the
enforcement point: extend them so every mapped enum_map value is either in the registered unified
set or explicitly declared venue-specific — a new unregistered label fails the suite.

Write-set note: touches the binance-family specs and the ledger coverage test; no other pending
task overlaps these files as of filing.

Positive dispatch trigger: public unified-contract change across four venue specs, cross-venue
invariant with CI enforcement.

acceptance_criteria: A frozen deribit positions body (inverse row, no request symbol) parsed through the real Unified.call fetch_positions path emits the documented margin-percentage fractions, never nil; a linear row still emits its correct branch

A frozen binance eapi ticker body parsed through the real fetchTickers (plural, no symbol context) path emits percentage in percent points (fraction x 100), matching the singular fetchTicker/fetchOption output for the same row
No unit/branch discriminator introduced in task 603 depends solely on request-context market: each is payload- or route-derived, and a test exercises each through a list read
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and the full offline suite green; carve register entries updated where the mechanism changed (payload/route guard instead of market gate), citing the venue's own field semantics

task.body:
Two shipped regressions from task 603, one root cause (ARC pass 2026-08-13): the 603 unit fixes
gate on the REQUEST-context discriminator `market.*`, but ReadParse.build_parse_opts/4 only
populates `market:` when params carry a "symbol" — so every LIST read has no market context and
the discriminator branch silently misses.

Bug 1 — LIVE-CONFIRMED on deribit testnet 2026-08-13: an open inverse BTC-PERPETUAL position
fetched via Bourse.fetch_positions/1 (currency-scoped, no symbol param — deribit's fetchPositions
never takes one) emitted initial_margin_percentage: nil and maintenance_margin_percentage: nil.
Before 603 the same row emitted the real quotient (~0.0295). The authored gate sits on
priv/specs/json/output/authored/deribit.json (~4794): market.inverse branches for
initialMarginPercentage/maintenanceMarginPercentage; with empty context the branch is absent and
ResponseParser.extract_field returns nil. The 603 test passes only because it hand-injects
market: %Bourse.Market{inverse: true} into parse_position/2 — the real list path never does that.

Bug 2 — binance fetchTickers with option market_type routes to eapiPublic_get_ticker with a
`symbols`/no-symbol request, so the new market.option discriminator on the ticker percentage
(binance.json ~25142) takes the false branch and emits the raw eapi fraction: plural option
tickers are still ~100x off. Only fetchTicker/fetchOption are fixed. Ground truth (live,
2026-08-13, production eapi): SOL-260814-66-P priceChange 1.42 / open 0.08 = priceChangePercent
17.75 — the wire value is a fraction; unified percentage must be 1775.0 percent points.

The class invariant (encode it, then fix both instances): a parse-time discriminator must be
derivable from the PAYLOAD (e.g. kind "when" on instrument_name — the mechanism
annotate_bybit_market_category already uses) or from the ROUTE (`_bourse_endpoint_route` is
injected at response-parse time and survives list reads — task 601's mechanism), never solely
from request-context market. For deribit: instrument/settlement is derivable from the payload row
(instrument_name suffix or size_currency). For binance: the eapi ticker ROUTE fully determines
the fraction source unit regardless of singular/plural.

Deliver 603's unmet emitted-output criterion where it matters: assert through the real
Unified.call list paths (fetch_positions without symbol; fetchTickers on the eapi route) against
frozen venue bodies — not by hand-injecting parse opts.

Write-set note: overlaps task 605 on binance.json — harness write-set serialization sequences them.

Positive dispatch trigger: live-confirmed value regression on margin/risk data (money-adjacent),
cross-venue parse invariant.
