task.body:
Completes the product decision task 605 shipped: unified ledger `type` is a registered cross-venue
taxonomy (15 values + venue-faithful snake_case remainder), documented in Bourse.LedgerEntry. Task
605 remapped the binance family and OKX; bybit and hyperliquid still carry pre-taxonomy labels, so
the same economic event still splits cross-venue on the integrated surface. This is contract
coherence work on our own published vocabulary, NOT a provider-proven correction - bybit's and
hyperliquid's raw literals are and stay venue-owned; only our unified aliases move.

Premises (verified 2026-08-13 by direct read of the authored specs, ARC pass on the 605 landing):
- bybit.json enum_map (base field_map, mode passthrough): LIQUIDATION -> "trade", SETTLEMENT ->
  "trade", DELIVERY -> "trade", INTEREST -> "transaction", TRANSFER_IN/TRANSFER_OUT ->
  "transaction", FEE_REFUND -> "cashback" (binance FEE_RETURN sits under rebate), BONUS -> "Prize"
  (a CCXT wallet_fund_type literal - capitalized, not bybit's own word, not snake_case).
- hyperliquid.json maps vaultWithdraw -> "withdraw"; the raw withdraw literal also passes through
  unmapped - one character off the registered "withdrawal". The only in-repo consumer branch that
  filters deposit/withdrawal (Bourse.Emulation.deposit_or_withdrawal?/1) would drop those rows;
  the branch is currently unreachable, so this is latent, not live breakage.
- The registry test currently accepts venue_specific declarations for events that DO have a
  registered class (bybit Prize/transaction, hyperliquid withdraw) - the guard ratifies the split
  instead of catching it, and venue_specific_format is applied only to the okx scope.

Authority: bybit's own v5 enum docs for the UTA and contract transaction logs (the two URLs already
cited as sources in the registry test) define each literal's meaning; hyperliquid's ledger-update
union in the official gitbook does the same. Confront each remapped literal against those tables
and record CONFIRMED/DIVERGE per docs/authored-specs.md. Where a bybit literal genuinely has no
registered class, keep it venue-faithful snake_case of BYBIT's own literal (not CCXT's), and let
the tightened gate plus format rule derive that mechanically where a recorded/documented rendering
source exists. No live venue calls are required for this task - the vocabulary tables are the
provider-owned contract; live bybit transaction-log rows remain nice-to-have evidence, and the
demo/testnet limitations (read-only testnet key) make them optional, not gating.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1786622569557-38be212b, 94da38693f058b7ad474b7b462b754cd3fb59094).

task.title: Money-field discriminators must be payload-derived on every symbol-less read: deribit trade cost is 2.5e9x off, and the endpoint-route key is not an identity
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.fetch_my_trades on deribit without a symbol emits inverse trade cost = amount / price: a frozen BTC-PERPETUAL row (amount 10 USD at price 50000) through the privateGetGetUserTradesByCurrency route emits cost 0.0002, never 500000.0; the payload annotation mechanism task 606 built for positions extends to the trade parse type
direct parse_trade callers keep the request-context market.inverse path as a degradation branch (same when/else shape as commit bc837d9), pinned by a direct-parser assertion

an invariant test enumerates every authored money-field rule whose branch depends on request-context market.* (inverse_op selection or discriminated market.* rules) and fails when such a rule is reachable from a unified method whose required params carry no symbol - the deribit trade cost repro is the seed case, and the test names each surviving rule so a new one cannot land silently

_bourse_endpoint_id is a route identity: it carries every section plus the HTTP method plus the path (repro: 70 first-section/path pairs collide across HTTP verbs in binance.json and binanceusdm.json, 71 in binancecoinm.json, e.g. fapiPrivate/order covering GET+POST+PUT+DELETE); the bare-path fallback stamp in read_parse no longer shares the same key; a spec-level test asserts id uniqueness per venue

the deribit inverse classifier consults exchange.markets first and falls back to instrument-id parsing only when the row's market is unknown, mirroring the okx precedence in read_parse; live testnet markets pin the two shapes (BTC-PERPETUAL inverse true, ETH_USDC-PERPETUAL inverse false)

live evidence: a real deribit testnet fill followed by a symbol-less Bourse.fetch_my_trades pins the observed cost against the fill's amount and price in a tagged integration test; missing credentials flunk with the exact env vars
mix test.json --cover on touched read-path modules stays at tier (Bourse.Unified.ReadParse measured 83.10 percent on 2026-08-13; do not regress below 80)
out_of_scope: Position notional/contracts/contractSize unit semantics (separate task filed the same day)
ledger taxonomy work (separate task)
non-money fields that read request-context market.* (flag them in the invariant test as documented exemptions if intentional)
task.body:
ARC wave review 2026-08-13 (post 606/607 landing), finding F1, live-verified through the unified path: deribit routes fetch_my_trades without a symbol to privateGetGetUserTradesByCurrency, and trade cost's inverse_op selection reads request-context market.inverse, which does not exist on a symbol-less read - so the mul branch fires and a 10-USD-at-50000 inverse fill emits cost 500000.0 instead of 0.0002. Provider semantics per https://docs.deribit.com/api-reference/trading/private-get_user_trades_by_currency.md: amount is USD units for perpetual and inverse futures, price is base currency, so inverse cost is amount / price. Task 606 already built the payload annotation (_bourse_inverse from instrument_name) but scoped it to parse_type == "position"; this task closes the CLASS - no money field may depend on request-context market.* on a read reachable without a symbol.

Secondary hardening from the same review (F5, F8): _bourse_endpoint_id drops the HTTP method and every section past the first (70+ colliding pairs per binance-family venue - premise verified 2026-08-13 by enumerating the authored describe.api trees), and read_parse's bare-path fallback stamps a second namespace into the same key; the first guard authored against a colliding pair will match silently. The deribit inverse classifier also re-derives from the instrument id what exchange.markets already carries authoritatively - mirror the okx markets-first precedence.

Authority boundary: docs.deribit.com and live testnet traffic decide semantics; the repo doctrine (docs/authored-specs.md) applies. Dispatch trigger: money handling on a public unified read.

task.title: Close the remaining ledger-taxonomy splits: bybit funding is invisible, promotional credits and converts split cross-venue, passthrough remainders split by casing
acceptance_criteria: a bybit consumer can read funding payments: the SETTLEMENT arm is confronted against bybit's own enum text (type uta-translog: 'USDT Perp funding settlement, and USDC Perp funding settlement + USDC 8-hour session settlement') and either splits on a payload discriminator the provider documents so funding rows emit funding_fee, or the carve records with evidence why row-level discrimination is impossible and which single class was chosen; a cross-venue invariant test asserts every venue with perpetuals can emit funding_fee from its ledger vocabulary, with any impossible venue carried as a named documented exemption, not silence

one promotional-credit decision applied to both families: bybit BONUS (plus the unmapped BONUS_RECOLLECT/BONUS_TRANSFER_IN/BONUS_TRANSFER_OUT family) and binance-family WELCOME_BONUS/CONTEST_REWARD/BFUSD_REWARD emit the same label; if a new registered class is introduced, Bourse.LedgerEntry's registry, the Descripex hint, and the coverage-test registry update together; carve entries in both registers cite the provider enum tables

bybit CURRENCY_BUY/CURRENCY_SELL (provider text: 'Currency convert, and the liquidation for borrowing asset (UTA loan)') and the unmapped CONVERT literal are confronted - okx maps convert bills to conversion and binance maps AUTO_EXCHANGE to conversion, so 'trade' needs a DIVERGE justification or the arm moves to conversion; outcome recorded in docs/authored-spec-carves/bybit.md

every hyperliquid ledger literal with a registered class stops emitting camelCase: spotTransfer, vaultLeaderCommission, vaultCreate, vaultDistribution, rewardsClaim, spotGenesis are each confronted against the WsLedgerUpdate union at the gitbook URL already pinned in authored_ledger_contract_coverage_test.exs and get a registered class or a venue-faithful snake_case label - authoring from training recall is forbidden

the integrated surface never emits the same economic event under two casings (repro: bybit passthrough ADL vs okx venue-specific adl): the passthrough-remainder rule is encoded once in the coverage test for all scopes, so a raw literal whose casing diverges from a sibling venue's declared label for the same event fails the suite
the cross-family emission test covers the newly decided arms through parse_ledger_entry with venue-frozen rows, and mix ccxt.oracle_gate stays green
out_of_scope: INSURANCE_CLEAR settlement-vs-liquidation (open prod-verification-ledger entry)
okx subtype-level refinement (info retains raw subtypes)
new live recordings for events the demo/testnet accounts cannot produce - tier stays honest at 2 with the gap named
task.body:
Completes what 605/607 started: one taxonomy, same economic event = same label, on the whole integrated surface. Four residuals, all evidence-backed on 2026-08-13 (ARC wave review F2/F7/F9 with the bybit enum text fetched live from bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/enum, plus the 607 reviewer's proposals):

1. F2 (serious): bybit SETTLEMENT covers funding settlement per the provider's own enum, but 607 mapped it to settlement - so bybit is now the only perp venue whose ledger can never emit funding_fee (binance family FUNDING_FEE and okx bill 8 both do). A consumer summing funding across venues silently reads zero on bybit. 607's carve C-T607a even says CONFIRMED as funding/session settlement - the per-task reviewer had no cross-venue seat to reject the collapse.
2. Promotional credits split: bybit BONUS emits bonus while binance WELCOME_BONUS emits cashback - same economic event, two labels. The likelier defect is binance's side (cashback means money returned, not a promotional credit); either answer is fine if confronted, including a new registered class, which is a vocabulary change needing LedgerEntry+Descripex+test updated together.
3. F7: CURRENCY_BUY/SELL is a mixed arm (convert + UTA-loan liquidation) that 607 hardened into the test as 'trade' without a carve entry, contradicting conversion on okx/binance.
4. F9 + 607-reviewer proposal: hyperliquid still emits camelCase for six literals with obvious registered classes, and the same defect class exists at bybit in a different casing (ADL vs okx adl) - scope the fix as the casing/remainder CLASS in the coverage test, not per-venue patches.

Authorities: bybit enum docs at the pinned commit 5ccd3010, hyperliquid WsLedgerUpdate union (gitbook), binance IncomeType.md at the pinned connector revision - all already cited as sources in authored_ledger_contract_coverage_test.exs. Live calls optional (bybit demo translog was empty server-side on 2026-08-13; frozen provider-documented rows + carve confrontation are the evidence path). Dispatch trigger: public label contract + provider confrontation across three venue families.

task.title: Position carries one unit contract: notional is quote-denominated and contracts x contractSize reconciles, on every venue
acceptance_criteria: a cross-venue invariant test asserts for every venue with a position slice: notional is quote-denominated, and contracts x contractSize reconciles to notional (or the venue's carve documents the exception by name) - seeded with frozen rows per venue so a future field-map edit that flips a unit fails the suite

deribit stops being the outlier: for the provider's own get_positions example (size 50 USD, size_currency 0.006687487 BTC on BTC-PERPETUAL), the emitted Position carries quote-denominated notional (50), a populated contractSize (10 USD for BTC futures, market-derived, never hardcoded per-symbol), and contracts consistent with size/contractSize; the base-denominated size_currency lands in a field whose meaning says base, with the decision recorded as a CONFIRMED/DIVERGE carve citing https://docs.deribit.com/api-reference/account-management/private-get_positions.md

live evidence: a small deribit testnet position pins the emitted notional/contracts/contractSize against the venue's own get_positions response in a tagged integration test (repro from 2026-08-13: a 10-USD position emitted notional 1.57394e-4 BTC - base, not quote); missing credentials flunk with exact env vars
no other venue regresses: alpaca market_value, hyperliquid positionValue, lighter position_value, binance/derive computed notional all stay quote-denominated under the new invariant test
mix test.json --cover on touched modules stays at tier and mix check.dispatch passes

PortfolioRisk consumption of notional (bourse_trading owns exposure math)

task.body:
ARC wave review 2026-08-13, finding F4: deribit's position field map sends size_currency (base BTC) to notional and size (USD) to contracts with contractSize null, while every other venue emits quote-denominated notional (alpaca market_value, hyperliquid positionValue, lighter position_value, binance/derive computed). Per the provider contract (docs.deribit.com private/get_positions: size = quote currency for futures, size_currency = base, futures only), a BTC-PERPETUAL position of 50 USD emits notional 0.0067 today - a consumer aggregating notionals across venues silently mixes BTC units into a USD sum, and with contractSize nil cannot even reconstruct the right value. Live-confirmed on testnet 2026-08-13 (10-USD position emitted notional 1.57394e-4). Pre-existing defect, but it sits inside the exact field map 606 touched and is invisible to any per-task review - this is the whole-surface invariant crystallized into CI per the repo's encode-domain-truth rule.

Authority boundary: docs.deribit.com + live testnet decide; deribit market data (contract_size 10.0 for BTC futures, live-verified 2026-08-13) supplies contractSize - never a hardcoded per-symbol constant. Dispatch trigger: money-adjacent public contract change across the unified Position type.

task.title: Deribit linear futures break the fresh unit contract: notional guards on kind, not settlement, so the USDC book emits base-coin notional labelled as quote
acceptance_criteria: A live testnet position on a LINEAR deribit instrument (e.g. ETH_USDC-PERPETUAL or BTC_USDC-PERPETUAL, opened and reduce-only closed in the test) pins: notional is quote-denominated (USDC, consistent with size x mark within tick tolerance), base_quantity equals the base size, contracts equals base size / contract_size with the venue's linear contract_size (e.g. 0.001 BTC), side correct
The existing inverse live assertions stay green: BTC-PERPETUAL notional == |raw size| USD, contracts == notional/contract_size (10), base_quantity == size_currency

Populated recordings for BOTH a linear and an inverse future position are captured from test.deribit.com and registered in the reality manifest, and mix ccxt.oracle_gate goes red if notional sourcing regresses on either branch (this supersedes the separate 'register a populated deribit future-position recording' proposal from run run-1786664191188-0f4ace4b)

The frozen linear row in position_unit_invariant_test.exs and deribit_authored_spec_test.exs asserts notional/base_quantity/contracts VALUES (not just nil-ness) such that swapping the base/quote sourcing turns the suite red — the invariant must catch a base/quote flip, not only a label change
docs/authored-spec-carves/deribit.md and global.md state the inverse/linear split with the provider citations; the wrong 'both quote-denominated' sentence is gone

task.body:
Task 610 routed deribit future `size` to `notional` behind `{"kind":"when","guard":{"field":"kind","in":["future"]}}` and derived `contracts` as |notional|/contract_size — correct for the INVERSE book, where the provider documents size in USD. But deribit `kind` is "future" for the LINEAR (USDC/USDT-quoted) book too, and there the provider documents size as the underlying base coin (docs.deribit.com private-get_user_trades_by_currency / public-get_instruments: "For perpetual and inverse futures the amount is in USD units. For options and linear futures it is the underlying base currency coin."; support.deribit.com "Linear Perpetual": position size fixed in ETH). Linear contract_size is base-denominated as well (BTC_USDT-PERPETUAL 0.001 vs BTC-PERPETUAL 10). So a linear position currently emits base-coin notional in a field the struct documents as "Absolute quote-currency position value", and the C-T610f/global.md carve line "Deribit future size and market contract_size are both quote-denominated" is wrong for half the venue.

The discriminator already exists: the position payload is annotated with `_bourse_inverse` (task 608's markets-first classifier), and the margin-percentage rules in the same field_map already guard on it. Gate `notional`, `contracts` and `base_quantity` sourcing on `_bourse_inverse` the same way: inverse -> notional = |size| (USD), base_quantity = size_currency, contracts = |notional|/contract_size; linear -> notional = |size| x mark_price (or the venue's own quote-value field if one exists — confront with provider docs before computing), base_quantity = |size|, contracts = |size|/contract_size. Correct the carve register (deribit.md + the global.md exception table) to state the split.

Evidence trail: the wave's own linear fixture (`ETH_USDC-PERPETUAL`, size 0.5, size_currency 0.5) never asserts notional; the reality manifest carries only a zero-size future row and an option row, so the oracle cannot catch a regression of either branch (this folds the 610 reviewer's proposal to register a populated recording). ARC review 2026-08-14, finding 1 (serious); premise verified against the live spec JSON and the fixture the same day.

Seed cases stay pinned: BTC-PERPETUAL inverse, ETH_USDC-PERPETUAL linear, BTC-31JUL26-65000-C non-inverse, BTC-FS-31JUL26_17JUL26 inverse, and at least one multi-strike option combo (e.g. BTC-CS-...-100000_200000) plus one single-strike strategy id are non-inverse on the degradation path

task.body:
The `_bourse_inverse` payload annotation decides inverse-ness twice: `exchange.markets` (authoritative, derived from the venue's `instrument_type` enum) when the row's instrument is loaded, and a hand-rolled instrument-id string parser (`deribit_inverse_instrument_id?/1`) when it is not. Task 608's review already caught one divergence (plain options, 2500x cost error, patched by excluding the -C/-P suffix), and ARC review 2026-08-14 found the next instance in the same class: deribit OPTION COMBOS (`BTC-CS-31MAR23-100000_200000`, single-strike strategies like `BTC-STD-31MAR23-100000`) split into shapes the parser reads as inverse — head token without underscore — so a symbol-less combo fill takes `amount / price` where option-combo amounts are base coin (`amount * price`): an error off by price^2. ~188 of 4971 live instruments are combos per the carve register. Nothing fails when the two classifiers disagree.

Make one classifier authoritative. Preferred shape: derive the degradation answer from the same parsed market ontology the market field_map produces (a market-parse of a synthetic row), or keep the id path but make it return false ("not inverse", the mul identity) for every shape it cannot positively identify as the inverse book — guessing inverse is the only direction that produces a squared money error. Then add an agreement gate: a test that enumerates the registered/live deribit instrument-id corpus and asserts the loaded-market answer equals the degradation answer for every id, including option combos and future combos.

Provenance: ARC finding 2 (moderate) + the 608 reviewer's proposed task from run run-1786661082431-e53ff712 (merged here — do not file it separately). Authority: docs.deribit.com instrument naming + instrument_type semantics; CCXT is reference-only (note: CCXT marks deribit options inverse:true — our carve diverges deliberately and correctly, keep it).

task.body:
Task 610 left two prose-only escapes on the Position unit contract, and ARC review 2026-08-14 (findings 3+7) plus the 610 reviewer (run run-1786664191188-0f4ace4b, concern 4 and two proposed tasks — merged here, do not file them separately) all point at the same class:

1. `notional` has no machine-readable unit. binancecoinm stays coin-settled under the prose exception C-T610/binancecoinm-inverse-settlement-notional (0.01 ETH where the quote value is 20 USD), and lib/bourse/position.ex documents notional unconditionally as quote — a consumer summing notionals across venues can still silently mix units. Decide the contract: either quote-denominate COIN-M notional (positionAmt x contractSize x price semantics per Binance COIN-M docs) or add an explicit unit/settlement-currency field on Position that every position-authoring venue populates.
2. `base_quantity` exists on deribit futures only, is documented unconditionally as populated, has ZERO assertions in the unit-invariant rows, and is nil on deribit options although the provider documents option size as base coin. Either populate it on every position-authoring venue (the value is contracts x contractSize on the other nine, per global.md) and freeze it in the invariant rows, or scope the field docs to the venues that emit it.
3. The invariant test's frozen rows pre-seed the synthetic _bourse_* keys, so the read_parse annotation pass (okx_position_contract_size, binance/hyperliquid/derive notional annotations) is not exercised — a unit bug introduced in the annotation would not fail it. Drive the rows from raw venue payloads through the annotation path, and make the reconciliation a unit check rather than a dimensionless identity where the venue data allows it.

Authority: each venue's own position/instrument docs; the existing carve lines in global.md name the per-venue sources. This is a public-contract change (Position struct/docs) — dispatch-gated.

2026-08-18 — consumer-supplied tier-1 evidence for the INVERSE branch. bourse_trading
recorded a non-flat deribit BTC-PERPETUAL position off test.deribit.com (opened and

Their three independent derivations agree: venue size_currency 1.55547e-4,

because account identifiers do not go into a repo — the raw file is otherwise complete.
Source file: bourse_trading docs/deribit-inverse-position-2026-08-18.json (commit f2c67c1).

task.body:
Task 609 mapped bybit transaction-log SETTLEMENT to funding_fee — type-level correct (the UTA enum pins SETTLEMENT as perp funding settlement, there is no separate FUNDING type). But the enum text reads "USDC Perp funding settlement + USDC 8-hour session settlement", and the Get Transaction Log doc states funding and session settlement are represented in a single record, with `funding` carrying the funding fee and `cashFlow` the session P&L. The unified `amount` maps from `change` (= funding + cashFlow), so a USDC-perp SETTLEMENT row reports realized session P&L inside a funding_fee amount. The frozen 609 row is a linear-USDT case where cashFlow is 0, so the mixed case is untested; C-T609a's own text names the field-level split it then dismisses.

Fix: on type=SETTLEMENT source the unified amount from the `funding` component (confront: what carries the sign, and what should happen to cashFlow — likely a second emitted entry or documented residual), pin a frozen USDC-perp row with funding != change, and update C-T609a to state the field-level split. Authority: bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/enum + /docs/v5/account/transaction-log (pinned corpus commit 5ccd3010). Demo transaction-log history is server-side purged (established 2026-08-13) — frozen provider-doc-derived rows plus the oracle are the evidence path; if a live USDC-perp funding row IS reachable on demo, pin it, else record the gap honestly in the carve.

acceptance_criteria: A caller-supplied native value survives shaping for every authored conditional entry: with an explicit params value for the native key, the shaped request carries the caller's value — unit-pinned across the seven authored conditional entries (binance/binancecoinm/binanceusdm setMarginMode.marginType, deribit createOrder.trigger and createOrder.type, okx fetchMarginAdjustmentHistory.subType, okx setPositionMode.posMode)

task.body:
Consumer bug report (BUGS.md 2026-08-14, deribit createOrder): a caller-supplied native
`trigger` selector (e.g. `trigger: "index_price"`) is deleted during request shaping, so
stop/take orders land with the wrong trigger reference price or without the selector Deribit
requires.

Mechanism (read 2026-08-14, lib/bourse/unified/request_shape.ex:379
`put_authored_conditional/4`): the function never checks whether the caller already supplied
the native key. When no authored case matches and the entry has no `source`/`default` (deribit
createOrder.trigger is the one source-less entry), the fallback resolves nil and the
`is_nil(value)` branch runs `Map.delete(params, native_key)` — wiping the caller's explicit
value. When a case DOES match, `Map.put` force-overrides the caller's value. Both branches
violate caller precedence. Class scope: seven authored conditional entries across five venues
(enumerated in the acceptance criteria); the deribit trigger is the live-verified instance.

Authority: docs.deribit.com private/buy — `trigger` (enum `index_price | mark_price |
last_price`) is required for stop/take orders. Live consumer evidence: trading_dashboard's
`@venue_request_shape_supplements` workaround re-authors the entry as native_passthrough; with
it the order reaches Deribit's business logic (real `10035 trigger_price_too_low` rejection),
without it the selector never arrives.

Fix shape: caller-supplied native key takes precedence — the conditional (and its default)
apply only when the key is absent from params. `Map.put_new` semantics for the match branch
and a `Map.has_key?` guard before the delete branch, or equivalent.

Dispatch trigger: order-placement request shaping is money-class surface with live external
evidence required.

task.body:
ARC finding F2 on the landed 591 wave (2026-08-14). Task 591 deleted the venue-agnostic
compensation clause that wrapped a lone %Bourse.TradingFee{} into a symbol-keyed map. Doctrinally
right — but the clause it now falls through to (lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:679-684) reads:

    structs when is_list(structs) -> {:ok, index_by_symbol(structs)}
    other -> {:ok, other}

so a POPULATED single struct escapes as {:ok, %TradingFee{}} where the unified contract for all
nine @symbol_dict_return_methods is a symbol-keyed map. Verified in the running BEAM: a binance
single-object commission payload parses to a bare struct, reported as success. The landed test
pins only the all-nil struct case, which errors for an unrelated reason (empty_parse) — the
populated case passes silently. This is the "missing coverage fails open" class from CLAUDE.md;
the fix shape is the same as the path_param_name/1 rule: make the day-it-happens failure LOUD
with a raising/erroring clause, never a quiet passthrough.

Exposure is real, not hypothetical: binance fetch_trading_fees resolves per market type to
dapiPrivate_get_account | fapiPrivate_get_accountconfig | sapi_get_asset_tradefee, two of which
return single objects, and the entire binance trading-fee slice is unverified in the oracle gate
(no recording) — the shape is unproven either way. Provider docs + a live testnet call are the

acceptance_criteria: An offline test enumerates every unified read whose Descriptor opts carry :since, shapes a request per venue through Bourse.Unified.RequestShape.apply/4, and fails on any raw "since"/"until" key surviving outside a written-out allowlist — each allowlist entry naming the provider contract that justifies it (no time-bound support, or a documented drop/reject carve)

task.body:
Merges the two reviewer proposals from the task 553 run (run-1786676066430-6adad89a, 2026-08-14)
— they are one invariant seen from two sides.

Side 1 (measured during review, not inferred): 91 of 139 venue/method time-window pairs still
pass raw since/until through RequestShape.apply/4 to the venue — binance 16, binanceusdm 17,
okx 16, deribit 10, hyperliquid 10, binancecoinm 6, derive 5, alpaca 4, bybit 4, lighter 3. On
silently-ignoring venues the client-side ReadParse filters mask it (correct window, lost reach
and efficiency); on the binance family it is the loud -1104 class 553 just closed for four
methods. The 553 matrix cannot reach these pairs: they sit in its exclusion list precisely
because the accounts return no populated boundary rows. The assertion that CAN reach them is
offline and derived — shape the request, assert the translation happened.

Side 2 (mutation-tested live during review): deleting okx's until translation reddened the 553
matrix (proving non-vacuity), but deleting the since translation survived all 18 probes —
ReadParse.filter_ohlcv_by_since/2 (read_parse.ex:139) and filter_by_since/2 (:1090) rebuild the
boundary client-side, and the probe picks its boundary inside the venue's default page. The
request-side guard from side 1 closes this detection gap by construction; the alternative (or
complement) is probing a since older than the default page.

Authority: each venue's time-bound parameter contract per its authority manifest; binance spot
residual named from the provider's own allOrders/myTrades/openOrders contracts.

ARC amendment (2026-08-14, wave-2 architect pass) — two adjacent findings folded in rather than
filed as siblings:

(a) until-inclusivity asymmetry: request_shape/okx.ex compensates the exclusive `before` cursor
(`since - offset`) but leaves `after = until_ms` uncompensated, while binance `endTime` and
deribit `end_timestamp` are inclusive — a candle whose timestamp equals `until` is kept on
binance/deribit and dropped on OKX. C-T553d states the exclusivity in prose, and
request_shape_test pins `after == until_ms`, freezing the divergence instead of deciding it. The
553 live matrix cannot see it (@boundary_pad_ms pads past the boundary). Decide ONE unified
`until` inclusivity semantic, state it once, and either compensate OKX or carve the divergence
with a written rationale.

(b) exclusion ratchet: the inventory test accepts any exclusion whose tracking matches
`task N` (16 probes vs ~120 exclusions today), so a live probe can be silently demoted to an
exclusion — mirror the :known_defect only-shrink governance. Context: the ARC pass already
corrected three exclusion reasons that claimed account-state blockage on public reads and
promoted deribit fetch_trades to a live probe, which immediately caught a missing until mapping
(authored + live-verified as C-T553f in bourse d117176).

All four watch_* default channels for binance and binanceusdm are audited against the provider's own stream documentation; every template either matches a documented stream name or is corrected, with the confrontation recorded in the venue carve registers

task.body:
Inbound consumer bug (BUGS.md 2026-08-14, trading_dashboard Task 68): `Bourse.WS.watch_order_book/3` on binance subscribes `orderbook:btcusdt` — the socket acks it silently and no frame ever arrives. Mechanism (verified by code read): binance authors no `watchOrderBook` channel entry, `Bourse.WS.Channels.@method_fallbacks` falls back to `watchOrderBookForSymbols`, whose authored template `orderbook::{symbol}` is a CCXT-internal message-hash/cache key, not a Binance stream name; `collapse_separators/1` folds `::` to `:`. The class is wider than order book: binance and binanceusdm (`resolved_from: binance`) both carry `trade::{symbol}`, `myLiquidations::{symbol}`, `:{symbol}`, bare `miniTicker`/`kline`/`name` — none are provider-owned stream names. binancecoinm authors `channels: null` (fails loud with :no_channel_templates — acceptable, but note it).

Authority: Binance WS streams documentation (spot: wss://stream.binance.com `<symbol>@depth<levels>@<speed>` partial / `<symbol>@depth@<speed>` diff, `<symbol>@trade`, `<symbol>@miniTicker`; USD-M futures equivalents on fstream). CCXT is reference-only and is the source of the leaked hashes — do not verify against it.

The failure class is silent-accept: Binance acks unknown stream names, so a subscribe-ack test certifies a dead stream green. Evidence must be frame delivery — a live public integration test that receives at least one data frame on the default channel per method. Consumer workaround exists in trading_dashboard `market_data/transport/local.ex` (subscribes `depth20@100ms` directly, live-verified run-1786673501096-c9939b07); it can be retired after this lands — append a dated fix note to the BUGS.md entry.

task.body:
The Deribit `api-openapi` artifact pinned at sha256 430b3f0b… (etag `2.1.1; W/"b96f2b26…"`, retrieved 2026-08-10) moved upstream on 2026-08-11 and its bytes are no longer fetchable. Observed on 2026-08-14: sha256 2ac2867b…, etag `W/"05muB64FICWdauQ2"`, 1391568 bytes, still 178 operations and 10 `WebSocket Only` tags at OpenAPI 2.1.1, but 410 schemas where the pin recorded 411. The observation is committed at `priv/authority/deribit/current-rest-drift-2026-08-14.json`; the pin was deliberately not moved there because doing so re-binds three other tasks' committed proofs in one step.

The consequence is concrete and already blocking: `mix ccxt.contract_compare` refuses the observed bytes against the pinned manifest hash, so no new exact-revision inventory can be produced. `test/fixtures/provider_operations/_manifest.json` cannot gain operations beyond the two task 556 registered, which means task 557's read-evidence sections cannot register captures through that corpus at all until the pin moves.

Run the authority corpus's own controlled refresh, not an ad-hoc hash bump. The point is that every artifact quoting the old revision moves together and the historical record stays readable: the 2026-08-10 refresh report remains a dated record of that refresh, and the 2026-08-14 observation remains a dated record of this drift.

2026-08-18 (ARC wave-3, runs for tasks 599/558): two folds. (F3) Task 599's require_inventory_public re-derives authentication from a congruence inventory digest-pinned to authored/deribit.json (inventory.provenance.authored_spec_canonical_sha256) — and the only regenerator is mix ccxt.contract_compare, which the stale pin blocks. Net effect today: ANY byte change to authored/deribit.json reds mix ccxt.oracle_gate with no green path, i.e. deribit spec authoring is locked until this task lands. The re-pin must leave behind a runnable inventory-regeneration path, not just moved hashes. (F6) MutationAdjudication.facts!/0 exists but its only call site is its own test; contract_compare still reports reachability=unknown for all 81 adjudicated operations. Wire it during the corpus regeneration this task already performs.

task.title: Signed requests are retried with a frozen signature, so a transient 408 becomes a permanent recv-window rejection
acceptance_criteria: A retried signed request is re-signed before each attempt: an injected 408 on a signed GET is pinned by a test asserting attempt 2 carries a DIFFERENT timestamp/nonce and a recomputed signature than attempt 1 — asserting the retry count or the final result alone does not satisfy this

The re-signing lives at the signing/dispatch boundary, not in a caller opt: either signed requests opt out of Req's retry: and bourse drives the retry loop itself through Signing.sign/4, or the retry hook re-signs before each attempt; the chosen mechanism is stated in the Bourse.Http moduledoc and a caller-supplied retry: opt cannot silently reinstate the frozen-signature path

Coverage spans signing patterns, not just binance: at least one HMAC query-signed venue (binance family, timestamp in the signed query) and at least one non-query pattern (deribit / hyperliquid / derive, nonce or deadline in the signed payload) each prove the re-sign, so the fix is not binance-shaped

After retries are exhausted the returned Bourse.Error names the transport failure that caused the retries (the 408/5xx), not the venue's follow-on rejection of the stale signature; a test pins the error type and message so an operator is sent to the network path, not to the API keys

The primary evidence is the injected-408 assertion above, NOT a live venue run: the reporter withdrew the causality of the live log sequence on 2026-08-18 (the binance futures testnet account plane was returning -1021 / -1000 on FIRST attempts with retry disabled, at a measured clock skew of -8 ms, so those logs cannot prove the retry caused that incident). A live re-sign differential may be recorded as supporting evidence when the venue plane is healthy, but a red or flaky testnet must never block this task or be read as reproducing the defect
The deterministic zero-delay retry controller is used for the error-path tests so production Defaults.retry_policy/0 backoff is unchanged and the offline suite runtime budget is not regressed
Bourse.Http and Bourse.Signing meet the 95% critical coverage tier; mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Consumer-side changes in trading_dashboard
Which status codes :safe_transient retries, and retry behaviour for unsigned public requests
The InvalidNonce classification split — landed as task 604; this task only fixes which error survives to the caller after exhausted retries
Clock-skew correction or a time-offset sync mechanism
task.body:
Consumer bug (BUGS.md entry 2026-08-18, reporter: trading_dashboard, money path). Every private
read is signed once and then handed to Req WITH a retry policy, so Req replays the SAME prepared
request — timestamp and signature frozen at sign time — until the venue's recv window has closed.

Mechanism confirmed by code read 2026-08-18:
- lib/bourse/dispatch.ex:227 calls Signing.sign/4 once, building timestamp + signature into the URL.
- lib/bourse/dispatch.ex:246 passes that frozen signed struct to Bourse.Http.signed_request/4.
- lib/bourse/http.ex:242-258 builds req_opts with retry: Defaults.retry_policy() (:safe_transient)
  plus retry_delay_opt(). Req retries the prepared request; nothing re-signs between attempts.

With Req's exponential default backoff the last of four attempts lands roughly 7 s after signing,
well past Binance's default recvWindow of 5000 ms. Only private READS are exposed: :safe_transient
retries GET/HEAD only, so signed POSTs are untouched — which is why the symptom surfaced on a
reconcile loop rather than on order placement.

Evidence status, corrected 2026-08-18 by the reporter (td_orchestrator) after filing: the defect is
established from the SOURCE, and only from the source. The originally filed live log sequence
(three 408 retry warnings at 905 / 1986 / 3753 ms, then a recvWindow rejection, three consecutive
BracketGuard cycles) is real but CONFOUNDED — a follow-up measurement with retry disabled found the
binance futures testnet account plane failing on FIRST attempts anyway (fetch_open_orders -> HTTP
400 / -1000; fetch_positions and fetch_balance -> -1021) at a measured clock skew of -8 ms testnet
and -9 ms mainnet, with public endpoints healthy on both. A first-attempt -1021 at that skew is not
explained by the clock, so the venue plane itself was answering correctly-stamped requests with
errors. Do NOT treat those logs as a reproduction, and do NOT chase a green testnet as proof; the
injected-408 assertion is the load-bearing evidence.

Class scope, not a binance quirk: every venue whose signature covers a timestamp, nonce or deadline
is exposed the same way — the binance family (recvWindow), bybit, okx, deribit, hyperliquid, derive
and lighter all sign time-bound material. The fix belongs at the signing/dispatch boundary so a new
venue inherits it, not in a per-venue patch.

Second, independent half of the defect: the error class lies. A transient network timeout reaches
the caller as the venue's follow-on rejection of a stale signature, which points an operator at the
API keys instead of the network path. Task 604 already split InvalidNonce out of :authentication_error
on main (the reporter observed the pre-604 released 0.4.0 behaviour), so the classification of the
follow-on error is handled — what remains is that the follow-on error should not be the terminal
error at all: after exhausted retries the caller must see the 408.

Authority: the venue's own contract for the signed time window (Binance USD-M recvWindow and the
timestamp signing rules; the equivalent nonce/deadline semantics for each non-query pattern). Any
retry that re-uses signed time-bound material contradicts those contracts by construction.

Positive dispatch trigger: signing surface on the money path, class-wide across ten venues, and the
verification needs live external evidence rather than a fixture.

task.title: Unified client_order_id is one-way on deribit: it goes out as label and never comes back — make the round-trip a cross-venue invariant
acceptance_criteria: deribit round-trips the identifier live on test.deribit.com: an order created with a unified client id comes back as %Bourse.Order{client_order_id: <id>} AND the matching private fill row from private/get_user_trades_by_instrument carries the same client_order_id — the same value observed on both surfaces in one recorded test, not order-only

The deribit mapping and the existing binance _bourse_client_order_id synthetic (lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:3205) resolve through ONE declared mechanism — the fix does not add a second hardcoded venue branch in the parse layer
A carve entry in docs/authored-spec-carves/deribit.md records the decision with the deribit authority cited; no CCXT-as-authority language

Re-opening the Derive request-side decision landed by task 473
task.body:
Consumer bug (BUGS.md entry 2026-08-17, reporter: trading_dashboard). Live on test.deribit.com: a
labelled market order returns %Bourse.Order{client_order_id: nil} while order.info["label"] carries
the value, and the private fill row carries "label" with no client_order_id key at all. A consumer
that must recognise its own orders by a self-assigned id falls back to reading raw info.

Confirmed by code and spec read 2026-08-18:
- deribit's authored normalization.field_maps.order and .trade carry NO client_order_id entry, so
  nothing maps label back.
- The only back-mapping that exists anywhere is binance's synthetic _bourse_client_order_id
  (lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:3205), a venue-specific branch in the parse layer.

Correct one premise in the report before building: it attributes the request-side mapping to
lib/bourse/unified/request_shape/derive.ex:166-173. That module is the DERIVE venue's shaper, not
deribit's — deribit has no unified-client-id to label mapping either, and the reporter's live call
worked only because it passed a native params: %{"label" => id} passthrough. Both directions are
unauthored for deribit; do not assume the request half is already correct.

Scope this as the class invariant, not a deribit patch. Task 473 (landed) fixed exactly this defect
shape on Derive's request side alone, and the deribit instance surfaced four months later on the
other side of the same round-trip. The deliverable that stops the next venue spawning a sibling task
is the cross-venue test: a venue may map a client identifier in both directions or in neither, and
one-way mapping fails the suite.

Authority: deribit's own private/buy, private/sell and get_user_trades_by_instrument contracts for
what label is and where it is echoed; each other venue's own contract for its exemption or mapping.

evidence on the deribit testnet.

task.body:
Consumer bug (BUGS.md entry 2026-08-17, reporter: trading_dashboard, money path). Live against
GET https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/exchangeInfo on bourse 0.4.0: BTC/USDT:USDT normalizes to
%Bourse.Market{contract: true, linear: true, inverse: false} with contract_size nil. The inverse
counter-check is correct — binancecoinm BTC/USD:BTC arrives with contract_size 100 straight from the
provider's own contractSize field. A money or margin consumer therefore cannot derive linear order
notional from provider-owned contract facts.

Confirmed by spec read 2026-08-18: both authored specs map market.contractSize from the venue key
"contractSize" with no fallback. COIN-M publishes that key; USD-M does not (its order quantity is
base-asset denominated), so the field lands nil by construction.

The sharp edge that makes this more than a missing field: the repo already contradicts itself. Carve
C-T334a in docs/authored-spec-carves/binanceusdm.md states that linear contract_size IS the loaded
market's unit size, 1 for BTCUSDT — the USD-M position semantics are authored on top of a
market-level fact that fetch_markets never populates. Resolve the contradiction rather than patching
one side of it.

The guard against the obvious wrong fix: do NOT add a parse-layer fallback that turns a missing unit
into 1. Task 397 landed the opposite rule for exactly this field family — unknown or missing
multiplier and amount semantics fail loudly instead of defaulting to one — and a hardcoded 1 is the
domain-constant trap where a golden computed with the same assumption ratifies the bug. The unit must
come from Binance's own USD-M contract specification, be declared in the authored spec, and be
recorded as a carve; venues with no provider-stated unit keep failing loud.

Authority: Binance's own USD-M contract specification and exchangeInfo documentation for the linear
unit and the base-asset quantity denomination; the COIN-M dapi contract for the inverse side. CCXT's
contractSize 1 for linear is compatibility reference only, never the reason.

Positive dispatch trigger: money-path public contract on the market normalization surface, with live
provider evidence required on two venue families.

task.title: Mutation-lifecycle compensation holds under transport and parse failure: attempted-act tracking, session-label sweep, mutating-steps-before-cleanup plan rule
acceptance_criteria: A transport raise (send!/3), an unparseable act response (Jason.decode! on a non-JSON 200), or a redaction raise at the act step still compensates whenever the act request already left the process: the lifecycle tracks attempted-act before transmission, and the compensation report never claims no compensating call was needed after a request was sent

When order-id-targeted cleanup is impossible (no parsed order id from the act response), a private/cancel_by_label sweep on context.session_label runs as the compensating call — the operation is already adjudicated approved in the register — and its outcome is recorded in the compensation report

Plan validation rejects any plan whose @mutating_roles step runs after the cleanup step without declaring its own compensator; the current reject_wrong_tick-style post-cleanup placement is either moved before cleanup or carries an explicit compensator, never silently uncompensated

Deterministic request_fun regression tests pin each failure path (transport raise mid-act, non-JSON 200 body at act, redaction raise at act) and assert both that compensation executed and what the report says
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.oracle_gate stay green; the committed deribit mutation evidence and register are unchanged — no live re-capture is required for these control-flow fixes
out_of_scope: Re-adjudicating any operation or changing reachability/safety judgments in priv/authority/deribit/mutation-adjudication.json
The OpenAPI re-pin and inventory regeneration — task 619 owns that
New live mutations beyond the existing reversible BTC-PERPETUAL lifecycle if a live confirmation is chosen
task.body:
ARC wave-3 findings F1+F4+F7 on the landed task 558 surface (commits 9267848 / 8e59758 / b1f61b7); F2 (double-compensation on observation failure) was already fixed by the audit agent in b1f61b7. This subsumes the 558 reviewer proposal (cancel_by_label fallback).

F1 (the load-bearing gap): run_steps! catches raises from run_step and compensates from the PRE-step state, so acted? is still false when the transport call itself raises (send!/3, lifecycle.ex ~:323), when Jason.decode! rejects a 200 body (~:111), or when redaction raises after a successful act. In all three the venue may have accepted the order, yet compensate! sees acted?=false and reports "No compensating call was needed" — a resting order survives with a report that says the opposite. Fix shape: set an attempted_act? flag (or advance the state) BEFORE the request is transmitted, and compensate whenever attempted_act? is true and no terminal observation cleared it.

F4: when the act response never parsed, there is no order id to cancel by — the compensator needs the private/cancel_by_label sweep on the run's session_label (labels are set as "bourse-mutation-<ms>"). cancel_by_label is adjudicated approved in the register, so authorize/3 permits it.

F7: the plan currently runs reject_wrong_tick AFTER cleanup with compensation disabled; validate_plan! should enforce that every @mutating_roles step precedes cleanup or names its own compensator, so a future plan edit cannot reintroduce an uncompensated tail mutation.

Dispatch trigger: mutation-safety / money-adjacent control flow with live-venue consequences — earns independent review.

task.body:
Task 623 landed the venue-level `markets.contract_unit` slot and authored it for binanceusdm.
The recording-less / nil sweep it added still names three first-class venues as known gaps
(test/bourse/linear_contract_size_sweep_test.exs @known_linear_nil_gaps, committed in 884af46):

Those allowlist reasons are the durable record that 623's sweep AC required. They are also

is compatibility reference only.

task.title: A market's declared type and its capability flags disagree, and multi-leg instruments carry no quantity semantics at all — a consumer keying on either signal computes a meaningless exposure
acceptance_criteria: A manifest-wide test over every authored venue's recorded fetch_markets asserts the type/flag contract in both directions: a market with type "option" carries option: true, a market with type "swap"/"future" carries contract: true, and any row that declares a type without the matching flag is enumerated in an explicit allowlist with a per-row reason — the allowlist may only shrink

Deribit multi-leg instruments (kind option_combo and future_combo) are confronted against Deribit's own combo documentation and the live testnet catalog, and the outcome is recorded as a carve: either they stop declaring a leg type they do not satisfy, or they declare it AND carry the quantity semantics that type implies

A derivative market that carries no resolvable quantity semantics (native_quantity_unit nil with no other authored unit) is machine-detectable by a consumer — a field or a documented predicate, not prose — so an exposure calculation can block on it instead of multiplying by a contract_size whose unit is unstated

The mark price of a multi-leg instrument is documented as a spread/premium difference rather than an underlying price wherever contract_size or quantity semantics are documented, so notional-style arithmetic against it is visibly wrong rather than plausibly wrong
An offline regression pins at least one live combo row per shape (spread, calendar, straddle, iron condor) such that reintroducing the divergence turns the suite red

Folded from superseded task 612 (2026-08-19): inverse classification has one source of truth — the degradation-path instrument-id classifier (deribit_inverse_instrument_id?/1) and the loaded-market answer agree for EVERY id in the recorded/live deribit instrument corpus, combos included, per whatever this task's combo adjudication decides; a shape the id parser cannot positively identify as the inverse book answers false (the mul identity), because guessing inverse is the only direction that produces a squared money error; seed cases stay pinned (BTC-PERPETUAL inverse, ETH_USDC-PERPETUAL linear, BTC-31JUL26-65000-C non-inverse, BTC-FS-31JUL26_17JUL26 inverse, one multi-strike option combo and one single-strike strategy id on the degradation path)
mix check.dispatch green; no previously-green fixture turns red
out_of_scope: Combo SYMBOL grammar and id round-tripping — tasks 236/299/305 settled that under carve C27 (native ids retained)
Option notional/base_quantity semantics for genuine options (named gap G-T610-options, task 613)
task.body:
Reported 2026-08-18 by the bourse_trading consumer, with live testnet evidence.

Deribit's live market list (testnet, 2026-08-18) carries 4156 markets with `type: "option"`.
46 of them have `option: false`: multi-leg combos such as `BTC-CS-18AUG26-64000_64500`
(call spread), `BTC-CSR12-18AUG26-64000_64500` (calendar spread), `ETH-STRD-18AUG26-1925`
(straddle), `BTC-ICOND-19AUG26-60500_61500_64500_65500` (iron condor). All 46 carry
`option: false`, `inverse: true`, `contract_size: 1.0`, `native_quantity_unit: nil`.

The divergence is deliberate at both ends and neither end is wrong on its own:
`market_type_from_raw/1` and `deribit_market_type/1` in lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex
both map `kind: "option_combo"` to the option type, while the authored `option` flag maps
`kind` through `{"enum_map": {"option": true}, "enum_default": false}` — so a combo declares
the type without the flag. `Bourse.Unified.OptionQuantity.normalize_market/3` gates on
`%Market{option: true}`, so a combo never receives `native_quantity_unit`,
`native_amount_step` or a scaled precision; it keeps a bare `contract_size: 1.0` whose unit
nothing states. `Bourse.Unified.OptionSurface` already knows the divergence and works around
it privately (`option_combo?/1` excludes combos from the option chain) — that workaround is
the tell that the contract is unstated rather than absent.

The consumer consequence, observed: an exposure calculation that routes on the `option` flag
sends all 46 into the derivative path and computes `contracts * contract_size / mark_price`.
A combo's mark price is a premium DIFFERENCE between legs, not an underlying price, so the
result is a number with no unit that would have been summed into a delta bucket. A consumer
that instead keys on `type == "option"` gets the mirror-image error: 46 multi-leg
instruments treated as single-leg options. Both readings are defensible from the struct, and
both are wrong — that is the defect. The consumer has since blocked these rows explicitly,
but they had to discover the divergence by counting live markets.

Scope this as the CLASS, not the deribit patch: the general invariant is that a market's
declared `type` and its capability flags must agree, and that a derivative carrying no
resolvable quantity semantics must say so in a machine-readable way rather than presenting a
unit-less `contract_size`. Confront Deribit's own combo documentation for the multi-leg
semantics; CCXT is compatibility reference only and its own combo handling is not evidence.

task.title: Make split-host WebSocket subscriptions own and reuse connections
acceptance_criteria: Repeated watch calls for channels on the same authored host reuse a bounded connection rather than opening one socket per subscription
Mixed Binance USD-M /public and /market subscriptions both deliver through the caller's configured message handler, and heartbeat plus other connection options survive host routing
The public lifecycle API closes every connection it owns without requiring callers to reach into Handle.ws; tests prove no routed socket remains open after closure

An offline instrumented transport test pins connection counts, option preservation, mixed-host subscription delivery, and cleanup; the live task-627 ticker plus task-618 depth/trade paths remain green

Raw Bourse.WS.subscribe/3 and WS.Adapter.subscribe/3 route by authored host as well: a market-host stream name sent on an authored USD-M public connection either reaches the host that carries it or returns an error naming that host — never an acknowledgement followed by silence — and a mixed public+market channel list drops neither family

Authoring Binance COIN-M channels
task.body:
Post-merge audit of task 627 on 2026-08-18 found a connection-lifecycle gap in the split-host routing. In the landed code, each watch_ticker call made from the documented /public connection reaches ensure_stream_host/2 and opens a fresh /market ZenWebsocket connection; only the returned Handle carries that socket while the input connection stays open. reconnect_public/2 also builds connection options from an empty list, so a handler, heartbeat override, or other option supplied to connect/3 is lost on the routed socket. The WS moduledoc still demonstrates closing the input socket, which does not close the routed one.

2026-08-18 (task 627 reviewer proposal, folded in rather than filed as a sibling): host routing runs only in watch/4 via ensure_stream_host/2. Adapter.handle_call({:subscribe, ...}) calls WS.subscribe/3 directly, so a raw SUBSCRIBE of {symbol}@miniTicker, @ticker, @aggTrade or @kline_* on the authored public socket still acks with result null and then delivers nothing — the same silent-dead class task 627 closed for the unified wrappers, one layer below it. Same routing code, same reviewer pass. Do not change the watch_ticker default template to @bookTicker.

Make connection ownership explicit and bounded across authored stream hosts. A caller should be able to mix and repeat public watch subscriptions without accumulating hidden sockets, losing message delivery configuration, or learning an internal Handle field to clean up. Preserve the provider-owned /public versus /market semantics already confronted and live-verified by task 627; this task owns client lifecycle and option propagation, not venue re-authoring.

task.title: Mixed-host WS subscribe must not leave a live half when the other host fails
acceptance_criteria: A mixed USD-M public+market subscribe whose second host fails returns an error and leaves no live subscription on the host that already succeeded — retrying the same channel list does not double-subscribe the first family
Adapter.subscribe/3 does not record a mixed channel list as restored subscriptions when any host in that list failed

An offline instrumented-transport test pins the rollback: first host send succeeds, second host connect or subscribe fails, then the first host receives an unsubscribe (or equivalent close) before the error is returned
The success path is unchanged: a mixed list that succeeds on both hosts still delivers both families and reuses one connection per host

The connection registry survives its owner dying: if the process holding the routed-host clients exits abnormally, close/1 either still closes every routed socket or the sockets are terminated with it — a dead owner never leaves an orphaned host connection that no API can reach
out_of_scope: Changing the provider-verified USD-M stream-to-host classifications
Making single-host subscribe atomic across multiple frames inside one host
Retiring Handle.owns_connection?
task.body:
Post-merge audit of task 630 (landed b6346a9) found a partial-success hole in the new mixed-host subscribe path.

Bourse.WS.subscribe/3 now groups channels by authored host and walks the groups sequentially (subscribe_groups/2). When the first group is accepted and the second returns an error — connection_refused on the market host, a venue reject, or a down connection owner — the function returns that error while the first host stays subscribed. Adapter.handle_call({:subscribe, ...}) then keeps its tracked subscription list unchanged, so restore_subscriptions/2 will not replay the mixed list, but the first host is already live. A caller that retries the same list after the error double-subscribes the family that succeeded.

Evidence: read of lib/bourse/ws.ex subscribe_groups/2 (reduce_while halt on first error, no compensating unsubscribe) and lib/bourse/ws/adapter.ex handle_call({:subscribe, ...}) (merge only on :ok). The host_connection_lifecycle_test pins named host-unavailable errors and mixed-list routing, not the first-succeeds/second-fails leftover.

Pick one caller-visible contract and pin it: either roll back the succeeded host before returning the error, or return a result that names which hosts committed. Silent error-plus-live-half is the defect. Authority is the client's own subscribe/3 contract, not a venue document.

Do not treat this as a reason to reopen task 630's reuse/ownership work.

2026-08-18 (task 630 reviewer concern, folded in rather than filed as a sibling): the connection owner is an unlinked Agent. If that process exits independently of WS.close/1, the routed-host registry is gone and close/1 falls back to the root zen_client only, so every already-routed host socket is orphaned with no API left to reach it. Same registry, same file, same reviewer pass as the partial-subscribe hole above. Pick a supervision contract — link, monitor-and-close, or make the registry survivable — rather than documenting the caveat.

task.title: Binance-family order-type reads are not the inverse of the writes: every conditional type collapses to market or limit
acceptance_criteria: The native to unified order-type mapping is the inverse of the authored write mapping for every conditional type the write side accepts: creating with unified type T and reading the resulting order back yields T, for stop, stop_market, take_profit, take_profit_market and trailing_stop_market alike

A suite-level invariant pins the round trip generically — it enumerates the unified order types the Binance-family write path authors and fails on any one whose read-back differs, so a newly authored write type cannot land without its read counterpart

The spot and futures native enums are confronted separately against Binance's own documented type lists rather than served by one shared table: a native type that only one product carries is mapped for that product and not silently downcased for the other
A native type the venue documents but the table does not name fails loud or is mapped, never silently downcased into an unvalidated unified string

The pinned assertions that currently expect the collapsed values (binance_authored_spec_test.exs TAKE_PROFIT to market) are updated to the corrected mapping, and the change is recorded as consumer-visible in CHANGELOG.md
out_of_scope: Changing the write path's unified-to-native table — it already authors take_profit, take_profit_market and trailing_stop_market correctly
Extending the unified order-type vocabulary to venues outside the Binance family
Re-authoring the algo-book routing landed by task 580
task.body:
Reviewer of task 580 flagged that native TAKE_PROFIT parses as unified type "market". The generalized defect is larger: binance_order_type/1 (lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:3332-3338) is a single flat table serving spot, USD-M and COIN-M, and it collapses every conditional order type onto a plain one — TAKE_PROFIT and STOP_LOSS become "market", TAKE_PROFIT_LIMIT and STOP_LOSS_LIMIT become "limit" — while any type it does not name falls through to String.downcase/1 unvalidated.

The asymmetry is the sharp part: the write path already authors the conditional vocabulary correctly. test/bourse/binance_authored_spec_test.exs:2368 maps unified "take_profit" onto native TAKE_PROFIT, and :2313 pins that creating with unified "limit" plus take_profit_price produces native TAKE_PROFIT which then reads back as unified "market". A caller can therefore send take_profit and never read take_profit back — the order's own type field misreports what was placed, on every fetch_order, fetch_orders and algo-book read that task 580 just opened up.

Fix the class, not the one type. The read table should be derived from, or checked against, the write table so the two cannot drift again, and spot versus futures enums should be confronted separately — Binance documents different type lists per product, and one shared table is why the collapse went unnoticed. Authority is Binance's own per-product order-type documentation; a third-party client's mapping is reference material only.

task.title: Deribit shipped release 2.1.1 during a maintenance window: re-bind the current-REST corpus to the republished OpenAPI
acceptance_criteria: priv/authority/deribit/manifest.json pins api-openapi at the republished document (sha256, bytes, retrieved_at and the document_version_http_etag upstream_pin) with freshness reviewed_current

Every artifact bound to the old revision is re-bound in the same change so ensure_source_revision! holds: the provider_operations manifest source_revision, the provider-operation-plan, contract-baselines, mutation-adjudication, and each captured fixture's provider_artifact

The re-bind follows the runbook priv/authority/README.md records — contract_compare --rebind-provider-corpus, capture_provider_operations against the reviewed plan, then a plain contract_compare — and the reviewed plan is confirmed still safe and reachable rather than assumed
mix ccxt.authority_check (offline) and --online both pass, and mix ccxt.oracle_gate plus the oracle_provenance tests are green on the re-bound corpus

The operation inventory delta is stated explicitly: the republished current document now carries the same 182 paths as the upcoming document, so any operation that entered the current surface is named rather than silently absorbed

The manifest or README records a decision on whether this pin should key on the provider's declared document version rather than content bytes, given it went stale twice inside declared version 2.1.1 on a single day
out_of_scope: Re-authoring priv/specs/json/output/authored/deribit.json — this task re-binds provider evidence, it does not change client behaviour
Touching the upcoming-openapi, current-asyncapi or upcoming-asyncapi pins refreshed on 2026-08-18
Adding deribit to LIVE_DRIFT_UNREACHABLE_OK — a maintenance window is not a geo-block
task.body:
The weekly live-drift lane is red and stays red until this lands. Sequence, all on 2026-08-18: task 619 landed at 08:57 and pinned the Deribit current-REST OpenAPI at e85c22f5 (1392651 bytes). Deribit then entered maintenance — the production host answered HTTP 503 with its own error 11051 system_maintenance, which the client classified correctly as exchange_not_available and refused to grade green. When the host returned, the lane's live half passed for all 11 venues and the authority half failed instead: api-openapi had moved to 8dfbbe9f (1438107 bytes). The maintenance window was a deployment.

The republished current document is the shipped release. Its path set is now byte-for-byte the same 182 paths as the upcoming document (verified 2026-08-18: no path in one and not the other), while the upcoming pin itself did not move. That is the ordinary current-catches-up-to-upcoming rotation, not corruption.

Re-pinning api-openapi alone is not an option and must not be attempted as a shortcut to a green lane. OracleProvenance.ProviderOperations.ensure_source_revision! binds the provider_operations manifest, the plan, the baseline and every captured fixture's provider_artifact to one revision (provider_operations.ex:267 and :302), so a lone pin bump turns the offline gate red while the online one goes green — the corpus would claim evidence for a document it no longer references.

Note the churn for the recorded decision: both the stale pin and the republished one declare version 2.1.1. The declared version did not move; only the bytes and the HTTP ETag did. A content-hash pin against a document the provider rewrites inside a version therefore pages on every deploy, and each page costs a full corpus re-bind.

task.title: Unified until is declared inclusive but two OKX cursor sites still send it exclusive — decide once and guard the class
acceptance_criteria: One unified until/since inclusivity semantic holds across every venue read, or each exception is a named carve citing the provider contract — the claim and the code agree, whichever way the decision goes

The contradiction between the two landed decisions is resolved explicitly rather than left standing: task 617 states 'Unified since and until are inclusive' in the time_window_integration_test moduledoc, while task 456's carve C-T434/456 pins OKX fetchPositionsHistory as 'unified until=T maps directly to native after=T' with exclusive uTime < until semantics and tier-1 EEA-demo evidence — the losing side's carve text is corrected in docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md, not silently left contradicting the invariant

An offline guard enumerates every request-shape site that renames a unified time bound onto a venue cursor the provider documents as exclusive, and fails on any site that does not compensate — the two known uncompensated sites are RequestShape.OKX build_deposits and build_positions_history (both bare rename("until", "after")), against the compensated put_ohlcv_cursors
The guard is derived, not a hand-listed pair: adding a third exclusive-cursor rename without compensation reddens it, so this class cannot regress one venue at a time

Each venue's cursor exclusivity is confronted against that venue's own pagination contract per its authority manifest, not against how a sibling venue behaves; CCXT's handling is compatibility reference only
Request-shape goldens pin the decided boundary values; mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: The binance-family raw since/until residual — task 633 owns that, and it is translation-presence, not cursor exclusivity
Re-opening task 617's request-side allowlist guard, which measures a different thing (whether a translation happened at all)
task.body:
Two landed tasks decided the same question in opposite directions, each
internally consistent, each reviewed and approved. Neither reviewer could see
the other — the per-task gate sees one diff against one task's criteria, and
this contradiction only exists on the integrated surface.

Task 617 (landed 3ec50a81c045, 2026-08-18) compensated OKX's exclusive candle
cursor and wrote the universal claim into
test/bourse/time_window_integration_test.exs: "Unified `since` and `until` are
inclusive. Venues with exclusive cursors compensate on the request: OKX candles
send `before = since - 1` and `after = until + 1`."

Task 456 (landed earlier, carve extended from task 434) decided the opposite for
the same venue: docs/authored-spec-carves/okx.md records "map unified `until=T`
directly to native `after=T`", cites OKX's official pagination guide making
`after` exclusive, and pins the contract as "returned rows satisfy uTime <
until". That carve carries tier-1 EEA-demo evidence, so it is not a careless
mapping — it is a deliberate, verified decision that now contradicts the stated
invariant.

Measured, not inferred (lib/bourse/unified/request_shape/okx.ex, read
2026-08-18): put_ohlcv_cursors compensates both ends (:1214-1215), while
build_deposits (:1242) and build_positions_history (:1494) both do a bare
rename("until", "after") with no compensation. build_deposits also compensates
`before` for since (:1246) but not `after` for until, so a single builder is
inconsistent with itself.

Decide ONE semantic and make the artifacts agree. Either unified `until` is
inclusive everywhere and the two sites compensate (then 456's carve text is
corrected), or positions-history keeps a documented exclusive carve (then the
moduledoc's universal claim is narrowed to name the exception). What must not
survive is a stated invariant with unnamed violating sites.

The guard is the point of the task, not the two-line fix. A hand-listed pair of
sites reproduces the failure that produced this task: the next exclusive-cursor
rename lands uncompensated and no gate notices. Derive the check from the
request-shape sites themselves so the class is closed.

Authority is each venue's own pagination contract per its authority manifest.

task.title: Authority pins detect drift but cannot name it: reference_only artifacts retain no bytes, so every review reconstructs the delta by hand
acceptance_criteria: A drift review can name what changed in a pinned artifact from repo state alone — the review no longer depends on the previous bytes still being fetchable from the provider, which they are not once the document is republished

The retention decision is made per artifact class with its cost stated, not applied blanket: the corpus currently pins large documents (deribit current-asyncapi is 610300 bytes, current-openapi 1438672) and a naive retain-everything policy is a measurable repo-size commitment that must be named and accepted or rejected on the number

Whatever is retained is sufficient to answer the question a drift review actually asks — which named entities entered or left the surface — so a structural digest (channel/operation/path key sets, per-entity hashes) satisfies this criterion even where full bytes are declined
mix ccxt.authority_check and the drift reports keep working for artifacts that stay reference_only; the change is additive to the existing storage modes rather than a migration that reddens the lane
priv/authority/README.md records the retention policy and what a drift review is expected to be able to answer under each storage mode
The 2026-08-18 deribit AsyncAPI republish is the regression case: re-running the review against the retained artifact names the three added channels, which the hand review could not
out_of_scope: Changing which artifacts are pinned or their freshness semantics — task 579 owns drift-by-artifact-class and its decision stands
Re-pinning anything to restore green; the never-refresh-a-pin-to-restore-green rule is unchanged
task.body:
Task 579 split drift semantics by artifact class and explicitly accepted the
reference_only limitation in passing: "for storage=reference_only artifacts the
review compares the CURRENT page against the authored slice, since old bytes are
not retained." This task revisits that acceptance, because the 2026-08-18
Deribit republish showed what it costs when the workaround does not apply.

Two concrete costs measured in one session, both from repo state:

(1) Deribit republished its current AsyncAPI on 2026-08-18 (sha 70f51ead ->
759902bb, 563150 -> 610300 bytes). The channel count moved 40 -> 43 and the
operation count 80 -> 86, so three channels entered the surface. Naming them was
impossible: the prior bytes are retained nowhere in the repo, and the provider's
own JSON-RPC changelog has no entry for that deploy at all (its most recent
entry is Release 21.07.2026). The drift report records the added channels as
"unnameable_prior_bytes_not_retained" and answers the removal question instead,
by confronting all nine authored channel families against the live list. That is
a real answer to a different question — it establishes the authored surface
survived, not what the provider gained.

(2) The binance authority manifest pins four artifacts (spot-openapi,
spot-errors, spot-docs-source, spot-postman), all storage=reference_only,
path=null. A question about a Binance futures response enum could not be
answered from the corpus at all — the pinned contract is unreadable offline, so
the confrontation fell back to fetching provider pages live.

The gate detects drift correctly; both halves of this are about what a human or
agent can do AFTER it fires. Every drift review currently costs a live refetch
plus reconstruction, and once the provider rewrites the document the old side is
gone permanently.

Note what the same republish proved about pin keys, since it bounds the design
space: both `upcoming` artifacts served byte-identical content under NEW ETags
on the same refetch (upcoming-openapi kept sha 788ae5db / 1438672 bytes while
its ETag moved, likewise upcoming-asyncapi at 8fb075b8 / 609774 bytes), and the
ETag format changed from 32-char hex to a 16-char opaque token. An ETag-keyed
gate would have raised two false alarms on that fetch. Content hash stays the
pin key; this task is about retention, not about changing the key.

A structural digest may well be the right answer over full bytes — the question
a review asks is which named entities entered or left, not which byte moved.
State the cost either way; do not pick blanket retention without the number.

task.title: Lighter subscribe acknowledgement swallows the first market snapshot
acceptance_criteria: A default Bourse.WS.subscribe/3 on lighter (ack wait enabled) returns :ok and still delivers the provider's subscribed/* snapshot to the caller mailbox — the frame is not consumed solely as an acknowledgement
Subsequent update/* frames remain classified as data, not as a second acknowledgement
An invalid lighter channel still surfaces as {:error, {:subscription_rejected, frame}} with the provider error object
An offline instrumented-transport test pins both the preserved snapshot and the rejection path; a live sandbox probe confirms the same split against testnet.zklighter.elliot.ai
The venue carve register records the subscribed-vs-update confrontation against the provider WebSocket reference
out_of_scope: Unified watch_* templates and numeric-market-index resolution, which C-T544b left unresolved
Alpaca batched subscription acks, which are not market-data snapshots
Private Lighter WebSocket authentication
task.body:
Residual of task 544's public Lighter transport. Lighter's first reply after subscribe is type subscribed/<channel> and carries the current snapshot; later frames are type update/<channel>. Bourse.WS.SubscribeAck.classify/2 treats subscribed/* as :success, and WS.subscribe/3 consumes that success frame. The caller therefore never sees the snapshot when acknowledgement waiting is left on (the default).

Evidence: lib/bourse/ws/subscribe_ack.ex classify_lighter/1 plus handle_ack_frame/5 on :success (no requeue). The task-544 canary already works around this by passing ack_timeout_ms: 0 on the success path so the snapshot can be assert_receive'd, while the invalid-channel probe uses the default wait to read provider error 30005. That split is the bug, not a documented contract.

Authority is the provider WebSocket reference (https://apidocs.lighter.xyz/docs/websocket-reference) plus a live testnet subscribe to market_stats/0. The snapshot must remain caller-visible after a successful default subscribe; update/* frames stay data; an unknown channel stays a rejection.

Do not treat this as a reason to reopen task 544's transport authoring.
