task.title: Two canonical SHA-256 schemes hash the same operation-key set, so a REST surface digest will report false drift
acceptance_criteria: One exported helper computes the canonical key-set digest; ContractSource.hash_key_set/1, AuthorityCorpus.digest_key_set_sha256/1 and MutationAdjudication.validate_source_inventory!/3 all call it instead of re-implementing the serialization
The chosen serialization is stated once, in the helper's doc, as the canonical form -- the trailing-newline question is decided explicitly, not inherited from whichever call site was written first

Every pinned hash derived under the losing scheme is re-derived and re-pinned, including operation_key_set_sha256 in priv/authority/deribit/mutation-adjudication.json; the reviewed denominator still binds provider_count 182 and the same revision pin
An offline test asserts the three call sites agree on a shared fixture key set -- a second scheme reintroduced anywhere fails that test with the differing site named
mix ccxt.authority_check, mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch stay green offline
out_of_scope: Producing the REST-surface digest itself -- task 636 shipped the producer; this task only makes its output agree with the consumer
Byte-retention policy for reference_only artifacts, which 636 settled
The prior-slice validation gap, which task 640 owns
task.body:
Two call sites serialize a sorted key list before hashing, and they disagree
on one byte. Verified in the landed base:

- lib/mix/tasks/ccxt/contract_source.ex hash_key_set/1 and
  lib/mix/tasks/ccxt/authority_corpus.ex digest_key_set_sha256/1 both do
  Enum.sort |> Enum.join("\n") |> sha256 -- no trailing newline. These are
  also duplicate implementations of each other.
- lib/bourse/oracle_provenance/mutation_adjudication.ex
  validate_source_inventory!/3 does the same then Kernel.<>("\n") before
  hashing.

Both emit fields named *_key_set_sha256 into priv/authority/deribit/.
The existing surface digest already carries key_set_sha256.operation_keys
(181cad9a..., no-newline scheme) while mutation-adjudication.json and
current-rest-drift-2026-08-18.json carry operation_key_set_sha256
(65f45fa9..., newline scheme). The sets differ today, so the two hex strings
have not yet had to agree. They must once a digest covers the REST surface --
the declared purpose of 636 -- and then the same 182-key set carries two
hashes and validate_source_inventory!/3 reports drift that did not happen.

Fix by construction, not by patching one site: export one helper, call it from
all three, and re-derive whatever pin the losing scheme produced. The offline
test is the part that closes the class -- a fourth site added later must fail
it rather than silently pick a scheme.

Reported by the wave-7 architect pass; the code divergence and the two
conflicting field values were re-verified against the landed base before
filing.

task.title: Surface digests carry unvalidated inferred provenance and stale not-nameable claims the digest itself now disproves
acceptance_criteria: The offline gate validates the digest's prior slice the same way it validates the top-level key sets -- a prior hash that does not match its own key list fails mix ccxt.authority_check

A prior key set that was reconstructed from release notes rather than parsed from retained bytes is marked as inferred in the digest, and ContractComparator surfaces that marking instead of passing it downstream indistinguishably from a parsed set

The records claiming the three added Deribit channels cannot be named are corrected or superseded now that the digest names user.isolated.liquidation, user.liquidation and user.lsp -- including the duplicate claim in test/fixtures/provider_operations/_manifest.json; a dated supersession note is acceptable, silently rewriting a dated record is not
An offline test pins both new behaviours: an unvalidated prior slice fails, and an inferred prior set is not reported as hash-backed evidence
mix ccxt.authority_check and mix check.dispatch stay green offline
out_of_scope: Re-fetching the vanished upstream bytes -- the artifacts stay reference_only
The canonical hash-scheme unification, which task 639 owns
Widening the digest to venues other than deribit
task.body:
Two provenance defects in what task 636 shipped, both from the wave-7
architect pass.

1. The prior slice is unvalidated. authority_corpus.ex checks only the
   top-level key_sets against key_set_sha256; the digest's prior hashes fall
   through the offline gate entirely. Worse, current-asyncapi.json records
   that the 40-key prior set was reconstructed from release notes rather than
   parsed from the artifact's bytes -- which no longer exist -- yet
   contract_comparator.ex hands it downstream as an ordinary hash-backed
   delta. An inferred set and a parsed set must not be indistinguishable to a
   consumer deciding whether drift is evidenced.

2. Several records still say the three added channels cannot be named because
   the bytes were not retained. The digest names them. Leaving both claims in
   the corpus means a future reader has to guess which one is current.

The two are one concern: whether the digest's stated provenance matches what
it actually contains. Do not resolve (2) by editing a dated drift report in
place as though it had always said something else -- supersede it.

task.title: Bybit inverse position contract_size is nil in production but the unit invariant is proven on an injected field the venue never sends
acceptance_criteria: Bybit inverse Position.contract_size is either authored from the provider contract (Bybit documents the inverse BTCUSD contract unit as 1 USD) or the inverse-Bybit row is removed from the C-T610 unit matrix -- the two halves must stop delegating to each other
The decision is recorded once, with a provider-owned source, and C-T625b and C-T610 agree with it and with the parse result

test/bourse/position_unit_invariant_test.exs no longer injects a contractSize key into the Bybit inverse row; the fixture row it asserts against carries only keys present in test/fixtures/responses/bybit/fetch_positions.json
A guard rejects any unit-matrix row whose payload carries a key the recorded venue response does not contain -- the class, not just this row
The comment at lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:3734 stops citing bybit.ts parseMarket as the authority for the linear contract unit; the authored carve is the citation
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Linear Bybit contract_size, which C-T625b already authored as the venue constant 1
Other venues' rows in the C-T610 matrix unless the new guard reds them, in which case fix or register each
Re-recording the Bybit fetch_positions fixture
task.body:
This is the delta_calc class: the golden was computed with a field the venue
does not send, so coverage ratifies the gap instead of catching it. Verified
against the landed base.

read_parse.ex:3736 returns nil for inverse contract_size, deferring to a
market-derived value ("C7"). C-T625b in docs/authored-spec-carves/bybit.md
resolves the market side by stating inverse Market.contract_size stays nil.
Each half defers to the other, so production Position.contract_size for a
Bybit inverse row is nil.

C-T610 (docs/authored-spec-carves/global.md, the unit matrix) nonetheless
lists inverse Bybit under `contracts x contract_size = notional x mark`.
That row is green only because position_unit_invariant_test.exs:257-269
injects "contractSize" => "1" into the payload with markets: []. The recorded
response test/fixtures/responses/bybit/fetch_positions.json has 41 row keys
and contractSize is not one of them -- /v5/position/list does not carry it.

So the invariant is asserted on a payload that cannot occur. Decide it from
the provider contract: Bybit documents the inverse BTCUSD contract as 1 USD.
Author that, or drop the row. Either is acceptable; leaving both claims is
not.

The fourth criterion is the part that closes the class -- a matrix row whose
test payload contains a key absent from the venue's own recording must fail,
so the next injected field is caught at the guard rather than by an architect
reading two documents side by side.

Found by the wave-7 architect pass; every fact above re-verified against the
landed base before filing.

acceptance_criteria: A parameter that exceeds a venue's authored max_length surfaces from the non-bang public API as {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} with reason max_length_exceeded, the same shape a rejected parameter value already returns
The bang variants keep raising; only the non-bang boundary is unified
The deliberate reraises stay deliberate -- OrderPrecision's load_markets/1 fail-loud guard still raises, and the change is not a blanket rescue that swallows it
A test pins both inputs through the same public entry point and asserts they return the same error shape, so a third caller-input validator cannot introduce a third contract
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Raw generated endpoints, which bypass Unified.call/5 validation by design
Changing which parameters carry a max_length or a value constraint
The identifier_reference normalization already in the rescue
task.body:
Tasks 622 and 587 landed in the same wave and each chose a different error
contract for the same class of defect: caller input the venue will reject.

Verified: request_shape.ex:357-370 enforce_max_length! raises
Error.invalid_parameters with reason max_length_exceeded. unified.ex:704-713
rescues Bourse.Error at the public boundary but converts only
unresolved_identifier_reference to a tuple and reraises everything else --
deliberately, to keep OrderPrecision's fail-loud guard loud. 587's
validate_param_values/2 returns {:error, %Error{}}.

Consequence: a 65-character client_order_id escapes Bourse.create_order/…
as an exception while a keyword-list price comes back as a tuple. A caller
writing a `case` around the non-bang API handles one and crashes on the
other.

max_length_exceeded is caller input, not an internal invariant -- route it
through the same tuple path (or add it to the rescue allowlist). Keep the
reraise for the guards that are meant to be loud; the test in the fourth
criterion is what stops the next validator from picking a third contract.

task.title: Shipped 0.6.0 connects the USD-M private stream to a host Binance decommissioned on 2026-04-23, and the failure is silent
acceptance_criteria: The USD-M private stream connects to wss://fstream.binance.com/private/ws with the listen key as a ?listenKey= query parameter, matching Binance's own migration notice -- not the legacy wss://fstream.binance.com/ws/<listenKey> path form
The events= parameter is decided explicitly and the decision recorded: either the streams the caller subscribed to, or a documented default -- not omitted by accident
The listen-key credential embedding stops assuming a path segment for this venue; whichever venues still authenticate by path keep working and are covered

An offline test pins private_url and the assembled private connect URL for USD-M the same way public_url and market_url are already pinned, so the private half can no longer drift while the public half is guarded
A live probe proves the private stream actually pushes a frame -- a connect that succeeds and delivers nothing is the exact failure mode being fixed, so connection success alone is not evidence
url_routing.ex authored_usdm_hosts/1 either checks exchange.id or its name and doc stop claiming a scoping the code does not perform

The sandbox host claims task 627 recorded are re-confronted: the carve in docs/authored-spec-carves/binanceusdm.md must not rest on demo-fstream evidence that the same carve disclaims as not enforcing the split
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: COIN-M, which has no route split on dstream
The public and market halves, which task 627 migrated correctly
Rewriting the listen-key HTTP round-trip itself
task.body:
This is shipped in 0.6.0 and it fails without an error.

Verified in the landed base: spec_config.ex:73-78 migrated the public and
market halves to /public/ws and /market/ws but left private_url as
"wss://fstream.binance.com/ws", and ws.ex:201-214 appends the listen key as a
path segment via join_path/2.

Binance's own change notice (fetched 2026-08-19, developers.binance.com,
"Important WebSocket Change Notice" under usds-margined-futures) states the
three new base URLs and gives the private form as
wss://fstream.binance.com/private/ws?listenKey=<listenKey>&events=... It also
states verbatim: "Legacy URLs will remain available until 2026-04-23, after
which they will be permanently decommissioned", and that unmigrated
connections "will ONLY be able to receive data from
wss://fstream.binance.com/public. Channels under /market and /private will
stop pushing data."

That deadline passed roughly four months ago. Every consumer watching USD-M
order updates through this client is connecting to a dead route.

Why nothing caught it: the offline tests pin public_url and market_url only,
the live probe runs against demo-fstream, and 627's own carve says that host
does not enforce the split. A wrong listen-key route connects and then
delivers nothing, so there is no error anywhere in the chain. The fifth
criterion exists because of that -- prove a frame arrives, not that the
socket opened.

Found by the wave-7 architect pass; the code and the provider notice were
both re-verified before filing.

task.title: watch_order_book returns nil on deribit and both binance futures surfaces, and one socket with several symbols collapses every book onto one key
acceptance_criteria: The authored apply_mode of every registered venue is handled by Orderbook.classify_update/2 -- an authored mode the state machine does not know must fail loudly at spec load or at connect, never degrade to :unknown and return an empty book

The three venues authoring apply_mode incremental (deribit, binance, binanceusdm) deliver a populated book from watch_order_book; where the subscribed template is a partial-depth replacement stream the authored mode is corrected to match what the venue actually sends, with the provider contract cited

Two symbols watched over one connection keep separate books and separate broadcast topics -- either by using the combined-stream host so each frame carries its own stream name, or by one socket per symbol; the choice is recorded against Binance's own documentation
An offline instrumented-transport test pins both: a populated book after the first frame, and two symbols not overwriting each other
A live probe on each affected venue shows a non-empty book with bids and asks
mix check.dispatch green

The apply_mode coverage is asserted as a computed set with drift in both directions, in the shape task 617 landed for request shapes: the modes the state machine handles are compared against the modes the authored corpus actually declares, so a corpus value with no clause fails AND a clause no venue declares any more is flagged as stale rather than lingering. Naming the three known venues in a test is explicitly not sufficient - a fourth apply_mode value must redden the suite by construction
out_of_scope: Venues whose authored apply_mode is already handled and whose books populate today
Checksum validation and sequence-gap recovery
The USD-M private host migration, which task 643 owns
task.body:
Two defects that together make watch_order_book unusable on the affected
venues. Both verified in the landed base.

1. Authored apply_mode "incremental" is not a case the state machine knows.
   priv/specs/json/output/authored/{deribit,binance,binanceusdm}.json all set
   websocket.orderbook_semantics.apply_mode = "incremental". classify_update/2
   (lib/bourse/ws/semantics/orderbook.ex:70-79) matches only "snapshot",
   "delta", "replace" and "both"; everything else falls to :unknown, and
   :unknown returns Map.get(state.books, key) -- a book that is never written.
   Task 628 fixed the routing; the state machine still ignores the authored
   mode. Note that the subscribed binance template is a partial book depth
   stream, i.e. a full top-N replacement rather than a diff, so "incremental"
   may be the wrong authored value in the first place -- decide it from the
   venue's documentation.

2. The routing key drops the symbol. Binance partial-depth frames carry
   neither an `e` nor an `s` field, so 628's channel "depthUpdate" reaches
   adapter.ex:238 as key = market_id || channel, and
   MessageRouter.extract_market_id("depthUpdate") is nil. With more than one
   symbol on one /ws socket every book lands on the same key and the same
   broadcast topic.

The first criterion is the class fix: an authored mode the code cannot honour
must be loud, because the current behaviour is an empty book with no error --
indistinguishable from a quiet market.

Found by the wave-7 architect pass; re-verified before filing.

task.title: Every WebSocket reconnect leaks a connection-owner process, and the ownership check that would have caught it is dead code three docs still describe as live
acceptance_criteria: A reconnect closes the previous connection before replacing it -- an adapter that reconnects N times holds one connection, not N
A test asserts the process count is stable across repeated reconnects, so the leak cannot silently return
ConnectionOwner is supervised and linked or monitored by whatever depends on it; an owner whose death is invisible to its dependents is not acceptable
owns_connection?/1 is either restored to a real check or deleted, and the three documentation sites describing it stop describing behaviour the code does not have
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: The USD-M private host, task 643
Orderbook semantics and routing keys, task 644
Reworking the group-router design task 630 landed
task.body:
Reported by the wave-7 architect pass, from the WS lane.

Adapter.handle_info(:connect, ...) at lib/bourse/ws/adapter.ex:176-180
overwrites the stored ws without closing the previous one, so each reconnect
strands an owner process. Nothing bounds it. ConnectionOwner is neither
supervised nor linked and monitors nobody, so a stranded or dead owner is
invisible.

owns_connection?/1 (lib/bourse/ws.ex:581-599) returns false on every path
since task 630 replaced the ownership model -- it is dead code, and three
documentation sites still describe it as a live check. Delete it or make it
real; leaving a described-but-inert guard is worse than either.

These are one concern -- connection lifecycle after the 630 group-router
change -- and one reviewer verifies them in one pass over one diff.

task.title: fetch_funding_rate answers for markets that have no funding: a spot symbol silently receives the perp's rate stamped with the spot symbol
acceptance_criteria: A symbol whose market has no funding (spot) does not return a FundingRate -- it returns a named error identifying the symbol as fundingless, never a plausible number borrowed from a different market

A symbol the venue surface cannot serve (a COIN-M symbol asked of a USD-M-routed surface) returns a named error, not {:ok, []} -- the empty-list fallthrough is made loud the same way task 616 made the struct fallthrough loud

backfill_request_symbols/4 stops stamping the requested unified symbol onto a record parsed from a different market; the symbol written back must be the market the venue actually answered for, or the read must fail
An offline test pins all three: fundingless symbol errors, unservable symbol errors, and a served symbol keeps its own market's identity
A live probe on binance reproduces the original three cases and shows the new behaviour: BTC/USDT (spot), BTC/USD:BTC (COIN-M on a spot-configured surface), BTC/USDT:USDT (served)
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: fetch_funding_rates plural, whose symbol-dict envelope task 616 already made loud, unless the same fix naturally covers it
Funding interval and cadence semantics
Adding funding support to venues that genuinely have none
task.body:
Two symptoms, one defect: the funding-rate read answers even when the market
it was asked about has no funding.

Reproduced deterministically against the testnets by the wave-7 architect
pass:

  fetch_funding_rate(binance_spot, "BTC/USDT")       -> %FundingRate{symbol: "BTC/USDT",       funding_rate: 8.235e-5, timestamp: 1787097890001}
  fetch_funding_rate(binance_spot, "BTC/USDT:USDT")  -> %FundingRate{symbol: "BTC/USDT:USDT",  funding_rate: 8.235e-5, timestamp: 1787097890001}
  fetch_funding_rate(binance_spot, "BTC/USD:BTC")    -> {:ok, []}

Identical rate, identical timestamp, identical mark for the spot symbol and
the perp. Spot has no funding. The request resolves to the perp's market id
and read_parse.ex backfill_request_symbols/4 then writes the *requested*
unified symbol onto the record, so the answer carries the spot symbol and a
real-looking number. Nothing errors. That is the domain-ground-truth class --
it survives every mechanical check because the value is well-formed.

The {:ok, []} case is the same read on a symbol the routed surface cannot
serve at all. Task 616 made the struct-escaping-a-symbol-dict fallthrough
loud; the empty-list fallthrough is still silent. A consumer matching
{:ok, %FundingRate{}} gets an undiagnosable MatchError, one matching {:ok, x}
reads [] as "no funding" rather than "wrong surface for this symbol".

Verified statically on my side: the symbol backfill at read_parse.ex:2192-2203
is the mechanism that makes the wrong answer look right. The live repro is
the architect pass's.

Any venue deliberately left out of the live smoke carries a registered reason in the same structure the time-window matrix uses for its exclusions, so the list cannot silently shrink again

Credentialed tiers

task.title: Account class and margin model are not readable as unified facts, so a consumer cannot tell a derivatives account from a spot one
acceptance_criteria: A unified account read separates three distinct facts: product access, the account-level margin model, and the position-level margin mode -- they are not collapsed into one field

Each fact is sourced from the venue's own classification fields, and the provider field names are recorded per venue: bybit unifiedMarginStatus and marginMode, deribit portfolio_margining_enabled and margin_model, alpaca multiplier and shorting_enabled, binance accountType/permissions plus position isolated, hyperliquid crossMarginSummary and leverage.type, lighter account_type/account_trading_mode plus position margin_mode
A fact the venue does not report stays explicitly unknown or unavailable -- a venue capability flag or a caller option must never be substituted for an observation
The raw provider payload is preserved in info so an integration test can pin the documented field names
Each venue's mapping is live-verified against its sandbox or testnet with a real response, and the confrontation is registered in that venue's carve register
mix ccxt.oracle_gate and mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Venues beyond the six named in the report
Changing fetch_balance or fetch_positions return shapes
Deriving an account class where the venue reports nothing -- that case stays unknown
task.body:
Consumer report, ../bourse/BUGS.md entry dated 2026-08-18, filed by the
trading_dashboard consumer (its task 166).

The raw endpoint functions exist, but there is no common account-fact result
that preserves the venues' own classification fields. fetch_balance and
fetch_positions prove reachability and normalize some position modes, while
losing the independent account facts entirely. The consumer's stated
consequence is the one that matters: without them a caller can treat a
derivatives account as spot because it is going by a configured label rather
than an observation.

Filed against the general defect -- account classification is not a unified
fact -- rather than against any single venue's missing field. The six venues
in the report are the evidence, not the scope boundary of the design.

The third criterion is the load-bearing one: the failure this prevents is
substituting a capability flag or a caller-supplied option for something the
venue never said.

NOTE 2026-08-19: task 602 (account-level portfolio-margin summaries in
Bourse.PortfolioRisk) was superseded — Bourse.PortfolioRisk moved to the
bourse_trading repository (client CHANGELOG v0.4.0, commit 8e0eb3f, 2026-08-11),
so its premise is void in this codebase. Its provider surface overlaps this
task's second criterion (deribit portfolio_margining_enabled and margin_model
from private/get_account_summaries — note the carve register: get_portfolio_margins
is RETIRED, -32601 live). If the consumer also wants the numeric account-level
margin summaries (initial/maintenance/projected margin), they ride this account-fact
surface or a bourse_trading task — decide at implementation; do not re-file here.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787146246444-a5bab029, f291108000f5720a98cf14f53fcb60a1bfeb7ad6).

task.title: Nothing pins the capability surface across releases, so answering whether a has? flag changed means unpacking two hex tarballs by hand
acceptance_criteria: Every runtime venue's capabilities.has map is pinned in the offline gate, so a changed flag fails a check and forces an explicit re-pin instead of shipping silently
The pin records the value per venue per capability -- not a count, not a hash alone -- so a diff names which capability changed and in which direction
A test proves the gate catches a flip: temporarily flipping one flag reds the check and names the venue and capability
The pin is cheap to read across releases: answering "did this flag change between two versions" must not require unpacking published artifacts by hand
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Fixing a binanceusdm stop-market regression in this client -- the reported flip is falsified: the flag reads true in the v0.6.0 tag, in HEAD, in both the 0.4.0 and 0.6.0 hex tarballs, and in the consumer's own deps tree, with the binanceusdm capability map byte-identical across the two releases
Diagnosing the consumer's own capability gate, which is where that defect most likely sits
Changing any capability value
task.body:
Re-scoped 2026-08-19 after the premise of the consumer report was falsified.

The report (../bourse/BUGS.md, 2026-08-19) said has?("createStopMarketOrder")
flipped from true to false for binanceusdm between 0.4.0 and 0.6.0, costing a
capability-gated consumer its stop-market protective orders -- a position sat
without a stop at the venue. The impact is real; the stated cause is not.
Checked independently from two seats: the flag reads true in the v0.6.0 tag,
in current HEAD, in the published 0.4.0 and 0.6.0 hex tarballs, and in the
consumer's own deps tree, and the binanceusdm capability map is byte-identical
across the two releases (157 keys, none added, removed or flipped).
Exchange.build_capabilities/1 copies capabilities.has verbatim and has?/2 is a
plain lookup, so no derivation sits between the spec and the answer.

So there is nothing to fix in this client's binanceusdm capabilities, and a
task pointed there would send an implementer and a reviewer looking for a
defect that is not present.

What the incident did expose is real and independent of where the defect
finally sits: answering "did this capability change between two releases"
required unpacking two published tarballs by hand. There is no pinned
capability surface, so a flag governing whether a protective order may be
placed could change between releases with nothing failing. That gap is what
this task closes.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787106314363-54b1f893, 38d4b5f7d683f4b30d757098681c353cdbe217e0).

task.title: The scheduled live lane probes two methods per venue while the WebSocket corpus that would have caught the last three outages runs nowhere
acceptance_criteria: The scheduled live run executes the existing :network and :capability_live corpus, not only ops/live-drift.sh -- the WebSocket auth smoke in test/bourse/ws/auth_live_smoke_test.exs is included

Every venue with WebSocket support is probed for a real first data frame, not a subscribe acknowledgement: task 628 already showed an ack proves nothing about routing, and task 643 showed a dead route connects and then stays silent
A run that connects but receives no frame within a bounded wait fails the lane and names the venue and channel -- silence must be a failure, never a pass
The lane's results are aggregated into one durable artifact per run, listing per venue and per surface what was probed and what the outcome was, so a later reader can tell coverage from silence
Venues or surfaces deliberately not probed carry a registered reason in the artifact, the same way the time-window matrix registers its exclusions
One scheduled run is executed end to end and its artifact recorded as evidence; only testnet or demo credentials are used

The lane classifies the first frame it receives per venue and channel, not merely that one arrived. This is the detection half of task 638: that fix closed its class by vocabulary - any venue classifier may now answer {:success, :data} when its acknowledgement doubles as the first snapshot - which lowers the cost of the second venue to one return line but detects nothing, because only the venue itself can reveal that its ack carries data. No scan over our own code can find it, so the live lane is the only place that can, and a first frame that is an acknowledgement carrying payload is reported as such rather than counted as connectivity
out_of_scope: Building live test code that already exists -- tasks 188 and 527 shipped the :capability_live matrix and the always-on scheduled host; this task widens what the schedule executes
The pinned capability surface, which task 649 owns -- do not duplicate it here
Production credentials or any mutating order on a live-money host
task.body:
The scheduled weekly lane on the always-on host (task 527) runs
ops/live-drift.sh = mix ccxt.authority_check --online + mix
ccxt.verify_live_drift. Its surface is two methods per venue -- a public read
and fetch_balance, with lighter substituting fetch_closed_orders and
coinbaseexchange marked not_applicable. That is a reachability and auth smoke.
It answers "can we reach the venue and authenticate", and nothing else.

Meanwhile a live corpus exists that no schedule executes: over twenty files
tagged :network or :capability_live, including test/bourse/ws/
auth_live_smoke_test.exs with its differential WebSocket handshake probes.

Every severe finding of the last weeks sits outside those two methods:
task 618 (dead WS channels, found by a consumer), task 643 (the USD-M private
route decommissioned on 2026-04-23 -- socket connects, delivers nothing; found
by an architect pass one day after the 0.6.0 release), task 647 (a venue
completeness assertion red and invisible behind --include network). None of
them touches fetch_ticker or fetch_balance.

Caught by hand three times is a missing test, not a habit. The building blocks
are all present; what is missing is the schedule and the aggregation.

The third criterion is the load-bearing one. Both 618 and 643 are failures
where the connection succeeds and nothing arrives -- a lane that treats
silence as absence of error reproduces exactly the blind spot being closed.
task.implemented: Landed by cursor via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787107612446-759249c3, ca7abaf848412ed6c0c25fea3d4e32b748476786).

task.title: Two caller-input rejections still escape the non-bang unified API as exceptions, so the public error contract depends on which field was wrong
acceptance_criteria: Bourse.create_order/6 with both stop_loss_price and take_profit_price on a binance-family venue returns {:error, %Bourse.Error{type: :invalid_parameters}} carrying the multiple_conditional_legs reason, instead of raising out of the non-bang API
Bourse.create_orders with an empty or missing orders list on bybit returns {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} instead of raising Error.bad_request
The bang variants keep raising for both, and OrderPrecision's fail-loud markets_not_loaded guard still raises - the conversion is an allowlist of caller-input reasons, never a blanket rescue

The contract is enforced as a class rather than a third allowlist entry: a test sweeps every public non-bang unified entry point with the known caller-input rejections and asserts a tuple, so a fourth validator added later cannot introduce a fourth contract without reddening the suite
test/bourse/binance_authored_spec_test.exs stops pinning assert_raise on the non-bang Bourse.create_order and asserts the tuple instead
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Changing which parameters carry the constraint, or the wording of the venue-side rejection
Raw generated endpoint functions, which are not part of the unified non-bang contract
Errors raised by the transport or signing layers - this task covers caller-input validation only
task.body:
Reviewer proposal out of the task-642 run (run-1787098161945-85b19222), verified by code read before filing.

Task 587 established the invariant that no exception escapes a public unified function for a caller-input problem, and task 642 converted max_length_exceeded to a tuple at Unified.call/5. The rescue clause is an explicit allowlist keyed on the error's raw reason, so every reason not on it still reraises. Two caller-input rejections are still off it:

1. lib/bourse/unified/request_shape.ex reject_multiple_binance_conditional_legs!/3 raises Error.invalid_parameters with reason multiple_conditional_legs when a binance-family create_order carries both stop_loss_price and take_profit_price. test/bourse/binance_authored_spec_test.exs pins that raise on the NON-bang Bourse.create_order, so the wrong contract is currently protected by a test.
2. lib/bourse/unified/request_shape/bybit.ex batch_orders/3 raises Error.bad_request for an empty or missing orders list.

Both are the caller getting an argument wrong, which is exactly what 587 said must be a tuple. The consumer-visible effect is that the non-bang API has two contracts and which one you get depends on which field you got wrong.

Filed as the class closure rather than as two patches: the allowlist shape is the thing that lets a fourth validator quietly pick a fourth contract, so the deliverable is the sweep test over the public entry points, with these two sites as its first failing cases.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787103315177-7c3d8dff, d6d105b711947ef6f8ea04d7163bbcff090422dc).

task.title: Every emulated read rebuilds the parameter map from three hardcoded keys, so all other caller parameters are silently discarded before the delegated call
acceptance_criteria: No emulated handler constructs the delegated parameter map from a literal list of string keys. The caller's params map is carried through to the delegated read; a key the emulation itself consumes is removed explicitly and the removal names why

The mechanism that keeps it closed is a scan, not an example: a test walks the AST of lib/bourse/emulation.ex, collects every private handler that reaches call_method/5, and asserts the map each one passes is derived from the incoming params rather than built literally. A tenth emulated handler added later cannot reintroduce the drop without reddening the suite

Coverage is computed, not hand-listed: the set of methods asserted is derived from the capability tables - every venue/method pair whose support value is "emulated" - so a venue that starts emulating an eleventh method is swept automatically

Drift is asserted in both directions: a param the emulation deliberately does not forward is a named entry with a stated reason, and an entry naming a param the code no longer drops fails the test as stale

Concrete regression from the task-633 review: binanceusdm and binancecoinm fetch_closed_orders, fetch_canceled_orders and fetch_canceled_and_closed_orders put endTime on the wire when the caller passes until. Pinned by an HTTP request golden, not by a RequestShape.apply assertion - the whole point is that the request-side translation was already correct and never got the value
mix check.dispatch green

A parameter the emulation does not forward is compensated or refused, never silently ignored. until is the proving case: it does not occur anywhere in lib/bourse/emulation.ex and filter_by_since_limit/4 filters only value >= since, so an emulated fetch_closed_orders(ex, symbol, until: T) returns rows after T with no error today. Each non-forwarded param must be (a) forwarded, (b) compensated by a real local filter, or (c) refused with a typed error naming the param and the method - and the drift assertion is over compensated-or-refused, not over a documented list
out_of_scope: Changing which methods are emulated on which venue, or adding native endpoints to replace an emulation
The RequestShape raw since/until allowlist itself - tasks 617, 633 and 637 own that surface; this task covers only the params that never reach it
Local filtering semantics of the emulated handlers - filter_by_status and filter_by_since_limit keep their current behaviour
task.body:
Found by the orchestrator seat reading the task-633 verdict, then confirmed in code. The task-633 reviewer approved with a warning naming one symptom: emulated USD-M and COIN-M fetch_closed_orders and fetch_canceled_orders drop until before delegating, so endTime never reaches the wire even though 633 made RequestShape translate it correctly. The code is worse than the symptom.

lib/bourse/emulation.ex handle_fetch_filtered_orders/5 does not filter the caller's params - it discards them and builds a fresh map:

    symbol = extract_param(params, :symbol)
    since = extract_param(params, :since)
    limit = extract_param(params, :limit)
    params = %{"symbol" => symbol, "since" => since, "limit" => limit}

handle_fetch_canceled_and_closed_orders/4 repeats the same three lines, and handle_fetch_order/4 extracts the same three. So it is not until that is dropped; it is EVERY caller parameter other than symbol, since and limit - venue-native passthrough params included. The value is gone before the delegated fetch_orders call, which is why a correct request-shape translation downstream can never recover it.

WHY THIS SURVIVED NINE PASSES AT THE SAME CLASS. Raw time-window handling has been touched in tasks 246, 366, 456, 532, 540, 553, 617, 633 and 637. Task 540 named these exact handlers - "the emulated handlers build the param map unconditionally" - and fixed the half where a nil serialized as an empty query value, leaving the half where a present value is discarded. Every later pass then asserted at the request-shape layer, which is downstream of the discard and therefore green regardless.

That is why the acceptance criteria above demand a scan over the handler surface and a coverage set computed from the capability tables, rather than a pin on the two methods the 633 review named. The existing guards for this class are sound where they sit - the request-shape sweep keeps an empty, shrink-only allowlist with a staleness assertion, and every remaining raw since/until row cites the provider manifest that leaves the bound unmapped - but all of them observe the request AFTER the emulation has already thrown the parameter away. A guard cannot see a value that never reached it. The missing assertion is the one on the emulation boundary itself.

SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-19, after dispatch, verified in the landed base and steered into the run. The literal rebuild occurs at seven sites, not the three named above: lines 618, 638, 741, 754, 773, 824 (ledger, code/since/limit) and 1166. Several further call_method/5 sites pass a literal map inline without ever assigning to params. fetch_and_filter_by_trade_ids/7 and fetch_and_filter_by_order_id/7 take symbol/since/limit as function arguments, so their caller lost the rest one frame higher - an AST scan for literal ASSIGNMENTS misses them, and the scan must find the point where the caller params stop being carried.

And the defect is worse than a lost parameter: until appears nowhere in emulation.ex, and the only local filter is the lower bound value >= since in filter_by_since/3. On every emulated path until is neither forwarded nor compensated, so the caller gets rows past the requested upper bound with no error - a silent wrong result, the same signature as tasks 644 and 646.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787120511758-a10bfd45, b1c97d9ece1123bcc92b33eca3b94629e2938080).

task.title: RequestShape still raises ArgumentError for caller-input problems, and the 651 class sweep cannot see them
acceptance_criteria: Every RequestShape ArgumentError that is caller input (wrong field combination, unsupported type, missing required identifier the caller must supply) surfaces from the public non-bang unified API as {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} instead of escaping as ArgumentError
Fail-loud setup and spec guards stay raises through the non-bang path -- markets not loaded, a loaded market missing the fields needed to shape, and authored-spec bugs are not converted

The 651 class sweep (or an equivalent successor) reddens when a new caller-input ArgumentError is added to RequestShape, the same way it already reddens for a new raise Error.* without a converted reason
Bang variants still raise for the converted cases
mix check.dispatch green

The one ambiguous site resolves into THREE cases, not two, and merging the two clauses is not the fix. hyperliquid asset_index/2 answers one no-market-asset-index message for: (1) markets never loaded - find_market/2 catch-all returns nil when markets is neither list nor map - which is setup and keeps raising, same as derive and lighter; (2) markets loaded but no entry matches the symbol - caller input, returns a tuple naming the symbol; (3) a market matched but carries no asset_index under any of the three accepted spellings - incomplete market data, keeps raising with its own message, the same class as the lighter missing-precision keep. Three cases, three messages, split across both categories. The Exchange markets field is inspectable before find_market/2 runs, so the distinction costs one guard. That guard tests for nil, never for truthiness: asset_index is 0-BASED and the first market genuinely carries 0, so an idx || default or an if market.asset_index would report the venue-position-zero market as missing. The three existing clauses already use when not is_nil(idx) and the rewrite keeps that discipline
out_of_scope: Transport and signing ArgumentErrors
Raw generated endpoint functions
Changing which field combinations or types are invalid
Converting OrderPrecision's markets_not_loaded guard, which 642/651 already kept as a raise
task.body:
Open decision for the orchestrator before dispatch: classify each current RequestShape ArgumentError as caller-input (tuple) or fail-loud setup/spec (keep raising). The inventory below is evidence, not a conversion list.

Task 587 said no exception escapes a public unified function for a caller-input problem. Tasks 642 and 651 closed that for raise Error.* by allowlisting raw["reason"] at Unified.call/5 and sweeping RequestShape for those raises. The landed scanner only matches raise Error.fun(...) and ignores ArgumentError, so a fourth validator that raises ArgumentError still gives the caller a third contract.

Verified by reading lib/bourse/unified/request_shape/**/*.ex after d6d105b: ArgumentError raises remain in binance (batch type/field/price/closePosition combinations), lighter (missing l1_address, non-limit type, bad side/TIF/numeric), okx (cost-based market on a derivative, unsupported option underlying or open-interest period), hyperliquid (bad timeout/duration/amount types), and derive (missing loaded market / market info). Some of those are the same class as 651 (caller got an argument wrong). Some are the same class as OrderPrecision's markets_not_loaded (setup; keep raising).

The deliverable is the class closure, not a one-off rescue. A new ArgumentError caller-input raise added later must redden the suite the way a new Error raise without a converted reason already does.

ORCHESTRATOR CLASSIFICATION 2026-08-19, which the body above asks for before dispatch. Every site read in the landed base after d6d105b. This is the disposition, not a fresh survey - an implementer that disagrees with an entry says so and why, but does not re-derive the list.

KEEP RAISING - setup or authored-spec defect, nothing the caller can fix by changing an argument:
  request_shape.ex:382  validate_unified_source! - an unresolved unified source for a given exchange and method is a spec bug; the caller is not involved at all. The clearest keep.
  derive.ex:118,122     loaded market / loaded markets absent - the markets_not_loaded class that 642 and 651 already preserved.
  derive.ex:148         the loaded market carries no venue info; the message itself says to reload markets.
  lighter.ex:110,114    same market-absent class.
  lighter.ex:121        the loaded market lacks precision data - a market-data gap, not caller input.
  okx.ex:1459           unsupported open-interest ENDPOINT PATH - the path comes from the authored spec, not from the caller.

CONVERT to an error tuple - the caller got an argument wrong:
  hyperliquid.ex:112,280,285,498,616,620,643,647   value and type rejections (timeout, duration, amount, integer, numeric string).
  lighter.ex:54         missing l1_address. The comment at the site states the intent - require it loudly rather than ship the venue 20001 - which is exactly a caller-input contract.
  lighter.ex:135,138,143,147,154,161,181,185       precision misalignment, non-numeric, non-limit type, bad side, unsupported TIF, non-boolean, non-integer.
  binance.ex:157,169,184,187,200,204,221,225       batch-order type and field-combination rejections.
  okx.ex:270            a cost-based market order aimed at a derivative - an unsupported caller combination.
  okx.ex:1391           unsupported option underlying - a caller value.
  okx.ex:1478           unsupported open-interest PERIOD - a caller value, unlike the endpoint path two clauses above it.

AMBIGUOUS, one site, and it is a defect on its own: hyperliquid.ex:574 and 575 raise an identical message from two different clauses, so the no-market-asset-index answer today means either markets-absent or symbol-unknown. Split per the acceptance criterion above.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-19, which closes a question this split raised. The comment over asset_index/2 reads as though asset_index itself is often nil on live loadMarkets, which would mean a live caller hits case (3) with a valid symbol while every offline test passes on fixture-injected data. Measured against the venue instead of reasoned from the code: Bourse.fetch_markets on hyperliquid sandbox returns 1462 markets and ZERO without an asset_index, running consecutively from 0 (SOL/USDC:USDC is 0, APT/USDC:USDC is 1) - exactly the universe position the L1 field expects. So the comment refers to the discarded id and base_id fallbacks, not to asset_index, and carve C-T339 is right. There is no live defect here and no follow-up task.

This strengthens case (3) rather than weakening it: live it is UNREACHABLE, because the venue supplies the field without exception. Reaching it means the loaded market data is wrong in a way the caller cannot cause and cannot fix, which is precisely what must stay loud.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787109557313-9aa31267, 98978d2ec572147f8d9e37595e9e05703e87a065).

task.title: Umbrella binance inverse symbols denormalize to a compact id the COIN-M premiumIndex does not list
acceptance_criteria: Without load_markets, a unified inverse perp such as BTC/USD:BTC denormalizes to the provider's COIN-M id (BTCUSD_PERP), not a concatenated compact id

Live fetch_funding_rate on umbrella binance (sandbox: true, no preloaded markets) for BTC/USD:BTC returns %FundingRate{symbol: "BTC/USD:BTC"} from demo-dapi premiumIndex, not the task-646 unservable empty-list error
Spot BTC/USDT on the same surface still returns the fundingless error from task 646; a linear perp still keeps BTC/USDT:USDT
An offline request golden or dispatch assertion pins the native id on dapi /dapi/v1/premiumIndex
mix ccxt.oracle_gate green
out_of_scope: Revisiting the task-646 fundingless / empty-list loudness
Loading markets as the only way to resolve the id
Dated COIN-M delivery contracts beyond the perpetual grammar
task.body:
Task 646 made fetch_funding_rate refuse a silent {:ok, []} when umbrella
binance is asked for BTC/USD:BTC. That empty list is not because the
umbrella surface lacks dapi: fetchFundingRate already selects
dapiPublic_get_premiumindex when market_family is inverse. Live 2026-08-19
on Exchange.new!(binance, sandbox: true) with no loaded markets, the
unservable error fires because the outbound id is not the provider's
BTCUSD_PERP. The implicit swap pattern concatenates BASE/QUOTE:SETTLE into
a compact id dapi does not list; the offline cadence stub that sends
native_symbol BTCUSD_PERP still returns a FundingRate.

Binance COIN-M documents perpetual ids as {BASE}USD_PERP (see
https://developers.binance.com/docs/derivatives/coin-margined-futures/market-data/rest-api/Index-Price-and-Mark-Price).
binance_contract_symbol/2 already knows that grammar on the read path for
binanceusdm/binancecoinm. The write/denormalize path for umbrella binance
does not.

Do not treat load_markets as the fix: the live public read is issued
without a catalog, the same way the task-646 probe ran. After this lands,
the task-646 unservable error must remain for a genuine empty premiumIndex
and must not become the inverse-perp happy path.

task.title: A post-parse backfill re-supplies the value the authored field map already produces, so oracle replay cannot tell a working envelope clock from a broken one
acceptance_criteria: The balance timestamp has exactly one source. Where the authored field map declares it - hyperliquid declares source "envelope", key "time" - the parsed value comes from that rule and the post-parse assignment does not overwrite it. Where no venue authors it, the field is absent rather than synthesized from a hardcoded envelope key

A discriminating test proves the authored path is the one that runs: replay the recorded hyperliquid fetch_balance with the ENVELOPE clock removed and assert the parsed timestamp is absent. Stripping time from the row cannot discriminate here, because the authored source is the envelope and the backfill reads the same envelope - carve C-T562 currently claims the row-stripped confrontation is sufficient and that claim must be corrected in the same change

The class is held closed by a scan over lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex: no post-parse step may assign a struct field that a field map is capable of populating, unless the site is a named entry stating why the authored layer cannot own it. Drift asserted in both directions, so an entry whose field later becomes authored fails as stale

Every venue whose balance timestamp is populated today keeps the same value after the change, or the change in value is stated with the venue and the reason - this is a correctness fix, not a silent behaviour change
mix check.dispatch and mix ccxt.oracle_gate green

The guard is verified by BREAKING it, not by reading its test. The report states the mutation that was introduced, the exact failure message the guard produced, and that the mutation was reverted. A passing test proves the assertion runs; only a deliberate break proves it is wired to the gate and that its message names the offending thing. A guard whose test is green while its wiring is missing looks identical to a working one
out_of_scope: Authoring balance timestamp sources for venues that do not declare one - the absence is the honest state until the provider contract is confronted
The envelope-source vocabulary itself, which task 562 landed and this task consumes
Non-balance parse types, unless the scan finds the same shape there - a site the scan flags is in scope, a speculative sweep of unrelated types is not
task.body:
Reviewer concern from the task-562 run (run-1787061258517-9e4fb311), approved and never addressed, surfaced by reading the settled verdicts rather than the verdict lines. The reviewer wrote it plainly: hyperliquid unified fetch_balance still backfills timestamp from body.time in put_balance_info/2, so oracle replay of that venue would stay green even if the field map missed.

Confirmed in the landed base. lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:

    defp put_balance_info(%Bourse.Balance{} = balance, body) do
      balance
      |> ...
      |> Map.put(:timestamp, balance_timestamp(body))
      |> put_datetime()
    end

    defp balance_timestamp(body) when is_map(body), do: Bourse.Safe.integer(Map.get(body, "time"))

It is an unconditional Map.put that runs AFTER the field-map parse, for every venue.

And the authored layer already owns this field. hyperliquid's balance field map declares, in its always-guard branch:

    "timestamp": {"key": "time", "source": "envelope", "coercion": "safeInteger", "format": "ms"}

So both mechanisms read the same envelope key and produce the same value. That is the self-confirmation loop: if the authored envelope rule broke tomorrow, the backfill would supply the identical timestamp and every replay, every oracle gate and every fixture assertion would stay green. The suite cannot observe the difference, so it is not verifying the authored path at all.

WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DOES NOT CATCH IT. Carve C-T562 states that the confrontation "reads that mapping against the recorded envelope with time removed from the row, so a post-parse body.time backfill cannot mask a field-map miss". Removing the key from the ROW cannot discriminate these two sources, because the authored rule reads source: envelope and the backfill reads the envelope too. Only removing the ENVELOPE clock separates them. The carve's claim is therefore stronger than the evidence supports and is corrected here.

This is the domain-ground-truth shape: internally consistent, fully covered, and blind in exactly the place the coverage was supposed to look. Scoped as the class - a post-parse step that duplicates an authored source makes the oracle blind to that field, wherever it occurs - with the balance timestamp as the instance that proves it.

task.title: The critical-module coverage tier is doctrine that nothing enforces, and six modules on the money path are below it while every wave mutates them
acceptance_criteria: The set of modules held to the critical tier is declared in the repository as data, not inferred from prose, and each entry names its threshold and why the module is critical

A check measures per-module coverage against that declaration and FAILS when a declared module is below its threshold. A doctrine no command can fail is the defect being fixed, so a report that only prints is not sufficient

The declaration is a ratchet: a module may be added, and one may be removed only with a stated reason in the same change. A declared module that no longer exists fails as stale, so drift is caught in both directions

The memory constraint that keeps --cover out of the dispatch gate is respected and its resolution stated. mix.exs records that :cover instruments every loaded beam and spikes multi-GB on cold trees, which is exactly what a harness worktree is - so the enforcement must not reintroduce that cost into every run. Either scope the instrumentation to the declared module set, or run the gate on a lane that is not the per-run dispatch check, and say which was chosen and what it costs

The measurement basis is stated in the output: offline-only coverage excludes the :network and :integration tiers, so a module's number is a floor rather than its true exercise. A reader must not be able to mistake one for the other

The six modules measured below tier on 2026-08-19 are recorded with their numbers as the starting state, so the first run of the new check reproduces them rather than starting from an unmeasured baseline

The guard is verified by BREAKING it, not by reading its test. The report states the mutation that was introduced, the exact failure message the guard produced, and that the mutation was reverted. A passing test proves the assertion runs; only a deliberate break proves it is wired to the gate and that its message names the offending thing. A guard whose test is green while its wiring is missing looks identical to a working one
out_of_scope: Writing the missing tests to bring any module up to tier - this task makes the tier binding and states the gap; raising a specific module is separate work under the rule it establishes
Changing which modules are critical as a judgement call beyond recording the current reading of critical-rules; a disputed entry is recorded with its dispute, not silently dropped
Parse-slice and recording coverage, which tasks 550 and 551 own - this task is ExUnit line coverage and nothing else
task.body:
Measured on origin/main in a gate worktree with mix test.json --cover, 2026-08-19. Overall 89.74%. Below the critical tier that critical-rules RAISE COVERAGE BEFORE MUTATING sets at 95% for money, signing and parser surfaces:

  Bourse.Unified.RequestShape.Hyperliquid   66.5%
  Bourse.Unified.RequestShape.Lighter       82.3%
  Bourse.Unified.ReadParse                  83.5%   (331 uncovered lines)
  Bourse.Dispatch                           89.2%
  Bourse.Parser                             90.0%
  Bourse.Unified.RequestShape.Binance       91.9%

These are the request path, the response path, and the dispatch between them. RequestShape.Hyperliquid at 66.5% is a DEX request builder: a third of what gets signed and sent is unexercised offline.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, to be carried into the deliverable rather than dropped: this is offline coverage. test_helper excludes the :network and :integration tiers, so live exercise raises these numbers by an unknown amount. The doctrine measures exactly this way and the task-641 reviewer measured the same way, so the readings are comparable - but they are a floor, not the whole truth about how much of each module is actually exercised.

THE DEFECT IS NOT THE SIX NUMBERS. It is that the tier binds nothing. No gate measures it, no check fails on it, so in practice the rule does not exist - and we mutate these modules every wave. Task 641 touched ReadParse; 633 and 651 touched the RequestShape layer. Under our own rule none of those mutations should have started before coverage was at tier, and nothing stopped them. The task-641 reviewer measured 83.5%, wrote it into its concerns, and approved anyway, which is the correct behaviour for a reviewer grading one task against its acceptance criteria - the rule was simply not part of anything it could fail.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS NON-TRIVIAL, and the reason this is not a one-line alias change: mix.exs already documents why --cover is absent from every gate - ":cover instruments every loaded beam, multi-GB spike on cold trees". A cold harness worktree is precisely that case, and a memory spike there surfaces as review_stuck rather than as a coverage failure. So the naive fix, adding --cover-threshold to check.dispatch, would trade a silent doctrine for flaky dispatch. The deliverable has to place the enforcement somewhere that pays that cost once rather than per run, or narrow the instrumentation to the declared module set, and state the trade it chose.

Filed as the instrument rather than as six coverage tasks: six tasks would each raise one module and leave the tier still unenforced, so a seventh module could drift below it the same week.

task.title: The fundingless predicate names one of the four market types the taxonomy already distinguishes, so an option or dated future is only caught when the venue happens to answer empty
acceptance_criteria: Which market types carry funding is decided against the providers own contracts and recorded as a carve, not asserted from the predicate. The claim under test is that a perpetual swap is the only type that funds, and that spot, dated futures and options do not - confirm it per supported venue rather than inheriting it

fundingless_symbol?/1 answers from that decision across the whole taxonomy. Symbol.detect_market_type/1 already returns option, future, swap and spot, so a predicate that names only spot is narrower than the vocabulary it reads

The populated-payload path is covered, not only the empty one. shape_singular_funding_rate/2 has two clauses: the empty-payload clause is type-independent and catches any market the venue answers nothing for, but the non-empty clause returns ok for every non-spot symbol - so a venue that answers a stale or zero row for a fundingless market still delivers it as a valid rate. That clause is where this task is verified

A fundingless market reports the fundingless reason rather than the unservable one. Today a dated COIN-M future reports unservable_funding_symbol, which says the venue would not serve it, when the truth is that the market has no funding at all - two different facts for the caller

Regression pinned per market type, with the live case chosen so it cannot rot: COIN-M demo still lists contracts that expired in 2021, so a probe that picks any dated future is likely to pick a dead one. Filter by expiry or state why the chosen contract is stable
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: The empty-payload clause and the loud-refusal behaviour task 646 landed, which stand and are live-verified
The plural fetch_funding_rates surface, unless the same predicate reaches it
Symbol denormalization for the binance inverse family, which task 583 owns
task.body:
Follow-on from the live verification of task 646, filed on evidence rather than on suspicion, and deliberately narrow.

646 landed and is confirmed live on binancecoinm demo, with a real before/after on the same venue: before, fetch_funding_rate for a dated future returned {:ok, []} - silent AND shape-violating, since a caller matching on a FundingRate struct receives an empty list; after, it returns the loud refusal. The perp control returns a populated rate. That part is closed.

What carries the dated futures is not the fundingless predicate. It is the empty-payload clause of shape_singular_funding_rate/2, which is venue- and type-independent and therefore the more robust of the two - it needs no taxonomy at all, only the observation that the venue returned nothing. The predicate itself reads:

    Symbol.detect_market_type(parsed) == :spot

while Symbol.detect_market_type/1 distinguishes option, future, swap and spot. So the predicate answers a four-valued question with a one-valued test, and the second clause of shape_singular_funding_rate/2 returns ok for every non-spot symbol whose payload is non-empty.

THE GAP, stated exactly. A fundingless market is caught today only when the venue answers empty. A venue that answers a stale row, a zero row, or the underlying perp's row for an option or a dated future produces a FundingRate the caller cannot distinguish from a real one - the original 646 defect, surviving in the cases where the venue is not helpfully silent. We have NOT observed such a venue; that is why this is scoped as the confrontation plus the predicate widening rather than as a bug report against a named venue.

Not done inline despite being a small diff: the load-bearing part is a domain claim about which market types fund, and that has to be read out of the providers own contracts per venue rather than out of our predicate. That is the class of assertion CLAUDE.md warns about hardcoding - a venue constant that is internally consistent, fully tested, and wrong about the world.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-19 - this task is now OBSERVED, not speculative, and the scores were raised accordingly. Measured on the landed base against two testnets:

  bybit option  BTC/USDT:USDT-270625-80000-P  -> ok, %FundingRate{symbol: the option symbol, rate: nil}
  bybit option  BTC/USDT:USDT-270625-80000-C  -> ok, %FundingRate{symbol: the option symbol, rate: nil}
  bybit swap    0G/USDT:USDT                  -> ok, rate 5.0e-5     (control)

So bybit hands the caller a FundingRate struct for an option - a market type that never funds - stamped with the option symbol and carrying a nil rate. That is the task-646 defect exactly, surviving in the case where the venue does not answer empty, and it lands through the non-empty clause of shape_singular_funding_rate/2 because fundingless_symbol? only recognises spot.

AND THE VENUES DISAGREE, which is why the per-venue confrontation criterion stays rather than being replaced by a blanket rule. deribit refuses the same class at the venue:

  deribit option  BTC/USD:BTC-260819-56000-C  -> error, bad_request (-32602)
  deribit future  AVAX/USDC:USDC-260819       -> error, bad_request (-32602)
  deribit swap    1000BONK/USDC:USDC          -> ok, rate 0.0        (control)

A blanket predicate change would be right for bybit and would mask, on deribit, that the venue itself is the one refusing. The deliverable is still the confrontation plus the widened predicate, but the widening now has a measured failing case to close rather than a hypothesis.

task.title: The unified symbol for a bybit dated future carries the venue-native date form, so every unified method crashes on all 44 of them
acceptance_criteria: future_ddmmmyy produces a canonical unified date the way option_with_settle already does. Both bybit patterns declare date_format ddmmmyy and the option normalises correctly while the future does not, so the fault is in the pattern handling and the authored spec is NOT to be changed

A convert_date/3 clause that accepts the venue form as a canonical input is explicitly the WRONG fix and must not be the deliverable. It removes the crash and permanently cements a unified symbol carrying a venue-dependent date form, after which every consumer that compares, stores or reconciles symbols across venues is silently wrong - loud replaced by quiet

convert_date/3 stops being able to raise FunctionClauseError, as the fallback rather than the fix. It is public with a spec and has no catch-all, so any unenumerated format pair kills the caller today; the final clause fails with a message naming both formats and the offending input. If the normalisation is right this path is unreachable for bybit

Verified in BOTH directions, not by absence of a crash: for every supported venue and every market type whose authored pattern has a non-null date_format, market.symbol goes through to_exchange_id and back, asserting the unified symbol carries the CANONICAL date form and the round trip yields the venue-native id. The set is computed from the authored patterns plus a market list, never hand-listed

The four measured calls that crash today on BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26 - to_exchange_id, fetch_ticker, fetch_ohlcv, fetch_order_book - complete or return a typed error, and the report names which pattern handler was wrong and why option_with_settle was already right
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: The RequestShape ArgumentError inventory, which task 653 owns - same contract principle, different module
Funding semantics for non-swap market types, which task 657 owns
Adding or removing supported venues or market types; this task makes the existing ones callable
task.body:
Measured live on bybit testnet 2026-08-19, on the landed base after 646 and 649. Found while probing task 657 - the probe run crashed.

    Bourse.Symbol.to_exchange_id  BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26  -> FunctionClauseError
    Bourse.fetch_ticker           BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26  -> FunctionClauseError
    Bourse.fetch_ohlcv            BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26  -> FunctionClauseError
    Bourse.fetch_order_book       BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26  -> FunctionClauseError
    fetch_funding_rate on a swap                          -> OK    (control)

    no function clause matching in Bourse.Symbol.convert_date/3

BTC/USDT:USDT-21AUG26 crashes identically. bybit testnet lists 44 dated futures, so every one of them is uncallable through every unified method - this is not funding-specific, it dies at the symbol layer before any method-specific code runs.

CONFIRMED IN THE CODE, and the structural fault is wider than the one format. convert_date/3 is public, carries a @spec, and its clauses cover only the pairs among yymmdd, ddmmmyy and yyyymmdd. There is NO catch-all. So the function is fatal for any format pair nobody thought to enumerate, and adding a fourth clause for whatever bybit emits leaves a fifth pair equally fatal. That is why the acceptance criteria ask for the unknown-pair behaviour to be decided once rather than for one more clause.

Not folded into 653 or 657, and the reason matters. 653 is the RequestShape error-contract inventory - 28 raise sites, none of them this one, because this lives in Bourse.Symbol. 657 is funding semantics for non-swap market types. Three different surfaces that happen to have been found in one probe run. Folding them would produce a task no single reviewer could verify as one thing.

The severity is what separates it from both: 657 hands the caller a wrong value, this hands every caller of a whole market type an exception, and it is a venue we support.

ROOT CAUSE LOCALISED AFTER FILING, 2026-08-19 - and it moves the task. The stacktrace points at convert_date/3, but that is the symptom. Compare unified symbols produced by fetch_markets on the same codebase:

  deribit future  AVAX/USDC:USDC-260819          canonical yymmdd
  deribit option  BTC/USD:BTC-260819-56000-C     canonical yymmdd
  bybit   option  BTC/USDT:USDT-270625-80000-P   canonical yymmdd
  bybit   future  BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26          VENUE-NATIVE ddmmmyy

The bybit dated future never gets normalised, so to_exchange_id/2 converts what it believes is a canonical yymmdd date and hands a seven-character string to a six-byte clause. The authored spec is right: markets.symbol_patterns declares date_format ddmmmyy for BOTH future and option, and the option comes out canonical - so the difference is future_ddmmmyy versus option_with_settle, not the declared format.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE HARMFUL ONE, which is why this is written down rather than left to the implementer. Adding a convert_date clause that tolerates the venue form makes the crash go away and locks a venue-dependent date into the unified symbol permanently. A consumer comparing or storing symbols across venues then gets wrong answers with no error at all. Loud becomes quiet, which is the trade this repository refuses everywhere else.

RADIUS MEASURED 2026-08-19, so the implementer does not have to guess it. Round trip of market.symbol through to_exchange_id, three symbols per cell, across the supported venues:

  deribit        option ok   future ok   swap ok   spot ok
  bybit          option ok   FUTURE 0/3 CRASH      swap ok   spot ok
  okx            option ok   future ok   swap ok   spot ok
  binance                    future ok   swap ok   spot ok
  binancecoinm               future ok   swap ok
  binanceusdm                future ok   swap ok
  hyperliquid                            swap ok   spot ok
  derive         option ok               swap ok   spot ok    (100 dated options)
  alpaca                                           spot ok    (14241 markets)

24 venue/market-type cells, exactly ONE broken: BTC/USDT:USDT-25DEC26, -21AUG26 and -04SEP26, all bybit future, all FunctionClauseError. okx also carries dated futures and derive carries 100 dated options, and both normalise correctly - so the mechanism exists and bybits future pattern is the exception, not the rule.

NOT MEASURED, stated so the table is not read as complete: lighter and coinbaseexchange were not probed - the first needs a credential form the probe did not build, the second failed in the probe script at construction, which is a defect in that script rather than a product finding. Both are perp- or spot-only and their authored patterns carry a null date_format, so they are unlikely candidates; the computed class test covers them regardless once it reads the market lists.

TWO CONSEQUENCES. First, the class test should come up green everywhere except that one cell on its first run - a ratchet documenting a state already nearly reached, not a migration. If the implementer finds MORE than bybit-future red, that is either something this measurement missed or a test measuring something else, and either is worth reporting rather than quietly fixing. Second, it refutes the reading that convert_date/3 is generally too narrow: eight other cells traverse it successfully. Making its unknown-pair behaviour loud stays right, but as the fallback, never as the diagnosis.
task.implemented: Landed at 9631b7f. What shipped is NOT what the re-scoped task asked: a four-line unconditional passthrough catch-all on convert_date/3, not the future_ddmmmyy normalisation. Root cause was later read in the landed tree — read_parse.ex bybit_yymmdd/1 stamps Calendar %d%b%y despite its name, so the market symbol never reaches the pattern handler. Task 660 carries the correction; recorded here rather than reopening.

task.title: OrderPrecision snap_value MatchError is a third contract for non-numeric order amounts
acceptance_criteria: A public non-bang create_order, create_orders, create_twap_order, or create_market_*_with_cost on a rounding venue (bybit, derive, hyperliquid, okx) with a wire-encodable but non-numeric amount or price returns {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} instead of raising MatchError
Bang variants still raise Bourse.Error for those cases
A scanner over OrderPrecision reddens when a new caller-input path can escape as MatchError, the same way 651/653 redden an unconverted RequestShape raise
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: RequestShape ArgumentError conversion (task 653)
Changing which values are invalid
OrderPrecision markets_not_loaded keep-raise, which 642/651 already kept
task.body:
Found while converting RequestShape caller-input ArgumentErrors (task 653). Unified.validate_param_values/2 lets atoms and other JSON-encodable non-numbers through. On rounding venues, OrderPrecision.snap_value/4 then does `{:ok, value} = Decimal.cast(original)` (lib/bourse/unified/order_precision.ex, snap_value). A failed cast raises MatchError from Unified.call/5, which is neither {:error, %Bourse.Error{}} nor a classified keep-raise.

Evidence: read of snap_value/4 after the 653 conversion. Hyperliquid create_order with amount: true would hit this before RequestShape.number_string. add_margin is not in the precision matrix so it does not; create_order is.

This is the same 587 class as 642/651/653 — a caller-input problem escaping as a third exception type. Do not weaken the assertion; convert or reject with Error at the precision snap, and close the class so a later MatchError bind reddens.
task.implemented: Landed by cursor via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787120633405-0504f04c, bc207e976089994300be5d1351a9772818469abe).

task.title: Bybit dated-future unified symbols still carry venue-native DDMMMYY after the 658 pass-through
acceptance_criteria: fetch_markets for a bybit LinearFutures or InverseFutures instrument emits a unified symbol whose expiry is canonical yymmdd (BTC/USDT:USDT-260904), not Calendar %d%b%y (BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26)
option_with_settle remains canonical yymmdd and the authored bybit future date_format stays ddmmmyy — the stamp is the bug, not the spec
A convert_date/3 clause that accepts DDMMMYY as a yymmdd input is not the deliverable. The 658 catch-all already did that and locked the venue form in

convert_date/3 unknown-pair behaviour is loud: the catch-all names both formats and the offending input instead of returning the string unchanged. This path stays unreachable for a correctly stamped bybit future
The class test asserted by 658 (every venue and market type with a non-null date_format) asserts the UNIFIED side is canonical yymmdd, not merely that native ids round-trip after a pass-through
The four calls that used to crash on BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26 still complete or return a typed error when the caller uses the canonical unified symbol BTC/USDT:USDT-260904

Outbound native ids for bybit dated futures keep the venue-padded day (04SEP26, never 4SEP26). Deribit continues to accept the day width its live ids actually use. Do not globally pad convert_date/3 without confronting each venue
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: RequestShape ArgumentError inventory (task 653)
OrderPrecision MatchError (task 659)
Funding semantics for non-swap market types (task 657)
Changing authored symbol_patterns.future.date_format
task.body:
Task 658 asked for future_ddmmmyy to emit a canonical unified date the way option_with_settle already does, and named a convert_date/3 pass-through that accepts the venue form as the WRONG fix. What landed (9631b7f / d0aabbe) is that forbidden pass-through: convert_date/3 now returns the input unchanged for an unenumerated pair or a non-6-byte yymmdd source, and the new tests pin BTC/USDT:USDT-04SEP26 as a valid unified symbol.

The crash is gone. The unified symbol is still venue-native.

ROOT CAUSE, read in the landed tree, not inferred from the 658 stacktrace. fetch_markets does not reverse the future pattern. lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex bybit_market_symbol/4 builds LinearFutures and InverseFutures as Symbol.build(base, quote) <> ":" <> settle <> bybit_expiry_suffix(raw). bybit_yymmdd/1 is named for the canonical form and then does Calendar.strftime("%d%b%y") |> String.upcase(), so market.symbol carries 04SEP26. Options on the same venue already go through Symbol.from_exchange_id/3 and come out yymmdd. reverse_future_ddmmmyy / parse_bybit_future already convert DDMMMYY to yymmdd (BTCUSDT-04SEP26 -> BTC/USDT:USDT-260904). The pattern handler is not the missing conversion; the stamp never calls it.

The 658 class test then hid the miss: it starts from market.symbol (already DDMMMYY), to_exchange_id pass-throughs, from_exchange_id canonicalises, and to_exchange_id of that canonical form is never asserted to equal the original unified symbol. Days 1-9 would also fail the native round-trip because convert_date yymmdd->ddmmmyy emits unpadded 4SEP26 while Bybit's live ids pad (04SEP26, measured 2026-08-19). Deribit tests currently expect the unpadded form, so a global pad_two in convert_date/3 is not the fix.

Do what 658 asked: stamp canonical yymmdd from deliveryTime (or reverse the native id through the existing future pattern, the way options already do), make the convert_date/3 unknown-pair clause fail loud, and rewrite the class test so a venue-native unified expiry reddens. The public_api_live_test.exs dated-future assertion currently pins Calendar %d%b%y and will have to move with the stamp.

FIRST verification move is a live bybit testnet fetch_markets on a dated future plus to_exchange_id of the returned symbol, not a fixture replay of the 658 pass-through tests.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787120630739-850c2563, 44257b40f110626d2e94f5bcda456ae344747241).

task.title: Bybit InverseFutures native ids are quarterly codes, not DDMMMYY
acceptance_criteria: Live bybit testnet InverseFutures ids match the venue form measured 2026-08-19 (BTCUSDU26, BTCUSDZ26, ETHUSDU26, ETHUSDZ26), not BASE-DDMMMYY
