to_exchange_id of the stamped unified symbol (BTC/USD:BTC-260925) without loaded markets emits the live inverse id (BTCUSDU26), not the Deribit inverse shape (BTC-25SEP26)
from_exchange_id of BTCUSDU26 under :future recovers the canonical unified symbol BTC/USD:BTC-260925
Linear Bybit dated futures stay BASEQUOTE-DDMMMYY with the venue-padded day (BTCUSDT-04SEP26). Deribit inverse stays BASE-DMMMYY
A live fetch_ticker or fetch_order_book on the inverse unified symbol reaches /v5/market/* with symbol=BTCUSDU26 (or the live equivalent) and returns a typed success or typed provider error
apply_future_ddmmmyy/2 selects the venue id grammar from the authored spec, not from the market shape: the branch on quote == USD and settle == base no longer decides that a market is Deribit-inverse
pad_ddmmmyy_day/1 is reachable only for the venue whose ids actually pad the day; it does not sit in a venue-agnostic catch-all branch

convert_date/3 from ddmmmyy to yymmdd fails on a malformed input instead of returning it unchanged: the regex fallback clause no longer returns date_str, so both directions of the pair behave the same way
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Changing the InverseFutures unified expiry stamp (task 660 already stamps yymmdd from deliveryTime)
Changing authored symbol_patterns.future.date_format
Globally padding convert_date/3
task.body:
Task 660 stamps Bybit InverseFutures as canonical yymmdd from deliveryTime (BTC/USD:BTC-260925). The live native id is not DDMMMYY.

Measured 2026-08-19 on api-testnet.bybit.com fetch_markets: four InverseFutures — BTCUSDU26, BTCUSDZ26, ETHUSDU26, ETHUSDZ26. apply_future_ddmmmyy treats quote=USD settle=base as Deribit inverse, so to_exchange_id("BTC/USD:BTC-260925") without loaded markets emits BTC-25SEP26. That is not an addressable Bybit instrument.

parse_bybit_future only matches BASEQUOTE-DDMMMYY (the linear family). The inverse quarterly grammar (root + month code + yy) is not reversed either, so from_exchange_id("BTCUSDU26", :future) cannot recover the unified symbol.

Do not invent the month-code table. Confront the live InverseFutures catalog plus Bybit's own instrument-id docs, then author the reverse and the outbound so a markets-unloaded to_exchange_id of the 660 stamp equals market.id.

FIRST verification move is a live bybit testnet fetch_markets of an InverseFutures row plus to_exchange_id of its stamped symbol, compared to market.id.

2026-08-19, orchestrator whole-surface pass: the bybit-inverse symptom is one
instance of a class. apply_future_ddmmmyy/2 in lib/bourse/symbol.ex chooses the
id grammar by inspecting the parsed market -- quote == USD and settle == base
means Deribit inverse, separator underscore with USDC means Deribit linear,
everything else falls into the catch-all -- and never consults which venue the
config belongs to. Bybit inverse satisfies the first predicate, so it is emitted
in Deribit form.

Task 660 then added pad_ddmmmyy_day/1 into that same catch-all branch. Its
comment says the padding is a bybit rule, but the branch is every venue that is
not one of the two Deribit shapes. Today only bybit and deribit declare
date_format ddmmmyy, and both Deribit families take an earlier branch, so the
padding is bybit-only by accident of the venue set rather than by construction.
A third ddmmmyy venue with unpadded ids would silently inherit bybit padding.

Scope this task as the class fix, not as a bybit-inverse patch: the outbound
builder must dispatch on the authored venue spec. Fixing only the inverse case
leaves the next venue to rediscover it.

2026-08-19, measured on the landed stand by the gate session, not derived: the
four inverse markets were already broken before 660. A worktree on bc207e9 ran
the same script and emitted the byte-identical wrong id (BTC-25SEP26) for
BTCUSDU26. 660 changed only the unified form beside it (25SEP26 becomes 260925),
which is the part it was meant to repair. So this task is a pre-existing defect
with no regression share -- four markets on one venue, both directions dead,
since from_exchange_id cannot recover BTCUSDU26 either. Nothing about 660 needs
reverting.

Same pass found a second, narrower survivor of the 658 shape inside symbol.ex:
the ddmmmyy to yymmdd clause still has a silent fallback returning its input
when the regex does not match, while the opposite direction reaches the new
raise. One pair, two contradictory contracts. Folded in here rather than filed
separately because this task already owns the date handling in this module.

task.title: An unrecognized caller option is reported as a recoverable venue network fault and melts the circuit breaker, taking every read on that venue down
acceptance_criteria: A caller-supplied option the client does not recognize is rejected before any HTTP request is attempted, with a non-recoverable Bourse.Error (recoverable: false, no :network retry class) whose message names the offending option -- not a :network_error attributed to the venue
A rejected caller option leaves the venue's fuse untouched: a test issues more bad-option calls than the melt threshold and asserts Bourse.CircuitBreaker.status(venue) is still closed afterwards

A genuine transport exception raised inside the request still classifies as :network_error and still melts -- pinned by a regression test, so the fix cannot be satisfied by making the rescue stop melting altogether

The rescue in Bourse.HTTP no longer treats every raised exception as a transport fault: transport faults and caller/programming faults are separated, and the melt decision flows through the same classification path the other branches use instead of the unconditional CircuitBreaker.record_failure

The option surface of Bourse.load_markets/2 is decided deliberately and stated in its @doc: either it accepts the account-selection option its sibling private reads accept, or it rejects unknown options loudly -- the choice and its rationale are recorded, so a caller threading one request_opts list through several reads gets a defined answer instead of a silent divergence
Live on Binance testnet: the reported call Bourse.load_markets(ex, type: "swap") returns the decided behavior, and Bourse.CircuitBreaker.status("binance") is :ok both before and after
mix check.dispatch green
out_of_scope: Circuit-breaker thresholds, and which venue-returned error classes melt -- the Phase 13 retry classification stays untouched
Adding account-selection semantics to any method beyond deciding load_markets/2's option surface
The consumer-side workaround in trading_dashboard
task.body:
Consumer report: ../bourse/BUGS.md, 2026-08-22, trading_dashboard
(TradingDashboard.Risk), verified live against Binance testnet.

The reported symptom is that `Bourse.load_markets(ex, type: "swap")` fails while
`fetch_balance/2`, `fetch_positions/2` and `fetch_open_orders/2` accept the same
option, so a caller cannot thread one request_opts set through
`PortfolioRisk.scope/3`. That asymmetry is the visible half. The damaging half is
how the failure is classified: three Binance credentials in one snapshot melted
the venue fuse, after which every Binance read in the application failed with
`Binance circuit open`, pointing at Binance for a fault that originated in the
caller's own keyword list.

Verified mechanism on the landed tree (not taken from the report):

  1. `Bourse.HTTP.request/4` builds `extra_opts` with `Keyword.drop/2` over a
     fixed list of known keys (`:params`, `:headers`, `:timeout`, `:base_url`,
     `:body_encoding`, `:endpoint_weight`, `:endpoint_rate_limit`). It is a
     deny-list: any key the client does not know about survives.
  2. `extra_opts` is merged into the Req option list and forwarded verbatim, so
     Req is the first thing that sees the unknown key and raises.
  3. The rescue in `execute_request/6` catches it, calls
     `CircuitBreaker.record_failure/1` unconditionally, and returns
     `Error.network_error(message: "Exception: ...")` -- recoverable: true,
     retry_class: :network.

Step 3 is the invariant gap. Every other branch of that same case statement
routes through `CircuitBreaker.record_result/2` so the melt decision flows from
the retry classification; the rescue bypasses it and melts on anything that
raises. The adjacent hazard was already noticed once -- the comment above the
rescue records that task 255 moved the response classifier outside it so a
classifier bug could not be mislabeled as a network error -- but the rescue
itself still conflates a caller programming error with venue downtime.

The class is broader than the reported instance: any unrecognized option, on any
venue and any method, is forwarded to Req, raises, melts that venue's fuse and
blames the venue. `Bourse.Error` already carries `:bad_request` in its
non-recoverable set, so the correct classification exists and is unused here.

Note that the `api/2` declarations in `lib/bourse.ex` already state each method's
accepted option set (load_markets declares plug/params/timeout). Nothing enforces
the declaration at runtime, which is what lets an undeclared option reach Req at
all -- worth confronting when deciding criterion 5, since an enforced declaration
would answer both halves of the report at once.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787379342610-20a28171, fda5fa71726225679f93b4396897cb9a61194256).

task.title: The unified write boundary silently discards caller intent: an uninterpretable `side` routes to a DEFAULT direction instead of erroring
acceptance_criteria: A `side` value the library cannot interpret returns a tagged `{:error, _}` naming the invalid side and the accepted forms, BEFORE any HTTP request is issued — proven by an offline capture asserting no request reached the plug — for every unified method that takes a side (create_order and its create_*_order siblings, create_market_order_with_cost, edit_order and its siblings)

The atom forms `:buy` / `:sell` are accepted and normalized, or rejected — pick one, state which in the moduledoc with the reason, and make every venue agree; the current state where `RequestShape.Lighter.side_is_ask!/1` accepts `:sell` while deribit's endpoint selection does not is the defect

This validation is unconditional: it does NOT depend on `sanity: true` (default false, task 411) and does NOT depend on markets having been loaded — pinned by a test that calls create_order with a bad side on an exchange with no load_markets

No conditional endpoint selection whose branches differ in ORDER DIRECTION carries a silent `default`: an unmatched side is an error, never a direction. deribit `endpoints.request.endpoint_selection.createOrder` (`{cases: [{path: sell, when: {side: sell}}], default: buy}`) is the live instance; audit every authored venue for the same shape and record the result

Live deribit testnet confrontation, recorded in the completion note with instrument, order ids and cleanup: an atom-side call is refused client-side with no order placed, and the string-side call still places correctly in both directions

The `params:` channel facet is confronted live and its verdict recorded: pass `%{"reduce_only" => true}` to a deribit create_order and determine whether the value reaches the wire. If an unrecognized caller param key is silently dropped on a write path, that is the same defect class (caller intent discarded without a word) and is fixed here; if the venue-native key is `reduceOnly` and the report used the wrong spelling, record that as the finding and make the drop audible
`mix check.dispatch` passes and no previously-green fixture or gate turns red
out_of_scope: Re-litigating task 411's decision that market/limit/precision sanity checks stay opt-in — only enum interpretability becomes unconditional here
Adding new unified order types or venue coverage
WebSocket order entry
task.body:
Consumer report 2026-08-22 (`trading_dashboard`, live Deribit testnet, BUGS.md top entry):
`Bourse.create_order(ex, "BTC-PERPETUAL", :market, :sell, 10)` placed a **BUY**. Three
consecutive calls each increased an existing long instead of reducing it. The string form
`"sell"` is correct. No error, no warning — the venue echoed `direction: "buy"`.

Root cause, read from the code (evidence, not hypothesis):

- `priv/specs/json/output/authored/deribit.json` →
  `endpoints.request.endpoint_selection.createOrder` is
  `{"cases": [{"path": "sell", "when": {"side": "sell"}}], "default": "buy"}`, and the same
  method's request defaults carry `"_omit": ["side"]`. On deribit the direction IS the
  endpoint — nothing else on the wire carries it. So an atom `:sell` fails the string match,
  falls to `default`, and becomes a buy with the side param omitted entirely.
- `Bourse.Order.Sanity.check_side/1` already rejects anything outside `~w(buy sell)`, but
  sanity is opt-in (`sanity: true`, default `false` — task 411's deliberate decision) and is
  skipped when markets are not loaded. So the one guard that would have caught this is off by
  default on the money path.
- The venues disagree with each other today:
  `RequestShape.Lighter.side_is_ask!/1` matches `["sell", :sell]`;
  `RequestShape.Bybit` does `Map.get(params, "side", "buy")`;
  `RequestShape.OKX` derives `posSide` from `params["side"] == "sell"` (an unmatched side
  silently becomes `long` on a hedged account — the same failure in a different field).

The defect is not "deribit does not accept atoms". It is that **the unified write boundary
lets caller intent it cannot interpret pass through as a default** — and on a direction field
the default is a position in the opposite direction. The fix is one strict resolver at the
boundary (next to `Bourse.Unified.validate_param_values/2`, which task 587 already
established as the place where non-encodable params are refused before dispatch), plus the
removal of every direction-bearing silent `default` in the authored selection layer.

The reporter also observed `params: %{"reduce_only" => true}` echoed back as
`reduce_only: false`. **Premise unverified — confirm before building on it:** the deribit
authored request sources `reduce_only` from `reduceOnly` (`native_passthrough`), so the
reporter's snake_case key may simply never have been a recognized param. Either way the
outcome is the same class — a caller-supplied protective flag vanished without a word — so
the confrontation and its verdict belong in this task, per the acceptance criterion.

Dispatch trigger (routing): money path and order direction — a wrong-direction order is the
worst failure this library can produce — plus a public error-contract change across every
order-taking unified method. Live testnet evidence is required, which no inline session
should fabricate.

Consumer impact recorded in the report: `trading_dashboard`'s own write path stringifies
before calling, so it was not hit in production; the exposure is any REPL/operator call and
any new consumer writing idiomatic Elixir. Cost of discovery: three unintended testnet buys.

Doc authority for the venue side: https://docs.deribit.com/api-reference/trading/private-sell
— a sell is its own endpoint, so the direction is chosen inside this library, not by the venue.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787393524982-4c7f35a0, 5cde00f5976a00b7d53e274d3769252426aaaf25).

task.title: Unified `notional` is authored nil for every non-future deribit position kind, so an open option contributes nothing to a size fold
acceptance_criteria: A deribit OPTION position returns a populated `notional` with a `notional_currency` that names the unit the figure is actually in — derived from the venue's own contract, not from a convenient assumption; the derivation and its authority are recorded as a carve register entry
The future rows keep their current values byte-for-byte: `notional` still comes from `size` for `kind = future`, and the existing DeribitPositionUnits contract-quantity reconciliation is unchanged

When the inputs the derivation needs are NOT in hand — the common case of an exchange built without `load_markets`, where no `contract_size` is available — `notional` stays nil rather than being computed from a guessed contract size. Pinned by a test that fetches positions on an exchange with no loaded markets
`put_notional_currency/2` still refuses to ship a populated `notional` without a currency: the `{:error, {:missing_position_notional_currency, _}}` path is exercised for the new kind, not bypassed

The other option-carrying first-class venues (okx, bybit) are audited for the same authored guard and the finding is recorded — fix them here if the same derivation applies, or state per venue why it does not
Live deribit testnet evidence, recorded in the completion note: one account holding an option and a future at once, the raw payload and the resulting unified rows for both, with the arithmetic shown
`mix check.dispatch` passes; the provider-live REST-read contract lane (`mix ccxt.verify_rest_read_contracts`) shows no case that was green before this change turning red
out_of_scope: Making an option notional additively summable with a future notional — delta-weighting is the consumer's problem and the report says so explicitly
Populating `contracts` / `contract_size` differently for futures (task 626 territory)
Emulating any field the venue does not publish
task.body:
Consumer report 2026-08-22 (`trading_dashboard`, live Deribit testnet, BUGS.md top entry): a
deribit **option** position comes back with `notional: nil` and therefore `notional_currency:
nil`, while the sibling **future** row on the same account is populated. The consumer folds
open positions into a long/short notional pair that feeds hedge sizing; a nil coerced to zero
made an open option contribute zero to the hedge book while printing a `0` that reads as real.

Confirmed in the tree (evidence, not hypothesis) — the nil is **authored, not accidental**:

- `priv/specs/json/output/authored/deribit.json` →
  `normalization.field_maps.position.field_map.notional` is a `when` rule guarded on
  `kind in ["future"]`, `then` reading `size`, **`else: null`**. The sibling `contracts` rule
  is the mirror image: null for futures, `size` otherwise. So for an option the map
  deliberately declines to call `size` a notional — which is correct as far as it goes,
  because deribit option `size` is a contract count, not a value.
- `Bourse.Unified.DeribitPositionUnits.reconcile_position/2` matches only
  `%{"kind" => "future"}`; every other kind falls through the catch-all at the bottom of the
  module untouched.
- `put_notional_currency/2` short-circuits on `%Position{notional: nil}` and returns the
  position unchanged, so the unit is never attached either — consistent with `Position`'s
  moduledoc ("Populated whenever `notional` is populated").

So the gap is the missing derivation, not a broken mapping: nothing converts an option's
contract count into a value, even though the reporter shows every input in hand
(`contracts` on the struct, `contract_size` on the option market, `mark_price` and
`index_price` / `average_price_usd` in the raw payload).

**The substance of this task is the unit question, not the multiplication.** Deribit quotes an
option's `mark_price` in the base currency per contract, so the natural product is
base-denominated — a different currency from the future row's, which is why
`notional_currency` exists and why shipping a number without it is not acceptable. Read
deribit's own position documentation
(https://docs.deribit.com/api-reference/account-management/private-get_positions) and decide
what the venue actually publishes before choosing the formula; the reporter's
`0.1 x 1.0 x 0.00701189 = 0.000701189 BTC` is a plausible reading offered as evidence, not a
specification to implement unexamined.

**The markets-not-loaded caveat is load-bearing.** The repro ran without `load_markets`, which
is why even the future row shows `contracts: nil` — `market_units/1` had nothing to build
from. A derivation that needs `contract_size` therefore cannot silently substitute 1.0 when
markets are absent; nil is the honest answer there, and the acceptance criteria pin it.

Dispatch trigger (routing): live external-system evidence is required — an account holding an
option and a future simultaneously on deribit testnet — and the change alters a
money-relevant unified field consumed for position sizing. Serialize against task 663: both
tasks write `priv/specs/json/output/authored/deribit.json`.
task.implemented: Deribit option positions now derive notional as abs(contracts) * contract_size * abs(mark_price) in the parsed settlement currency, only when loaded markets supply a positive contract_size; future rows unchanged, carve register entry C-T664 records the derivation and its authority. OKX/Bybit audited: neither authors the future-only null notional.

task.title: A side that is not exactly "buy" or "sell" still becomes a direction on every batch write path
acceptance_criteria: A batch write whose first order map carries an uninterpretable side (the atom `:sell`, an unknown string, a number) returns a tagged `{:error, _}` naming the invalid value and the accepted forms, BEFORE any HTTP request — proven against a live testnet venue by asserting the error is returned with no order appearing in a subsequent live `fetch_open_orders`, for every batch method that takes `:orders`
The refusal is unconditional: it does not depend on `sanity: true` and does not depend on loaded markets, pinned by a test on an exchange built without `load_markets`

Every valid batch call still works unchanged: a two-entry `create_orders` with string sides in both directions places both orders on a live testnet venue and both are observed in `fetch_open_orders` before cleanup

No RequestShape function maps an uninterpretable side to a direction any more. `RequestShape.Hyperliquid.buy_side?/1` is the named instance; audit every venue's RequestShape for the same shape and record the result per venue

A guard test proves the class rather than the enumerated list: adding a method whose side lives inside a nested map, or a RequestShape clause that defaults an unmatched side to a direction, turns the suite red

Live confrontation on deribit testnet, recorded in the completion note with instrument, order ids and cleanup: a batch call with a nested atom side is refused client-side with no order placed, and the string-side batch still places correctly in both directions
`mix check.dispatch` passes; the provider-live REST-read contract lane (`mix ccxt.verify_rest_read_contracts`) shows no case that was green before this change turning red
out_of_scope: Re-litigating task 663's decision that atoms are rejected rather than coerced — this task extends that decision to the remaining entry points, it does not revisit it
Validating anything about an order entry other than its side; amount/price/type sanity stays where task 411 put it
task.body:
Task 663 made an uninterpretable `side` a hard `{:error, %Bourse.Error{type: :invalid_parameters}}` before dispatch — but only for the positional-side methods. The guard is derived from the method table: `lib/bourse/unified.ex:524` builds `@side_methods` from `:side in params`, and every batch write declares `[:orders]` instead (`create_orders`, `create_spot_orders`, `create_contract_orders`, `create_uta_orders`, `edit_orders` — verified in the method table at lines 254-293). So a nested `side: :sell` inside an `orders[]` entry never reaches `validate_side_param/2` and still falls through to whatever the venue shape does with an unrecognized value.

The invariant this task establishes is the whole class, not the batch instance: NO unified write entry point may turn a side it cannot interpret into a direction. That includes the last-resort layer — `Bourse.Unified.RequestShape.Hyperliquid.buy_side?/1` (lines 276-277) maps every non-binary value to `false`, i.e. silently to SELL. Task 663's boundary makes that unreachable from `Unified.call/3` for positional sides, but it is still a live footgun for batch entries and for any direct RequestShape caller. Make the refusal structural rather than enumerated, so a method added later cannot re-open the hole by declaring its side inside a nested map.

task.title: Option position notional is derived per venue with no shared rule, so the same field carries a different unit on each one
acceptance_criteria: The unified meaning of `notional` on an OPTION position is stated once, in the moduledoc, with the reason — and `notional_currency` names the unit that figure is actually in on every venue that populates it

okx coin-margined option rows no longer take the inverse-perpetual path: the value is derived from a field okx itself publishes for options, chosen against okx's own API documentation, with the choice and its authority recorded as a carve register entry
bybit option rows are confronted against the same rule — either they already satisfy it (asserted against a live bybit testnet option position and said so) or they are corrected here

okx and bybit SWAP / linear / inverse perpetual rows are unchanged, asserted against live testnet perpetual positions on both venues with the arithmetic shown — this task must not move a perpetual notional
Where the derivation's inputs are not in hand (no `load_markets`, no contract size), `notional` stays nil rather than being computed from a guess, pinned per venue
A cross-venue invariant test fails when any venue populates an option `notional` without a `notional_currency`, or derives one through a code path authored for a different instrument kind

Live testnet evidence per venue, recorded in the completion note with the raw payload, the resulting unified row and the arithmetic shown — an account holding one option position on okx and one on bybit
`mix check.dispatch` passes and no previously-green fixture, oracle or gate turns red
out_of_scope: Making option and future notionals additively summable — delta-weighting is the consumer's problem, as task 664 already recorded
Re-deriving deribit's option notional; C-T664 stands unless this task's shared rule contradicts it, in which case the contradiction is stated and deribit is brought into line
task.body:
Task 664 gave deribit option positions a real `notional` derived from the venue's own contract (`contracts * contract_size * mark_price`, in the settlement currency, carve `C-T664`). The audit it ran surfaced that the other option-carrying venues do not share a rule — each arrives at `notional` by a different route, and at least one of them produces a unit nobody chose:

- okx coin-margined options (`BTC-USD-...-C`) match `okx_inverse_inst_id?/1` (`lib/bourse/unified/read_parse.ex:3371`), so an option row takes the INVERSE PERPETUAL formula `contracts * ctVal / markPx` against a premium-denominated `markPx`. On an okx option row that is a different figure from either published field (observed `notionalUsd` 649.947 vs `optVal` 0.0000001084604966; re-confirm against a live okx demo option position). Without loaded markets it is nil for lack of `contract_size`.
- bybit option rows read `_bourse_notional` from the published `positionValue`.
- deribit now derives from the premium per task 664.

Three venues, three units, one field name. Decide the unified contract for what `notional` MEANS on an option row, name the authority for each venue from that venue's own documentation, and make every venue either satisfy it or state per venue why it cannot. The deliverable is the shared rule plus a cross-venue test that holds it, not a third per-venue patch.

task.title: Replace REST read semantic tests with provider-live E2E contracts
acceptance_criteria: An independent provider-contract inventory enumerates every supported REST read operation and every provider-defined semantic branch across all eleven venues; the runtime authored specs and the tests being replaced are not the denominator or oracle

Every inventoried case performs a real call to the provider-owned production-public or testnet/demo host and asserts domain semantics from one real success and one relevant real error; no fixture, mock, recording, self-authored golden or CCXT artifact can make a semantic case green

The test definitions are data plus ordinary Elixir scenario functions; macros may generate ExUnit shells, tags and mechanical completeness checks, but may not encode provider semantics, expected values or branch judgments

Missing credentials, an unreachable host, an unsupported account state or an unexercised inventory row fails loudly with actionable setup text; no semantic case skips, excludes itself or accepts arbitrary errors
Superseded fixture/mock REST-read semantic tests and helpers are deleted in the same delivery, and cloc over non-JSON test source is lower than the 74,276-line baseline measured at bourse 57284d8
One documented command executes the complete REST-read contract lane without hidden default exclusions and reports the inventory denominator, executed count and failures
mix check.dispatch passes; if canonical commands or reviewer rules change, CLAUDE.md is updated and AGENTS.md is regenerated in the same delivery
out_of_scope: State-changing REST operations, which are covered by the dependent write-lifecycle task
WebSocket semantics, which are covered by the dependent stream-lifecycle task
Deleting committed recordings that remain useful as provenance or an explicitly non-authoritative offline replay cache
Using the current test directory layout as the architecture template; inspect legacy tests only to identify what the new contract supersedes and delete it
task.body:
Design the REST-read verification lane from the provider contract outward, not by reshaping the current test tree. The target architecture is a compact contract matrix whose denominator comes from provider-owned docs/specs/SDKs and whose execution always reaches the real venue. Cover all eleven supported venues and every supported read call plus distinct provider-defined request/response/error branches.

A case must prove meaning, not merely HTTP status or JSON shape. First observe the live success and a relevant live error, confront their meaning against provider-owned authority, then encode the durable integration assertion. Runtime authored specs, CCXT, recordings and existing tests are implementation/reference inputs only and cannot certify the behavior.

Keep abstraction mechanical: data describes cases; ordinary functions perform and assert scenarios; a macro may generate repetitive ExUnit registration and completeness checks only. Delete the fixture/mock semantic architecture that each new live contract makes redundant. The current non-JSON test-source baseline is 74,276 lines (cloc over test plus native/lighter_signer/golden_test.go at source commit 57284d8), so this migration must be deletion-led rather than additive.

Routing trigger: live external-system semantics plus repo-wide test/check infrastructure. Harness reviewer must independently run the real lane with provisioned credentials and treat missing access as red evidence, never as green.

task.title: Replace REST write tests with real sandbox state-transition lifecycles
acceptance_criteria: An independent provider-contract inventory enumerates every supported state-changing REST operation and every provider-defined semantic branch across all credentialed venues; the runtime authored specs and legacy tests are not the denominator

Every inventoried write case changes real state on the provider's testnet/demo/paper environment, verifies the resulting state through an independent real read, and restores a clean state; HTTP acceptance alone is insufficient

Where the provider environment offers trading, the lane performs minimum-size real buy and sell lifecycles and covers the supported branches for market/limit, open/close, long/short, time-in-force, reduce-only, post-only, conditional, edit/cancel and batch behavior when those branches exist

Each relevant failure assertion comes from a deliberately triggered real provider error with its exact semantic meaning; no catch-all accepted error, fixture, mock, recording, self-authored golden or CCXT behavior can make a case green
Cases use unique client identifiers, bounded condition polling rather than sleeps, and verified cleanup of orders and positions; the suite never sends a write to a production-money host
Missing credentials, funds, liquidity, account mode or provider capability fails loudly with exact remediation; no write case silently skips or converts environmental inability into success
Superseded fixture/mock write semantic tests and helpers are deleted in the same delivery, and non-JSON test source is lower than the post-REST-read baseline
A documented command runs the entire write-lifecycle lane, reports inventory/executed/cleanup counts, and exits red if any residual test-owned order or position exists; mix check.dispatch passes
out_of_scope: Withdrawals or transfers that can leave the provider sandbox or move production value
WebSocket verification except when a stream is only used as an additional observation of a REST state transition
Deleting recordings retained as provenance or non-authoritative replay data
Preserving legacy fixture/mock tests merely to maintain historical coverage percentages
task.body:
Build provider-live state-transition contracts for every supported mutating REST call. This is the trading lane: real sandbox/demo/paper orders, real minimum-size buys and sells, real fills where the venue offers them, and separate reads that prove what changed. Derive the case matrix from provider-owned contracts rather than the current test layout or runtime specs.

Cover every branch the supported public API exposes, including order types and lifecycle controls only where the venue actually defines them. A successful response does not prove a write: observe order/position/account state, then cancel or close it and prove cleanup. Use unique client identifiers and bounded polling on provider state; never Process.sleep as correctness.

Failure cases deliberately trigger the exact provider error being asserted. Account restrictions, missing balance, missing liquidity or missing credentials are not acceptable pass paths. No production-money host may receive a write.

Delete the fixture/mock semantic tests and helpers superseded by this lane. The result must reduce test-source lines again rather than layering a second architecture over the first.

Routing trigger: money handling, live external-system semantics and repo-wide test infrastructure. Run only after the REST-read contract task has landed on origin/main.

acceptance_criteria: An independent provider-contract inventory covers every configured public/private WebSocket section and every provider-defined authentication, subscription, unsubscription, renewal/reconnect and rejection branch across the supported venues
Every success case connects to the real provider host and receives a provider data/event frame whose domain content is asserted; a connect result or subscription acknowledgement alone is not success

Coinbase Exchange's intentionally unconfigured WebSocket surface remains an explicit contract returning websocket_not_configured, distinct from unsupported_exchange

Using the legacy WebSocket test modules as the architectural template
task.body:
Design the WebSocket E2E lane from each provider's own stream contract. Cover all configured venue sections and their meaningful branches with real connections and real frames. An acknowledgement proves only that the provider accepted a request; success requires observing provider data, and private streams must be driven by a real provider-side account event when necessary.

Use ordinary scenario functions and compact case data. Macros may register ExUnit shells and check inventory completeness but may not encode venue semantics. Trigger real invalid authentication and subscription errors instead of replaying synthetic frames. Preserve Coinbase Exchange's deliberate no-WebSocket contract as a local boundary assertion.

Delete all stream mocks, fixture-semantic tests and local fake transports that the live lane supersedes; retain only genuinely pure protocol mechanics. The migration remains deletion-led.

task.title: Make provider-live E2E the canonical gate and delete residual legacy test architecture
acceptance_criteria: Every external-semantic assertion in the canonical suite is provider-live; grep and an architecture guard find no fixture, mock, recording, self-authored golden, CCXT artifact or local fake server acting as an oracle for REST or WebSocket behavior

Only provider-live E2E contracts plus minimal deterministic pure-mechanics tests remain; each retained offline test names the pure invariant it proves and cannot pass or fail based on an external provider semantic claim

The canonical mix test.json and mix check.dispatch paths actually execute the REST-read, REST-write and WebSocket contract lanes with no default tag exclusions capable of producing a green result without them

CLAUDE.md describes the resulting test boundary and canonical commands without stale fixture-first guidance; AGENTS.md is regenerated and mix ccxt.agents_md --check passes

task.body:
Converge the repository onto one testing model after the three provider-live lanes have landed. Delete every remaining semantic test whose authority is a fixture, mock, recording, generated expectation, authored runtime spec, CCXT artifact or local fake service. Retain small offline tests only for truly deterministic mechanics such as encoders, pure transformations and state-machine mechanics; each retained case must state that boundary.

Make the canonical commands honest. A default green must mean that live REST reads, real sandbox state transitions and real WebSocket frames all ran. Missing credentials or an unavailable provider makes the gate red, not excluded or skipped. Recordings can remain for provenance and opt-in replay/debugging, but cannot grade correctness.

This is a deletion and gate-flip task, not another additive suite. Compare final non-JSON test-source lines against the 74,276-line baseline at bourse 57284d8, remove obsolete helpers and tags, update CLAUDE.md, regenerate AGENTS.md, and verify the delivered origin/main with the complete live lane, mix check.dispatch and mix ci. Cleanup is part of correctness: no test-owned order or position may remain.

Routing trigger: CI/check infrastructure, repo-wide invariant and live trading safety. Dispatch as a solo final wave after the REST and WebSocket migrations land.

task.title: Make the provider-live REST-read contract compact and green
acceptance_criteria: The landed live runner, provider-authority pin validation, ordinary scenario functions and mechanical ExUnit generation remain; catalog machinery that only mirrors runtime metadata is removed rather than preserved for its own sake

The REST-read denominator is independently derived from pinned provider-owned contracts and explicit provider semantic branches; runtime-authored specs, __unified_endpoints__, provider_operation_prefixes and the inventory itself may detect drift but cannot define or shrink coverage

mix ccxt.verify_rest_read_contracts executes every supported branch against the real provider host with denominator equal to executed and zero failed, skipped, excluded or invalid cases; an out-of-environment provider branch stays visibly unverified with exact provider, host and account evidence and is never counted as verified

Every success case asserts exact domain meaning from provider-owned authority; generic shape, struct-only, any-field, recursive-key-substring and arbitrary-empty checks cannot make a case green, and an empty result is valid only when the scenario deliberately creates and asserts that provider-defined empty state

Every supported operation and semantic branch proves one real success and one relevant deliberately triggered provider error; a venue-wide invalid-symbol probe cannot stand in for unrelated operations

Every live failure present when implementation begins is resolved through a client, authored-spec or scenario correction, or remains explicitly unverified with evidence; deleting a red row, accepting arbitrary errors or weakening its assertion is not resolution, and the provider-live-only guard remains green

The canonical aliases and documentation describe the lane truthfully and execute the complete REST-read matrix at most once per gate; an independent reviewer records green mix ccxt.verify_rest_read_contracts and mix check.dispatch runs with the provisioned credentials, and any warning or failed live check requires rejection

task.body:
Task 667 left a useful provider-live runner around a self-grading, runtime-derived catalog. Keep the live execution, provider source-pin checks, ordinary scenario functions and mechanical ExUnit shell; replace duplicated catalog rows and generic assertions with compact shared semantic scenarios derived from provider-owned contracts and observed live behavior.

Fix client, authored-spec and scenario defects exposed by the lane. The provider-live-only boundary established by source commit 1995bde remains intact. No fixture, replay, mock or legacy semantic suite returns, and the canonical gates execute the complete REST-read matrix once rather than layering duplicate runs.

Routing trigger: live external-system semantics, public API contract repair and a repo-wide test invariant. Do not dispatch task 668 until this task is reviewer-approved and confirmed landed on origin/main.

The compile-time loader rotates the disk format back so the in-memory spec map is unchanged: a recorded deep-equality check (old loaded map == new loaded map) passes for all eleven venues, and Bourse.Spec.Schema still raises on any missing/forbidden slot with unreduced strictness

task.body:
The operator's stated goal (2026-08-23): the authored specs must be reviewable against each venue's real published API documentation. Today each venue is one monolithic facet-major JSON (binance ~500KB post-cleanup, ~20 top-level keys) where a single endpoint's definition is smeared across up to 9-14 sibling maps — request defaults in one, parse mapping in another, params in a third. No human or reviewer can diff "our deribit private/get_positions" against Deribit's docs page for it.

Rotate the disk layout endpoint-major: one endpoint = one object, the unit of authoring, review and diff. Split each venue document into a small set of clearly named files under priv/venues/<venue>/authored/ (suggested: venue.json for identity/urls/signing, markets.json, endpoints.json for the unified methods, raw.json for raw endpoints, errors.json — adapt if the data argues otherwise). The compile-time loader (Bourse.Spec) reassembles the exact facet-major in-memory map so Bourse.Spec.Schema, the exchange generator macro and every consumer stay untouched; the deep-equality of loaded maps before vs after is the mechanical proof, and the 427-case provider-live contract lane is the semantic proof. Keep @external_resource coverage so edits to any split file trigger recompilation.

A pre-cleanup session measurement (2026-08-23, before commit 1cb12e5 deleted the unread descriptor sources) found ~3.6x descriptor duplication across the binance family; re-measure on the current tree before hoisting and report actual numbers rather than reusing that figure.

Routing trigger: repo-wide format invariant across all eleven authored specs plus the compile-time loader, gated by live external-system evidence (the contract lane).
